review_text: Very nice atmosphere. The restaurant has a very unique and delicious menu. I recommend The Hen In The Wood appetizer with the black pepper pasta with poached egg. Enjoyable beer selection the IPA is on point. Very nice fine dining experience. Only disappointment was no invitation to the soft opening even though I work next door at the custom shoe store. Lovely restaurant, will be coming back soon.

Alsatian cuisine at its best. Yes true I am from Alsace but the following dishes were exceptionnal:
- langoustine appetizer
- sweetbread dumplings
- foie gras / squab

There were other good dishes my wife and I ordered (eg the quail) but if you order from the prix-fixe the above are a must-have.

The amuse bouches added a nice touch. Bread was good but not an Alsatian specialty ! The variation on Kugelhopf was interesting.

On top of this we had a gewurtztraminer from Alsace (2012 I believe) for $55.

Only thing missing was a tarte flambee - my favorite dish from The Modern.

Might be back for the tasting menu.

We went the third night it opened and had an extraordinary meal.  The service was formal but incredibly warm and gracious.  Every course was delectable. The restaurant is incredibly thoughtful from the beautiful plates, gorgeous interior, to a varied and dynamic menu to choose from.  Even the crumb dusters had character!  The cocktail and wine selections were both excellent as well.

Already here second time after two days. Yep, it is that GOOD :) Also happened to catch up with a foodie friend, I suggested GK without even thinking. Because it is the best new restaurant top of my head right now. 

Since it is my 2nd time around, I will just go straight to the food. When I first time here two days ago, we prob tried out 1/3 of the pre-fix menu except for the pasta section. So my goal tonight is to try out the rest of the uncharted territory on the menu. So here we go.

Prior to the dinner we are presented the traditional Alsacien bread with chive fromage blanc. When it came on the table it is still warm - light crispy outside and flurry, scallion fragrant inside. My friend joked it is a healthier, tastier version of Chinese scallion pancake :/ The star is the chive fromage, it is just right amount of creaminess so it is easy to spread. And I love chive for its delicate, onion-y fragrance yet not as overpowering. Adding it to the fromage helps alleviate the heaviness of cheese. Before we knew it, we have scrapped all the cheese and bread...Warning! Don't do the same mistake as we do! There are three rounds of different bread during the meal. Take a bite each and stop!  We didn't and were stuffed before the end of our courses and I have to pack my main and skip the dessert :(

Amuse bouche - peach soup (apricot, last time, I think), corn custard and curried cracker with english pee puree. All taste as good as they are presented. Def wake up your taste bud and appetite. 

Starter: Langoustine tartar with flying fish roe, salty fingers, seasoned with cauliflower-macadamia puree. This is exceptional. I have always loved langoustine - I will have them everytime I go to Barcelona. Here the little monster is deformed and mixed with tiny, crunch flying fish roe and a salty little plant called salty fingers, dressed with nutty-savory cauliflower and macadamia puree. On top of that, some thin burn caramel (?) crisp. The whole combination is a piece of art, visually and gustatorily - sweet vs. savory, tender/juicy vs. crunchy/salty. It goes really well with the NV La Caravelle rose champagne. 

Remember I have also tried the compressed hamachi as starter (friend had it this time)? Which is better? Tough question. I like the hamachi more because it is more on the savory side and I am addictive to black truffle. But if you prefer lighter and refreshingly sweet/salty starter, go with the langoustine. If you could, get both :)

Moving on. I skip the pasta straight to fish and meat sections. I opted for the herb crusted Hawaiian Mero AND chef's signature dish, Squab & Foie Gras Croustillant (mind you, this is for 2 person).

I really enjoy the fish dish, which is presented as if an abstract painting - white fish, golden melted leeks, green baby ramps, mashed purple yam; all contrast against the bright orange stroke of pimento nage. Check out the pic! The mero, I figured, has a similar taste and texture of seabass tho prob less fat. It is cooked perfectly. Yet what's more interesting is the "pineapple bun top" accompany the fish - it is made of "melted" leeks and bouchot mussels. The melted leeks are leeks simmered in melted butter on low heat till it is super tender (hence the name melted) then adding white wine thyme (?) and mussels. It is savory, buttery and pack of flavors.  The pimento nage is a very nice touch, adding sweet herb and veggie aroma to the tender fish. 

Drum roll please! The Squab and Foi Gras Croustillant!! For all you have been to the Modern back in the days, you would recognize this is chef's signature dish. And needlessly to say, a master piece. The bird and foie are expertly cut, seared and wrap in "sandwich" with cabbage leaf. Then the squab & foie gras sandwich is rolled in a thin crispy dough sheet, served with summer veggies and bay leaf jus. Every bite is a symphony of juicy meaty squab meat and savory rich foie gras. It is a shame we are both beyond full by this point and we have to pack this home :/ 

Service is friendly and courteous as always. The maître d', Jonny, has already recognized me. For me, that is what fine dining is about, services and attention to details. For that, GK will be one of the top in my book. 

Before I headed out, I was gifted a little GK notebook with chef Gabriel Kreuther's autograph :) I am a very happy girl.
Loved every minute here. Elegant deco, attentive service, and most importantly, beautiful food (yes, beautiful) from presentation to texture to taste. Every dish we ordered is like a piece of art.

An assault on the senses or maybe I'm just too old to appreciate the hedge-fund magnitude of a restaurant where no surface remains un-designed.  Everything is artfully conceived and with all the current tasteful clichés from the miniaturized brushed steel hatracks brought to the table to hang purses to the specially conceived white wine glasses made to keep the fragrance in and the nose out.  Being old and sensible, we asked to exchange them for glasses that we could actually drink out of.  We couldn't figure out if the leather knife rests were  mouse pads in disguise.  And we were amused by the special silver plated utensils for the amuse bouche.    Too bad when the real show is behind some massive plated glass windows in the kitchen where a master chef is actually presiding in putting together the most intricate dishes being done in NYC.  With a menu and a mastery that rivals NYC's other prix fix four star restaurants, its four course menu is a bargain.  There's a difference in quality when the chef is actually present and on-the-line.  We were enthralled by his quiet intensity, his careful scrutiny of each order, old fashioned paper orders on a magnetic bulletin board, which he carefully annotated as plates were prepared.  And it was Gabriel who put finishing touches.  We watched him use tweezers to add garnishes.  And when you realize he begins before lunch and goes through dinner, we for the first time saw  the work behind these extravagant dining experiences.  The menu is as complicated as the décor.  The Alsatian touches strain to be heard.  What leaps off the printed page though are some amazing tastes bathed in subtle, memorable sauces.  Frogs legs melt in a exquisite sauce, a miniature sauerkraut and sturgeon tart is outstanding despite being presented under a glass bubble that kept in steam and made the tart soggy.  The dessert section descriptions sounded heavy and overdone.  I resigned myself to a chocolate something with kirsch, I hate kirsch, and was absolutely astonished when a pinnacle of dark chocolate soaring out of a sauce that tasted more like chocolate cherries arrived and I could have eaten more.  A cheese millefeuille was equally delicious.  Several amuse bouche appeared and 3 different breads.  This is a restaurant  that deseves to be about food and the chef. The best seats in the house look into the kitchen.  The staff is young, the chef is young, the food is exuberant, I only wish somebody had said, "Stop Already, less is more."

My husband and I ate in the lounge twice.  We wanted to avoid the prix fixe--too much food. Don't like the restrictions. The tarte flambé was delicious, especially the traditional one. We had a lobster small plate dish that was good, but about $28.00. We would love to make GK a regular option but the "ambiance" is overkill.  I agree with the reviewer who commented on the purse rack and the silverware.  Way too affected, kind of felt like being in a classroom for hotel management.  Haute dining with no sense of humor or light touch.  Servers  trying way too hard to hype the food, the vibe.  I saw GK surveying the scene from the back and wanted to give my 2 cents on all the fussiness. But I suppose we are not the crowd he is seeking. I imagine that the food in the dining room proper is really good. I just think the service and everything surrounding the food needs some tweaking.

Absolutely amazing!! 
The staff was very knowledgeable and the ambiance was impressive yet very relaxed. The food was delicious and even the tableware was beautiful. The silverware was from VPur Moonlash collection. Love love love! I'd really like to try the squab next time. 

These are the things that really stood out to me: 
-Kugelhoph bread
-Raw diver scallops 
-Ruby Fizz cocktail 
-the amuse bouche charcoal cracker (not sure what cheese was in the middle) 
-the quail 
-tableware was unique every dish was a beautifully composed work of art
-my waiter was really young and handsome.

Delicious meal in a very nice setting and while formal it didn't feel too stuffy. The service was excellent. Favorite dish was the squab which was fabulous and goes on my list of top dishes of all time. The lobster and Hawaiian mero courses were great as was the sturgeon tart. The langoustine course was interesting with maybe a little too much going on for my taste but it was not bad.  Desserts were expertly prepared. Yes, some people have complained about the funky stemware and silverware. I disagree that it impacts the meal much but understand their chirping.  They are something to talk about though. The fomage blanc they give with the first bread course is perfect. We also enjoyed the amuse bouches. Wines by the glass were all good. 

If I was to be critical I would say that I wish the entrees were slightly bigger like the mero fish. I also wish you could add a course but have different price points. I don't see the reason why anything you want to add is a minimum of $26 bucks. Most appetizers shouldn't be the same charge as a piece of fish or meat. Instead of the baguette with bamboo ash I would have loved to have tasted his tarte flambé!  All in all this is a solid fine dining destination. This is a high caliber of cooking. It is clear they are going for Michelin stars. I hope he will open up a casual place like other top chefs in the city.

From the friendly reception on, everything is as good as it gets.  Delicious, imaginative food, beautifully presented, far outstrips the already excellent food at Kreuther's two previous restaurants.  The service is wonderful, attentive without being fussy, correct yet friendly.  This is a place where everything has been thought out anew, from the cutlery, the astonishingly good wine glasses, a wine list full of excellent choices below $100, the originality of the food preparation and the elegant calm decor.  Our best new restaurant experience in years!

Loved this new restaurant! The space is beautiful, as is all the food - it almost looked too pretty to eat! My favorite dish was probably the creative, and incredibly flavorful, twist on gazpacho I had as an appetizer. Also, although usually I feel bad filling up on the free bread, make sure you try their bread course - it is noteworthy and delicious!

This place made our trip to NY very memorable! The best meal ever if you love love food!  Alsace cuisine extraordinaire! We had the prefix lunch with a glass of  Alsace Reisling. Heavenly 1st & 2nd course! Location, Ambiance, service were outstanding! our friend from the UN recommended this gem of a place! Hats off to Chef Gabriel!

Came here for a friends' birthday dinner (party of 3). We had made reservations before coming but you really didn't need to make any. 

Decor:  Upon entering the restaurant, you immediately notice the decor and the vast open space. You see tons of exposed beams and a chandelier made out of shapes of birds. There is also a bar area and tons of couch type seating.

We all decided on the chef's tasting menu. At the end of the night, it was about 15 dishes, including petits fours and amuse-bouche.

1st dish: citrus cured mackerel - I really loved the way he prepared this dish. The fish was fresh, not smelly, and the pickled watermelon rind and vegetable vinaigrette balanced out the dish.

2nd dish: summer strawberry - this contained tomato gelee, lovage, crispy pig ears. The pig ears were light and crispy but I wouldn't call this dish adventurous. I thought the tomato gelee was a little too sour for the dish and the strawberry jam wasn't able to balance it out. I think if the pig ears had some salt, it could have helped.

3rd dish: charcoal cracker - this had english pea and goat cheese mousse. I don't recall the flower in the dish but it really made the dish quite aromatic and I thought it elevated the dish. The goat cheese mousse was interesting. I liked it and I thought it went well with the charcoal cracker. To me, it was a spin off of guacamole and tortilla.

4th dish: 10 days cured brandt beef tenderloin - this had razor clam vinaigrette and horseradish. This was by far one of my favorite dishes of the night. The cured beef was amazing. The 10 days of curing really added flavor to the beef. Basically, they just served the meat medium rare without any sauce and when I took my first bite, it was super flavorful. Tons of flavor with minimal work. I wish other places would serve their meat similarly. The horseradish wasn't overpowering and it was balanced with the razor clam vinaigrette. 

5th dish: langoustine tartar - it also had flying fish roe, salty fingers, cauliflower-macadamia puree. I absolutely loved the cauliflower-macadamia puree. It was quite aromatic from the macadamia and it felt like there was some "roasted" flavor in it. The langoustine was delicious as well but I felt it was a little too fatty. Despite some shortcomings, I would definitely order this again.

6th dish: compressed hamachi - it also had black truffle, foi gras terrine, and celery. This dish surprised me the most. I am usually not a fan of foi gras terrine. It's just like Pâté. However, this is the first time I've had a terrine paired with fish. Chef Gabriel was really smart pairing the two. The fish helped cut through the "fat" and the texture of pâté. In addition, there were big pieces of black truffle so this dish has tons of strong ingredients. Despite all that, somehow the fish really balanced it all. The choice of the texture of the fish was well thought out. It wasn't too chewy or too meaty or too fatty. On the side, they have 3 slices of grapes and 3 rounded balls of celery. I basically split the terrine into 3 bites and in between each bite I would "palate" cleanser with a slice of grape and celery. I would say that the slice of grape could have been thicker but it may not have looked as pretty or choose a different fruit. I think it's important to have the fruit on the side but I haven't given much thought into what it would be. I would highly recommend this dish.

7th dish: sturgeon & sauerkraut tart -  it also has american caviar mousseline and applewood smoke. I think there was too much "cream" for the tart. I liked the tart crust though. It was fluffy and had a nice crunch to it when taking a bite. At the bottom of the part, I think there was a leaf of spinach and I was surprised because spinach usually contains a lot of water but the tart crust was not soggy at all. Great technique! The sauerkraut was okay. It wasn't overbearing but I feel that there's an imbalance between the caviar and "cream".

8th dish: gnocchi - with black truffles and fava beans. I've had bad experience with gnocchi but I actually liked this dish. The gnocchi was light and not too doughy/chewy. The black truffles and fava beans really helped to add flavor to the gnocchi. I think the dish might put some people off because of the color profile but the flavors are spot on. If the dish could be brighter, it would be more attractive.

9th dish: baked dorade royale with fennel seed coriander broth and green tomato marmalade. I got a chance to learn about this fish and royale means that the fish was line caught versus net caught and it is the highest end of this fish. The dish was flavorful and this was my 2nd favorite dish. The fish tasted clean, fresh, and not "fishy". Everything was balanced. 

10th dish: mangalitsa lardo poached maine lobster with squid ink gnocchetti, cockle ragout, baby artichoke, and jamon emulsion. I thought this was another great dish. I didn't like the "plant" that was added. Ran out of space to finish my review.

This man can cook! This man can design! This man can run a world-class restaurant!

Gabriel has outdone himself with his new place. From the beautifully chic, yet cozy decor, to wonderful lighting and great acoustics, his new restaurant was worth the wait on every dimension. Beautiful table settings, a "purse tree" tableside, dishes that look like they belong in a design museum.

Imagine having a great table that's not on top of your neighbor's. Being able to hold a conversation over dinner or drinks without screaming. Waiting in anticipation for the next food course because the last was so amazing in taste and presentation. Professional and friendly service from the entire staff without being a nuissance. This is what you'll find at Gabriel Kreuther.

We had the 4 course menu and were thoroughly impressed with the entire meal. The food is so creative without being weird and too trendy. Gabriel's cooking makes us try things we would never try elsewhere because we just know it's going to be delicious. We've traveled, lived and dined at some of the best restaurants in Europe and Asia for many years and we put this at the top of the list. 

PS ... We were introduced to Tarte Flambe while Gabriel was at The Modern and spent 3 years in Europe trying to find one 1/2 as good as his. It's just as we remember it. So happy he has it on the bar menu!

Gabriel Kreuther has put together a delightfully curated experience in a beautiful setting in the Grace building off Bryant Park. The 4 course dinner comes is a great value for midtown, coming complete with 3 excellent bread courses and additional amuses throughout the meal. The dishes are technically complex, with a many elements coming together in each bite, but many of the flavors are familiar ones - like the red wine-marinated Brandt skirt steak - elevated by Chef Kreuther and his team. My favorite dishes were (in order of serving):

- Green tomate cocktail: not your typical tequila and lime type drink, this one adds a depth of flavor with the addition of a green tomato emulsion that creates a pleasant balance. I loved the design of the glass, too!

- Kugelhopf bread with chive fromage blanc: savory bread served with a buttery yet tangy spread, served with a story of Chef Kreuther's grandmother baking it in his childhood and a beautiful ceramic egg holding the fromage.

- Coffee cracker with corn creme amuse: creamy, slightly sweet, slightly earthy and totally tasty

- Langoustine tartar: the langoustine really shines in this dish which the chef makes interesting with a bit of acid and a crunchy brulee-esque crust that's fun to break with your spoon

- 10 Days Cured Brandt Beef Tenderloin tartar: this is really two dishes in one, the first a pure serving of the beef that was the most savory, umami-filled bite I've ever had, and the second served with razor clam vinaigrette which creates a great play of salt-acid-sweet-umami.

- Lobster: jamon emulsion and braised in mangalista lardo. YUM

- Braised pork collar and cheek: another strong showing for mangalista pork as it's savory, fatty deliciousness combines with sweet stone fruit and some sort of pickled vegetable to make every bite interesting and new.

- "Comfort" dessert: as our server called it, the "sleeper hit" of the dessert menu. nuttiness from pistachios combines with another brulee'd sugar crust and light flavorful sorbet for a great way to finish the meal

Also, don't miss the chocolates at the end of the meal - they were awesome.

I was very happy to saw that unlike many haute-cuisine menus, by the end of this one I was pleasantly full. The service was technically flawless and constantly available (there's a team of servers for every table and the multiple sommeliers were always around to provide tips). It did seem a bit busy the night that I dined, so they didn't seem quite as friendly as the atmosphere would suggest they could be. Overall though, our server gave quality advice when asked on everything from which dishes to order (and in what order) to which dessert wine to pair (a 2011 pinot gris fit the ticket).

I recommend heading up to GK soon to enjoy the masterful dishes before other people find out that there's a place serving the highest quality cuisine in a beautiful setting for a solid value. Oh, and they're opening a PDR in the next couple of weeks just in time for the fall party season.

Personally, I can't wait to go back to try a few more of the cocktails (good price and extremely creative for midtown!), the tarte flambee classic in the lounge (mmm cheese), and the squab & foie gras dish (looks amazing in all the pictures here!).

My husband and I ate here with business associates on Wednesday night and we have never had such a horrible experience with an incompetent and almost abusive waiter in our lives. My husband has several food allergies--most nuts, stone fruits, apples, and pears. And the waiter actually had the audacity to question him and tell him that if the stone fruits were cooked he could eat them. When my husband told that he could NOT eat them cooked, the waiter responded, "Well I've never heard of that." 

Thank god we weren't footing the bill for this monstrosity of a meal. They really have some nerve--completely stuck in the '80's with the idea of tiny portions = amazing food. If you eat at Gordon Ramsey's Maze or Le Bernadine you get amazing food, presentation, and you actually leave feeling like you ate something. 

This place is rubbish and their attitude sucks. What a freaking tourist trap. New Yorkers, go elsewhere and save this one for the people with the fanny packs.

Elegant and classy. Food is top notch, and presentations are a stand out.  I can't wait to see what they whip out in the fall! 

Warning-  if you're expecting lots of food, you might be disappointed.

Some of the first things I noticed about Gabriel Kreuther was the stunning location and sightly decor.  The service was impeccable.  The amuse-bouches were delicious. 

The food in itself was good.  I wasn't blown away by my plates (Compressed Hamachi, Sweetbread Dumplings, and Montauk Fluke).  Regardless, I will be coming back here again.  The menu is extensive and the space is simply too beautiful to stay away.

Not much for superlatives, but here goes:  Get a reservation before it becomes impossible, and enjoy one of the best meals to be experienced in NYC 2015.

This review will surely be quickly lost amongst the myriad soon to be posted about this place.  Brush the nit-picking complainers into the dustbin and focus on what's important.  The. food. is. astounding.  If this was in any other city it would be packed to the gills, they'd be renting out the local convention center to seat the drooling, fork-clenching masses. 

Four course (3 savory + dessert) prix-fixe under a hundred bucks.  Roast Squab, Langoustine Ceviche, Caviar, Foie Gras and all things luxe and tasty and crafted/plated with Classic French (Alsatian) precision... which from a value standpoint, factoring in the various amuse-bouches and individual bread courses and compound butters and chocolates and the to-go pastries for the next morning translates into the collective fourth floor of the Time Warner Center sending out job applications.   

Just checked wikipedia and the average Per Se diner spends $851.  Been there.  Loved it and treasure my T.Keller rosary beads.  But this place is in the ballpark, and just left of home plate.  It opened mid-June and this rolling stone is picking up speed.  Line up or be moss.

Just had the most amazing dinner at Gabriel Kreuther!! Everything was impeccable from the deliciously creative food, beautiful decor, and top notch service. The $98 pre fixe menu was completely worth the price...on top of your four dishes you get 3 additional bread courses, an amuse bouche, and one pre and one post dessert. Surely one of my best food tasting experiences. The topper of it all was the staff who were the friendliest I've ever had at such a high end establishment. Mr. Kreuther you are certainly doing something right, so glad to have eaten at your restaurant that I opened a yelp account to review it!

From start to finish this was an extraordinary experience. The space is gorgeous and we were welcomed warmly when we entered by Christina. 
The dinner service by Alex and Cody and Emilie was impeccable. Every single dish we savored was absolutely perfect. I am a huge gazpacho fan and their gazpacho with Maine lobster and cucumber was mouthwatering. Do not miss their signature sturgeon and sauerkraut tart with caviar which is gorgeous in and of itself.  We particularly enjoyed the Colorado Lamb rack. Be sure and partake in their cheese course because the presentation is very special. We are excited to return and also to try their lunch menu.

Came for the prix fixe lunch, everything was so well done, from taste to presentation and creativity.  Would definitely want to try the dinner and come back for lunch again.  Very beautifully done space as well.  I had the Nori Campanelle with Alaskan king crab and Truffle Juice Broiled Quail were both amazing.  Everything down to the freshly baked baguette and little treats at the end were made with such finesse, and the service was impeccable.

One of the most tasteful and beautiful lunches ever! Blue shrimp appetizer was out of the world! We also enjoyed dorade Royal and Hawaiian mero- both dishes were first class!!!!
Wine and coffee selection just added to this beautiful and memorable lunch!
Let's not forget- the company was the cherry on the cake!
I will definitely return soon!! Not to be missed!
Food, service, wine and venue with relaxing music makes this spot a special one!!!

Terrific haut cuisine off Bryant Park.. ate dinner here the night before the NYTimes Review (3 stars) -- hope this place lasts; it deserves to -- will let the pictures do the talking (amazing!) :)

This is an independent review. I have no relationship to this store, nor to the best of my knowledge, know anyone who works there.

From the second we walked in the door, for our anniversary, every need was catered to. It goes without saying that the meal was exquisite - from taste to presentation - but we were blown away by the level of service. Truly an expertly-trained staff and want to give a particular shoutout to Cody, who showcased a level of sophistication and professionalism that fine dining is all about.

Mazel, team - well done! Michelin Star is around the corner.

KenScale: 8.5/10

Before opening his own restaurant this year, chef Gabriel Kreuther has been helming The Modern for a long time serving elegant and well-prepared Alsatian cuisine. His departure last year left me wondering what kind of food he will be serving at a new project that he said he'll work on. Finally, he opened the eponymous restaurant right across from Bryant Park, doing pretty much the same thing that he had been doing at The Modern. I'm not complaining even though the meal felt somewhat repetitive because the high quality of chef Kreuther's food is still well kept at his new restaurant.

The restaurant has a four-course prix fixe option for $98 at dinner, consisting of three savory courses and one dessert. While chef Kreuther's food seems closer to classical French, they are some interesting twists (as well as immaculate presentations) here and there that kept me excited with each meal. I didn't expect the raw marinated diver scallop to be immersed in jalapeno coulis to create a unique flavor to add to the tender scallop. I believe sturgeon and sauerkraut tart with American caviar mousseline is one of the carryovers from The Modern, and the complexity of flavor in this dish was also sensational. For the final savory course, I went with Colorado lamb rack in hay stack, which comes after brief presentation of lamb breast on the haystack. The meat was more or less perfectly cooked with juicy flavor that was memorable, and I really appreciated that the meat wasn't over-seasoned to my liking. Desserts from pastry chef Marc Aumont also offer some great selections. I went with the "comfort" dessert consisting of roasted apricot, pistachio mousseline and ten flavor sorbet, and it was not only beautifully plated but had the rich complexity of flavor that led me to finish the dish in 30 seconds. 

The restaurant has started getting extremely positive reviews from professional critics, so I suggest always booking ahead. I really liked the modern and elegant dining space of the restaurant, which would make it ideal for special occasions as well as business meals. There is diverse selections of wine (mostly from France), and you can definitely get some more affordable yet solid bottles here. Gabriel Kreuther is another welcome addition to New York fine dining scene. While there has been a lot of talk about casual wine bars and bistros taking over the city, it is restaurants like these that make New York's dining scene so much more sophisticated and something to look forward to.

I'm a sucker for beautiful wine glasses and silverware - I feel like a restaurant that cares to make an effort on these things shows attention to detail and a willingness to make all aspects of the dining experience unique and memorable for guests. Gabriel Kreuther impressed on all fronts. They use the VPur Moonlashes collection of silverware - such exquisite and unique pieces that I have been on a hunt ever since my visit to see where I can buy them retail. Wine is served in gorgeous Lehmann glasses - certainly a refreshing departure from the standard Riedels and Schott Zwiesels that proliferate in most fine-dining establishments. 

Now onto the food...The bf and I dined in the bar/lounge section of the restaurant because prices there are more affordable, and because I mainly wanted to try the tarte flambee that head chef Gabriel Kreuther is so famous for. I ordered the classic tarte flambee (which was a very reasonably $12) - it's like a thin crust pizza topped with cheese, onions and bacon. Sounds simple and rustic but oh so delicious! Seasoning was spot on, the crispy crust contrasted so well with the softness of the toppings, and of course...BACON! The other tarte flambees all sound super exotic - I will have to go back another time to try.

I also highly recommend the mangalitsa morcilla, which had such an amazing velvety and soft texture. And who knew that blood sausage and gewurztraminer would make such a great pairing! The acidity of the wine balanced really well with the richness of the sausage and the creaminess of the parsnip puree.

The menu is fairly limited in its vegetarian options, but the bf, who ordered the black pepper pasta and the summer salad (both vegetarian), was plenty satisfied with his meal. I am sure to come again and would love to try the prix fixe menu next time. Meanwhile, onwards with my hunt for a set of VPur silverware...

Overall: highly recommended. Had the tasting menu which is one of the best deals in the city as far as tasting menus are concerned. This is a 1 Michelin star at the moment that with a few tweaks could absolutely be at a 2 and I'm very excited for that.

The room is sizable but not in a soulless AltaMarea restaurant way. There is warmth there with light woods and cream colored seats. The space between the tables is simply enormous. My 2 top was approx 5 feet from another table in the corner. It was like dining on a couch, quite nice.

Service was fantastic. Everyone there was wonderfully cordial and was happy to discuss the menu and wine list at length. Sommelier was on-point and the dining room manager knows what he is doing.

My one issue with the operation is the way it feels like the restaurant is closing down at around 11-11:15 or so. There were tables still occupied and they closed the curtain to the kitchen which has the effect of removing some of the light from the room. A simple fix but important for later diners to keep that optimal atmosphere.

One note on the flat and dishware. Yes, it's slightly finicky at times. No, it won't impact your enjoyment of the meal. It's a matter of personal taste. I liked it, some may not.

The meal starts with some Alsatian style bread with a whipped chive spread. This was good but with two other breads coming later I wasn't about to fill up.  There are three breads total. The one mentioned previous and another with butter and the third another with whipped lardo. Yes to the latter.

AB - Fennel Pollen Gougere: (Better) Basically a puff with foie gras which was good except it could have done without the yuzu which made the small bite too acidic and overpowered the foie gras.

AB - Smoked Eel Mousse with Ogo Seaweed and Royal Trumpet Mushrooms: (Best) This was excellent, could have had this has a later course as well, just fantastic

1st Course: Langoustine Tartar - really lovely, great acid

2nd Course: Compressed Hamachi - enjoyed this a lot, an interesting idea although I do think the Hamachi is over powered by the foie gras, didn't care still loved it, the black truffle in-between brought it to 11

3rd Course: Raw Diver Scallop - the scallop was perfect and the jalapeno coulis and lemon confit just worked so well together

4th Course: Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart - I really enjoyed it but I wasn't blown away. The sauerkraut overpowered the sturgeon a bit. The caviar mousseline though was awesome, really great, overall still a positive dish

5th Course: Sweetbread Black Truffle Dumplings - I was so so so excited to have this dish and it wound up being my least favorite of the night. It sounds immensely promising. Who doesn't want a black truffle dumpling? I was completely disappointed. The truffle flavor was hardly present and after eating that the sweetbread was just an afterthought.

6th Course: Baked Dorade Royale - after the disappointment from the black truffle dumpling I was smiling again after this. The dorade was perfectly cooked and took on the coriander broth swimmingly. The green tomato marmalade was fine but didn't add a ton. I would order this as a main course any time.

7th Course: Shemogue Oyster - Really enjoyed this, the oyster was wrapped in lettuce and topped with caviar. Fantastic bite. The uni and rice cracker on top didn't hurt either.

8th Course: Lardo Poached Maine Lobster with Gnocchetti and Cockle Ragout - impressed with this although I'm not sure I tasted the benefits of being poached in lardo. Nevertheless it was very good and the layers of dish were enjoyable. The gnocchetti should be sized as small gnocchi as you can't get the real texture of the former's small size. The cockles were a nice touch. The ham emulsion added another layer of flavor to the lobster.

9th Course: Lamb Rack in Hay Stack - very good but not earth shattering, lamb was tender but a bit under-seasoned and I'm not convinced the hay stack does much of anything to benefit the lamb. Summer vegetables on the side were uninspiring for this dish in terms of flavor. They bring the dish out before hand in the hay stack and the aroma is wonderful. They should have served it in the hay stack because the aroma completely goes away when you remove it.

10th Course: Concord Grape Sorbet with Yogurt Meringue - solid palette cleanser

11th Course: Fantasy Chocolate Kirsch Amarena - yeah no, didn't like this at all. It was downright boring. I'll go so far as to say it's one of the worst tasting menu desserts I've ever had.

D 12th Course: Cafe Frappe - much better, whipped caramel cream and candied pecans make for a tasty treat although this wasn't enough to make dessert a strong point

Overall a really great primarily seafood tasting menu. Most dishes were hits, a few were enthralling, a couple fell flat. The desserts are a weak spot. That said I still highly recommend Gabriel Kreuther. It will only get better from here and I'm excited to see where it goes.
Awesome experience with Exec sous chef Joe. Very talented. Beautiful dining room reminiscent of the bourgeois 60's.

Congratulations Chef Kreuther on your michelin star it is well deserved! My husband and I went there for dinner last night and were delighted. I absolutely loved the Amuse Bouche in a sea urchin container, the Nori Campanelle and the herb crusted Hawaiian mero- they all had that amazing taste of the sea without being overwhelming. A very difficult feat for any chef to do well. The Brandt beef skirt steak was also well executed, but didn't take my breath away like the others. 
The decor reminds me of back home in Canada with its high ceilings and long wood beams. Beautiful location right off the park. I was less impressed with the cutlery, although it looks dainty and elegant we didn't find it that functional. 
Overall great edition to the New York scene!

All around fabulous dinner.   We went for a post theatre matinee dinner as it was just a short walk from the theatre.   I read the great reviews and was not disappointed at all.  The food was wonderful, the langoustino tartar was outstanding, the fish was nicely done, and the dessert, Ecstasy was truly ecstasy.  My spouse had the beef tenderloin appetizer, and duck.  With all of the freshly made breads, really loved the kugelhof with the chive spread spread, and the many amuse boy he's, it was a great fine dining experience.  The service and hostess staff were outstanding.   Rachel was our server but with the other staff were all great in explaining the various courses.  Also kudos to the reservation staff.  They were able to accommodate a slightly larger party than we originally had reserved at the last minute with a completely full restaurant.  A wonderful dining experience.  I hope that Gabriel Kreuther continues to wow the NYC dining scene with his creative and delicious cuisine.

Amazing spot.  We are in the bar area, plates were small and around $20 a pop but delicious.  We had the sausage, pepper pasta with an egg, and the tarte flambee.  Oh and the dessert.  All were terrific - would especially recommend the sausage.  The place has a great, upscale vibe and despite all the open space they've managed to carve the room into smaller spaces so it feels cozy.

The drink menu is well put together too.  A good list of German and Austrian whites and a good curated beer list too.  The smoked German lager was excellent.

This is a great addition to midtown - on the expensive side for dinner but a terrific option for drinks or a light dinner with a friend.

Highly recommended by a sybarite friend of mine; he was right. Went there yesterday (10|2015) for lunch and was pleasantly impressed with great service, elegant contemporary bright setting, and a very creative menu. The food was excellent, especially their "Foie Gras Terrine" and the "Baked Dorade Royale"; presentation was superb!

Am I the only one who does not love this restaurant?  

Gabriel Kreuther

The food we ate was well executed  and somewhat tasty but not memorable (other than the stomach ache it gave me).
The truffle supplement was $70 (before tax and tip) for tasteless black truffle that was shaved on the Squab & Foie Gras Croustillant and never exposed to heat.  In my opinion, black truffle requires some heat.  I tried it as is and found it tasteless.  I buried it under the cooked food and still found it tasteless (the food and dish were not hot enough to extract any flavor).  I mentioned it to the staff and received no response.  

Service was presented with a smile but it also lacked substance. 
My dining companion enjoyed the cacao beans provided alongside the dessert and asked to take the three remaining beans home but was told he could not as they would be reused.  Really?  
They kept filling the water glasses even when they were 85% full.  
They brought several breads with different accompaniments (creme/ butter/ lardo) but the bread plate was never changed.

The courses were served on large an impressive plates but the servings were lilliputian.

The sommelier recommended a $133 wine that was too young to be enjoyed (IMHO). It was Le Sang 2012 ($133  charged but $28 at retail shops). 

The artisinal cheese plate featured nothing special.  The server did not identify them.  I pointed to the Humboldt Fog and identified it and the server said yes.  It is a good cheese, but readily available at every supermarket in America.  The other cheeses were not memorable.  One remained on the "board" untouched as the server removed it without asking if I was done.  

We had: 
10 Days Cured Brandt Beef Tenderloin tartar * razor clam vinaigrette * horseradish.  (where's the beef?)

Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart American caviar mousseline * applewood smoke (crunchy and tasty but there were no pronounced flavors of sturgeon or sauerkraut).

Mangalitsa Lardo Poached Maine Lobster squid ink gnocchetti * cockle ragoût * jamón émulsion (supplement 15)

Nori Campanelle Pacific red crab * smoked parsnip purée * dulse seaweed (quite tasty if not a little too al dente)

Squab & Foie Gras Croustillant (for two) seasonal vegetables * bay leaf jus, with truffle supplement for $70.  (the pigeon was tasty, the cold shaved truffle supplement was tasteless)

Artisinal cheese plate. (meh)


All I have to add is "tutto fumo niente arrosto."

This is my favorite restaurant opening of 2015, and totally deserving of it's newly minted Michelin star!  Gabriel Kreuther was previously the chef at the Modern, which was a 4* NYT pick, and he is continuing to do amazing things at his new namesake restaurant.  It's located right off Bryant Park on the ground floor of what appears to be an office building but it's a welcome new addition to the Times Square area which is sorely lacking in fine dining establishments.

There are two menus here - a $98 four-course prix fixe (two appetizers, one main, one dessert) and a longer tasting menu at $185.  I opted for the former, and between all the amuses bouches and bread courses it definitely felt much longer.  A quick sidenote on the bread - there are three (or was it four?) courses of it here each paired with a different spread and every single kind was absolutely amazing.  Normally I try not to stuff myself with bread but I couldn't help it so DO come hungry.

I started with the foie gras terrine, which had bits of duck proscuitto and was served in a butternut squash reduction.  I had the Sturgeon and Sauerkraut Tart next and this was absolutely delicious.  There was a generous amount of caviar on top and there was a great smokey flavor to it.  For the main, my dining partner and I opted to go for the Squab and Foie Gras Croustillant (this dish requires two participating parties although I think for a surcharge you can get it alone).  This was sensational and dare I say better than the Nomad Foie Gras Chicken (they aren't really the same thing at all except for the poultry + foie mix).  

I was absolutely stuffed at this point but powered onto dessert where I opted for the Fantasy (basically a chocolate cone with sponge cake and sorbet).  It was good but not as strong as the apps or mains.

Reservations are still relatively easy so do yourself a favor and go before it gets more difficult!  Service was spot on and they give you a small pastry to take home for breakfast the next morning.

I randomly searched on Yelp and decided to treat a friend of mine here for lunch. Turns out to be a great decision. The desserts are really, really good. The beignets are soft, chewy and amazing with marmalade. The beer sorbet that comes with the beignet is also really tasty. The chocolate coffee dessert is also very creamy and puffy. My date and I really enjoyed the two dishes we had.

We sat at the lounge and the decor is superb. The service is friendly. We ordered a la carte, got oysters and salmon ceviche. I have to say, I have had better for both, although both dishes are very beautifully presented. Overall, dessert is the strongest point at this place. Well deserving of its Michelin Star.

If you are looking for an exciting fine dining experience, Gabriel Kreuther is your spot. Located right next to the theater district on 42nd Street, this is an ideal spot for after theater or early pre theater dining. I would rate this restaurant as among the best in the city.

So so so good.  Better than La Bernadin imho. Service was that sublime balance of warm, knowledgeable but giving you the space to enjoy the moment and savour the flavours.  The highlights for me were the scallops, langoustine tartar and the compressed hamachi. 

Excellent special occasion spot.  In fact, the kind of place that will make any occasion special
Beautiful presentation, great location, food could be a little bit tastier and larger portions. Extensive wine selection.

Definitely one of the best table in New York,
Great value, quite an experience.

The second I stepped into GK, I know there's gonna be discrimination between bar room and main dining room; however they did it in a mild way that both areas present amid ambience.

Since I'm in a hurry of an event at night, have to settle myself with the prex fixe menu, with three savory dishes and one dessert. Of course GK also offered a couple of small bites. Surprisingly, I liked their baguette a lot - with the crispy crust and a black filling, interesting! 

Coming to GK, raw is something that you cannot skip. Both the scallop and the langoustine tartare were freshly prepared and absorbed the flavor perfectly. Didn't remember the taste of blue shrimp (second course) clearly, probably because I'm not a big fan of milky soup...for the main course, I would personally suggest going for the duck, but people might have different opinions on that.

Ok now time for dessert! Cannot wait! Opted for the fantasy and textural. I guess if one thing I could remember, that would be how pretty the presentation can be - girls always go for beautiful stuff and I cannot help with that...

Back on track, delicious food, fantastic presentation, awesome atmosphere - not at all surprised GK was raised to one Michelin star within the first year of opening!
All the courses were great Wait staff very knowledgeable service was impeccable very nice atmosphere

Because of a 7pm theater time we changed our 5:30 pre-theater reservation to 9:45 (post-theater) and were very glad that we did! This is a delightful new restaurant near the theater district. the ambiance was warm and enjoyable, using rustic beams from a Vermont bard to create an inviting feel for this Alsatian-based chef. Service was superb and helpful and the food was fantastic!! They have one Michelin star after only a few months in existence but deserve at least two!!! A great experience in every way.
Great power lunch atmosphere, perfect for Suits and Celebs.  High end foodie's will not be disappointed.  Great service and the food itself was outstanding.

The food was amazing and the ambiance was incredible! I was very impressed with the quality of food and service. The staff was incredibly professional and the seasonal salads and scallops were crafted to perfection. The only caveat is that it's VERY expensive; however, if you are looking for a delicious meal at a classy restaurant, this is the place to go!

Came for lunch. Food was very good and service was in some ways even better.

Note the lunch menu on the day we came was different from the one posted on the web. They replaced the squab main option (for two) with a venison option (required supplement). We'd wanted to try the squab but went with other meat options instead. We added one course and skipped dessert, just ate the chocolates instead. 

First complimentary bread and amuse were good, the butter / mousse that came with it had a chive flavor and tasted amazing. 

The Cold part of the menu is the best imo, showcases the talent that makes this a Michelin starred restaurant. Highly recommend the langoustine tartare, foie gras, and above all the raw scallops. Scallops dish is amazing, so many flavors and perfect quality seafood. Foie gras was airy, and interesting with base of dark chocolate. Couldn't figure out what the orange sauce was, it came with two toasts tucked into a towel hah. Langoustine was a bit fishy tasting and I realized I don't really like the slippery quality of langoustine tartare, but don't think that's a ding on the dish or restaurant, it's just personal preference. Sturgeon tart is really good with firm smoked fish, tart sauerkraut, creamy sauce.

Mains were good, we got meat so it was all medium rare. Preferred duck dish over the beef, which is typical for me since I'm usually not that into Western style beef. 

All staff from front desk to servers were pleasant and professional. Hope to be back! Might opt for lounge instead since most of the dining room menu items I really wanted to try we have tried now hah. GET THE RAW SCALLOPS! Can't emphasize that enough.

This place is beautiful!  I wish my house was decorated like this place.  I went for lunch.  There is an option for a 2 course menu for $52 (If I remember correctly) and each additional course $22.  We each did 3 courses.  I had the Foie Terrine which was fantastic!  I then has the Diver Scallops and the Mero.  My partner had a couple cocktails and a very nice red burgundy they pour by the glass.  I just had coffee, which was also very nice.  We had to be to an appointment and did not have time for dessert.  The service was a little slow.  We waited almost 15 minutes between course one and two with empty drinks.  I could care less about the food taking that time but it would have been nice to have been offered a re-fill on our drinks.  The bread was also very good!  We will have to come back and try dinner.

Beautiful decor. Delicious food and presentation! The hostess Sade was very nice and helpful :) I had a great time dining here. Service is way better than Le Bernardin! GK deserves at least 2 Michelin stars not 1!

I enjoyed a fabulous meal here with a colleague!  The location was amazing as it was near our hotel and office.  I should start that I adore meals like these...

My colleague and I were both impressed by the food and presentation.  Service was superb and I liked their tasteful uniforms, which were a posh grey suit ensemble for the ladies.

We were seated near the kitchen and I enjoyed being able to look in and see Chef Gabriel Kreuther preparing his creations.  

I enjoyed one of the foie gras offerings (the seared one, not the terrine), the lamb (which was prepared to perfection) and their Fantasy Chocolate Kirsch Amarena.  Wasn't a huge fan of the dessert but it was my own fault for selecting something chocolate.  All of our selections paired perfectly with a Brazilian bottle by Lidio Carraro.

When I first saw the menu for this place I did not think it was something I would enjoy. I love a good meal but there are some things that I am just not down with eating and animal insides is one of them. So when I saw that a whole bunch of the menu items included foie gras and concluded that there wasn't much on the menu for me to choose from, I was concerned. But boy I was I wrong!

First of all the space is amazing and if you are wanting a less formal experience, the bar area is much more laid back. The main dining room offers a tasting menu and it allows you to choose ANY three savory mains and a dessert. That was key for me because I didn't have to pick anything from the first section of the menu which didn't have any items that really spoke to me. So instead, I opted for a choice from the second section, the fish section and the meat section. I had the sunchoke soup, the halibut, and the skirt steak. For dessert I had the caramelized apples. Other people at the table had the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart, the hamachi, the foie gras, the Hawaiian mero, the duck and the pork. For dessert, they had the chocolate kirsch, the pear and vanilla mousse and they gave us the grape meringue to share. Everything was delicious.

They started us off with some scallion bread with scallion butter, which was a great start to the meal. Then they gave us an Alsace tart with bacon which was amazing. The bacon flavor was really dominant and I knew after this that my perception of the meal was way off. This was going to be a kick ass dinner. They also gave us smoked eel with arugula vichyssoise, these black biscuits filled with kale and ricotta, a fresh baguette with butter, rosemary buckwheat rolls with mangalitsa pork lard, a pre dessert of pear marmalade, ice cream, red wine gelee, and a gingerbread crumble, a beautiful display of chocolates, half with yogurt and grape and the other with caramel and passion fruit, coconut and chocolate pocky sticks, and finally to finish us off they gave us a coffee mousse with caramel, biscotti, a caramel custard, and crushed pecans. Out of all of that delicious food, the only thing I didn't care for was the pre dessert and that's because I don't like gingerbread. 

Seriously everything here was expertly prepared. The sunchoke soup was so silky and delicious and had so much depth of flavor, without being too rich. The halibut was cooked to perfection and the sauce had elements of sweet sour and salty with cockles, shrimp, reisling and grated bottarga. The skirt steak was so tender and expertly prepared, and the green peppercorn sauce wasn't overly peppery. Overall this was one of the best meals I have had and it is definitely worth the price. Don't miss this place.
Excellent lunch, presentation and service. Very creative preparation and just delicious.

Super good food and services! Went there today for lunch and ordered two course prix fixe. Personally recommend: Herb Crusted Hawaiian Mero and Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart. 

So the Mero dish is a very tender fish, with crusted mussels on top, dip in a yummy sauce. Its also the waiter's favorite. The tart is very pretty and crispy. Sturgeon and sauerkraut is something that tastes like white kimchi :p

I really like their complimentary dishes -- pretty and delicious. The restaurant really put a lot of thought into this. See pictures!

The whole meal costs $100/each person including tips.

My family went to the restaurant Christmas week and had a memorable dinner. The service was impeccable. The chef's creation are as tasty as they are beautiful. It is only a matter of time before the restaurant receives it second Michelin star. I would recommend that you attend now before the critics review this wonderful. The fois gras dishes were superb. The roasted scallops were jumbo sized. The three courses of bread were perfection. The squash for two was infused with the flavors of the meats juices. The duck breast was perfect. Desserts were sculptural beautiful. Petit fours and a take home cake completed a perfect night.

Beautiful space. Competent but sterile, soulless service (although they made a mistake on the bill which could have been remedied more gracefully) 

Precious food for precious diners.  People need to stop pretending that is OK to give a restaurant $250 / person and still leave hungry. I don't mind dropping serious coin when the art and creativity are on par with substance (i.e. Torrisi, Bouley, Daniel, EMP ETC) but this was just comical . 

Minimal piece of shrimp for the amuse Bouche was uninventive. Marinated diver scallops could've easily been done at home. Kraut tart was delicious . Halibut entree drenched in butter. Dessert was sexy

Were it not for the accompanying bread , I think I ate 8 tablespoons of food over the course of the evening

It's up to YOU NY...

Beautiful restaurant with a stunning design. However the dinner options in the bar area were poorly explained to us by the host and we found ourselves with overpriced limited options. The food in itself was good.

Outstanding food and service, would highly recommend.

A friend and I treated another friend to his birthday here as a surprise, but he had (to our surprise) dined here earlier this week. However, the server noticed him and said, "Welcome back," as we sat, which was surprising yet entertaining and generally reflective of the service we had that evening. We had the chef's tasting menu and specifically requested that we have the langoustine and the lobster as part of our meal, which they gladly obliged. The langoustine in particular was delicious, but everything that we had was very well executed and tasted great, especially the foie gras dishes.

The drinks were also excellent, and the ambiance as a whole was fantastic. Definitely a place I'd recommend for a nice, more upscale meal.

My wife and I don't get many chances to go out, so we try to go somewhere special when we do. We've been to most of the high-end French restaurants in the city and were excited for this one.

We arrived early so we could have a cocktail in the bar. The space is welcoming, though the ceiling in the main dining room has the most institutional paint color in the whole place - odd, to be sure.

We ordered cocktails, and five minutes later a server said they had just sold the last one of mine. An 86ed cocktail? Yes. So I decided to order a Sazerac, which I like with one large cube (call me a philistine, I like ice). The server confirmed one large cube, after asking if I'd prefer a sphere. Then, about ten or fifteen minutes later, the drinks came. No ice in mine, one large cube for my wife. I reminded the server about the cube. I shouldn't have. They dropped in the cube, but the drink was already so weak that further dilution was a mistake. My wife's was the same. Fail. Not to mention the spicy shrimp (or fish skin?) crisps served with the drinks - they weren't bad, but I can't imagine too many diners wanting a seafoody snack with their cocktails.

Our table was ready fifteen or twenty minutes late, but as our cocktails were delayed we didn't mind too much. On to the meal. The amuse featured more crisps - beet and nori this time - that were fine. The Parmesan dumpling was so-so. We ordered the 2012 Rolly Gassman Pinot Noir, which was good for the price: earthy, a little sweet, and clean, if not exactly complex.

Our first courses were outstanding - we had the velouté and langoustine tartare, which reminded me of fresh amaebi. The next courses were less so. My wife's halibut was hearty but lacking contrasts in flavor, except for the garnish. My sturgeon tart arrived under a smoky dome - hasn't that trick been done to death by now? - and tasted like the smoked salmon Benedict I could buy around the corner for $15. The mousseline tasted like Hollandaise and congealed within minutes. Between the sauce and the smoky sturgeon, I couldn't taste the American caviar on top or any sauerkraut. Sorry, but I didn't come here for breakfast. I couldn't even finish half of it. To their credit, the servers offered to bring something else. I declined.

We shared the croustillant next. When I order a dish meant for two, I expect it to be served out at the table. This was not - the croustillant was already cut in half and delivered on separate plates. Regardless, it was hearty and very good. I've never had a small bird cooked so tenderly.

The palate cleanser was another highlight, with berry and ginger. The desserts were, again, fine - tasty, but nothing to blow our minds.

Other points: The servers seemed a little green, certainly competent but lacking the knowing confidence of more experienced staff. We liked the warm ambience; at least, we found it warmer than the minimal, modern rooms at Jean-Georges and Le Bernardin. But I think we'd go back to either of those - and certainly to Bouley as well - before we returned here. For the money we paid, we expected a bit more. This was a four-star meal where we were paying for five, hence the three-star review.

Had a nice meal here last night for my father's bday. Been wanting to try GK for a while since it opened and it's so close to my office. Made a reservation through Open Table and everything  went smoothly. They called to confirm the day of as you would expect. 

Wine list is pretty nice and it comes in an iPad which I actually don't like but thats personal preference. I think corkage is around $100, last time I checked so similar to Per Se ballpark. As another Yelper mention it is very odd for a meal like this to not have wine pairing as a option. I guess different to Masa, Brooklyn Fare or Atera you get to choose your courses rather than a chef's table type of deal but with the limited options it should not be hard to have a flexible pairing. My father was still under the weather and I only really drink to pair with the food so we opted for some champagne to start and a half bottle. 

Service is excellent and food was very good though the portions are much larger than I expected. I added in some wild caviar to the mix and for 30g at 85, it was a steal. We have the bay scallops, Foie Gras Terrine, 2x Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart, Long Island Crescent Duck, Brandt Beef Skirt Steak and for dessert the Revisited, Pear Vanilla and the Textural, Concord Grape Pistachio. 

Out of everything that we ordered I would say the bay scallops and the 
Wild American Sturgeon Caviar were the best. Total for the bill was around high 5s. I would say that michelin got it right on for GK, it's a true one michelin star. 

Areas of improvement for GK: 
- Prepared wine pairing option 
- Perhaps smaller portions, before I even got the 3 course I was fairly full and it was an uphill battle at that point 
- Need more space between the tables. This one I am very serious on. I took the seat on the outside and every time someone walked behind me I felt it. Also I was able to hear the full conversations on the tables to my left and right. This means that they can hear mine as well, which does not make well for private conversations or business.

I have aligning opinions with the rest of the folks here who rated this place poorly; our complain in common? SERIVCE.

I dined here Friday on a 8pm reservation.  Immediately observation of the restaurant was the gigantic atmosphere is a bit "stiff".  Note: don't leave your stiletto at home.

We did the $115 menu consisting of 3 savory + 1 sweet course with complimentary amuse bouche, bread courses, and palate cleanser in between.  The menu is divided in First, Second, Fish and Meat course and diners are able to mix and match their 3 savory courses whichever ways.  The sweet courses were very seasonal-focused, not too sweet and really good. Our hostess, waitress, and even bus boys were all great.  Our cup of water were never emptied and our server was great at walking us through the entire menu.  For wine, we were introduced to their wine manager.  (I say wine manager, because this man who helped us does not uphold any quality of a properly trained sommelier)   He picked a wine for us on an extensive "ipad" wine list from his mediocre knowledge and description but everything was still fine besides his lacking.  We carried through dinner with great conversation about the food, wine, and gossips.   

Our perfect Girls Night Out quickly changed when a remark was made at an instant one of my friend held her phone up for a photograph of a beautiful dish. Sure, Asian-taking-picture-of-their-food is a common mockery and issue for many restaurant to maintain their ambiance.  I am sorry for this stereotype.  It was in our absolute intention to first act as respectful diner then as obnoxious paparazzi.  We paid utmost attention and respect to the beautiful plating. We shared opinion and articulated the flavor and texture of each courses. We took photographs in hopes to share our positive experiences with others.  Isn't that what a proper dining experience should be?  I am sorry a certain type of comments that contained prejudice were made at us in the dining room, FRONT OF THE HOUSE, literally a feet away from our dining table.  And of course the remarks were made by their wine manager.

We confronted the Maître D and GM of this, but only received brushed-off apology from the GM: "I don't know what I can do at this point but to offer you complimentary champagne".  How genuine .  Besides this incident,  I would never compare the services to somewhere like say, Eleven Madison Park.  But it was decent, just not justifiable for their price tag. There was a lot of hustling and bustling in the front of the house.  We had at least 3-4 faces through the night who helped us instead of one designated server.  During course number 3, because my friend went to the restroom and return later only 2 of us were served first.  It was awkward.  Overall the service here never felt personable and lack substances.  Until their front of the house staff can catch up to par with the superb production from their kitchen, they need to get over their heads.

Amazingly delicious, EVERYTHING was fabulous!!!! The vibe, the comfortable booth, the amazing service, the FOOD= ALL of it was SO GREAT!!!  We felt welcomed from the minute we walked in, and the space is impressive and beautiful.  We ate slowly and never felt rushed even though we had late reservations,  and we had got the wine pairing with the tasting menu and the sommelier was very knowledgable.  The latin waiters are all adorable, and the all sauces and foams and delicious fish and every dish was so pretty--SO beautifully presented.  It's a sin that this restaurant is only one Michelin star, it really deserves THREE.  I can't wait to come back.

Outstanding food and service. Perfect execution of every dish, including the bread. And when we were there, apparently another table had some questions and Kreuther himself came out of the kitchen and talked to the other table. To be honest I was just going for the tart but pleasantly found all the other dishes were stellar. would definitely recommend!

I had just returned from San Sebastian before dining at Gabriel Kreuther.
Everything GK was as good as the best, the food was perfect and the staff was close to invisible but yet very attentive... perfect service!
A not to be missed restaurant in NYC.
Nice place, great service, the food is amazingly good and tasty!!!

One of the best tasting menus in New York!! The service was fantastic, just like the food.
EVERYTHING tasted so fresh and flavorful. I got the supplemental Halibut with FG to start and it was one of the most unique dishes I've ever had - totally decadent!

I had the Mero for the main and it tasted like it was just caught,  They use gastronomy in several dishes and wish there was more because they are experts!

I'm not big on desserts but could not believe how incredible the meringue grape dessert was. It's quite a filling meal, so this was the perfect light topper for a perfect dinner.
Will go back!!

Truly divine. Their Valentine's Day details filled me with so much happiness - ornately patterned gold menus fastened with jeweled butterfly and tuxedo button pins... Cut out romantic/restaurant-themed words for us to "make our own love poem"... Vanilla bean fortune cookies at the end filled with love-themed proverbs and quotes. Amazing. And the staff were so, so friendly and kind. 

The food (obviously) was all IMPECCABLE. Zero complaints. My husband's favorite was the porcini mushroom cappuccino. So imaginative and flavorful! Blown away.

I have high standards, and they were surpassed in every imaginable way. A perfect evening I'll remember forever.

After walking by this restaurant so many times we decided to go in for a dinner on a late Monday night. Chef Gabriel Kreuther has an impressive résumé and his restaurant is an evident outcome of that success and experience.

To our surprise main dining room was completely packed and there were only couple of tables available in the bar/lounge area. We just wanted to have few dishes to share and couple of glasses of wine anyway so sitting in the lounge and ordering a la carte suited us just fine. Main dining room only serves the four course prix fixe at $115/pp or the Chef's menu at $195/pp. Perhaps we'll try that for a special occasion.

Lounge menu is somewhat more casual and rustic. While diners in the main dining room are enjoying truffles and caviar, lounge patrons have options like Tarte Flambe (Flatbreads), various house made sausages and smaller dishes which are perfect for sharing with wine, beer, cider or cocktails.

Some of the musts are; Sturgeon Tart, Beef Tartare, Fois Gras, Maine Lobster Cappuccino and the Duck Confit. There were some other dishes that both sounded and looked very good but they will have to wait for the next visit.

Sommelier helping at the lounge area was very knowledgeable about the wine pairings and she offered large number of wines by the glass, more than your average restaurant so no need to commit to a bottle.

Finished the meal with the Beignet and the Coffee Macchiato Dome on a sweet note.

Although some what pricey, quality of the food, preparation, service and ambiance justifies the cost. Our table overlooked the Bryant Park on a wintry night while we stayed cosy with our French countryside fare and red wine. Enjoy!

WOW. 1 tasting menu. 3 girls. 13 courses each. 3 hours of culinary bliss. Start to finish, everything was fabulous. The food was amazing. I looked like I was crying at times because it was so good I didn't know how to quietly react.  Wine was amazing.  Service- Cody- was amazing. I knew it would be a wonderful night as soon as he brought over a purse tree for our handbags.  I think my favorite dish was the hamachi with foie gras because I found myself thinking about it during bootcamp class the next morning! 
What a treat, loved every moment.

What a wonderful experience we all had at this restaurant, would recommend it to anyone visiting NYC ... it was a  beautiful place and had such nice space to celebrate my birthday evening with my 8 girlfriends.  The staff was excellent and the drinks were tasty and fun.  The desserts were over the top. We will be back for sure  ...the food was great and the staff was so accommodating..
"My Birthday was fantastic"  ... Thank you.

Just go. Try it. The presentation beautiful. Sashimi perfect. Foie gras melted in my mouth. Duck impeccable. Dessert super, super chocolaty. And they fill you up with different types of breads and butters between each plate. Everything was so FRESH. Quiet inside the restaurant in such a busy area of the city.

Beautiful interior, outstanding food, professional service.

This is a one-star Michelin restaurant and you can tell:  refined food, amuse bouches, palate cleansers, pre-desserts, chocolates after dessert, small portions.

- Foie gras terrine was superb; basically a ball of foie gras rolled in truffles
- Hamachi appetizer with truffles was amazing
- The sunchoke soup was superb
- The sauerkraut tarte is more of a mousse:  avoid if you don't like caviar as the flavors blend really well together (and you'd miss out only getting half)
- The wagyu beef was, shockingly, not the best -- I'd give it a 4 out of 5 and one was ever-so-slightly overcooked

The service was professional but not fawning.  The by-the-glass wine list is a irritating because they offer both 3 and 6 oz pours so I accidentally ordered $46 glasses of champagne instead of $23 ones because of the confusion.  At a restaurant of this quality, a glass of wine should be a glass of wine; let's get rid of the two sizes thing.

The desserts were superb.  An amazing touch to serve the final chocolates in a cocoa pod.

3.5 STARS

We had a nice meal at Gabriel Kreuther. Though the food was generally good and inventive, there wasn't anything that totally blew me away. The squab and foie gras croustillant and langoustine tartare were my favorite dishes. I thought the restaurant space was nice, but didn't have a cohesive feel. Also, it seemed as if they were understaffed and our server, while she was very friendly, was often gone for long stretches of time. 

I still enjoyed my meal at Gabriel Kreuther, and I feel like I'd give the restaurant another try, but I wasn't 100% sold on it.

I read all the reviews on here, and I am just not sure what happened, but our meal was not amazing. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't balls-to-the-wall great. The flavors were fine, nothing made the angels sing. The current menu is different now from what I had (langoustines, scallops, and duck), and the only thing memorable was the chocolates served in a cacao pod, because the chocolates rest on a bed of nibs which are quite fun to eat. I also remember how long the service was (~45 minutes between the second and third courses), and the whole meal was just a belabored and overextended affair.

One of the reviewers on here said it was a sin that GK didn't have more than one Michelin star - like someone at Michelin needs to go to confession because they didn't shower the restaurant with stars, but honestly, one is enough. And going here once was enough for me and going here none is probably enough for you, if you're interested in checking out the ol' Gabester.

Perhaps it was my selections, or it just might be the oeuvre of the restaurant but this place bends a little more heavily toward the German side of Alsace than the French. "Sour" (tart) flavors are ever present and pickled accents show up on most plates. The German wine pairings seem to work just a touch better. In reality, it probably makes no difference. This was a stunning assortment of food. I really enjoyed everything. 

The Veloute appetizer was rich and creamy, the sauerkraut tart capped with a light mousseline and hiding smoked sturgeon was like nothing I've tasted before and the duck was served as a beautiful pink shard with an earthy sausage next to pungent, complimentary red cabbage. Dessert featured a basket of tropical fruits mixed to properly rest a well used palette. 

Before leaving one of the staff members asked about the highlight of the evening. I was dumbstruck. Each and every element was so on-point I stumbled through an incoherent response. Isn't it great when food makes you a blathering fool?

Not sure how this restaurant has received the accolades it has.  Interior is gorgeous but service was  slow and lackluster to the point that empty plates weren't cleared after sitting there for extended periods congealing. Food was certainly nothing to write home about - and definitely not up to expectations. No one was blown away at our table and the men left hungry. Dessert of caramelized apple gel balls with bland vanilla ice cream was woefully sad.  A lot of hype for such mediocre food.  Really not worth it when there are so many other excellent choices in NYC - choose better.

With family now living in different parts of the country,  our times all together are rare, so we decided to treat ourselves and celebrate our daughter's birthday with dinner at GK.  From the time we were seated and our daughter was presented with a personalized menu until we departed several hours later, we enjoyed and savored every moment.  The service was stellar, with each member of the team knowledgeable and attentive, yet unobtrusive.  Each course, from the amuse-bouche, first, second, third, bread, meat, fish, to dessert, was delicious and created with the freshest of ingredients, plated elegantly and served with synchronicity.  The sommelier, after asking about our particular tastes, suggested wines that paired perfectly with our meals.  Our thanks to the entire staff for making our evening one to remember.

I went to GK for my anniversary. The place is well decorated. The recommended wine pairing is excellent. I tried the dinner prix fixe (3 savory- 1 sweet). The food was good for a one-starred restaurant but the service was not good enough. The only problem was that my duck wasnt warm enough but I didnt say anyrhing about it. Also, our table had pieces of bread which should had been cleaned but no one did until I asked a server to do it. The servers dont explain the food in a fluid way. Anyways, I had a great time. I would go again when they change the menu.

From start to finish, we had a fantastic dining experience at Gabriel Kreuther!  Beautifully decorated, delicious cocktails, amazing food and attentive service. The desserts are a work of art! It was a perfect evening and I highly recommend GK!

We went to celebrate my husband's birthday and were treated like a king and queen! The service was impeccable! Everyone was incredibly nice, precise, and the attention to detail is truly an art! It almost feels like a performance how synchronized the servers' steps of service were but not over the top like other upscale dining experiences we've had in the past. 
The food is something we've never experienced before and was just phenomenal! We honestly left the dinner and were in a cab heading home and were saying "wow, what just happened?! That was beyond amazing!" 
The restaurant's ambiance is spot on and while it is incredibly beautiful and pristine, it has rustic elements that make you want to redesign your own home!! 
Thank you, Gabriel Kreuther (front of house,back of house, Colby Lehman!, everyone!)! Our night was one we will never forget! My husband felt so special and it was the BEST way to celebrate his birthday!

Don't like the location, but everything else was beautiful.  From the moment you walk through the entrance, you'll see their seamless and perfect service while it's not stuffy.  
I sat at the bar while waiting for my dinner companions.  The bar area is really nice and modern but still with the discreet but thorough service.  Dinner was wonderful and really beautifully presented.  There were some small things that we weren't sure if they were edible or we didn't know exactly what they were.  But when asked, the staff always had a detailed answer, which told me they were well trained and well informed.  The restaurant is modern with some classic touch - every section you look, you'd find something different.
My expectations were totally met, and I walked out feeling that $ was worth for the wonderful dining experience.

I was very excited to try this place based on the reviews, 2016 Michelin star nod and a personal recommendation from someone while we were having dinner at Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare.  

I don't get why the reviews are so stellar. 

Food: We had the Langoustine Tartare, Sunchoke Soup, 7X Colorado Wagyu Beef Strip Loin, and the duck, Tropical and Coconut Exotic Fruits and the chocolate dessert.
