Everything was just okay, nothing stood out, nothing was memorable.  There are so many amazing restaurants in NYC.  I don't think this one measures up to the greats, but I'm glad that I tried it once. 

Atmosphere:  The dining room is very elegant.

Sincerely, what an incredible meal. The food
was beyond. (We ate in the bar... Do not miss the sturgeon tart, or the flounder tartar. And of course the tartes flambé). The service was incredible. The room was exquisite. I had to stop myself from stealing the silverware. 

I loved everything. It was just beyond and I will remember it forever. Thank you so much. Your staff took extra care of us and we really appreciated it.
What a wonderful experience!  Loved the room, service, and amazing food!  The best fois gras ever.  Chef Gabriel Kreuther's rocks.

So wonderful - food, service, ambiance, wine - it was all magnificent!   My husband and I went on the recommendation of the concierge so we didn't really know what to expect.  Gorgeous presentations.  Amazing food!  We asked the sommelier for a wine pairing and she accommodated us. When we asked her to write down what we drank with each course (we each had different things) she printed up both of our menus and delivered them in the menu sleeve for us to take with us.

I was very excited to try this place after a recommendation from a friend. I went last night 4/15. Maybe I should've lowered my expectations or ordered different items, but the second course and fish were just mediocre bordering on inedible. The space is gorgeous with beautiful wooden columns and the service was amazing. The servers took care of us the entire time. For those reasons I'll give this place 2 stars. 

Now I'm going to give a 3rd star because their bread was really good and the first course and dessert were also both good. But the rest of the meal was just so bad especially for the price we paid that I can't in good conscience give another star. This place is more like 2.5 but I'll round it up to 3.

The items I ordered: Foie Gras Terrine & Black Truffle Praline, Crispy Sweetbreads Roasted in Duck Fat, Nova Scotia Halibut. The Foie Gras was great, but when is foie gras not great. The Sweetbreads were just alright, there was something with the flavors that didn't go well for me. The halibut was really bad, it was very dry, it tasted like it was overcooked. The butter sauce was good but it just couldn't save the meal, I barely ate it. Which is sad for a $180 meal after tax+tip. My friend order the Alaskan King Crab and Diver Scallops and she said both also tasted like they were overcooked.

I've been to my fair share of restaurants with great tasting menu and this dinner was just so disappointing that I don't suggest eating here. Maybe the kitchen had an off night but the food was just not worth it for the money. I'm honestly left wondering how this place received a Michelin Star.
I am a regular here -- innovative dishes and great service.  GK should get at least 2 Michelin stars (at least in my book ;))

Great everything!
In April 2016, about a couple of weeks apart, we had two dinners at Gabriel Kreuther. We were his fan from The Modern and wanted to explore his new venture. On both occasions, we had a great experience. First, the welcome and the ambiance were fabulous. The décor is very pleasant and the tables are set such that one has breathing room. The service is remarkable in that the server to client ratio seems to be around 1:3, with constant attention to everything. The bread service is interesting as several kinds of bread are brought to the table during the meal, with different spreads as well as butter. The ficelle however, is hot from the oven, crisp on the outside and chewy on the inside, delicious. We tried several items from the changing prix fixe menu and can recommend the foie gras terrine, the squab/foie gras croustillant, the king crab, the sunchoke soup and the langoustine tartare. The interesting thing is not so much the main ingredient in these dishes as the complementary flavors that enhance them in the sauces. GK has a great wine list, with some less known gems at reasonable prices as well as very good wines at not exorbitant prices. Sommelier service, especially Mr. Gorsuch, is most helpful and accommodating. We look forward to our next trip to NY; thanks GK!

The food presentation is impressive and comes close to being considered art on occasion. The service is very professional and the atmosphere is crisp as you should expect here. The food was good overall and in some cases excellent. An enjoyable investment!

Coming here for the first time while reading mixed reviews made my experience there all the more memorable. Due to the mixed reviews, I didn't set the bar too high. I think that made it all the more special.

We had a reservation at 6pm but got there earlier. Got seated at around 5:45 and the waiter was extremely courteous. His name was Cody! 

Without even getting a good look at the menu, my boyfriend told me I didn't have to choose. He already chose carte blanche for us.

We started with a moist, delicious bread with a compound butter. My boyfriend and I love good baked breads so definitely a plus there. Then came a cute course that was composed of 4 miniature starters. The most memorable was the yuzu pâté de fruit.  Next came the caviar which was just delicious. Reminiscent of caviar on mashed potatoes - just more elegant! 

Next came a compressed hamachi with fois gras terrine. I'll be really honest with you - I've never had foie gras. Okay, I've never had truffle either but the foie gras I've heard of from food network. Never would I have thought I'd eat it much less like it! The truffle gave it an earthy taste as well. 

My boyfriend's favorite came next which was the ocean trout. It was so creamy and reminded us of an extravagant salad. Would definitely want to savour again! More bread came and it was so reminiscent of our dates at L' ecole and his days of courtship with bread. It definitely kept me smiling the whole night. 

Onwards to our next meal was - sweetbreads! Gosh, never in a million years would I believe I'd try that. Just like the foie gras though, I sucked it up and decided I will try it. It was actually not bad! Pretty good and very rich. I actually didn't think I'd like it but it definitely surprised me for liking it. Next was the king crab - and being a person who doesn't eat crab much, I loved it as well. It was also lighter than the previous dish which was pleasant. After that, we had another dish which was a tad spicy - loved it. The mangalitsa morcilla. Too bad my mother called and I missed out on what made it. 

More bread - the rosemary buckwheat rolls - very fragrant. Dwindling down, our next star was foie gras - and the chef was not shy about it at all. When I smelled it, the aroma reminded me of Vietnamese pho & after speaking with my boyfriend, it was also very reminiscent of Chinese restaurant's roast duck. Braving myself for a big chunk of it, I dug in and loved it. Definitely more fatty and softer than the texture of roast duck - but more delicious. Yum!
Our final entree was the duck confit which was a perfect way to end the meaty portions of our meal.

The next upcoming was the dessert. Something tart to clear our palate was the rice pudding with pineberries, strawberry gelee & elderflower champagne granite (my boyfriend just said darn! We should've gotten champagne). Then came a congratulations on a plate with a candle that starred the fleur de temps & raspberry white chocolate. Lastly was a demonstrative course of crème brulée by our lovely waiter Cody. 

Our course of multiple tastings was definitely pleasing and I would definitely go back. But it wasn't only the tasting menu that's got me wanting to come back.

The wait staff was extremely courteous and attentive. Cody even realized my boyfriend got me a gift. Coming to our table, he asked about it and found out we would be new graduates. Taking that into consideration, it surprised us in our desserts. Even put a candle for us which made our meal tonight all the more special. But honestly what made their staff more attentive was when my boyfriend sneezed. He walked over and told him "bless you". With that kind of attention, how could our night not be special? The other wait staff constantly refilled our water and cleaned after our breadcrumbs. I'm very glad I came here in lieu of my graduation formal. Definitely more worth it to be with someone special and a welcoming atmosphere by everyone there.

This place is a 1-michelin star restaurant that really should have 2 stars.  I assume they'll get there shortly because it is very inventive with excellent attention to every detail.  We came here for a pre-theater dinner and absolutely loved the tasting menu and wine pairings.

They have custom plates, custom silverware, custom wineglasses that are designed to convey the food and drinks in the way most intended by the chef.  Lots of little bites come in between courses to keep things interesting, and topping it off with impeccable service leaves you feeling like a million bucks.

I would definitely come here again.

Overpriced - a bit ostentatious for my taste. It's certainly not classy - they wanna be though.service was good, waiter was very helpful. Area managers were walking around with their hands behind their back - not pleasant at all seeing that. They looked like prison guards, observing. Way over the top. Food was average, very disappointed.

What a wonderful dining experience!  The four-course tasting menu comes dear, but it is worth every cent.  My friend was held up at work, but they sat me at a beautiful table anyhow, rather than making me wait at the bar.  That wouldn't have been an unpleasant situation either, but going to the table is what I preferred.  The cocktail menu has a great blend of classic and new, with even a section for non-alcoholic drinks.  I tried a fruity drink with gin, watermelon and basil called "In Bloom."  It was perfectly refreshing.  Then I switched to my standard Jack Daniels. The menu leans towards seafood, and what amazing food it was.  amuse-bouche was so playful and had a great blend of salty, sour and sweet flavors. The courses were perfectly timed and each one was delightful.  But the bread, oh my how wonderful was the bread?  There were three different flights of bread, each paired with a different kind of spread.  The first was the best--so good actually that we asked for another one and polished it all off along with the chive cream smear. I loved the seared foie gras and fruit chutney.  So sweet and seared to perfection.  I nearly appalled my friend by adding salt to it, but that wasn't because the chef did anything wrong, I just like a salty foie gras. The halibut was cooked to perfection and my tropical dessert was unusual in a great way.  Something to note was that the decor and flatware was just gorgeous.  I have never seen anything like it and I wanted it all.  The only reason why this wonderful place gets 4 instead of 5 stars is that the service got a little less attentive towards the end, but I think that is due in part to how busy the restaurant became.  I will save up to return again sometime in the not-too-distant future.
Took a client for business lunch, service was very slow. Great restaurant but will not come back very slow service for lunch.
Phenomenal. Top notch service to match the top-notch cuisine. Can't wait to go back.
Dinner was fantastic. The tasting was relatively quick at around 2 hours. My favorites were the foie gras and sea scallops. Service was excellent.

This place is excellent, a 5-star restaurant indeed! Came here for an early dinner before seeing a Broadway play. The restaurant is in a great location as it is close to the theater. This is one of the fanciest restaurants I have been to. The service is impeccable, I truly felt I was on an episode of Top Chef the way the food was presented, executed and served. The Food was absolutely delicious! The flavors opened up my palate to flavors unknown. Although this restaurant is quite pricey, you definitely get what you pay for here. I would love to come back and try new dishes as I'm pretty sure the entire menu is spectacular.

Expensive for meh quality food. My family and I were really looking forward to eating here, but the meal was honestly mediocre. 

First course, chilled white asparagus soup with what I can only describe as puffed wheat that tasted eerily similar to Kashi granola. It was bland and I felt like I was eating a bowl of granola. 

Second course was tempura soft shell crab. It was alright but again lacked flavor. 

Lastly the wagyu beef that was served cold with two pieces of asparagus. The beef was alright but not worth the extra surcharge. 

THE SAVING GRACE OF THIS PLACE ARE THE DESSERTS. I had the decadence and caramel cake. And the breads of course.

Excellent excellent place!!!!! Loved this place so much - the food just melts in your mouth!!! I got the duck confit entree and beignet as dessert . Best duck confit dish I've ever had so far!!! Their fork and knife were interesting too! One note is that if you want to order individual item alone (if you just want to order one entree for example), ask to be seated at the bar. If you get seated on the restaurant side, it is a four-course meal only.

Modern French at it's finest.. big, bold and surprising flavors are beautifully presented at GK. Highlights were the scallops. I really wanted the raw scallops from the bar menu as my first course (they were nice to do it for me) and it was out of this world. Every bite was light, fresh and the flavors kept evolving as I mixed the components. The entree scallops were perfectly cooked.  Passionfruit dessert was heavenly. Loved the chocolates served in the cacao bean at the end. Nice touch. I agree with the other reviews that the restaurant should have 2 stars. I enjoyed it much more than Eleven Madison and Bouley. Only negative was service, but perhaps it was an off night.

5 star service, 4 stars for food, 5 stars for ambience. My first visit was for a special Valentine's Day menu, and it was a really lovely experience. Creativity seemed to outweigh taste for some of the dishes, but overall there was a very nice progression of courses. The bread, amuse bouche, and chocolates were generous. I also appreciate half pours on a wine list, which allows you to make your own wine pairings throughout the meal. 

I recently visited for a birthday dinner and sat in the bar area which is a la carte. They were very accommodating and patient (not always the case with large parties!). Portions are on the small side, so I recommend an app + entree + dessert per person. 

The scallops are a refreshing app and they come dressed with a bit of sea urchin. Foie gras and the sturgeon tart were also excellent choices for a bit of old-school glamour. The tarte flambé is a flatbread (we got the mushroom) and is perfect for sharing. The Baked Dorade had the most delicious foam, a lighter entree option with great flavor composition. The duck confit is heartier and cooked perfectly, not too fatty with crisp skin. The only disappointment was the saffron gnocchetti, which lacked depth of flavor and was surprisingly unsatisfying for a pasta. It may have been my mistake to expect gnocchi when it was actually more like shell pasta - not airy and pillowy, yet also not al dente and chewy. 

The ambience couldn't be better - elegant and comfortable with floor to ceiling windows facing Bryant park. I would recommend the tasting menu over the bar. The price difference really accounts for the added touches throughout the meal, and the prefixe price is very reasonable for other restaurants of this caliber. They really know how to take care of their diners - highly recommend as a restaurant for special occasions.

Hard to not give Gabriel a 5* rating.  Truth be told, I would give it a 4.8 if I could, but obviously we can't do that.  My wife and I went here for lunch to celebrate our 20th anniversary.  I had made my reservation on OpenTable through the Gabriel website.  So I was a little taken aback when we got there that they said they did not have my reservation in the system.  I searched my emails and looked at their reservations on their system to no avail.  No reservation under my name.  I was a little bummed out as I had been looking forward to this meal.  No worries the host told us as we could sit in the bar/lounge area.  While this was not ideal and I was still steaming my wife was fine with it.  

Our server was fantastic (sorry I do not remember his name) and the waitstaff in all was also great.  We ordered the bar lunch special menu (an appetizer, entree and dessert) along with an extra dish.  My wife had the classic tarte flambée (personal I loved it while my wife thought it was good, not great), the grouper (spectacular) and the cheesecake (excellent).  I had the pea soup (spectacular), tripe (very good to excellent.  Would have said excellent as there were too many potatoes.) and the beignets (very good, not excellent.).  The staff also sent out a special tart, to celebrate our anniversary, which was excellent.

Besides the fact that my reservation that was not in the system (I later found out, after returning to home, that when I submitted, after entering my credit card details, the credit card system was "temporarily off line" (I never waited to receive confirmation and the screen was still on my computer when I opened it later that evening!) and some very, very minor food gripes, Gabriel Kreuther's is a place I would love to return to some day in the future, especially for dinner.

How to critique  an excellent lunch hour or two.  Reception was warm, service, competent and intuitive, and as for the food...just wonderful...A bit more generous than expected (a caution from the waiter might have helped us avoid over ordering), but the carry-out will serve us well.  Presentation was only exceeded by the taste of each offering.  A beautiful room and deserving of repeat visits.

4.5 Really, but fell a little short of expectations.

To start, really great staff, our plane was late getting into JFK and Jet Blue succeeded in losing our one bag with the dinner wine in it (Frank Family Rutherford Reserve '07 and Chateau Montelena '96 - AHHHH), leading to a desperate call to GK from the cab.  They kindly and calmly changed our reservation from 6:30 to 7:45, giving us time to recover and actually get there.

The location is billed as "Overlooking Midtown's verdant Bryant Park", but there is actually no view at all from the main dinning room, however, the space is elegant yet relaxed.  The service was exceptional, especially the gracious Sommelier who helped me climb back from the loss of my favorite wines with an excellent Cremant Rose and Hestan second growth (we did eventually get our bag and wine back).  They keep the bottles off the table, and they were a touch behind in keeping up with the glasses, but possibly all for the better.

The four of us combined to try most of the offerings.  The Wild American Sturgeon Caviar was outstanding with a very unique presentation of Caviar layered onto a creamy mixture reminiscent of creme fraiche and al-detente potatoes, one of the most successful tastes of the night.  The Chilled Provence White Asparagus Soup was fabulous, and the Seared Sullivan County Foie Gras was perfect. The most successful Third offering was the Grilled Maine Lobster with shellfish-coconut nage, really well-developed and inspiring.  All of the bread was amazing.  The desserts we tried succeeded more on presentation than taste.  There were some misses in our opinion as well.  The Compressed Hamachi was unappealing, introducing an odd bitterness to an otherwise amazing fish.  The Langoustine Tartare was bland, and the Foie Gras Terrine & Black Truffle Praline, Soft Shell Crab Tempura, and Crispy Sweetbreads Roasted in Duck Fat were OK not great.  The Wagyu Beef Strip Loin was a little short on cabrales blue and seasoning, a bit disappointing.

We will definitely be back.  You can not go wrong with a meal of Wild American Sturgeon Caviar, White Asparagus Soup, Seared Sullivan County Foie Gras, and Grilled Maine Lobster !  That pairing is truly 5 Stars.

My family celebrated my son's graduation @ Gabriel K .Surely, it was a beautiful dining experience,full of wonderful surprises.The food,service,and the staff were great.Foie gras was the best!!! in my opinion.

I was here for my semi milestone birthday on a Saturday evening. A beautiful and airy dining space with a lot of richy looking people... I saw many elegant dresses and fine jewelries...  In any event, we had the tasting menu which lasted for almost 3 hours - I believe it was about 10 savory courses plus desert.  It hits all the spots - caviar, uni, foie gras, truffles, wagyu, etc. Everything was creative but not overly complex. Three hour meal can be a bit exhausting and the service could be faster but I was not uncomfortably full at the end the dinner and was able to enjoy till the last course (without wine paring).  I believe they have pre theater and I'd try that next time.

Everything was absolutely perfect from start to finish!  An amazing experience!  We can't wait to go back!  The space is breathtaking with attention placed on the smallest of details.  Every course was delicious!

I went here for lunch with my sister, and it was awful. Nice service, but the space is big and soulless, and the worst part was the food. I don't mind a tiny dish for $29, but it has to be amazing, unfortunately it wasn't even any good, it was bad. We sat at the bar, and watched as bartenders fumbled around gallons of ice tea. I realize it's only lunch, but with these kinds of prices and pretentions they've got to nail it.

I had the pleasure of visiting Gabriel Kreuther Bar twice while in NYC for work. I found the staff both gracious and attentive, and the fare excellent. I highly recommend the boringly named but fantastically complex "West Wind" cocktail, which I would rename "A Song of Smoke and Ginger". The Gran Marnier Baba is also not to be missed; it may sound good on the menu but the presentation will exceed expectations.

Many thanks to Sam, Cesar, and the rest of the staff that made both of my visits exceptional. I don't know when I may return to NYC, but I do know that I will make a point to return to Gabriel Kreuther Bar!

Stunningly sensuous spectacular dining experience. It says French on Yelp, but this is Alsatian food very German influenced. The main dining room is a sophisticated room with round creme. Banquettes and a few artfully placed pillows. This meal was stellar.
Ate:
Two course savory $52 plus desert $16 plus wine $15 Lunch
Dorade with green tomato marmalade w/ coriander fennel foam
Young organic poussin w/ licorice jus
Decadent blackberry over chocolate mouse & milk chocolate w/ caramel glaze
The foods starts coming and doesn't stop. Amuse bouche looks like a beach scene with umbrellas & coconut mango cold soup. The kugelof w/ scallions & fromage blanc is a mix of cake & bread kind of like a brioche. That's the first bread course. The dorade with its foamy top is lick the bowl amazing. The poussin was very good & loved the licorice jus. Second bread was whole wheat ficelle with cultured butter. Dessert was a work of art & the special milk chocolate mousse with caramel was bananas. Not finished, a coconut shell with house made stunning chocolates arrived. #PUREPLEASURE #PERIOD!

My husband and I had early dinner at the bar last Thursday. Since we are vegan, I emailed the restaurant in advance to make sure they can accommodate, given our culinary preferences. I received a prompt reply from their guest relations, assuring me they will be all set. I appreciated the attitude. 
Btw, you can now make reservations for the bar area, via Opentable. Note that the "bar" does not refer to A bar, but to the left side of the restaurant. There are actually two bars at GK - one on the right side of the restaurant (referred to as 'the main dining room', more formal) and one on the left ('the bar').
Staff was very friendly and attentive, food was beautifully presented, as expected from such an establishment, but I must honestly say, nothing extraordinary taste wise. Had the sweet pea soup, the spring salad (all vegan), the chef's entrée, which was prepared especially for us, and delicious fruit and sorbet for dessert. 
Again, solid meal, but didn't knock us off our feet, and we did expect them to do just that.
Also worth mentioning- maybe due to the early hour - 6 pm - crowd was mainly in their 50s - 60s,  so you might want to take this under consideration ;)

AB-SO-LUTELY. YUP!

I am extremely picky with high-end Michelin-type restaurants. I eat at about 3 per week and am mostly unimpressed. I was told that GK was a game changer and quite good. I figured that I had to check it out!

First of all, the presentation was amazing. I was blown away. I have eaten at Alinea (in Chicago) where they give you a helium balloon made of apple for dessert and everything is extremely well presented. In NYC I've eaten at almost all of the 3 Michelin starred restaurants and a huge handful of the 1 & 2 starred.

GK for NYC takes the cake. In my opinion, it's better than 11 Madison Park, absolutely.

I had a cocktail with watermelon and basil which was so light and refreshing. It started my evening off on the most positive note. I have a stomach issue and have extreme reactions especially to acidic drinks, so it was awesome to be able to choose from a menu with an extensive selection of juices and cocktails to choose from.

The staff was great. There was one hiccup where a course was swapped (I received the wrong plate and had to switch), but I didn't mind it one bit. Other than that, everything was perfect from start to finish. The waiter had great recommendations and was very accommodating to my stomach issue. It's refreshing because even in some of the very high-end establishments, waiters are not briefed on what allergies mean what (for instance, a lot of the times when I say I have a stomach sensitivity to acid, they bring me a drink with grapefruit or OJ in it which are both extremely acidic). Awesome to know we were in good hands!

Now on to the food
+ Cured Tasmanian Ocean Trout with sweet peas * parma prosciutto * dill - MUST ORDER. Absolutely heavenly. I tried some of the other starters and this was by far the best.
+ FOIE GRAS - Perfectly seared and heavenly. I'm a HUGE fan. 
+ Grilled Maine Lobster - Also heavenly.
+ Awakening * Strawberry Rhubarb with poached rhubarb * buttermilk panna cotta * strawberry sorbet - Again, perfect.

There were some little things that the waiter brought out (for instance, palate cleansers) which were extremely well presented and tasty. I almost don't even want to post pictures to ruin the surprise. 

For a special occasion, business dinner, business lunch, any type of lunch/dinner, romantic dinner, or just simply the want to embark on a culinary journey, Gabriel Kreuther is your place!

I love the attention to detail in the ambience, plating, and silver/plateware. The squab and foie gras croustillant is a must try if you like foie gras at all. I got a lobster dish as my main course, but I thought it was not very memorable compared to the squab and foie gras. They also served many different types of bread with different pairings between each course which I really enjoyed.

Drinks and appetizers at the bar area were awesome, definitely will make plans to come back for dinner! "The William" and "West Wind" were phenomenal. No doubt, all cocktails are carefully crafted with painstaking attention to detail. Mushroom/onion/chive flatbread was delish and an ample portion to share as a hearty snack.

Great setting/ambience and bonus points for location right across the street from Bryant Park, can stroll right over. Corporate crowd certainly tends to dominate the scene here, but I would go for a special personal occasion as well.

Spectacular lunch - one of the best we've ever had in our 13 years in NYC. Not being zillionaires, we highly recommend trying GK's prix fixe 2-course lunch and splitting a dessert. 

You will have SO many wonderful bites. This isn't one of those joints where you need a sandwich after the meal. Generous, intriguing amuse-bouche with 5 different items. Two distinct breads and spreads, one for each course. Plus complimentary truffles & marshmallow with the check. Tremendous flavor and freshness across the board. Fancy but not fussy.

Warm staff greetings and service from the debonair host, waiter, servers, everyone. 

Honestly, this is exactly what a fine restaurant should be. Go.

We had an amazing evening at Gabriel's. The chef tasting menu is a must,  every dish has its own personality and variety of flavors. Every detail is looked after, and every dish takes you through an amazing tasting trip. From the #amuse beach dish, all the way to the fabulous deserts the menu is a must if you are visiting NYC. My compliments to the chef.

Another multi-course expensive place to dine in Manhattan.Well stars for the food and ambience, the personel hat and purse stand, the sour cream butter with the bread( divine) . I will not be going back, i was invited by a friend on an expense account. Too much about everything for my taste, but the butter, and the Martini were 6 star.

Good service and outstanding food. The ambiance was good, really nice decor, and have I mentioned the food was amazing?
The hostess could have been friendlier, the sommelier acted as she was better than any of us, but our server was friendly.
It still deserves the 5 stars.
Cheers

Oh gosh. I was lucky enough to be taken out here for lunch, and it was fantastic. We all did the 2-course lunch prix-fixe (there is no a la carte dining here) and split two desserts. I had the spiced beef tartare and Hawaiian mero, both of which were executed flawlessly. The mero may have been one of the best fish dishes I've ever had, and married French preparation with Thai flavors.

Desserts were fantastic and presentation was especially lovely. We ordered the Decadent and the Tropical, and the Decadent was definitely the bigger hit of the two.

Service was on par for this caliber of restaurant.

Lunch also included four (!) amuse bouches and two bread courses. All in all, a fantastic value if you have the wallet and the time for this experience.

Beautiful ambiance, incredible food, stellar service!  I can't say enough about this restaurant.

I found it online and am so happy I did.  My husband and I had the most delicious meal and left delighted and stuffed.

What a lovely find in NYC!

Wow, so enjoyed my experience here, even before I finished my dinner I already made a plan of coming back in two weeks.

The food is truly amazing. I love that the food is so flavorful, to me the food is comparable to any michelin two stars restaurants. I may not pay extra money for my beef course next time, that is not worthy the extra dollars. 

Service was great, but I can see there are room to improve it to make it more professional and more upscale. It is a relatively new restaurant, so I am confident that can be done very easily, especially the management team are very positive, warm and really care about the customers. 

Will definitely suggest this amazing restaurant to all my friends!

Do not go through life without having tried the foie gras terrine & black truffle praline. Life changer right there. 

Every facet of the dining experience at Gabriel Kreuther leaves me in awe. From the decor to the impeccable service to the carefully crafted attention to each dish (especially including the transitional ones), everything was to perfection. 

Do make a reservation and allow your palette to be blown away.

First you need to understand how far I am willing to go for good food. When traveling you must research great restaurants in the area and when staying in Morristown, NJ I couldn't find much. So as I flew into Newark and I immediately headed to Manhattan for dinner.

Using my 5 star rating (1 star for each category): 

Atmosphere (.75) - restaurant was beautiful but the bar area is open next to the dining room and I could hear crying babies and cackling, which ruined the mood.

Service (1) - fabulous. I ordered a glass of champagne but after starting my meal I realized I wanted red. They took back the champagne with no fuss/no issues and never charged me for it.

Food (.75) - 4 courses + 4 intermezzo. Bread/butter choices w each meal (didn't love all the choices). Trout was sooo good (and I don't even like trout). Foie was amazing, perfectly cooked. Halibut was perfectly cooked and a big portion for a tasting menu. The dessert intermezzo of homemade marshmallow was fabulous but I had the cherry almond as my actual dessert that was only ok, I little lacking in flavor.

Would I recommend (1) - absolutely. Great food at a great price.

Would I go back (1) - yes

4.5 stars

We loved Gabriel's food at the Modern and were looking forward to trying his new place. It did not disappoint! The decor is beautiful, the cocktails really well thought out and the food is amazing. 
We started out with Caribbean/hispanic amuse bouche which was unexpected but totally delicious. The fried queso blanco was really really good.   
 Do not miss the sweetbreads. No matter what, don't miss the sweetbreads. They are hands down the best I have ever had. I could have put that sauce on a on a rock and eaten it. 
The smoked trout was delicious and balanced, the smoked sturgeon cream was amazing. I wish I could have ordered two.
Desserts and the breads (different type of bread with spread comes for each course) were wonderful as well. The chocolate mousse with caramel was also some of the best I have ever had. The dacquoise was also very decadent. 
Service was flawless. Attentive and friendly but relaxed. Can't wait to come back and eat at the bar. That menu looks great and Gabriel is serving his liverwurst from the Modern there. You will never taste better. 
My only complaint is that you can't possibly eat everything but you will try. 

This is a restaurant you come back to a few times to try out the whole menu.

The food itself is a solid 3. Found a gnat in my trimbach, so that takes it down two stars. 

We sat for the 3 savory + 1 sweet prix fixe and ordered the following:

First--
Citrus Cured Tasmanian Ocean Trout
Foie Gras Terrine & Black Truffle Praline

Alright, first off, the trout was doused in some sort of weird nondescript sauce, with nary a hint of the wasabi mentioned in the menu description line. I felt like I was stuck in Smorgasburg, eating crap quality salmon diced up and served in a bowl (or as they would like to call it: poké). This was a poor showing for sure and I definitely expected something more impressive. 
The foie gras dish? Meh. Everyone knows what foie gras tastes like, so at that point I'm not going to be blown away by the texture, taste, or appearance of the foie gras. I'm hoping to get some measure of inventive creativity, but instead am presented a balled up foie gras in ...truffle---yay for originality-- surrounded by a prison of dry, yet somehow moist, cubes of toast. Nope. 

Second: 
Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart
Crispy Sweetbreads Roasted in Duck Fat

This set was much better. The sturgeon came in a large dish enveloped by your typical gimmicky smoke bowl (à la most cocktails served at Angel's Share in St Marks) but I found this dish to be absolutely delicious and was pretty much what I expected when sitting down for a meal at this wildly popular restaurant. 
The sweetbreads were cut pretty poorly and came in large globules that were a bit awkward to chew or even cut...but I can't say that this dish fell flat. It was decent. 

Third:
Nova Scotia Halibut
Long Island Crescent Duck Breast

The halibut was good...but when is halibut ever not good? It's the easiest fish in the world to serve and I don't think Gabriel did anything remarkable to spruce it up or enhance it in any way.
Duck Breast was definitely on the heavy side, but perfectly doable.

Dessert:
Decadent - Chocolate Caramel
Tropical - Coconut Exotic Fruits

Desserts were fine. Again, nothing that blew me away and nothing too memorable.

What I do remember though is the gnat chilling in my wine as the server poured it. That's cool. Really--it is. It just means you have a crappy way of storing wine, and likely that the wine was sitting open for a long period of time before it finally made it over to my glass (talking hours more than minutes here...if not, dare I say-- days?). What is not cool is the server's handling of the situation. He glanced at it, said "oops sorry" and quickly scurried away. Brought back a new glass, and poured it again. Now-- if I have to be completely honest, it would've been nice to see him offer SOME form of apology in the form of, oh I don't know, another glass of wine? or...maybe an extra amuse bouche? I got nothing man. And that's frankly so unprofessional and such a shame, especially if Gabriel Kreuther is really trying to establish himself and itself as a restaurant on par with the best of the city. Because if that's the level of service you're providing to your diners, then you're a very, very long way from being called one of the best restaurants in the city.
Celebrated birthday with two other friends who were born on the same date. What a coincidence right?!!!!

There isn't anything I disliked Gabriel Kreuther yet easily prefer it to Jean-George's, where Kreuther used to be.

I dined here  for lunch and got the prix fixe menu ($52 for 2 courses or $78 for 3). For dinner the prix fixe is 4 courses for $125. The ambiance is elegant yet comfortable, warm, and inviting. To the left there's a stunning bar-area with multiple tables in a lounge-like setting. To the right is the official dining room with several 2-person and 4-person tables.

Service was continuously attentive yet friendly as well. Each person made just enough small talk and was still knowledge in each and every course.

Standouts included the coconut amuse bouche- absolutely gorgeous and delicious! All dishes I had were amazingly delicious as well. The duck breast dish I had was so moist and absolutely exquisite with the broth- quite easily better than French Laundry/Per Se's liberty duck dish.

Nice touches like a bread course with each dish was wonderful. I also liked the chocolates mignardises at the end- beautiful yet tasty!

All in all, easily a new favorite in NYC and can't wait to return. Easily accommodates a casual or special occasion alike!

Had a great night celebrating my friend's birthday. Here's a breakdown of the pros and cons and why I ended up giving this place 4 stars instead of 5. 

Pros:
Great food (duh)
Great drinks - had a watermelon-basil-gin drink. So refreshing. 
Great wine selection - especially if you like German wines like Rieslings! I love dry Rieslings and not a lot of restaurants have a good selection. This place did.
Great menu - I liked the fact that you can do a 4-course prix fixe or the chef's tasting consisting of 7-10 courses. 

Cons:
1) The server was rushing us a bit. We sat down at 5:30 and the server didn't really give my friend and I time to enjoy our wine. He came by once to explain the special and came by a few minutes later to take our order. My friend was a little hesitant but I could tell the server didn't care. Here's the best part - he got my dessert selection wrong! I ended up not saying anything because I was too full to care. 
2) I understand that every restaurant has to sell and aim for the up charge. But this place overdid it a bit on the black truffles and caviar. There was a spätzle appetizer that, in my opinion, was fine without the black truffle. But if you wanted it, you had to supplement $35 for roughly 1/2 a black truffle for each person. I think I would have been fine with that up charge for an entree (same amount of black truffles). It was a bit too much and unnecessary for appetizer. 
3) Another issue with the up charge. So we paid $75 for 1/2 ounce of caviar to start. For this amount of money, normally you would get a few extra pieces of blinis. Here, we got 5 nickel-sized potato chips. Really?? Couldn't we get a bit more?

I would have liked to give them 4.5 stars but decided to round down. This is because I couldn't get over getting rushed while the restaurant had empty tables all around us. If a restaurant was packed and I was rushed to accommodate other reservations, I totally get that. But we left at 9 and I definitely saw lots of empty tables with no parties waiting to be seated. For a $720 tab (for 2 people) and no waiting parties, there really was no need to rush us.

We had a company dinner here and while the food was delicious, the service was good, but at this price point, the service should be great, which is the reason for 4, instead of 5 stars.  Service was a little bit more challenging to get their attention that one would expect, with the exception of the hovering bus boys. The server basically disappeared after we placed our order and we coudlnt' recall seeing her again until the check presentation.

We ordered cocktails for the table and one order, the first, was forgotten, so we waited for it to arrive and no one noticed that 7 people were not drinking their cocktails for quite a while.  Eventually, we had to flag down a person and the missing drink was re-ordered and then delivered and we all had our round of, not quite as cold as we hoped, cocktails.  (Though they were delicious!)

 A well curated wine list was available and the sommelier, was knowledgeable about the list.  His suggestions were excellent matches for our meals and shockingly affordable, even though we didn't mention a thing about price.  A mineral heavy riesling from Alsace and a surprisingly bright grenache both paired excellently with everyone's 2nd and 3rd courses.  Everyone wished we'd had the opportunity to order a bottle for the first course, as well but we didn't see the sommelier before the first course had already come out. At about $200, it was the least amount we've spent on wine for this annual dinner, in the past decade.  There were more opportunities to keep refilling our glasses, that were missed.  None of us had hangovers the next day though, so I guess that was the silver lining.

The food itself was wonderful and presented in creative glassware and tableware.  Even the flatware was uniquely styled.  (The brass colored spoons were my favorites of the evening.)  The paired bread courses are a wonderful idea and executed brilliantly.  The mushroom? soft bread with a chive fromage blanc was the best of the evening's bread courses, imho.  We all chose to do the 3 savory + 1 sweet course pre-fixe and were all quite pleased.  My favorite of the courses was the lobster (though the claw meat tempura was a bit of an odd side addition to it and I wonder if it was even necessary.  It also wasn't my favorite because when someone tells an Asian person "Tempura something"- they will expect a crispy panko shell and I was disappointed.  Crispy, it was not.) though after having a bite of someone's scallop course, I'd say the two were neck in neck as the best of the evening.  My duck was delicious if a bit predictable and the chilled honeydew soup had some delightful tapioca? pearls which were a nice surprise.  I had a rhubarb and herbal sorbet as my final course and it was the perfect size to complete the meal.  It was whimsically plated and perhaps my favorite plating of the evening. Also the unexpected coco pod chocolates and macaroon finish were just delightful.

All in all, a wonderful evening that ended up being about half of what we traditionally pay for our annual dinner (though the lion's share of that was because we only had 2 bottles of affordable wine for 7 people).

On an unrealted to food note... whomever is doing the hiring over there definitely has a preference for very pretty men, front of house.  Some so pretty it might hurt to look directly at them (the sommelier and an Italian? food runner come immediately to mind). Strangely enough, they also prefer very stern looking women, out front.  They are beautiful but in the Katinka (Milla Jojovich's character) in Zoolander, kind of way. None of this will affect your dining experience but they definitely add to the ambiance of the place.

We came here for my husband's birthday dinner and had a wonderful experience.  The food was great, but what made the evening so memorable was the service.  Everyone went out of their way to make us feel special, when all I had asked for was to write "happy birthday" on the dessert.  We were first brought to the chef's table by the kitchen for a complimentary drink and two appetizers (a tuna and caviar dish, and a mushroom flatbread) before bringing us to our table.  

We ended up ordering the tasting menu because we couldn't decide what we wanted.  Most memorable dishes for me were the compressed hamachi with black truffle and foie gras terrine, abalone that had just arrived that day, roasted diver scallops, grilled lobster, and a grilled quail.  

Another shout-out for the very attentive service throughout the meal.  I'd highly recommend Gabriel Kreuther, especially for a special occasion so you can feel extra pampered.

We had drinks and shared a few dishes at the bar dining area on a Friday early evening. Great experience, we loved the restaurant, but the service was a tad disappointing. 

- space: modern, elegant, and warm, beautiful restaurant 
- food: well executed and delicious in a very refined way
- drinks: kir royal were very nice, I had the apricot flavor and paired well with the dishes 
- service: a bit off for a Michelin stared restaurant; one of our food items was not brought out and we had to ask for it; waiter did not ask if we wanted another drink despite our glasses were empty; waiter transitioned into the dining room and we were ignored. 

Given the food, drinks, atmosphere, we plan to return to try the main dining room, albeit with some hesitation.

This place is excellent in every way. The som, Emilie, has been rated the best in NYC (and if not the world, should be).  The food is amazing. Delicious, imaginative, and always changing in the best way. This is my favorite restaurant for a bit of a splurge night out.

What do you do when you're sickly but you have a long anticipated reservation that will cost you almost as much to cancel it as to go?  You take a nap in the park next door like a hobo and just hope for the best.  

Despite feeling like I was trapped in a bubble and been hit by a bus or two, my first dinner at Gabriel Kruether was a life altering meal.  I'd never tasted dishes that had so much going on in terms of texture, temperature, and flavor. I could be best compared to the first time I had Thai food in Thailand with a perfect balance of sour, salty, sweet, and hot.  The Fennel-Cockle Veloute did just that. The warm soup poured over the icy watercress granite with caviar for texture, and these little shrimp that got slightly poached from the stock.  Hot, warm, cold, crispy, smooth...how on earth is this all going on at once and it's working?  The smoked sturgeon and sauerkraut tart was almost as divine with it's flaky crust, smokey fish, smooth topping and that perfect hit of acid from the kraut. Oh and the bread! Perfect, crusty, piping hot bread.  I think Gabriel Kruether must be some kind of wizard to be able to whip up these beautiful, flavorful masterpieces.  Well, the wizard was there that night and everything was wonderful.   Unfortunately, my condition worsened throughout the evening and we had to skip dessert and get it to go.  The servers were great and recommended the one that would travel best and made sure we were good to go and everything was okay with our meal.  The dessert was still amazing the next day.  My only complaint that night was that the wine pairing I had asked was nothing special.  I didn't really care though since the food was so good.  This first visit was a solid 5 stars.

Fast forward to last month for my birthday.  My husband took me back here since I'd been raving about it for the past six months.  We decided to go all out and do the tasting menu since the four course blew us away last time.  I just ordered a cocktail instead of the wine. Everything started off on the right foot with tasty cocktails and fresh bread.  The appetizers were interesting in terms of acid and texture like I'd hoped.  Then we got into the main courses, and it was a train wreck from there.  Overcooked lobster, tough, dry chicken, pork fat for bread for someone who said they didn't eat pork, sugary Americanized dessert, long lulls in between courses, non-existent servers, and being charged for a supplement we never received.  This is inexcusable for the amount we were paying. It's probably needless to say, that the wizard was not in the house that night.  This was nothing like my experience in February, but cost us twice as much!

All of this is inexcusable for the price we paid, but I think if we would have stuck with the four course menu, some of these problems could have been avoided.  For example, on the four course menu you choose the dessert.  We got the tasting and got one giant chocolate sugary dessert off the regular menu.  In any other tasting I've had, you either pick something or they give you a few different things, or you get something special not on the regular menu.  Secondly, the portions were too large for a tasting.  I was full after eating the first main course.  They need to pace things out better.  This experience was about 2 stars since the bread and appetizers were good and service didn't start to fall until the mains.

I give Gabriel Kruether an average of 3 stars between the two visits.  I don't know if I'll be back though with some many wonderful fine dining options in New York City.  I will always have that memory of that one really good meal.  I guess that's something.

Made a reservation to have dinner at the bar. They have decent drinks here, some really interesting ones. The beer selection wasn't great, to be expected. Tried many dishes on the menu. The sausage was amazing. The service was great, very formal. The place is a bit stuffy, but nice overall. The prices are high as expected.

This fine meal began quite badly for us, entirely through my OWN FAULT.  We got to Gabriel Kreuther in a cab, and I put my hand back to get my wallet to find the pocket was empty.  I left Mitchell at the restaurant, and the cab took me back to our hotel to search for my wallet.  In the end, it delayed our meal about 45 minutes, and got me very stressed out, but staff in Gabriel Kreuther quickly helped me forget the ordeal of the previous hour, and that counts for a lot, to me.  Thank you!

Here's our menu for this spectacular meal, which I'll go through as time and energy allows.  This was a truly phenomenal meal, and our main waiter, Alex, along with a team of others, went out of their way to give "fine dining" true meaning with the way they served us.  Along with the meal, we enjoyed glasses of a vintage bottling from Dom Perignon along with the precursor of Siberian Osetra Caviar.  We moved on to a full bottle of 2009 "Altenberg de Bergheim" Grand Cru Blend from Marcel Deiss in Alsace, and finished with a half bottle of 2012 Opus One Cabernet Blend from Oakville AVA in the Sonoma Valley.  These wines were all selected by Mitchell, with nods of approval from the sommelier.  100/100 for the wines!

DINNER  Friday, September 30th, 2016
Siberian Osetra Caviar - 1 full ounce
This caviar is firm in texture with a nice pop, buttery, and with a lingering clean aftertaste.  It comes from the Acipenser baerii and is sustainably farm raised by Carolian Caviar, a Scandinavian producer in Varkaus, in southeastern Finland.
We've never dined on so much caviar before, but ooh lah lah, was it ever delicious!  Thank you, Mitchell, for so generously treating me!!   100/100

Savory Scallion - Kougelhopf  - chives - fromage blanc
Lovely savory flavors, which followed the caviar very nicely, and went very well with Mitchell's choice of the white wine blend from Alsace.   95/100

Rambutan-Orange - Blossom - lime zest - yuzu
Refreshing, and again nicely complimented by the Marcel Deiss - 95/100

Jackfruit-Tequila - aleppo pepper - orange zest

Coffee Seared Yellowfin Tuna - poblano peppers - macadamia nuts
two different versions were served, owing to my aversion to peppers.  The tuna was delicious!  95/100

Foie Gras Terrine & Black Truffle Praline - muscat gelée - seven grain toast
two of our favorite things, foie gras and truffles, and BLACK truffles, at that!  100/100

Cured Hawaiian Striped Marlin - wasabi leaf - finger lime - crystal lettuce
Fish  is definitely  a favorite for Mitchell, and this was a real winning combination of flavors.  100/100

Wholegrain Ficelle - cultured butter

Scottish Langoustine a la Plancha - smoked potato - mint - shellfish-coconut emulsion
Another winning combination, this one especially nicely paired with that Marcel Deiss, Mitchell really picked a great wine to compliment the menu!  100/100

Mangalitsa Morcilla - potato salad - parsnip puree
a bit like some comfort food, as we come near the end of the dishes we enjoy with the Marcel Deiss   95/100

Rosemary Buckwheat Rolls - whipped lardo - chili  garlic

Hazelnut Curried Veal Sweetbreads - arborio porridge - leeks - pickled cilantro
I simply adore sweetbreads, and am always thrilled when I see them on the menu.  These were really different from others, but just by what was combined with them, superb!  100/100

Long Island Crescent Duck Breast - fennel - roasted broccolini - pickled mustard seeds
I feel sorry for anyone who won't eat duck breast!  Done to perfection, and very well combined with the fennel, this worked so well with our Opus One, and vice versa, it was a real highlight to a marvelous meal.  100/100

Goat Milk Panna Cotta - pear marmalade - cranberry sorbet - rice tuile
Decadent Chocolate Caramel - mixed media crumble - chocolate mousse - caramel ice cream
Crème Brûlée Frappe - red fruit gelée - coconut dacquoise
Desserts sometimes just kind of go over the top, to where they're overwhelming instead of enjoyably closing to a delightful dégustation.  While certainly not minimalist, these three were pleasing and enjoyable and an easy ending to a complex and very enjoyable time at one of Gabriel Kreuther's tables.  Our thanks to our servers, the sommelier, and everyone working behind the scenes!  100/100

Chocolates - Petits Fours

Service was impeccable, and merits another 100/100
When averaged out, for us, the composite numerical score for Gabriel Kreuther is 98.5%
Thank you for helping us have a very memorable evening.

I've tried to upload the 32 photos I took here, but they just won't go through.  Maybe I'll manage in the future.

This place will have three Michelin stars soon, so go now. Had the sturgeon and was great. The fish was also amazing. Skip the flat bread, it's not worth it. The duck was fine but not amazing. You can order all of these at the Bar.

What a wonderful experience! We didn't have reservations but were able to eat at the bar. We had the flounder tartare which was amazing , served with a delicious multigrain bread. I had the champagne spraetzel and lobster which was outstanding; my husband had the sausage with sauerkraut- he said he could've had three they were so tasty. The service was attentive and perfect!

Well this deserves 5 stars, because the place looks great, service is great, and food was great. It just didn't blow me away, other than the price. Only a few wines by the glass avail. $14- $29, small pour (maybe 5 oz)
The wine list, expansive on Ipad, ran from $120- $thousands.
Even half bottles, we did half Riesling $39, half red $65, I think those were near the least expensive, but very good. 
The presentations were all very nice, obviously small portions, but between the amuse (smoked trout, was great), and the multiple bread courses, you do fill up.
The room is chic, tables for two are a little bit too big (go figure), your too far away for a romantic dinner. 
It was a nice experience, not my best, but sometimes things just don't click.
Very attentive service, all around.

Ordered:
2 glass Pinot Blanc, VG
1 glass Riesling, VG
1/2 btl Riesling, VG
1/2 btl Margaux, very good

Foie Gras App, very nice, not great
Sturgeon Tart, fume was nice
Hamachi/Foie, very rich
Poached Foie Gras, great
Wagu Steak, very good
Scallops, didn't blow me away
Etheral Almond, Ok
Concord Grape, very good

2 Coffee

$550 incl.all

Fantastic! Need I say more? Well, I guess I do need to explain my 5  rating. The dining area has a relaxed feeling, but modern. The wooden pillars keep it Midwestern I guess? 
The food is crazy delicious and some playfulness on the presentations. Great wine selections and great staff. I've hardly seen the timing of plating or removing of the dishes. But if you have more than 2 people at a table, they have a sequence to this, cool to see and like I said I hard have seen this done with classical ease. 

Found out they earned a Michelin star last year and I see why. 
Oh and saw the kitchen, and you know what? There were minimal conversations between chefs. The food was called out, acknowledged and done.  

Again, fantastic flavors, service and a feel good ambience with a great wine selection = 5 
 A must to try when in NY.
Fantastic restaurant.  Amazing food, impeccable service with a very nice view.  One of the nicest meals I've enjoyed in NYC.

Just amazing! This place is wonderful... everything from A to Z is so well taken care of.. from the moment you walk in... Sam .. "the bar manager" sorry if I am mistaken about it. He just make us feel more that welcome.. beautiful bar..service and drinks are spectacular!! Then when u are moved to your table.. the most amazing food journey starts .. 
The New Zealand langoustine carpaccio
The Grilled Monterey Abalone soup is so..so good. The Long Island crescent duck breast.. out of this world! Everything was good! The desserts were even better .. a must. The service? I don't think 5 stars is enough for it.. Alex.. Miguel .. " I am so bad cause I forgot the name of our server.. who was always so attentive I really thank him for all! And last.. A big shout out to the general manager Thierry Chouquet and his crew.. I finally made it there Thierry !!! Thank u.. for everything.

Everything we expected and more.

From the moment we arrived, we knew exactly where Gabriel Kreuther gets their Michelin star from. It was the warm and friendly welcome, the massive attention to detail, the unique food, and most importantly, the fun experience.

Kreuther once said:

"When I grew up, I never understood, why do I need to wear a tie to enjoy a good meal? It doesn't make my meal better. Why don't they let me go in in one of those places and just walk in with jeans and enjoy my dinner? It doesn't mean that when you have a tie on that the wine is going to be better..."

And that attitude is exactly why we picked this spot in the first place. Though there is a dress code (business casual, jackets for men are encouraged but optional), don't expect a stiff environment under the high ceilings and the hundreds of birds that surrounds the dining area. Our experience was everything but stiff.

Fun. Fun would be the word I choose here. Every single plate served comes with such a fun twist, we kept wondering how the chef managed to create the perfection that was served before us.

When the glass coche was lifted off of the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart topped with American caviar mousseline, be prepared to be taken by the whiff of the applewood smoke that leaves just the perfect trail on the dish.

The bread always comes warm, and in great variety in between the courses. The complementing small plates was a great bridge as we move from one course to another.

Service? Amazing attention to detail. To a point that they've noticed my husband's left-handedness and adjusted his silverware placement. Interior? Gorgeous and comfy.

Come with loose, stretchy pants. You're going to need to make room for plenty of goodness in this spot ;)

Love this place! Perfect balance of minimalism new American and fill your tummy dining. Great service and very beautiful environment. For less than usd200 for four courses, it's a decent price and good value for money. I will definitely be back with friends in tow!

We couldn't get the reservation at their dining room, thus we ended up only in their lounge. We ordered Maine lobster croquettes, liverwurst, foie gras terrine & black truffle praline, sturgeon tart to share for two of us. Everything was well executed but their foie gras praline was to die for. It was small but big in flavors and also melting in your mouth. We regretted that we didn't make the reservation early enough to be able to dine at their dining room.

Simply one of the best restaurants I have ever been in the city. Very well decorated place, with innovated, delicious food. My girlfriend and I really enjoyed our experience here.

I would definitely recommend it to my friends and I would love to go back.

This is one of the best fine dining experience. It's up there with the inn at little Washington. If you've heard of them. 

But this is our first Michelin star restaurant, and it did not disappoint. 

I'm not going to go into any of the details of our meal. I think that it's an atrocity if I were to spoil it for other customers. It's the surprise of flavors, and beauty that you pay for! 

I'll just say that the service is Michelin quality. They are very detailed. Even figured out that I was left handed and set up my utensils to accommodate. They made sure of my wife's food allergies and accommodated it with out compromising quality and taste. 

The decor is amazing as well as the food. Each dish was a work of art and my heart sank every time I had to ruin it to eat. It truly was beautiful and the taste was right on par. Not one complaint!!!! The most amazing experience we have had in a while!

Remarkable service, even by New York standards.   I came for a business dinner and unexpectedly my business partner fell ill just before our reservation.  We sat and tried to work through but had to end the night before our dinner.  But not before being able to experience a carefully crafted, creative cocktail as well invented as I've found in the city.   The waitress was thorough and spoke passionately on recommendations as I waited out whether we were going to eat or not.  She was attention, patient and passionate.  Our waiter brought my partner tea and was genuine in his concern and understanding of the situation and trying to make her comfortable.
The entire experience, rather than throwing the restaurant back onto the end of the 'sometime' list gets a fast pass to the top of restaurants in the coming weeks to come back to and really be able to enjoy their wonderful menu and service.

Again, the Gabriel Kreuther team didn't disappoint! 

My party and I ordered the duck confit and sturgeon tart. My favorite was definitely the duck confit dish, which was tender and well-balanced. If anything, I probably order the duck confit way too often! 

The service was attentive but not overbearing. Sam was our server and we had delightful, little conversations each time he came by my table. He was professional, sweet, and charming. Gosh, do I sound like I have a crush on him now? 

Consistency is something that I look for in restaurants. Gabriel Kreuther hits this factor very well - without having a snobby bravado.
Highly recommend the bar at GK. Went their Saturday night for drinks and apps and it was awesome.  Great atmosphere, great selection of scotch and bourbon and steak tartare was incredible!

Had a meal at it's neighbor - Aureole a few days before dining here, it was disappointing so I was kind of expecting similar experience. But I was wrong. This place was awesome. I loved everything I ate. The Hamachi was indescribably good, so was the soup and the duck breast.
Was a fixed 4 course meal.
Price was quite expensive obviously, but it IS a Michelin one star in NYC, so that should be no surprise.
Love the service. Waiters were extremely friendly and polite, so was the front desk.
Bathroom was very nice too.
5 stars fo sho.

In my opinion, Gabriel Kreuther merits the title of Best Restaurant in New York. The mantle has passed from 11 Madison Park (although you could argue that 11MP lost the title when Danny Meyer ceased his involvement with it). The food is fantastic, the room beautiful, the service exemplary, and the atmosphere warm and welcoming.

Gabriel Kreuther is formal in a classic American way, i.e. relaxed, warm and friendly, but rigorously focused on technique in the preparation of food as well as in the guest experience. In other words, the restaurant staff hold themselves to a very high standard, but guests are not expected to kowtow. That approach is very different from that of the classic high-end restaurant, where the guests are expected to be slightly awed and properly cowed by the pyrotechnics on display. GK doesn't hide the pyrotechnics, but the staff is so pleasant and competent that you feel that you're an integral a part of the process rather than an onlooker. After a meal at GK, guests leave feeling just a little more sophisticated, well dressed and smart than they did when they came in. 

The food is wonderful. A lamb dish I had at lunch was the most memorable I have had in years, and took me back to one that Daniel Humm did years ago at the original 11MP (unfortunately, it's no longer on the menu). Foie gras is treated with the respect it deserves, with a terrine that is brilliant. My wife concluded that her roasted scallop dish was the best presentation of scallops she's had in years, if not ever. The quail, pork and duck were all wonderful. 

The wine list is also great. It includes the great names and vintages you would expect of a top-end NYC restaurant, but also a surprisingly large number of well priced wines from less well known regions and producers. The sommelier is incredibly helpful, and clearly loves her job. Her enthusiasm in figuring out what to recommend is quite infectious.

I am so happy we have this wonderful restaurant in NYC. GK re-establishes NYC as one of the finest food towns in the world.

Had a phenomenal lunch at the Bar. For my appetiser, the tarte flambé is an absolute delight that perfectly balances the richer flavours with the lighter notes. The main course of grilled sea bass is unexpectedly juxtaposed with barley, forming a surprisingly harmonious union in my mouth. 

But the best part of my lunch is the dessert. The Grand Marnier Baba is refreshing and just the right amount of sweetness. The surrounding citrus notes, combined with a rich Baba and vanilla ice cream, resoundingly confirm why this place is superior to the Modern.

The best of American service and French technique. Everything is amazing. The desserts and the chocolates are of great quality and the perfect level of sweetness. The execution is as good as the best pastry shops in Paris. The staff is very helpful, professional, and friendly.

This is a review for the bar.

I had to try this place after finding out he left the modern to start his own restaurant, but procrastinated enough so that I got to try this place after the bar was opened.  The structure is very similar to what the Modern offered.  Dining room offering 4 course prix fixe and tasting menu whereas bar offers a la carte menu.  The interior structure was built in which you can see the dining room from the bar very well.  

We ordered a cocktail/mocktail and then had appetizer, entree with dessert to share.  I thought my sausage (liverwurst) was very well made and cooked.  Thought flat iron steak was adequately cooked with nice sauce to embellish the flavor.

Overall I thought it was a good experience and it would be worth trying the dining room in the future.

Just had a $115 prefix three course dinner with my sister tonight. Quite mediocre. Nothing special. Very pricey for the food. Because I had had an excellent experience with their lunch before, I am very disappointed this time. Wine and service was good. So 2 stars.
I was only here for drinks one night but found the place to be sterile. I also found it hard to understand what the bartenders were saying. Very heavy accents

Came here for lunch one day with the wife when we had the day off. They offer two savory course for $58 and we also ordered the wild American sturgeon caviar.

The service was great and decor

Came here for the bar lunch pre fixed menu.  It was a good meal.  The lobster stew as as an app was only okay.  A little salty with no payoff from that and not flavorful.  The trout was delicious. Well-cooked, seasoned and had interesting flavors to it.  The shitshito peppers were spicy and better cooked than other places (it's a common app now).  If you want dessert, head next door to his chocolate shop if you don't want dessert at the bar.  Cocktail was not worth it--boring even though the description seemed interesting.  Very good service.

Gabriel Kreuther's fairly new eponymous restaurant is a winner!  My husband, an old friend and I had the two course prix fixe lunch in the dining room today and the meal was outstanding.  From the amuse , the foie gras poached in gewirtztraminer and the sable and sauerkraut, the quail, the pork and the absolutely divine scallops in chorizo foam (who knew), the meal was beautifully presented and served with the utmost professionalism of a kind I haven't experienced in a long time. The sommelier was a young, knowledgeable professional who, in the absence of a desired red alto adige, suggested a terrific and well-priced substitute  from west of the A.A. in a similarly mountainous region of Italy to the south of Switzerland.  So many of these high end restaurants are tired.  This is definitely not one of them

Ok....This is not a normal rating for me as I tend to not offer 5 Stars.  Nor is this the type of "hearty" food I usually eat- pizza, hamburger, etc. 
I have eaten at the restaurant twice and find that it is always excellent.  Today we did the 2 course Prix Fixe and all 4 courses were excellent. 
As usual they brought out a Chef's selection bite to start and then added a small course in between the two selections. 
Well done again.

Hands down some of the best food I've eaten recently. 

My girlfriend and I did the chef's tasting menu (carte blanche) to celebrate our anniversary. The food and service were phenomenal. The foie gras terrine, langoustine tartare and veal dumplings were particular standouts...

From start to finish, every aspect of our meal was memorable. Well worth the money.

This is absolutely one of the most inventive meals I have ever had. Flawless service, amazing and incredibly creative cuisine, and like nothing else I have tasted. It wasn't too precious and every dish had something I ACTUALLY wanted to eat. Also foie gras in 2 out of 4 courses which made me a happy girl. A great value at $120 per person. We came here on an absolute whim on a Thursday night and really can't wait to return the next time that we are in the city!

Had cocktails and dinner here last night and found everything about it to be superb!  The service, staff, and food all exceeded my expectations.   Cocktails were on point, wine selection was extensive, and dinner was perfect.  Couldn't have had a better evening.  The manager, Sam Willy was very helpful and friendly and checked on us several times to make sure we were satisfied with everything.

Had an amazing dinner last Wednesday evening, January 18, 2017!
As fans of the Modern, we were happy to follow Chef Gabriel to his new restaurant and it was well worth the trip. 
We don't get to NYC too often so we were looking for something special and we found it.
Drinks at the bar-Thanks Katy and dinner in the gorgeous dining room.
Staff is fabulous and the sommelier, Kelly, was delightful.
I am still dreaming of dinner.
Thanks for making everything a night to remember.

Thank you for not kicking me out for being the only person in the whole restaurant for dinner who's not in a suit or formal wear. I apologies for coming in sweats and a sports jacket. My girlfriend and I came here for dinner but prior we were exploring the depths of New York so I was a bit under dressed. And thank you for having portable chargers for my phone! Saved my life in the world where technology is key and people cannot live without their phones. 

We sat in front of the kitchen where we watched the line chefs to magic and as well watch this empty table for VIP guests only be empty. We saw a couple sit down for all about 5-10 minutes, sipped on a glass of wine and then left. Seems like something the rich and famous would do, except we don't know who they are. We did however, spot Mr. Kreuther a few times in the kitchen! 

The food was tremendously good and the service was perfect. I think we'd come back if we had the chance. New York never disappoints. Great experience, great service, great food, i'll be back!

I'd been excited to go to Gabriel Kreuther since I read about its opening, but I only finally made it for an early birthday dinner with my wife this past week. The entrance is a bit innocuous (the chocolate store, with the chocolates being prepared at the window, certainly is more noticeable), but once you step inside, you forget you were just on 42nd Street heading towards Times Square and step into a wonderfully expansive space. With high ceilings, a well-stocked bar, and a main dining area that is separated by support beams that don't totally silo off the room from the bar at all, it has a very accessible and laid-back feel, despite the high-class nature of the food. While we had a variety of waiters serving us, our main waiter was really friendly, taking time to explain the dishes, soliciting our opinion of our food, and even asking us where the best soup dumplings in town were (a bit of a random divergence in conversation). The drink menu is solid, with good cocktails and an interesting beer menu (I had a smoked doppelbock - a complex beer that was a bit heavier but worked well towards the end of the meal).

The food here is a choice between a prix fixe 4-course dinner for $142, or the tasting at $215 - so you will definitely be opening your wallet no matter what. We went for more variety and settled on the chef's tasting, which turned out to be the right choice. My wife and I got a couple different courses along the way, allowing us to sample from a wider choice; the really nice gesture was comping us a course that charged a supplement - something that I don't think I have had anywhere else. We started out with a few unique bites, with the gelatinous 'Martini' standing out - very lightly alcoholic, but a very refreshing finish to help cleanse the palate for the meal ahead. I also very much enjoyed the thinly-sliced tuna, which was topped a healthy amount of herbs, giving each silky bite a lively taste. We then went on to the foie gras, served up as a terrine and coated in a black truffle praline...pure earthy, creamy decadence with each bite. I really liked the lightly-toasted cubes of seven grain bread, which paired very well with the rustic truffle flavoring of the dish. To finish off our initial courses, I had the striped marlin - a delicious fish, with the Hawaiian roots coming out with the sweetened macadamia-infused wafer on top. The langoustine tartare, though, is to die for - it's as fresh as any shrimp served at a sushi store, with the roe adding bursts of crunchy saltiness to the smooth, refreshing bite of each piece.

We moved on to the second course dishes, and the tart was a fantastic dish to start off on. I've never been big on sauerkraut, but the faint vinegary flavor really worked well with the egg and the dollop of caviar served on top, and the hint of smokiness gave it a very homey taste. These were followed up by a succulent veal dumpling, served in a rich consomme and topped with some shaved truffle (on the house - it wasn't part of the dish) - a perfect dish for a winter tasting menu. We then diverged again, with my wife getting the grilled lobster, while I was served the roasted scallops. The scallops were absolutely amazing - cooked perfectly, but with a fizzy emulsion of chorizo(!) topping it, giving it a very airy spice that really worked well with the kohlrabi-infused sauce the scallops were served in. The lobster was perfectly succulent, with a lighter coconut sauce serving as the base and giving the dish a bit of a tropical feel. Next up was seared foie served in chartreuse and poached in Gewurtztraminer - a slightly tipsy but heavily fruit-infused way of serving this iteration of foie gras - and definitely one of the better preparations I have had. Our mains were concluded with the amazing rack of lamb - such rich flavor smoked into each bite, and the jus really capturing the smoky flavor of the preparation.

The desserts were generally on the lighter side; we started with a very light coconut panna cotta with lime foam, clearing the way for the rest of the sweet dishes. This was followed by a pear jelly and sorbet served with a couple large pieces of gingersnap cookies wafers shaped like a moon - a mellow outing that wasn't the best dessert I had had, but one with a very pleasing aesthetic to finish dinner late at night. The creme brulee 'shot' was excellent, especially with the rich jelly/puree at the bottom filling up the airiness of the puffed-up frappe. To finish it off, we were served with a few chocolates, served in a cracked-open cacao bean - from the chocolate shop - an excellent sample of the delicious bites prepared next door.

With a phenomenal space and even better food, this is definitely one of the better dining experiences in NYC. The cost makes it a bit more prohibitive relative to other favorites I have in town, but it's worth the visit for a special occasion or for a bite in the bar space...a very cosmopolitan, delicious take on modern American dining.
Great experience dining for lunch and the food was amazing. Would strongly recommend this restaurant for lunch and you should definitely try their dessert!

What an amazing restaurant. 
We had the Carte Blanche (Tasting Menu) and it was worth every penny.  The chef does an incredible job at combining and bringing out the flavors of ingredients he uses while making them look like beautiful art work. 
Service was first class as well. One of the best meals I've ever had.  It was a magical evening!

This place is beautiful! The service, the decor and the food are just amazing. 

The service is top notch! They have a price fix price for a 4 course plus dessert or another of 7-10 course meal. Now when you see the food, you may think it's beautiful but I will not get full. However, they bring out a ore appetizer, a different bread after every course and everything tastes amazing! 
Did I say amazing? Yes absolutely amazing. 

The chef has played he has made himself and the cacao pods he has also made and serves chocolate in there after dessert. I felt so bad not being able to eat everything on my plate, but I wanted to try the next thing that was to come. 

It's an experience you should try. We paired our meal with a nice wine. They have quite an extensive list to pick from.  

If you are in NYC. Make a reservation here. It really was excellent and every single person working there was so nice!
