Stunning meal. I actual had a reservation at Noma in Copenhagen but decided it was too far a trip for a meal. But with a friend in NY that same day we decided to splurge and go to Gabriel Kreuther for dinner. We weren't disappointed. 

We did the Chef's Choice. A multi-course meal that was truly excellent. I think this place is underrated. Thought it's not cheap. The service was impeccable. The dining room is modern, white, and beautifully decorated. The kitchen is partially open so you can see the chefs at work. 

Highlights were the langoustine, marlin, lobster, truffle veal dumpling, blood sausage. Topped off with the aptly named Decadence, chocolate mousse. Everything was beautifully done and flavorful but not overly so. 

Dinner is a splurge but lunch in the main room or lounge are good deals. 
Highly recommend

Race segregated seating. I was there on Valentine's Day and was seated on the lower level. It turned out that the ground level was white people only. If you stops by you can take a look through the window, obviously there are no other races seated on the ground level at all.

Came here around 6 with a reservation on Lincoln's day (nice that it is open on a holiday)! The staff were accommodating and nice, they even gave us a portable charger because our phones were dying. The interior is also very beautiful -- elegant without being overly pretentious. The dress code is also nice because it means I get to dress up but not too dressed up where I become a human popsicle in NY's cruel weather. Ok sorry I got a bit carried away. 

I'll talk about what is important -- the food.
We had the four course meal, which included palate cleansers and a new type of bread and butter/spread in between. Every dish had beautiful presentations. For the first course, I got the foie gras terrine while my date got the langoustine tartare. It's my first time ever eating foie gras because I had always been afraid of it being too gamy, but I gave in to the power of the yelpers. What can I say? I was so glad because it was freaking delicious - the granola with the terrine had a nice contrast and flavor. My date's dish was just okay, nothing spectacular to me but he liked it. Second course I really wanted to try the infamous sturgeon and sauerkraut tart but my love for potatoes made me get the Yukon potato soup; which was great with an explosion of flavors and textures. My date got the poached foie gras, it's nice but after a while it can become overwhelming. Luckily they gave us so much bread that he was able to spread the foie gras and enjoy it that way. Third course, I got the pork tenderloin and yes they put the tender in loin because it was delicious and juicy. My date got the lobster which was also yummy, I wanted to steal his dish. Lastly, the dessert. I got the mango almond and he got the apple cassis. Both were amazingly balanced with the sweet and sour flavors, which was nice after the meal. Then they came out with the cocoa pod, which was so cute. I took like 800 photos. But the chocolates were overwhelmingly sweet for us (with enough water, it was nice). 

Wow I wrote at least 300 words explaining how nice this place is! Yay!

Came here for a Valentines day reservation.  The location of the restaurant is right across the street from Bryant park and the interior is beautiful!! 

However.   We got seated downstairs. The downstairs area looks like a bland catering hall. White walls. Corny paintings on the walls.  A stuffy, boring basement.   Completely ruined the ambience....  

The cocktails were amazing.  I usually drink wine or beer but my hubby and i tried their specialty cocktails and they were amazing....well for $35/ glass....they better be.  
The food was good.

The service waa really below average.
We had at least 7-10 people bring and take away dishea from the table.  

One random guy walked by, askes my husband how his drink was and without waiting for an answer, took, it away.  There was still 1/4 left!

One of the dishes that was brought to us was not explained at all.  The servers brought it, poured the soup over and left!!!  ....i think thats part of the experience !

In between meals, we were supposed to get a palate cleanser...fun bread and butter, etc.  Well, between 2 courses, they forgot to bring us one.  The tables to our right and left had a long bread that we didnt get.  And besidea thia, everyone was getting the same thing because it is a fixed menu.

The food was good.  But eating quietly in a basement with impersonal service....will not pay $$$$ for ever again.

We came for Valentine's dinner which was a prix fixe. The meal was excellent and the setting in the heart of Times Square was perfect. You cannot tell where you are during dinner as the space and windows block out the noise. Service was good and the food was cooked perfectly. They have farmed caviar, which didn't have the same saltiness of caviar from Russia but it was good with the cracker & buttermilk cream that they provided. There is also a chocolate shop next to the restaurant, which is worth a visit either before or after dinner.

We ate in the bar area on a weeknight. Super busy so I was glad we made a reservation. Incredible food and service. The dumplings were one of my favorite dishes. Plus the wine list was never ending - great selection. Will need to go back to try the other dishes.

Superb. Truly great restaurant. Gorgeous dining room, striking art and floral arrangements. Dish after dish of delicious culinary art, served by attentive non intrusive staff on dishware also highly imagined. Zagat has this as #7 on their top restaurants in NYC, for many excellent reasons.

Dining here ended up going not as planned but can say that the staff was extremely professional and accommodating.

Was going to dine here with the wife but she ended up coming down with a bug.  Showed up to the restaurant at the scheduled reservation.  The staff didn't blink, quickly adjusted the place settings for only 1 and seated me immediately.  There were no questions asked, no attempt to push me to the bar to dine instead of the dining room.

As for the meal it was excellent.  The sturgeon tart and the decadent dessert were real standouts.  Love the time and care that goes into the bread courses and that they have one in between every savory course.  The only criticism is that one of the courses just did not agree with me.  The hamachi/foie gras course just did not work for me.  There wasn't enough acid to cut the richness of the foie and just overwhelmed the hamachi.  Otherwise enjoyed everything I ate.

I hope that I get a chance to come back here with the wife and we both get to experience the goodness Chef Kreuther has been serving.

Wow. Worth every penny and every calorie! Was not expecting a prix fixe menu but the options were very unique and enticing. Be prepared for a delightful gastronomic experience. Thoroughly enjoyed the smoked eel carbonara (couldn't really taste the eel in the sauce but got the smoky flavor and the squid ink mini gnocchis were flavorful with a good bite for the texture), the Nova Scotia halibut was fantastic (mushrooms were very good with it but sauce was a bit heavy for me) and I enjoyed tasting my friend's duck breast and foie gras appetizer (really one of the best I have ever had). My hamachi/foie gras appetizer was likely the least liked but the additional amuse bouche and rosemary rolls and baguette wirh pork lard and butter made up for it. 

Dessert also was mind-blowingly delectable. Go big with the chocolate options - whether the milk chocolate or dark chocolate! Beautifully presented food with a lot of flavors. Edible art that brings a flavor explosion in your mouth. 

Decor was classic and elegant but still warm and not pretentious. Service was impeccable. Definitely worth coming, especially for a special occasion!

Had dinner at the bar/lounge. Service was good. Food was solid, although nothing extraordinary. The steak and cavatelli were both fine. The chocolate tart was the best part of the meal. 

However, I'm only giving 3* because of the foie gras appetizer. The cost of the appetizer ($39) was absurd given the minuscule amount of foie that was served. When they brought the dish to the table I thought I was being robbed. I know foie gras is expensive but this was ridiculous - you can get much larger portions at a lower price point and that taste better at many fine dining restaurants across the city.

Excellent food with very good attention to detail. I enjoyed every single bite of the prix fix menu. Staff was friendly and attentive Wylie every need without being pushy.  Fantastic wine list. Watch out as this place is expensive. Would go back

Food was amazing! I loved everything I got and it's definitely worth your money. If you look at the pictures, you'll realize that everything is pretty small-portioned. But you still walk out suuuper full. On top of whatever you ordered, they also give you some extra amuse-bouche and desserts. I took my chocolates to go cause I was so full... :3

I think my favorites of the night were the Langoustine Tartare, White Truffle Shaved Over Spaetzle (I'm a white truffle fanatic), and the Yukon Potato-Rosemary Soup. Probably will never forget those dishes. Ever. The Nova Scotia Halibut was cooked perfectly. The Comfort Caramel Pear Dessert was yummy and had a BEAUTIFUL presentation. 

I think the only thing that didn't work out for me (my own fault really because I didn't realize it) was that everything I ordered was creamy. I got the Langoustine Tartare (less creamy), Yukon Potato-Rosemary Soup, White Truffle Shaved Over Spaetzle, and the Nova Scotia Halibut. So towards the end of my meal, I was a bit overwhelmed by the creamy taste. And yet, after every dish I kept repeating "oh. my. god."

*Advice: I know the Savory Scallion Kougelhopf (bread) is yummy, but don't order more. My boyfriend and I loved it and made the mistake of ordering another one. Little did we know that they give you another set of different breads as you work through your meal, and you really don't need the extra order because you become so full at the end. 

Service was top-notch. Absolutely no complains. Our waiter was very accommodating and he explained all of our dishes really well. Not to mention he professionally answered our numerous questions with absolute patience. Wonderful! 

Interior is fantastically elegant. A beautiful blend of white, gold, & grey. I'm also a big fan of how the restaurant is well lit because I despise super dark restaurants. Just being in the restaurant made me happy. I'll definitely be back. Probably not soon because $$$$, but I will eventually come back!
My favorite spot , been here a few times, will back soon. Also the bar I visited a lot . Love the wine ... and the chocolate next the door .. made by hand .... delicious

One of the best meals that I have ever had. Came during lunch with a couple co-workers. We had the option to sit in the bar dining room or the fine dining room - we went with the fine dining option but the open space bar room was just as nice.

To start off with, they provided this soft bread with green seasoned butter, which was so good. The butter was very light and melted right away into the bread. They then provided us with complimentary amuse-bouche with three different items including fish, bread tart and this matcha jelly. They were small pieces but each one was delicious and unique! They definitely didn't skimp out on the creativity here.

For my starting course, I got the blue shrimp tartar, which was the last they had for the day. I can see why - this dish was surprisingly good! I was a little disappointed at first when I couldn't even see the tartar but then i realized that the tartar was stuffed in the mini lettuce / brussel sprouts. It was definitely a unique way to do it. The dish itself was light and refreshing but still very flavorful. It was a great way to start of the first course.

The main course came out immediately after we had all finished the first course. I got the roasted duck which came with a side of some kind of vegetable medley with some crunchy pieces on top. They also poured the sauce on the duck out of a small pot at the table, making the presentation overall very cool.

We finished off with desserts and i ordered the lambent which was this milk chocolate mousse with a sweet graham cracker like bottom. It also had pieces of milk chocolate and citrus flavored sauce, actual citrus and sherbert. The dessert had a very unique presentation and tasted amazing.

Finally to top it all off, they gave us complimentary Gabriel Kreuther chocolates - one with cinnamon and one with vanilla. They were both great but by that time, we were already beyond stuffed.

Other than the amazing food, the architecture and interior design of the space was beautiful  and there was no bad spot to be seated at. Their cutlery, plates and bowls were also very unique and different than anything that i've ever seen before at other places.

Celebrated my boyfriends birthday here and absolutely loved it. We had dinner fairly early at 6PM so when we first arrived the restaurant was pretty empty. 20 minutes in, it got pretty full and the ambience was perfect.

One negative prior to the start of dinner was that we didn't receive any hand towelettes so I had to go to the bathroom to wash my hands.

We all ordered the 4 course pre fix and all the dishes were beautiful just like art. We also had a complimentary appetizer. Before and after each meal, different types of breads were placed on the table. All very yummy. The portions were tiny but very filling. 

Dessert prettty much topped all the meals put together and were absolutely delicious. All the desserts were amazing. 

What topped everything else was the service. Never had better service anywhere else. Will love to come back for some more dessert !

Given it was half empty, service was poor. We arrived at 5:30 and asked to be done by 7:30. We had to beg to get our order taken - and no, we did not get the check until 7:45. The decor/ambiance was nice but not exceptional. As for the food - pick wisely and there are 5 star choices. The baked Dorade Royal is superb - the flesh is moist, almost silken. The foam packs a lot of flavor. The dish looks a bit blah but trust me, it tastes great. The foie gras terrine starter is rich and unusual. The famous sturgeon/sauerkraut tart was ok, I don't get the hype. The eel carbonara was deeply flavored but a bit disappointing - there are no pieces of eel - just eel flavoring in the sauce.( Honestly, the descriptions of the food can be misleading.)

Disappointments: the desserts! We got the pear caramel and the apple crisp and both tasted like nothing - except for the tiny excellent scoop of fruit sorbet. The pear was hard and the other ingredients were crispy - so it was impossible to put them together for one bite. It was like nibbling a sweet cracker and then nibbling some hard pear. Too deconstructed. I thought the apple crisp was similarly spectacular looking and meh tasting - though my dh liked it. The duck breast was also subpar - it was undercooked and tough. I like medium rare duck - this was barely cooked. I would have returned it but we were running late.

This is the kind of place I would enjoy if I wasn't paying for it. If I have to spend my own money - there are other much classier and consistent restaurants in New York. Jean-George V. has nothing to worry about!

Wonderful experience, excellent food.

Brought our 15 mo old and they were fantastic.  Maitre'd saw me entertaining my toddler counting herons and invited us for a tour of the kitchen.  Was honored to meet the executive chef and see the back room.  

I have a gluten allergy and they were very helpful and easily accommodated.

Dishes were delicious!
Noisy bar and "flamed" my orange zest oil with a bic lighter..."classy", right?
Wowza.   Impeccable service and food experience.  I brought my little food judges with me and they loved the wagyu beef, himachi, lobster and foie gras.
Love this place for elegant meals in the dining room or a nice business lunch in the bar.  Reggie at the front is great. Food is refined and delicious. A worthy treat!

Got a table for 4 so we were able to try most of the dishes.  

Here are the winning dishes for each course:
1st course - Foie Gras Terrine & Marcona Almond Praline
2nd course - Smoked Eel Carbonara
3rd course - Long Island Crescent Duck Breast

While we thought the dinner was good, we were not impressed.  However, all the desserts we ordered were amazing!  That was what we all walked away raving about.  

The décor is modern, simple, chic and welcoming.  However when I looked around the room, there is just one wall that did not fit the room.  It looks like Grandma's wallpaper.

Gabriel Kreuther is a delightful place, with its subdued and unusual elegance, and the attentive, unobtrusive service offered. The wine list is extensive, with - no surprise there - some very interesting Pinot Noirs from the Alsace. The menu was balanced; my husband started with a lovely tartare of langoustine, whilst I had delicious smoked striped marlin. The main course was also excellent: a juicy an perfectly cooked duck breast and a very good halibut. The disappointment was the foie gras; firstly, the portion was hardly larger than a sample; secondly, the acidity of the kumquat completely dominated the delicate smoothness of the liver. A pity, as this was the only flaw in an otherwise lovely dining experience.

Food was good, however service was excellent. 

Came to eat post graduation and was welcomed with a personalized menu along with a complimentary dessert. Appetizers were fairly good (I had the langoustine tartare). Entree (Duck) was good, but not anything special. What truly shined was the dessert (wild strawberry fromage), it was incredibly delicious and threw me back to eating strawberries in Paris. 

All in all, a good meal.

If I could give this restaurant 6/5 stars, I would. It honestly was one of the best dining experiences of my entire life. From the amuse-bouche, entre-courses, and attentive and helpful service we received, I enjoyed every minute of my dinner. They beautifully blended innovative culinary creations with classic food combinations in a wholly satisfying manner. The food is also plentiful--I could not have finished my meal without my boyfriend's help! It was truly a highlight of my time in New York.

Recommended courses:
-Of the second courses, the asparagus is a truly special standout
-Of the desserts, both the "decadent" and "awakening" were sinfully delicious

Today was my 3rd visit to Gabriel Kreuther. The previous two times that I've dined there, I've been impressed with the food. I dined at the bar and had 2 courses + dessert. I was really unimpressed with the tarte flambee. It was soggy and tasted average. Really enjoyed the chocolate tart though.

4 stars.  I have mixed feelings about this place.  I've been a couple times for lunch, most recently this summer and haven't decided whether it's somewhere I like enough to keep coming back.

The service is wonderful, everyone is nice and attentive.  They try to set everyone's plates down at the same time, but sometimes they mess up the timing, so if they're going to go for that, they should nail it down better.

This most recent time, we told the server that one of us was in a rush and needed to finish her meal, and they were very accommodating to this request, and brought things out for her faster than the rest of us so she could leave.

We received an amouse bouche, which was very tasty.  I think it was sweet corn marmalade with caramelized plantain hummus. 

For my appetizer I ordered the Foie Gras Terrine & Marcona Almond Praline.  Thought this was delicious, and though it had crunch from the almond crunch, I wish they gave some bread to spread the foie gras on.

For the main course, I ordered the Roasted Crescent Duck Breast, which was a HUGE portion, they give you two pieces of duck breast.  I thought the duck was a little over cooked for my taste of medium rare, and the crust was a little flaky/fell off, but the flavors were there.

We skipped dessert, because we were full and also were trying to wrap up our meal since we were tight on time.  The lunch tasting menu price is reasonable for the portion sizes and is comparable to others in this league.

Solid Five-Star. One of my favorite French restaurant in the city. My friend and I went there for lunch, which is a delicious while worthy experience. 

We both ordered the well-renowned Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart, the combination of American Caviar with applewood smoke, so soft! I like it so much that I even want to reorder again. For the main course, I ordered the Roasted Red Snapper. With its delicate design and well-cooked snapper, I would say it's one of the best red snapper I've ever had. For dessert, I had the Mandarin Milk Chocolate. It looks pretty, first. It tastes amazing, second. I don't like something too sweet, but dessert at GK was just perfect regards sweetness and portion. 

I would highly recommend this place, especially with its lunch, affordable while in high quality.

Possibly the best meal I have had in years!  Pictured are the green salad, white asparagus second course, Halibut, chocolates to end off the evening.  This is a wow dinner.  If you want to impress your tastebuds, dine here.  If you want to wow friends, family or clients, dine here!!!

Items Selected:
Granny Smith - Red Delicious Apple, Blueberry
Kugelhopf - Chive Fromage Blanc
Mango-Jalapeno Pate de Fruit - Masa Cracker, Corn Puree, Tomatillo, Avocado, Pickled Onion
Fried Plantain - Shiso Leaf
Foie Gras Terrine & Marcona Almond Praline - Smoked Pear, Cider Gelee, Five Spice Granola
Red Wine Braised Tripe Gratine - Du Puy Lentils, Thyme
Filone - Cultured Butter
Roasted Crescent Duck Breast - Black Trumpet Crust, Fleischnacka, Ginger Jus

Answering several questions about the sustaining appeal of Fine Dining in an era of 'hip' eateries serving share plates, Gabriel Kreuther opened in 2016 to great acclaim from critics and fans of the Chef during his days at The Modern, the eponymous restaurant immediately climbing to the top of a Big Apple Bucket List thanks to previous memorable afternoons dining in the shadows of MoMA.

Located at 41 West 42nd Street, a sizable footprint with both Bar and "Main Dining" menus much like that at The Modern, Garbriel Kreuther is best described as Alsace by way of New York both in terms of its offerings and a flowing space backed by a beautiful display kitchen, the walls adorned with art and beams supporting high ceilings - every bit a 'white linen' restaurant, yet at the same time young and vibrant.

Long considered one of New York's most admirable toques, Michelin Stars following him from kitchen to kitchen since his days at Jean Georges and L'Atelier, Chef Kreuther's first foray as Chef and Proprietor sees him joined by many staff members from his previous stint, the midday Manager on duty a youthful woman who stated that she had been with Kreuther for almost ten years while another server had also migrated over from the Modern along with Marc Aumont who remains one of Manhattan's top pastry talents while pulling double duty at the Restaurant and Kreuther Handcrafted Chocolate next door.  

Open six days a week for Dinner, Monday through Friday for a slightly truncated Lunch menu, it was having spoken to the restaurant in advance regarding the addition of Bar items to the $29 per plate Prix-Fixe that seating was offered along a lengthy banquet just two-tables away from Hollywood royalty, the service ever gracious for both he and everyone around him with as a savory Kugelhopf arrived even before an order was placed, the springy Bread excellent on its own and better with spreadable Chive Fromage Blanc.

Porting over some ideas from The Modern, though Kreuther's unique marriage of Continental Cuisine with Fusion is a fairly recognizable style that yields beautiful plates that remain accessible, it was with a non-alcoholic beverage of roasted Red Delicious apples and Blueberry that a pair of nibbles arrived, the Fried Plantain wrapped in a raw Shiso Leaf dynamic, if not a bit sweet, while the spicy Pate de Fruit topped by a Crisp with Corn, Avocado and Onion seemed oddly Mexican for a man from Southern France operating in Midtown Manhattan.

Always offering both hot and cold preparations of Duck Liver, and at this point actually four different dishes when accounting for both the Bar and Main Dining menus, late-Spring sees Kreuther's Foie Gras 'Praline' served after a roll in crushed Marcona Almonds atop Smoked Pear and Five Spice Granola, the flavors and textures both wide-ranging and well thought out with no additional Bread required for spreading the Terrine.

Turning to the Bar for course two, the menu there largely Alsatian with items like Liverwurst, Veal Dumplings and Flammekuech taking center stage, it was shortly after finishing the Foie Gras that a steamy bowl of Tripe arrived with Lentils Du Puy forming a thick and comforting Stew along with two types of Beans, both this dish and a follow-up of Duck Breast in a Mushroom Crust taking rustic ideas and spinning them elegant - the latter going so far as to pair the roasted Fowl with a classic French Pastry Snail filled with Forcemeat.

Unable to resist such good Bread, both the Kugelhopf and Filone with Cultured Butter mostly gone along with all of the toasted Baguette used for sopping up the Red Wine broth from the Tripe, it was with the Grand Marnier Baba from the Bar acting as a palate cleanser that the meal was placed in Chef Aumont's hands, the Fresh Mango and Vanilla Ice Cream deliciously hidden beneath a cloud of Milk while "Lambent, Mandarin Milk Chocolate" proved that Citrus and Cocoa can work beautifully when made with skill and subtlety, the crunchy Peanut Butter base and crumbled Pistachios beneath Orange Sorbet foreshadowing Mignardises including classic Financiers, a half-Macaron shaped Roasted Pineapple Chocolate and crunchy Praline.

While this hot, relatively new spot on the north side of Bryant Park is on my list to check out, the tab to eat here runs just a bit higher than I aim to spend on dinner, even the appetizer crawling sort for the most part. But, throwing a touch of caution to the wind, I joined my friend John at the bar for a couple of "adult beverages" before heading on to meet other friends for dinner. We had to at least try one of the more reasonably priced bar menu items (it's telling that the bar is packed with people having bar food ($18-39/item) and cocktails ($19-45 each), but the dining room virtually empty (where dinner runs either $142 or $215 for the two menu choices, without beverages). The classic Alsatian tarte flambe is plenty delicious, even if it is the least expensive item on the menu. I'd happily eat it again, though I'd probably go elsewhere for good pizza instead.

This restaurant is so damn good! My friend and I got the two course meal for $58. I had the sturgeon & sauerkraut tart and it did not disappoint. I normally do not like sauerkraut but this tastes so good! For the main, I ordered the Grilled Black Angus Beef Tenderloin and my friend had the Berkshire Pork Tenderloin. Both were so well plated and melted in our mouths. I preferred the pork tenderloin but both were so delicious! We also ordered the ambrosial mango almond and lambent mandarin milk chocolate for dessert and they did not disappoint either! Perfect way to end the meal. On top of that, the service was impeccable.

Whether this is your first foray into fine dining or you're a seasoned veteran, GK will not disappoint. I've had nearly everything on the menu, both main dining and bar, and am yet to find something I don't like. It's not cheap, but it's worth every penny. An unpretentious staff is more than happy to assist win any request, and seems to know what you need before you even ask. Don't leave without trying one of the specialty cocktails either!
Snacks were amazing, appetizer and entree were quite greasy for me, probably because I ordered foie gras... maybe that was a wrong decision. Will order something light if I come back again.

What a treat! The sturgeon and sauerkraut tart was innovative and delicious! Another appetizer we had was the foie gras which had a cherry compote, almond covered the ingredients matched perfectly.
For the main course we both had the tenderloin, it was like butter!
We ordered a rose champagne , le caravelle, reasonably priced and was balanced well.
Desserts were good , their chocolate is great.
Service was excellent.
This will be one of my favorite restaurants now.

Simply amazing experience that relies on good flavor and drinks to tell a culinary story. Their drinks were deceptively smooth and strong and the tasting menu was the best food I've ever eaten. I'll definitely be going back when I'm back in NYC.

Came here for a business lunch, and the lunch prix fix menu has very good value. I got seared foie gras for first course and diver scallop for the second. The group also ordered two desserts to share. The apple slices on the foie gras balances the greasiness and make a good combined taste. The diver scallop is accompanied by some bacon-flavored ingredient which makes the seafood more sophisticated. Two types of bread were served and both are good. Another thing worth noting is that the restaurant is very generous with complimentary dishes, we got two complimentary appetizers and two complimentary small-bite desserts, which are all somewhat innovative and very different from one another.
Consistently wonderful.  The food is very creative, good portions, fabulous presentation.  The service is always on point.  The price point is reasonable for what you get.

NY has a slew of amazing dining options and Gabriel Kreuther certainly ranks high on that list. The decor is not too ostentatious, the food is exquisite and Luis, along with the rest of the staff knows how to take great care of their patrons.
As soon as you are seated, you are promptly greeted and provided a wine and cocktail list. Not that this is out of the ordinary, but what is is that the cocktail list goes into the history of Bryant Park while providing interesting descriptions of cocktails that would have been available during that time period, but with modern ingredients added. The wine list was also exceptional and includes a few wines from France which I do not know a lot about, so I was grateful to the sommelier for patiently explaining and recommending a bordeaux that met my needs.
As mentioned by other Yelpers, they are very generous with complimentary bites to accompany your prix fixe dinner. I was completely stuffed by the time I left!
For the amuse bouche, they bring several options to include this wonderful bread with a cheese/butter spread. 
For my meal, I chose:
-Hamachi, black truffle & foie gras mille-feuille
-Seared sullivan county foie gras
-Grilled main lobster
-Decadent chocolate caramel

Each dish was aesthetically pleasing and just as delicious as their presentation. Throughout my meal, Luis also brought me some french bread and rosemary rolls. Both breads were very soft and warm accompanied by their own spreads. Also, after dessert, I was provided more complimentary dessert! Four pieces of their incredible house made chocolate and two coated bread sticks. The price is so reasonable and for the amount of food and service you receive, I would bet that Gabriel Kreuther would be hard to beat. I will be recommending this establishment to all of my friends and I cannot wait to come back when the menu changes to see what other delectable delights are in store.

Went here today for a special dinner with a friend - what a mistake! Overprice, over pretentious food that no longer even a hint of joy left in it.  The wine list has more $500 and up bottles on it than I think I have ever seen - and it is not that extensive...  if you want to impress your dinner date with the size of the bill and nothing else - this is the place.
Excellent service and great food! Try not to eat too much bread so that you can enjoy the food. We took home the chocolate they gave us at the end and it was delicious.

Absolutely fabulous! This was my first experience going to a Michelin Star restaurant and I wasn't disappointed. The space was so beautiful and felt like I was in a different world. The temperature of the room was perfect; not too cold and not too warm. My coworkers and I went here for lunch and were graciously met by our server who was in a pristine looking suit and tie. He was very accommodating, gave great recommendations and answered all of our questions (and we had a lot). He was very patient and always had a smile on his face.

There was a whole book of drinks that included the history of Bryant Park which was interesting to read about. I don't want to call it bread because it does not do it justice, but we were given a bread like starter with the most amazing green colored spread. I cannot tell you what it was, but I can tell you I can eat that for the rest of my life and be happy. We then were given an amuse bouche of four items. One was a cantaloupe shooter, a chip that tasted similar to a shrimp chip, a melon gelatin bite, and I forgot what the last one was called but it was a small ball completely packed with flavor on a small fracker. I didn't know such a small item can taste so much and well for that matter.

For an appetizer I got the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart. OH EM GEE. That was incredible, I highly recommend it. Part of the tart that is listed on the menu is applewood smoke. The course comes out in a glass dome and the server takes it off and swirls the smoke around in front of you. It was quite an experience. For my main course I got the Spice Roasted Dover Scallops. I have never tasted scallops done so well in my entire life. The lunch meal was a prix fixe for $58, which isn't bad compared to other Michelin star places, and the meal lasted about an hour and a half to two hours.

I was nervous that the smaller portions would leave me hungry, but that was far from the case. I was pleasantly full without feeling like I over ate. It was the ideal amount of food.

Decorate exquisite + Food delicious + Romantic ambience + Good service quality = Enjoy 
o (^  ^) o

Superb experience in a cozy lighted environment 
Great service
Exquisite tasting menu
My favorite upscale restaurant in the city. Incredible food. Incredible service. Love love love. The little chocolates you get at the end are heavenly.

Amazing dining adventure! Each item presented was spectacular, wine pairings even better. Staff knowledge and attentiveness was spot on! I will be back, wonderful! Looks like I gave them 4 1/2? Negative they are a solid 5!!

My boyfriend thought the food was heavy, and I told him the cuisine is Alsatian. But still, the bread with each course was unnecessary. The acidity in dishes can be overwhelming, but as someone who drinks rice vinegar straight out of the bottle, I appreciated it. The somm was overly aggressive trying to get us to buy bottled ports while I felt like I could barely walk. The dining room was crowded and loud, so I am not entirely sure that I came to the same place as the Michelin guys who gave it a three star comfort rating.

This place is good, but it is def not worth the money you pay.  The quality of food is just not up to par with let's say Daniel, which you pay the same amount, but the food is exceptional.  I think if it were 200 less, I would recommend it, but now I would say pass.  The service is great like any high end restaurant, but the food is just disappointing.

I love this place!

Last night was my fourth visit to this restaurant and each time I enjoy it more. Although I wasn't jazzed about the food choices in a couple categories of their prix fixe menu this time (I know eel is one of the "it" ingredients right now but how many people actually like it?? And, sorry, but sauerkraut is a good way to ruin a tart), the choices I made were, as they always are here, prepared perfectly and tasted amazing. I especially loved the amuses - a clever take on a clambake, including a clam chowder croquette with liquid center and a corn fritter; incredible!! - and the tenderloin entree, which melted in your mouth but was over far too quickly. 

This restaurant has one Michelin star but I suspect it won't for long. With their level of hospitality (service is excellent and very accommodating), their beautiful space (the lovely design of the restaurant alone makes it special and worth a stop) and the quality of their food (some of the best in the city), they should at least have two, maybe even three! Absolutely one of the top restaurants in NY. 

And, just when you think it can't get better, did I mention they operate a gourmet chocolate shop next door? Oh, yes!

If you can get a reservation here, do, because I predict it won't be as easy in the future.

Went for a dinner with friends as four of us on a Sunday night. As expected as for one star Michelin Star restaurant which you would not be disappointed with the food. Quite variety food for the tasting menu and a wide selection of wines. Breads offered at the beginning and during the courses, a bit of salty for all the dishes that night as four of us felt the same. The manager or the owner (I believed he was) came out to greet each table except our table.....oh well....Service was standard, no complaint. Worth a try but not necessary will coming back.

To put it simply, this was the best meal and dining experience I've had in years.  I won't attempt to detail the nuances of the different courses that were served because it really must be experienced first hand.  The food was excellent - in taste, in presentation, as well as in creativity.  The service was first rate, very attentive but not intrusive.  The ambiance - elegant and quiet yet not stuffy or pretentious (le bernadin anyone?).  I highly recommend dinner at Gabriel Kreuther and am looking forward to my next evening here!

Deserves every bit of its 5 star rating. The quality of the chocolate is just extremely high. Gabriel kreuther is an extremely talented chocolatier.   

I ordered the frozen hot chocolate which was absolutely amazing. You can taste the rich dark chocolate in every sip.   Was quite upset when it was empty. :(. 

I also got another item that was absolutely  amazing.   I forget the name, however the picture list shown in my review. I will come back 100%. 
On the expensive side but is worth every penny.

My dad and I came here after the concierge at the Roosevelt Hotel suggested it. I'll never be able to thank the concierge enough because Gabriel Kreuther is AMAZING. 
Obviously it's not cheap, but you are paying for the best food and service. All of the staff is incredibly attentive, helpful and kind. They made my dad and me feel like we were family. They look after you, provide the best recommendation, answer any and all questions, and ensure you are more than happy. The waiter learned I had just moved to New York, so he had a little chocolate cake with a candle and congratulations written on the plate sent out with dessert. I honestly can't speak highly enough of the service. 

For wine they suggested Emmanuel Giboulot Côte de Beaune - it was absolutely perfect. We asked for the waiter's suggestions ordering. For the first course I had the Cured Hawaiian Striped Marlin - it was delicious and there was a lot of fish. For the second course my dad and I both had the Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart - also amazing. For the third course I had the Spice Roasted Diver Scallops and it was TO DIE FOR - the best scallops I have ever had. For dessert I had the Fromage Blanc Fresh Strawberry - also outstanding, the strawberries were perfectly ripe. 

If you're looking for somewhere to really take your time to sit and enjoy company and the best food, this is the place.
The food is great waitress was very  attentive, knowledgeable and professional. No negatives. Every request was honored and food was amazing. I would recommend as a solid 5.

From the moment you enter this restaurant you are treated to an experience. The ambiance is magnificent to match the Michelin star cuisine. We had several courses and with each one there was a new experience, breads to complement the food, cutlery was changed and wine served. The attention to every detail makes patrons feel welcomed and pampered.  A very memorable experience and highly recommended. We topped the evening off with a visit to the chocolate shop and brought the taste of it home for the following evening treats. Over the top!

I usually save my 5 stars for cheap hole in the walls or mom&pop shops, but 5 stars here is very well-deserved. I came here with my boyfriend to celebrate his promotion. I put into OpenTable the reason for us coming and the entire staff seemed to be informed and congratulated him throughout the entire meal. Out of all the Michelin restaurants I've been to, the staff at Gabriel Kreuther was the most welcoming and attentive. Somehow we were able to get the best table in the restaurant according to our waiter. We were put into a cozy corner right under a window where you had a view of the entire restaurant.

We decided to go with the Chef's Menu for $215pp. There is no set menu for this. Instead you can express your likes and dislikes and they create a tasting menu based off your preferences. You can even request them to include certain items from their regular menu. I highly recommend the Chef's Menu for special occasions and if you have a lot of time. There was a total of 18 courses over a course of 3 hours.

They explain to you every course, but sometimes it is hard to catch what they are saying. But in the end they do present you with a printed menu of your entire course. You can see our tasting menu here: https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/gabriel-kreuther-new-york?select=BiWnWuPW-4aeZ7fv5LdBPw&userid=DC1hfeeSaYr2E1xwiEL81A

Among the 18 courses, these were the ones I most enjoyed and recommend requesting for the tasting menu:

Savory Scallion Kougelhopf with chive fromage blanc - We started out with this delicious scallion bread. It tasted very similar to an Asian scallion bun, so I enjoyed it immensely because of that. I believe they will give you one of these before your meal so this is an item you will not have to request.

Scallop Chip - This chip came as one of the four canapés in their Taste of New England course. To make the chip, they minced scallop and tapioca and dyed the chip with charcoal. I could snack on these all day if each chip wasn't so incredibly expensive.

Surgeon and Sauerkraut Tart - I was afraid the tart would be too creamy, but the mousseline was perfect as was the fish. The tart came with applewood smoke, which made for a fun presentation.

Foie Gras Terrine & Marcona Almond Praline with smoked cherry cider gelée and five spice granola - This somehow reminded me of a savory truffle. I loved the texture of the almonds and granola. 

Seared Sullivan Country Foie Gras with peach marmalade, pickled peaches, watermelon radish, mustard seeds and popcorn pudding -  I never really enjoyed foie gras until having this dish. The foie gras was incredibly rich and fatty. It went so well with the popcorn pudding and pickled peaches.

Frozen Lime-Rosemary Marshmallow with apricot gelée and candied almond tuile cookies - I normally don't enjoy marshmallows, but this was delightful. The marshmallows didn't have the off-putting gelatinous texture. This was a really refreshing dessert.

Fromage Blanc Fresh Strawberry - This consisted of fromage blanc sorbet and sweet strawberries on a hazelnut crumble. This was one of the best desserts I've had in a while. I was so full after so many courses, but I wanted more of this dessert. I'm sure their desserts change seasonally but if you are able to request this dessert definitely do.

We ended the meal with chocolates from the Kreuther Handcrafted Chocolate shop right next door. To our surprise, they also brought out a chocolate mousse cake with "Congratulations" written on the plate.

The only thing I did not enjoy as much were the breads served in between courses. Compared to the Kougelhopf in the beginning, the ficelle loaf and rosemary buckwheat rolls were not as stellar. I wanted to try everything, so the bread just made me too full in the end.

Needless to say both food and service here are top notch. There were so many courses, I actually almost felt overwhelmed. I definitely would not have been able to finish it all if it wasn't paced for 3 hours. I hope one day I can treat my parents to a meal here.

Gluten free versions for many of their dishes!! 
One of us had Celtic disease and the staff were all knowledgeable and accommodating, serving gluten-free versions of the dishes. They even had gluten free bread to start!!
We did pre theater and they got us out exactly when we had to leave, and we never even felt rushed. 
Amazing food, presentation, service and atmosphere. Very much recommend!

Wow, we had an incredible pre theater dinner at the bar tonight. Service was impeccable but restrained, drinks were excellent and the food was truly a revelation.  We started with the lobster croquettes, decadent but light as a feather and followed with three of the alsatian specialties.  The kugelhopf is a lovely little savory bundt cake with rich, thick chive fromage blanc to dip it in.  The veal and pistachio fleishnacka were luxurious but delicate.  The country sausage is really special; as someone who typically finds sausages hard to digest and heavy, this was incredibly flavorful, balanced and melted in your mouth with violet mustard they should seriously consider bottling and selling and yummy sauerkraut.  They brought nori crackers to the table at one point which were delicious as well.

Dessert was a tour de force. My partner was celebrating his birthday, so they brought a sort of caramely tart for him which he loves. They also had printed a menu for him that said Happy Birthday with his name, a thoughtful touch to the service.  We also ordered the beignets, airy and perfect with the marmalade and a scoop of caramel ice cream, and the chocolate and petit fours. The Kreuther chocolates are delicious and served on a sliver of chocolate on a bed of cacao nib.  They were served with cheesecake macarons, also perfection. Thank you Gabriel Kreuther for a showstopping meal! We can't wait to return for more bar snacks and to try the dining room!

Came here for the 4 course pre fixe dinner, fairly standard Michelin Star experience. Very attentive service, a lot of bread served in between courses, very specific ingredient choices and mixes of flavors that are unique to fine restaurants. I didn't give it 5 stars because there was no dish that got seared into my memory - I was lazy and didn't write this review for a few weeks and I already can't remember what I liked about each dish in spite of the pictures.

I went there for lunch and had a great experience. The food was very tasty and served very aesthetically. Of course, you can't leave without trying some of their desserts - they are fabulous! You might want to buy more for later in their neighboring chocolate store.

We went for my birthday celebration and had the four course dinner. We are vegetarians so the chef prepared his own menu. Each dish was interesting and tasty. The service was great and the atmosphere is light and airy. Desserts - the Apple crisp was average but the chocolate one was predictably good. Overall a nice restaurant for a special occasion.

This is a sleeper gourmet dining spot in midtown. Little known but highly recommended. The space is beautiful -- very open and spacious, with lots of light. Service is, as expected, top of the line. The food is also unique and diverse. The lunch prix fix menu does the job.

We came here for an anniversary dinner and everything was exquisite. The food, the presentation, and the service were all top notch. The head server fully accounted for our evening of culinary delight. They reserved a cute corner table for us in the back and even provided customized menus for us to keep. 

All of the dishes were inventive and flavorful. The risotto and foie gras were out of this world. For dessert, try their apple crisp. It's simply amazing. 

The chef keeps it real in the kitchen back there -- each dish took its time, and there was considerable waiting time between courses. They do not rush their craft. 

The sommelier made an awesome wine recommendation. He asked for our price range instead of pushing expensive bottles on us without asking about our preferences first. He was knowledgeable and friendly. 

All in all, a 5 Star experience and we will be back for other occasions!

This was an amazing dining experience.  The location is terrific, across from Bryant Park.  The staff was exceedingly attentive and detail oriented.  They were knowledgeable and friendly.  Prior to our meals, the small plates were delicate, yet very flavorful.  I started with the chestnut soup, which was terrific.  The chestnut purée was complimented by the mushrooms very well.  My main dish of black bass was perfectly prepared and delicious.  Love this place!
Sat at the bar. Ordered the squid ink orecchiette. Wonderful dish. Exquisite interior. Truly terrific restaurant, ambiance was lovely.
Very delicious chocolate. Tried the mint, coffee, passionfruit and salted caramel flavors. All were amazingly soft and beyond tasty. Highly recommend to try it.

A very nice place, probably deserves a second star for its food and great wine list and somelier. The service staff seems to not quite being used to the level of its own place. But, they will do that last little step to perfection hopefully with little effort. The restaurant is well designed, the food is the star of the evening. The beef tenderloin was cooked to perfection, a bit much salt, but an impressive execution. The languatine tartare was sublime, a masterpiece. The seared foie gras a top level showpiece. The amount and selection of bread was entertaining and tasty. I always like white bread at the table, but I am old school. Coffee tasted great, the dessert as always in the US charismatic but not overly sensual. I would like to come back and a spirited recommendation is in order. Compliments to the chef!
Amazing lunch, great value, wonderful hospitality and sublime food. Foie gras, beef tenderloin, sturgeon tart and Mr Aumonts dessert were exemplary. Look forward to returning

Just to keep it simple - everything was fantastic!  The service as soon as we walked in the door was delightful.  The ambiance is serenely elegant.  We had the 4 course tasting and it was all ingenious execution of an inspired vision we've not encountered before.

Deserves all of its accolades.  Deserves the visit and appreciation of anyone who adores creatively delicious food.
Amazing dining experience. From the greeting to the final glass of wine, the service was impeccable and the food Devine.  A must-go !

This place is good, careful execution, tasty but small courses. Unusual ingredients and a sense of occasion about it. It's porbably not he final say in terms of food taste and flavor but it makes up for it with invention and presentation. It will be expensive so reserve for business or occasions.

We went here last night to celebrate our 19th year wedding anniversary after having had good experiences when the chef was at The Modern.  We had looked at the menu online and the food does not disappoint or leave you hungry.  

My wife had a migraine and lately I don't like to drink as much alcohol when dining out, so we were really happy to see a selection of non-alcoholic "cocktails."  They offered four and we tried all of them.  They were all delicious with perfect balance of sweet, sour and interesting herbal, spice or other notes.  So nice to see a place put as much effort into creating a great drink for diners who don't want to have alcohol.  One of the managers was explaining to us that they use this non-alcoholic gin substitute for several of these drinks - you basically get the flavor profile of gin without the alcohol - sounds like a great to me and I can say the resulting drinks were fantastic.

We started with caviar service and had no regrets for splurging on this extra.  A nice half ounce portion for two people served on curry crisps with a nice buttermilk mousse.  

Some standouts for food included: the foie gras terrine, which was served in a ball shape encrusted with pistachio served over a bed of petals and a gelee and accompanied by a type of bread that was like a waffle with jam and other toppings.  The seared foie gras was also delicious and served with an assortment of fruit and mustard type sauce.  
The hamachi/truffle/foie first course was nice, with the main element being the fish and the other two background supporters - not a bad thing, just make sure to get a dish were foie is the main element if that is what you really want.  The sturgeon and sauerkraut tart is another solid dish - covered in a luxurious caviar mousse and served under a glass dome full of smoke - fantastic and beautiful presentation.  The squab an cassoulet was a filling a rich dish with multiple tasty components and the grilled lobster was also well done, with its accompanying carrots and fried leeks being especially noteworthy.  

Desserts were very nice with a starting palate cleanser before the main offerings.  In addition to the two desserts with our prix fixe, they also sent us a third dessert to celebrate our anniversary.  This third was a delicious chocolate caramel.  Our main desserts of Ambrosial/mango and Decadent/Chestnut red currant were very nice ways to end the meal.  Afterwards they brought some chocolates and macaroons which were very nice and we decided to go to the bakery next door to get some of those things for the kids. 

Bread service was very good; instead of a bread cart or tray, they continually bring different breads during the course of the meal.  This included a rosemary bread served with pork fat and another offering with a delicious creme fraiche.   

Some things to note: table water service - if they offer sparkling or still but you really want NYC tap, make sure to specifically ask for that, otherwise you will likely end up with a water charge on the bill (like we did).  Service: while service was friendly and efficient, we did feel like they took some of the food away a little too quickly, when we still had some portion left to enjoy.  The food is rich and filling, and while eating we would stop occasionally to digest and talk only to have the staff come take the food away.  We could have easily said we were still enjoying that course and they would have had no problem I'm sure, but it was just something we noticed a few times.  Otherwise we appreciated the staff and the conversations we had with several of them.  They seemed genuinely happy to have us there and wanted to make sure we were enjoying our experience.      

Overall, it is a very nice restaurant, with great service and food.  Total for water, one alcoholic drink, five non-alcoholic drinks, caviar service, and 2 prix fixe was $510 before tip.

We made a reservation for my birthday a month back. My first comment is that the service was amazing... perfectly done and attentive but not over attentive. 

Words cannot describe the food as it was innovative and creative, tasteful, well portioned, and by the time we were finished, there was no question if we had enough to eat... it was plenty. 

I have to comment on the service again... it was in the top 5 of restaurants I have attended over the last 20 years... yes... that good. My suggestion for them is to keep it up. 

Overall, the ambience was tasteful but I would not call this the type of New York restaurant where you go Ronen seen, but nonetheless, a great experience and to add my name to the menu, just a nice touch

1. Impressive service:
    A. We came here for anniversary celebration. We made our reservation 2 hours before our dinner, but when we arrived at the restaurant, everyone says "Happy anniversary" to us, even during our whole dinner---their memory is impressive.
    B. They also prepared a special menu for us, I keep it as a gift.
    C. They gave us a small beautiful cake as an anniversary gift. Nice.

2. Delicious food: Dishes are creative, beautiful and delicious.

3. Modern romantic decoration: The whole restaurant could become a classroom for learning modern art, great sense!

Came here on a Saturday night for a Christmas celebration with my boyfriend. The decor itself was worthy of a Michelin star. The dining room is probably one of the most beautiful I've been in. We were seated immediately, and given copies of the menu. We had some help from the staff about the wine to pick, and then ordered all our food. 
Shortly after ordering, the first amuse bouche was brought out. This consisted of some sort of peppermint flavored jelly, and pastry in the shape of gingerbread men, to celebrate the holiday season. 
We decided to go with the four course prix fixe menu, but there were many small in between bites, so we ended up eating a lot more. 
Everything was excellent, but the seared foie gras, pennsylvania squab cassoulet, roasted Maine lobster and foie gras millefeuille were clear standouts. The service and presentation were also outstanding. If you're going to have one splurge meal in NYC, this should be it.

We ordered the four course prix fixe dinner with wine pairings. The fluke was quite bland and was overpowered by the wine. The hamachi, black truffle & foie gras mille-feuille and its pairing was much better but not extraordinary. The risotto and its wine pairing stole the show: this was by far the best course! The wonderful flavors of the food were nicely complemented by the wine. The squab was neither here nor there: not terrible but I've definitely had better. The same descriptor applies to the desserts. The servers and the sommelier were attentive but lacked warmth. Overall, this was a solid 4-Star experience at a 5-Star price.

Everything here was great!! The service, the ambiance and the food. The food was elegantly plated and was delicious... 
(they also have a chocolate store next door which I also recommend) the staff is very professional and friendly. 
That day we had tickets for the ballet and were running a little bit tight with time... the staff managed to get all of the food served in a timely fashioned and we we're sat at our table promptly. If it wasn't for their great service we would've missed the first portion of the ballet. THANK YOU SO MUCH!! :)

Was in last Saturday night to celebrate my husband's birthday and we sadly had a less than stellar experience. The service was the biggest issue we encountered, and incredibly disappointing for this level of restaurant. 

When we arrived about 10 minutes early for our 9pm reservation, the hostess told us our table would be ready closer to our reservation time and that we were welcome to sit at the bar. We ordered some cocktails to enjoy while we waited, which were excellent. As someone who has to limit my alcohol intake, I was pleased to see a wide array of creative mocktails. At around 9:15 the hostess came over and said they were running behind because people from previous reservations were "lingering" and that they would seat us as soon as they could. While I understand that backups do happen (especially on a Saturday night) I feel like at fine dining restaurants, the service is just as important as the food considering the price tag attached, and it just seemed unprofessional and a little odd that she was blaming diners for scheduling incompetence on their end instead of genuinely apologizing and taking responsibility for the delay. Another fifteen minutes went by and at 9:30 we were finally seated by the same hostess, who halfheartedly apologized and then quickly followed it up with, "But you know...these things happen and you can't push people out." Way to make your customers feel special (especially when you know they're there to celebrate an occasion). It also didn't help that a couple who waltzed in 25 minutes after we did were magically seated at the same exact time as us. 

Despite the frustration of how our evening started, we brushed it off and looked forward to what we hoped would be a great experience from that point forward. Unfortunately the inattentiveness continued, as it took a good amount of time to even be acknowledged by a waiter and given menus. Service continued to be slow throughout the meal. 

As for the food, it was solid and thoughtfully presented, but not particularly memorable or mindblowing, and the portions were definitely on the smaller side in comparison to recent prix fixe meals we've had at similar establishments like Daniel and Marea. 

We both left feeling cheated, disappointed and wishing we had gone somewhere else.
The best restaurant I've been to. The service and the food were phenomenal. I'll be back.

This is what "fine dining" is all about.

Midtown is my LEAST favorite neighborhood in Manhattan, I avoid it like the plague.....however, we wanted dinner on a Saturday night before a play, so what's a girl to do?

Consult EATER and GRUB STREET....and boy, were they right.

Don't be afraid of the Michelin star rating, just go.   

Eat in the lounge and dive into chef Gabriel Kreuther's gorgeous Alsatian specialties like his Alsatian Tarte Flambe w/ lardons and creme fraiche....a gorgeous Alsatian sausage on choucroute w/ moutarde violette.    (we were fans when he was the head chef at The Modern).
Don't miss the hamachi crudo terrine and the sturgeon caviar tart.

Sip some wonderful Drappier Rose Champagne and feel like a queen.
The staff is the best in Manhattan.  So warm and welcoming.

and don't forget the apple strudel and beignets with dipping sauce if you have room (we always have room for dessert).
Gratis box of GK chocolates and macarons on the table with our dessert.

They treated us like VIPs and we forgot for a minute that we were on 42nd St.

This was a fantastic evening with fantastic food and service to match.
Felt like we were in Paris for an evening.

Great place for cocktails while in midtown too......

Go.

Amazing. This restaurant is heads and shoulders above Ai Fiori or Gramercy Tavern. A totally different class. Pork was amazing as was risotto, beef, fish appetizer. Desserts incredible. At this price point beats out others.

Very disappointed with some of the dishes: foie gras and fish didn't pair well and deserts were too sweet and lacked any originality.  However, the biggest disappointment was the $75 wine pairing, it was a roller coaster ride starting with an over ripe Gewurtsraminer  then cider (with fish?), then Carignan red with beef (cab would have been much better), and ending with Sauternes with chocolate (horrible pairing).  Did Gabriel Kreuther try this and approve it?

Amazing experience and the second favorite Michelin meal I've ever had. (Well ahead of two Michelin three star meals). We ordered the chefs menu and he customized both of the meals based on our tastes. Also, they included a signed copy of the order along with a printed copy which was a great touch. Overall, I cannot recommend enough with the taste and presentation.

I hardly know where to start this review. How do you describe the best meal and service of your life? In a word dazzling!

My wife and I opted for a Kir Royale accented by elderberry to start the evening. The uniqueness of this drink set the creative tone that never ended through the courses. Dinner began in earnest as we ordered the Chefs tasting menu. The staff was crazy attentive yet not overbearing. Our French sommelier was also a champ in guiding us to wine heaven.

Highlights were a gnocchi dish with fresh black truffles shaved table side by the Chef himself, the lobster, langoustine tartare and the tenderloin. Flavors were complex and displayed a layering of texture and creativity which earned their Michelin Star! 

We finished with cheese that included the best Epoisse I've ever had. As if wasn't enough our sommelier took us to the kitchen where we met the whole team.

Can't wait to return

The food was phenomenal and the service was impeccable.  The tables were set far enough apart that you had privacy and didn't have to listen to your neighbors conversation.  
If you only had one choice to pick a restaurant don't miss this opportunity.
 Bonnie Y.

My party of six had a incredible dining experience here this evening. I'm truly shocked this restaurant only has 1 Michelin Star, it definitely needs 3 stars.

The formal dining room is beautifully decorated and has a elegant ambiance. 

The service was superb and everyone was on point this evening. 

The food- Each course was presented perfectly, creative and delicious courses.

I'd suggest this restaurant to anyone
Delicious food, exceptional service and great atmosphere (very spacious and comfortable).  Great place to take clients for lunch or dinner if you are in the midtown manhattan area.

Came here for Valentines Day dinner, for which they raised the price to  375 pre-fixe and 285 for wine pairing (which I opted out of). I've been to the majority of other Michelin star offerings in the city, and I think this is the most I've paid just for the base dinner, so going in my expectations were sky high. Due to the high price tag, my comparisons are anchored to other fine dining establishments (Per Se, EMP, Jean George, Ko, Brooklyn Fare etc) If I'm not mistaken, only Masa has a higher price for pre-fixe

We were seated at a table side by side with a full view of the restaurant. The decor was a bit gaudy and high ceilings gave the space a cold feel.  While service was attentive, the servers seemed to pace around nervously and were a constant presence, vs in other fine dining experiences the waiters seem to disappear into the background and only appearing at exact the right times. They also were less warm, friendly, and polished than what I have come to expect at NYC fine dining places. 

While the food was very good and creatively plated, it was not particularly creative nor memorable. The pacing was also off - there were two times when the we waited over 30 mins between courses, so the dinner felt dragged on. 

I hate to be overcritical of a restaurant, but when you have the fortitude to charge these kind of prices for a meal and don't deliver, you deserve to be called out. Overall, I would probably not go back nor recommend it.

The ambiance is sophisticated and romantic, it is definitely more spacious than most restaurants in New York. The food was not bad, interesting first course that integrates aroma into the eating experience.

Very fancy and modern restaurant. The service was exceptional. My friend an I had a 7 meal course. Every meal was delicious and had an exquisite taste. We had a chance to see their kitchen and meet the chef Gabriel. We had a very good time. Thank you, Gabriel.
Great French restaurant with a very delicious food, beautiful designed and perfect service . Very enjoyable !

Great good accompanied by great service. My favorites were their hand cut tagliatelle, porcini consommé and the baked Hawaiian Mero finished with a beautifully plated dessert, lambent Mandarin milk chocolate. Another interesting piece was the petit fours that they shared served in a cocoa bean cast that represented the history of chocolate from its raw style to a finished Tahitian vanilla ganache. This place definitely ranked higher than my expectations!

1 Michelin star? A clear oversight. This restaurant deserves at least 2.

I would like to express my gratitude for the experience I had just a few days ago eating at Gabriel Kreuther. Everyone from the hostess when I entered, to my waiter, to those who brought my food and drink were exceptionally professional. I ate on both sides of the restaurant (which have different menus) in order to gain the full experience. 

One of the best (2) meals I've had in terms of the food and the full potential of the experience. Gabriel Kreuther elevates the art of food. I went to 4 restaurants with Michelin stars on my recent business trip to New York. This is by far the best one. 

I had a much, much better time with you than when I ate a few months ago at other well-regarded restaurants in London or at the other well-regarded restaurants at which I ate in New York. Not that they are not excellent, but you shine. 

I can't wait to come back. I look forward to it. You work hard and it shows (shines).
Beautiful ambiance, exceptional service, creative 'mocktails', and delicious food!

Thank you a wonderful pre-theatre dinner.  The service was gracious and on point. The menu was well selected and quality impeccable. Thank you again to an amazing team.  Also, completely taken with the coucou clock. Bravo to the decorating team.

This post is long overdue. In fact about two years overdue. We came here to celebrate our 17th anniversary of marriage 04-30-2016. Miguel was our server. They made this experience divine. Miguel and his crew made sure we were taken care of and went the extra mile as the night continued. You will forever be part of this wonderful day because 19 years before this day, we met on this same block in our early twenties. We are about to celebrate our 19th year married we remember you guys for making our day extra special. See you soon for one of our anniversaries! Thank you Gabriel Kreuther!

Love, love, love this restaurant (one of my favs. in NYC) and Gabriel Kreuther's modern French cuisine.

I don't know what the %^&* the Michelin inspectors are thinking, but this place is not a one Michelin star restaurant, way underrated. imo, GK is on par with the some of the greats in NYC, i.e. Gunter Seeger, Le Bernardin, EMP, and Bouley at Home, and deserves at least two stars. 

Just had one of the best dinners on my 2nd visit to the Kitchen Table (the table is all yours for the evening).  It's slightly more expensive than their tasting menu in the dinning room, but you get a wonderful view of the kitchen, and some of the courses are presented directly by the chefs.

Love the wine list here (they have some really nice wines by the half-bottles).

Impeccable service

Highest recommendation

: 10 calendars

Superb !!!!!

Gabriel Kreuther epitomizes everything wonderful about dining in NYC. Beautiful and creative preparations using squab. It will satisfy those who miss the days when the chef used to be at the Modern. The kitchen perform very well as far as the quality, plating, and timing. The service was impeccable.  A+ all around !!!!

I was disappointed in this place; went with a group of friends in early March and was subject to a large group of 8 people who were very drunk and very loud ; ironically my age range (the only sober one was a 30 year old); very well off; from Dallas so being from Houston Texas I was ready to walk over and wag a Texas finger at them but did not do so since it would really upset my spouse.  The restaurant manager came over after they left to apologize but that was way too late for action; the restaurant continued to serve them wine (counted 7 bottles) for 3 hours prior to them leaving.

I expect much better of a great restaurant; too bad...

This is an update to a review from about two years ago. Went on Sunday for Mother's Day brunch. Service is still off a bit. Plates came to table and were  put in front of the wrong diner.
At 2 PM half the tables were empty, one couple sitting in bar area yet it took quite awhile to be served cocktails.
Again place was pretty empty yet server came over to take our food order before cocktails had arrived. I said could you give us a few minutes. About three minutes later another server came over to take the order. Again I said could you give us a few minutes after we have our cocktails. During this exchange, my daughter asked what was the entrée that was being served at the next table. The server explained it to her. He then used that as a pretty stumbling attempt to force us to order when he came back over in about three or four minutes and said to her so I see you want that terrine, what else looks interesting? Very annoying and clumsy.

Food portions are pretty minuscule, even for fine dining. The geometric precision of the dishes is great but at some point you wonder if you would like less geometry and more food. 
Part of the amuse Bouche was a circular ceramic dish, the base of which was multicolored pastel jelly upon which sat six jelly like cubes of different infusions. There was a twig Sticking up in the middle of the plate. Also came a piece of slate with some other items, some of which had leaves underneath. Server had to explain what was in edible, namely this twig, leaves and jelly on the bottom of the plate. Pretty ridiculous
Gave this place to tries but will not be back
Went here in their private dining room. I really hope they didnt pay 250/p. Boring food, sloppy service.

Overall, it was a memorably good meal with excellent service in a somewhat noisy environment, given it's location in a hotel.
    We enjoyed the amuse bouchés, particularly the non-bread items. After our orders were taken and wines served, for example, the waiters brought out small plates of herb-flecked gelee, chocolate bon bons filled with some kind of savory broth, and soft cocoon-looking bites, which they said represented fire, water, earth and wind. It was clever--the green "water" gellee, for example, tasted like a cucumber mojito.
    We loved the foie gras appetizers. Entrees were delicious, as well, although when I ordered "squab 'en cassoulet," wish I had known I wasn't having just a substitution of squab for duck in a cassoulet. (I love cassoulet!) Instead, it was an order of roast squab (good, if a tad over-cooked) surrounded by a small spoonful of beans, a bit of cabbage and a tiny amount of sausage. 
     Desserts of chocolate mousse and coconut panna cotta with strawberries were beautifully presented. Before we left, the restaurant also brought out tiny chocolates, which we were too full to eat. 
    Everyone in my party was impressed with our experience (a couple of us having dined at "Daniel" & "Alain Ducasse") but no one could understand why GK isn't more well-known? It's not for the faint-of-wallet, though. Four prix fixe dinners, 1/2 bottle red wine & 3 glasses of (very good but not overly spendy) white wines = a little over $850 before tip.

Gabriel Kreuther is a nice Alsatian French restaurant on the ground floor of the Grace Building by Bryant Park.

I had the tasting menu and the food is absolutely incredible. I see why it ranked in the top ten on Zagat. Five stars.

But at a high end restaurant, I expect a bit more than a set of waiters who left us without any wine for nearly 15 minutes in the middle of the meal and did not bother to check in with us. Other times the service was not too attentive.

Not exactly what I was looking for in a $500+ meal.

The 5 or so support waiters didn't want to step up even when I gently started holding up my hand, and our main waiter was busy taking Instagram photos for the Millennial customers next to us.
Place rocked. Great staff. Great service.  Decent affordable wines or stupid pric d wines. Your choice.  Pretty room.  Had a great time.
Great experience! Food is delicious, with amazing presentation and great service! I think they deserve more than one star!

Our third visit and it was as wonderful as the first two! For us, dining at Gabriel Kreuther is left for very special occasions such as my wife's birthday. They effortlessly go out of their way to make the experience special from start to finish. The service blends perfectly with the sublime cuisine to create a 3 hour (approximately) experience that is worth the cost. Spoil yourself & make a reservation!!

Very bad experience. Made a reservation for wife's birthday mainly because they are supposed to put name on menu. Didn't happen. It was supposed to be a pleasant surprise that ended up backfiring. My wife told me she heard a waiter calling the woman at the next table by my wife's name and blamed me for screwing up.  My blood pressure rises whenever I walk by here since that day.

We got the tasting menu. The waiter asked if we wanted black truffle shavings on one of our entrees. We said sure and he never said anything else and never mentioned an additional charge. We got the bill and for these shavings on just one entree was $125. I'm sorry but if you're going to charge $125 in addition to the cost of a meal you have to at least mention the price. That was so unbelievably unprofessional. 

Not to mention the waiter was MIA practically the entire time, we had to ask the busboy to get him at one point when we wanted another drink. I've been to other Michelin restaurants, the service here was seriously lacking compared to those.

Went for my birthday. I enjoyed the food but I am not a big fan of French pâtés. Cavier and bread was good, we did the 4 course pre-fix desert and final course was more towards my taste. Other then my preference it was a great experience with great service and food.

Dinner on 6/21/2018 with my DH, four courses including dessert for $155 per person, plus a cheese course.  More than enough food!  This was my fifth meal at Gabriel Kreuther, a mix of lunches and dinners.  The bread is well worth the carbs - the rosemary rolls with the lardo paste was our favorite.  Loved the hamachi, black truffle & food gras mille-feuille, the sturgeon & sauerkraut tart, and the roasted black bass.  Squab with crispy skin and duck brisket was exceptional.  It was a treat to sit close to the window looking into the kitchen.  I highly recommend!

Outstanding. A dining experience like no other. Everything here is incredible... the presentation, the service, the bathroom with upbeat French music. I have never felt so pampered and catered to in my life. It's almost like a spa experience, but for food.

I had the foie gras as my appetizer and the pork cutlet as my entree.... I would highly recommend. Everything was delectable, including the greens (and I'm not usually fond of vegetables).

GK is an extraordinary restaurant in a city filled with good restaurants.  I cannot recommend it enough, it is amazing gastronomy, flawless and stunning service in elegant but relaxed environs.  I have gone both for business and personal pleasure and it never fails to please.  It is excellent value relative to the quality of food and style.

Spent our one year wedding anniversary here and got the three course prix fixe.  Food was incredible as usual and service perfect.  They went out of their way to make our meal special and even had a celebratory hand written card by chef Gabriel Kreuther (who was present).  Has been my wife's favorite restaurant since I brought her here for a birthday dinner.  Thank you again for a wonderful experience.

4.5 Stars ! I came here for lunch! I had the Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart to start. I was really surprised at how good this was. I had no idea how this would taste and I was pleasantly surprised with how well the flavors came together.  I had the pork tenderloin for my main. This one I wasn't that big of a fan of. The pasta that it was served with really didn't add anything to the dish for me. Finally, I had the chocolate caramel dessert. Honestly this was my favorite part of the meal ! It was so good! If you go for nothing else go for this dessert!
