Came me here for lunch for the second time. Everything is excellent. Started with the refreshing amuse bouche that included this frozen lemongrass drink and this lychee creation.  This was followed by a perfectly cooked seared foie gras complemented by a nice fruity sauce.  For entree, we all got the beef tenderloin cooked medium-rare.  It was only a few ounces and wow it was good. Definitely could have eaten more of that. The jus was so good we used all the bread to soak it. We passed on dessert but they gave us complementary mini brownies - so good and a few chocolates. The choco store is next door and not to be missed. Will definitely be back!

We went here for my birthday. I knew the service would be great after seeing the birthday card from the restaurant waiting for me at our table. The food was fantastic - standouts were the Foie Gras Terrine served with banana bread, which I thought was a new and inventive presentation and flavors that weirdly worked really well. The "Ambrosial" dessert was also amazing. It was like a margarita in dessert form - hit sweet, sour, and salty notes.  Will definitely come back.

Every bite is an amazingly delicious work of art!  The staff is friendly, courteous, informative and professional.  Only my second time here and we will be back.  The chocolates are also an absolute must try!

Well very overrated was there with a friend the food tested good small portion selection of wine and beer expensive place for the elite I don't even know how they get such a high ratting so many better place in NYC  Daniel ,le Bernardin ,boulet anyway if you want nice rip off go there's

Definitely my current favorite haute cuisine dining experience in NYC.  Every dish is scrumptious, beautifully presented and supported by outstanding service.  The decor and vibe of this place are both top notch.  And you'll definitely be tempted to nick a few items like the gorgeous golden apple sugar bowl!

Finally tried this Michelin restaurant. The environment/ decoration is excellent. It is amazing that the three course lunch prix fixe has so many free bites! The waiter forgot to give us the bread and butter at first but gave us later after we asked for bread.

Outstanding! Fabulous! Incoryable! 6 course tasting menu was fantastic. Don't let the Michelin 1-Star rating fool you. The level of perfection from the chefs to service from the Sommelier stands at 3 Stars to me. I feel the higher you get in Michelin ratings, the more extravagant chefs become in trying to create entertainment. In doing so, sometimes the food experience is lost on the artistic creation of each dish rather than focusing on memorable taste profiles. Grabriel Kreuther is a perfect mesh between memorable taste profiles and entertainment. It's a relatively modest price point but well worth the experience.

Wow.  Just wow.  From start to finish, this was an unforgettable dining experience.  Our table was situated near the large glass window overlooking the kitchen, in a comfortable table/booth.  The dining room is warmly modern, with just the right noise level to give it a fun, hip feel.  Without going through every dish, we opted for the nine course tasting menu, with the wine pairing, and it was spot on.  First, the wines were from mostly small and interesting producers (mostly French), and the sommelier a master at explanation.  Second, the food (with one small exception), was beautifully presented and richly flavored, with multiple layers of taste weaving through each dish.  While you certainly could do less dishes (four courses, etc), why not go for the glory?  For a special occasion -- if you're a foodie -- this is the place!

Well, let's start out by saying they must be gunning for another Michelin star because I don't think one star is enough.  We all had the four course tasting menu with the restaurant's suggested wine pairings.

Starting with the service, you know when you visit a restaurant and you are served by at least ten people that there is an attention to service which is obsessive, in a great way.  And when most of them can describe your dish in detail, yes that is Gabriel Kreuther.  We engaged the sommelier who had to pour at least two or three different wines with each dish, since each had to be paired uniquely.  He was knowledgeable and could answer all of our questions.  Many interesting wines were served, including orange wine which was so good, it made a believer out of one of us who never liked it before.

On to the food which was in all cases sublime, no shortcomings at all.  I had one of his signatures, the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart with mousseline and Applewood smoke, you could taste everything in perfect harmony.  The Hamachi black truffle and foie gras mille feuille was visually stunning and gorgeous in the mouth.  The squab was classic French in its preparation and although I thought the mustard greens could have been toned down a tad, the wine picked up the greens beautifully.

Others have mentioned the décor, it is beautiful and soaring.  Tables are placed well and the noise level is perfect, not noisy or deathly quiet.  You get a big city vibe which is exactly what it is.  I hope to see them get a second star!

From the Drink list, the choices on your 3, 4, 6 courses and the calm. I relaxed and indulged in a swank and wonderful place. The chef is gifted. The service is 93. There are a few too many new folks which denotes an opportunity in retention. For the price I expect just a tad better management/culture.

This was far and away one of the best meals I've ever had!  Every dish was delicious and beautifully presented.  From the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart to the cedar plank trout with champagne sauce to the ambrosia dessert, this was really a special occasion dinner.  The service was friendly and very professional.

Oh wow, this is a terrific restaurant! We went to dinner there for the first time last week and were blown away by the quality of the food and service, the atmosphere, the wine list and a dining experience that should qualify this establishment for its second Michelin star. Our comment are based on just one visit, however, so we'll withhold an opinion on its ranking among NYC's finest, except to say it ought to be close to the top of any list. 

The service is really amazing. There are legions of staff alertly responding to every service possible requirement, and they do so in the most unobtrusive manner, never distracting, always available. It was awesome. If course that wouldn't matter of the food was outstanding, which it was. Counting the various amuse-bouche that arrived it seemed we must have had a 10-course meal. Every course was beautifully  prepared to our requests and/or astonishment, and the serving sizes were finely calculated to leave us comfortably satisfied yet wanting more. How did they manage that? Our orders -- beef tenderloin, lobster, hamachi, fluke -- were just plain delicious, and the desserts, whether chocolate or pears (our choices), were stunning to view and even better to taste. We've had no better meal in quite a while. 

The atmosphere here is open and gorgeous. Diners are not seated close to one another (a rarity!) and the openness of the dining area is both handsome and noise-reducing. It's just plain lovely. By the way, there's an excellent wine list -- not the largest to be found in NYC restaurants but one with some very fine wines and some less-expensive choices -- and we found a super Burgundy at the suggestion of the knowledgeable sommelier. 

Finally, yes it is expensive. But you get what you pay for in this case, and what you pay for is an outstanding dining experience. Let's give 'em that second Michelin star and move on....

I'd give two stars for the service & noise-level, but five stars for the foods/presentation. My husband and I wanted to start the birthday meal with a glass of Veuve Clicquot, but the server said, "we might be out of it tonight. Let me check with the sommelier." turned out to be unavailable for the day.. Okay..things happen..  and later when we tried to order a glass of Gevry Chambertine, and again, he went on saying, "I don't think we have it today. Let me check with the sommelier.."  turned out to be also unavailable for the day again. Why would you even have anything listed on the menu if you don't even have them? As a Michelin Star restaurant, this is absolutely unacceptable. 

Also, my red wine was spilled during the serving and instead of offering to replace the whole table cover that was soaked wet, the waiter simply brought me a little cloth napkin to cover the wet area. Are you kidding me? Another major no-no for a Michelin-star restaurant. 

There were by far too many people working in the dining area. Some of them were completely lost about what they were supposed to do and were standing and chatting one another. Our 9-course meal was served by different server each time and I also agree with the previous comments made that most servers were non-English speakers with little knowledge of the dishes being served and had such heavy accents that my husband and I didn't understand anything what the server was describing about each dish. Moreover, we didn't understand why we couldn't locate any cheese trolley or cheese plates offered on the menu, whereas this super-premium Spanish Jamon Iberico Cinco Jotas ham was proudly offered and displayed in the center of dining hall in a 'French' restaurant. "C'est vraiment bizarre," according to my native French husband. 

Overall, a major room to improve in their service and 'attention to detail' department and a long way to go if they want to add 1 more Michelin star, but the foods and presentation were superb and we enjoyed the entire 9-course meal.

Absolutely spectacular meal. The sturgeon and sauerkraut soufflé was the dish of the night for me.  Beautiful wines from the extensive and well thought out wine list.  Fantastic service.   A great choice for a special occasion.

Upscale, elegant, classy, expensive come to mind at the posh NY eatery. Great service, wonderful drinks at the bar, escorted to our table with grace... worthy of the extra Michelin star recently garnered. A wonderful experience, make reservations so you will not be disappointed. Creatively artistic and delightful in their culinary wonders without being pompously and unnecessarily extravagant as all too often is the case when a chef is trying to live up to the hype. Worth a visit. A Relais & Châteaux establishment: Caractère, Courtoisie, Calme, Charme et Cuisine:-)

Always been a fan since they opened. Food is excellent and exciting, service is always top notch.  The team has changed and I miss seeing them. The seasonal dishes and the staple dishes are solid. Beautiful venue and ambiance. Amazing desserts; they have their own chocolatier next door.

I went here with my boy friend (now ex) for my birthday. I always passed the Grace building , but didn't notice the restaurant. I remember walking towards the building and was worried I was being taken to Chipotle. Nothing wrong with Chipotle, but for a girl friend's birthday?... Then I saw where we were going and I was relieved. Phew!

I walked in and the person took my coat and was asking me how I am doing. I, being a small child, was like "good. It's my birthday today." The guy was caught off guard because he knew it was my birthday because it was noted on the reservation and he was leading to wishing me a happy birthday. It was sweet and I just felt very special. The menu had "Happy Birthday Alice!" on top and I got to keep it!

Okay... so how was the food? The food was good. I don't really recall anything being over-the-top or super delicious, but I think these chef tastings or pre-fix are more about the experience than really about the food. I always end up being so full and exhausted after one of these. I have to admit though, the cocktails were not as good. I remember getting this really Kool Aid like red cocktail that alarmed me a bit because it was so artificially red. 

This place is definitely a place to celebrate a special occasion and show someone that you care. The staff makes you feel special and the place is really classy. I have a tendency to "steal" spoons at restaurants, but stopped myself here because their utensils are customized and designed by a butcher. Oh how beautiful their silverware was. I really wanted to cop one, but I thought I would be talking to an actual cop if I did.

Innovative presentations, an astounding mix of flavors, with impeccable service and tastefully appointed dining room. I was blown away from the dining experience, and my only regret is not having tried this place sooner. 

And on top of that - the waiter is knowledgeable and helpful in recommendations for gluten free dishes. They also offer gluten free toast with a butter that's to die for, and I absolutely loved my amazingly aromatic quail main dish. 

Look forward to coming back - before they get their other Michelin stars and the price jumps up - I can't imagine this place staying at just a single star.

Hungry cat approves, and starts scheduling her next return date ASAP.

A blood donation beforehand might cover the cost. But you can always make more blood.

Dropped in for a first-time post-theater bar menu meal.  Beef tartare, fennel mushroom pizza, sausage and pretzel bread.  It sound so mundane without the hemorrhage of flowery adjectives. 

But it is delicate and fabulous. Perfected tastes and flavors savored in a beautiful setting.   Plan to eat slow and bask.  It's really that good. 


Oh, the pictures do no justice. But the perfect glamour food photos hardly matter in magazines nor yelp.  Can't eat the screen.   But sniff close and smell the fennel.

Wonderful presentation and service. They print out the menu for you to take home too. I was so full I couldn't finish their signature chocolates at the end. Right across from Bryant Park. Fancy but not stuffy. 

Note: You have to take the stairs down one flight to go to the bathroom.

The service was excellent but the food was disappointing. None of the breads were special. The lobster entree had the taste of the lobster overridden by the sauce.  The bread with hog lard was tasteless.  There are many special restaurants in New York; to my taste this is not one of them!

Their marketing team reached out, and we finally connected after several tries. The team at GK really seems to care about the customer experience, and while acknowledging that there were several hiccups in the service that evening, I got the impression that they took the feedback seriously, wanted to improve and would take pains to ensure no-one else would have a similar service experience - as i noted in prior review - food was excellent. 

After the conversation, i felt assured that this would not happen again to other diners and have gone from - never again - to weighing whether to return to give them another chance to prove themselves.
Delicious date night dinner celebrating their 2nd Michelin Star and our first night in NYC! I highly recommend the chef tasting menu and the cocktails are not to be missed.

One of my most favorite restaurants in NYC now.
Highly recommended for dinner tasting menu with wine pairing. The service is fantastic and the food is wow!!!

The only thing I didn't like was the appetizers. Shiso covered with white chocolate was my least favorite dish that night. And three welcoming bites were wired. But other than that all the dishes were fabulous!!!!

The main course is amazing.

Try all the bread. Every single bread is a masterpiece.

All the staff members seem to be very happy smiling and attentive. Very professional.

This was an amazing experience from the second we walked in and were warmly greeted. The ambiance was just right - tables well appointed with comfortable seating. The service was professional, friendly, and knowledgeable about what they were serving. The food was delicious- I especially liked the seared fois gras. We had the four course menu with wine pairings and it was absolutely delightful. This is worth a revisit.

Wonderful dining experience. Ambience is classic yet not prestigious. Service was solid. Very knowledgeable. Sommelier was first class. Competitive with Daniel restaurant. He was very strong on wines from southern rhone. The dishes were good yet flavours blended. Nothing tremendously unique. Also, was the food truly inspired from Alsace? I didn't get that sense. On a side note, please be prepared for a 3-4 hour experience. Net net likely a 3 1/2 out of five. 

Enjoy!!

Holy cow!  My colleague and I sat at the Chef's table last night in the kitchen. Incredible experience to watch the symphony of food play out.  The terrific service started with the friendly check-in with the hostess and coatcheck. The wait staff were attentive, polite and professional. Nancy Schumann and Chef Joe Anthony provided great food and service.  We had the nine course tasting menu with wine pairings by Philippe Sauriat. But let me be clear, the food is the center piece of the experience... tasty, fun and inventive, yet not over the top.  Some chefs try too hard and get overly experimental when customers just want very good, tasty food. Gabriel Kreuther delivers. Treat yourself...HIGHLY recommend.

Pristine experience fit for royalty. My experience at Gabriel Kreuther was an unforgettable one. The concept is so well thought out, and every detail executed to perfection. The dishes and cutlery alone were an experience. I didn't confirm but I'm pretty sure they used Cutipol silverware which is my favorite! You must do at least a 4 course pre fixe, which includes a first, second, and third course, followed by dessert. I loved how many people they had working there because this allowed for the restaurant to work flawlessly, as a well oiled machine, and everyone- from the sommelier to the back waiters and beyond- was on point. The dishes, of course, were perfection. Each dish was elegantly crafted, the chef creating flavors I had never even dreamt of! Everything was superbly balanced, and although I am usually extremely critical, I wouldn't have changed a thing. Chef Kreuther's expertly polished French techniques shone bright in every bite. Might I add as well, we were celebrating my mother's birthday and were greeted with a hand written happy birthday note from the chef which we thought was a very nice touch. They also brought out a lovely candle adorned dessert with her name handwritten in chocolate. I cannot wait to return to this heaven on earth place!

Gabriel Kreuther is exactly what I imagine when I think fine dining. Service, atmosphere, interior was all immaculate and tasteful, while the food was all either delicious or at least different. Our table chose to opt in for the six course meal, and the chef thoughtfully gave us two different dishes per course so that we can try more of the menu. The staff was very accommodating, even when a slightly tipsy friend who did not have a reservation arrived they pulled up a chair and included him in the final course for dessert. All in all would recommend to someone who wanted to go to a nicer place for a special occasion.

Spectacular in every way. The service was unparalleled.  My husband treated me to an amazing experience here to celebrate a milestone birthday. Completely unforgettable.  Deserving of every accolade! Splurge!

What a wonderful experience! The restaurant is absolutely stunning, exactly what you would expect from a fine dining restaurant. It's actually not that large but the bar/lounge area is available for some seating.

The service was wonderful as they were professional and very helpful. I ordered the 2 course lunch, starting with the hamachi tartare and the roasted fluke. The hamachi was absolutely delicious although I wasn't sure how you're supposed to eat it. I think you were you are supposed to use your hands instead of a fork. The fluke was cooked to perfection brussells sprouts and bacon, while in a light mushroom sauce.

Highly recommend for a special occasion or a business lunch if you want to impress.
Excellent food.  Trout w roe was by far the best, but everything we had was amazing and we loved it.  The service was the best we've had yet!

Came here in different seasons of the year, the most memorable dish was the "four seasons" from the spring menu - unique, colorful and one of the a kind plating. Flavor wise my favorite is the hamachi/foie gras/black truffle "sandwich", apparently a menu classic available for a la carte in the lounge area. 
If you're a petite person, highly recommend the 6-course tasting menu over 9-course. Ordered 9 and couldn't properly enjoy the main entree which came on last right before the dessert. Service was...solid, could be better though comparing to other restaurants in the same category. The lighting is a bit brighter than most other French restaurants, but we enjoyed looking at the modern art on the wall.

My friend and I stopped by Gabriel Kreuther since we were in the area and had always wanted to try this restaurant. This review is for the bar seating not for the main dining room. The bar menu is typical bar foods and we had the beef tartare, shishito peppers, and potatoes. All met my expectations but if you're looking for a full dinner, the bar area will not be for you. 

The unexpected highlight of the evening was speaking with the Sommelier. We were looking for a bottle of orange wine (a rarer find on wine lists) and he detailed the options for us. He checked on us a few times to make sure we were enjoying the bottle and at the end of our meal, he kindly sent over two glasses of champagne! 

For a last minute dinner choice, the service exceeded expectations. Looking forward to returning for their main dining room soon!

If i could give GK 10 stars I would.  From the restaurant atmosphere to the service to the food everything was just absolutely perfect!!! I came on my birthday and they left a handwritten birthday card on the table which added such a personal touch!  We did the 6 course tasting between me and my husband and they let us each try different dish so we actually ended up with more than 6 dishes and i cannot even pick my fav becos all the dishes are devine.

I absolutely love the presentation of each dish, they are all presented in small cocottes/ textured plates etc and serve semi table side which are so charming! All the flavors are very sophisticated and simple.  I briefly mentioned that I dont eat pork but my husband does and they were so accomodating, they let my husband try some of their pork dishes while making sure there was no pork in mine.  GK deserves their two michelin stars (they should get 3!!)

This is such a memorable dinner I will never forget!

I had my wife's 40th bday dinner here - we chose the chefs menu (6 course)... amazing!!! The service and personal attention is really something that needs to be recognized as not many Michelin type restaurants provide in this way. The staff is professional but are very down to earth and fun - they make you feel really comfortable (Not strict and stuffy). They were beyond accommodating with adjustments to the menu for all 6 of us (you are not locked into what you see - but I did call a few days ahead to share likes and dislikes). Our som Matt was extremely helpful in choosing wines. Paul Lee (manager) was also soo helpful/fun and gave us a tour of the kitchen.
The food is over the top and so is the experience!!! our guests who are also foodies - said this was the best Michelin rated restaurant experience they have ever had- I agree.
Thank you again!

We had an amazing evening here. They have a great selection of wines. The food was super delicious and the service was impeccable. The four course dinner is 155 and they also offer wine pairing. We were seated facing the kitchen which was very cool because we got to see everything cooking in action and Gabriel himself! We had the himachi black truffle and langostino tartare. I loveeeeed the langostino tartare! Omg it just melts in your mouth. For the second dish I had the sturgeon tart and they served it covered in smoke and it smelled and tasted delicious! We then had the lamb for two for the main dish. We had the chocolate and grape sorbet for desserts. Such a great meal! Would recommend it for anyone who likes French food but hates the hassle of sitting for a ten course meal! This place has done a great job with both food and service. A well deserved Michelin one star.

This is true fine dining, with extremely attentive service and elegant food. I got a rosemary martini which was as smooth as silk. The two different foie gras preparations were spectacular. But not everything quite lived up to my expectations. The citrus cobia was not really special, to me, and my companions 4-cheese ravioli was also a bit average. I did love the charcoal grilled squab, and my companion loved the cedar-planked trout. I choose Texture for dessert, and while the pistachio and grape ice cream/sorbets were delicious, the large swaths of meringue overwhelmed the dessert and added excessive sweetness. Our waiter was chatty and very non-intimidating, but maybe a bit *too* chatty. To be honest, this is the first time I have ever eaten at a 2-Michelin-star restaurant, and it was a very enjoyable experience with many amazing little taste sensations, including special breads and butters with each course, several amuse bouches, and a lovely wine pairing. But there were a few places in which the meal could have been even better.

It pains me to downgrade my review, but I mulled it over for a couple of weeks and have to do it. 

Let me preface with this: the food is still outstanding and my favorite dish from 2016 was still freaking amazing (langoustine tartare)!! Please check out my photos, you won't regret it. The amuse-bouches were a little too funky for us (everything based on some form of chocolate) but the rest of the dishes were great. The interesting approach was that since my wife and I each did the 6-course meal, we would have some courses that were the same, and other dishes were different. The idea behind this was so that we could share, and everyone could maintain their dietary preferences. 

Upon arrival, my wife loved the decor (as I did the first time I came as well) and the host team welcomed us perfectly. We were lead to our table and greeted by the service staff, again perfect. This is where things got a little weird. Our server was very aggressive on the upsell - used-car salesman style. We were there to celebrate so we were ready to splurge but we didn't really have a chance to let her know our preferences. She would interrupt us and make suggestions, and every single one would involve an upgrade. We had indicated that we were interested in the 4-course prix-fixe but before we could ask some questions about that menu, she directly jumped to the 9-course carte blanche menu as a better representation of the chef's prowess. That makes sense, but my wife can't eat everything and there's some dishes that I've had before. My wife and I had debated between the 4-course and the 6-course anyway, so we mentioned that we toyed with the idea of the 6-course and she basically went on further about 6 courses being better than 4 (OK we get it!). Hoping to end this so we could start enjoying our dinner, we decided to go with the 6-course...But again, the upsell didn't stop. It was a celebratory event, did we want to start with champagne? Sure, I wanted to cheers with my wife so we said "of course!" She recommended three options, which of course turned out to be the three highest priced options on the menu (would have been nicer to have been shown ALL the options from the drinks menu, we know our champagne). "Did you want caviar?" No thank you. "Did you want the white truffle?" no thank you (We went to Per Se the night before and were drowned in white truffle so we were pretty set). "The white truffle cost can be split, so you guys can both have the vessel dish and we can share the shavings between you two!" No thank you and that wasn't the issue anyway. The one good thing though is that when I requested to have the wine pairing, I opted with the classic pairing and she didn't trying selling me on the higher priced pairing. 

She did make sure to get my wife's dietary preferences eventually but the ordering process went from being a casual exchange to a full on sales spiel. It didn't feel like the service was there to enhance our experience and make us happy, it just felt like they wanted to sell us the full thing and call it a day regardless of what we had in mind. 
After this rough start, things went smoothly again. The sommelier came through and introduced himself and poured my first drink while he explained to me how many glasses I'd be getting, and how much in each glass. In the end, for $105, the pairing was well worth it. Many interesting wines and nicely paired with the dishes that came out. Unfortunately, another issue here. From the beginning I notified the sommelier that I didn't care for dessert/sweet wines. He started asking for my preferences, asking if a port would work but I told him that I feel the same way about port so that was a negative. At that point he said "No problem, I will bring out champagne...Champagne goes with everything!" I was happy about that and agreed, and went on with our meal. Just over 2 hours later, when dessert came out, so did the dessert wine. At that point, we had to leave right after dessert for another appointment, so I didn't feel like arguing or sending it back so I just drank it. 

Throughout the meal, our server was often visiting in the beginning, but halfway through the meal she was less available as the sommelier would still check on us periodically. She did come by to bring our dishes and present them, and she did do a great job with that. After dessert, about 2.5 hours into our meal, we were ready for the check. For about 15 minutes, my wife and I sat there staring blankly at the dining room with nothing but water on our table. When our server finally came she just brought the check and said please take your time - didn't ask us if we wanted anything else. In the service team's defense, we didn't specify that we needed to be out by a certain time and the next round of diners was arriving. 

I guess they were probably too busy upselling the new diners to notice us. While the food was absolutely 2 Michelin stars and service was somewhat precise, this whole thing bummed me out.

This is supposed to be a schnitzel; however, it was an over cooked carbonized sheet of $34 garbage.  3 bites and I am tapped out. Bartender asks if I want something  else. Me: ahh well what is not burnt on the menu? That is inedible.  
  Manage comes over - sir I understand this was not cooked to your expectations.  WTF. Didn't look at the food. Didn't ask what was wrong. Didn"t look at the returned dish.  Just passive statements about my tastes. Why is that is was my expectations that were not met -- especially at this fancy pants facade?  You see at Gabriel it's your issue not theirs. Manager let's me know that I won't be charged for the item. Wow thanks.  I feel awesome now.  Then he proceeds to tell me that he likes this place so much that he quit and came back. Me... Man I am hungry and you fed me some garbage and now I need to lean into your backstory. Me hangry, you not getting it... Then another manager comes over. No context transfer between the two.  Hi -- I understand you had some issues with your meal. YES!  Check the dishwasher ask the line cook ask the other manager. We have a nice chat about customer service and then we laugh about where I should go to eat as at this point I am done with Gabriel's spot. So I start typing this review to channel some energy and hope that if others hit this craptastic service and food you have some perspective about where you are sitting.  I offered to share this directly with the chef, but manager number two laughed at me assuring that he would read it online.  Have a goodnight Gabriel - I am headed to Ai Fiori or maybe to just get a slice from some guy who actually gives a f+_k about their house and guests.

This place deserves its Michelin stars! From outstanding food to amazing service, they really try to spoil you. 

I came with my wife, sister and brother in law who were visiting from overseas. 

We were seated promptly and ordered drinks. We started with appetizers and enjoyed them. My sister isn't a big fan of raw seafood and when the appetizer arrived she didn't eat. The staff at restaurant noticed and offered to bring something else. My sister being said no, but they brought an amazing mushroom flat bread.

I loved the hamachi, Farro crusted fish and lamb chops. The desert was amazing too!

The service was amazing and one of the best I have seen in a while. The staff went out of the way make us comfortable.

** Review for the bar, not the restaurant 
If you are looking for a classy drink venue around midtown after work, the bar at GK guarantees a Michelin deux etoiles experience. The location is easy to access. Atmosphere and service are best fit for business occasions. It happened to be not busy at all on a Friday afternoon. That said, a reservation is still recommended just to be on the safe side. 

The most memorable item on the table was the "rendez-vous" cocktail. The spicy aftertaste from the jalapeno is not so unique, but when combined with hibiscus, honey and a strong dose of rhubarb, the end product is worth at least 10 minutes to take in and think through. Only recommend for those who are adventurous enough. 

The "now and then" is also unique but much easier to take in - a strong yet well-balanced mix of gin, chartreuse and vermouth. Definitely less layered compared the previous one. 

The bread sticks, not usually something one pays much attention to, are surprisingly delicious. It is the black and white sesame seeds that cover the sticks that make them so special.

I took a good friend here for his birthday dinner, and it was an exceptional experience from the moment we stepped in till the moment we walked out. We had dropped by the Gabriel Kreuther chocolate shop next door before arriving for our dinner and picked up some treats - when we were seated we were greeted with a hand signed card wishing my companion an lovely birthday, and since the restaurant was quite warm, they took our bags of chocolates to store in their fridge while we enjoyed our dinner. The service was accommodating, without even a hint of the pushiness some others had experienced. The chef was kind enough to allow me to select a couple of specific dishes that I had been so excited to try as part of our 6 course tasting. In fact, they gave us each different dishes on some courses so that we could enjoy more of the menu.

Rendes-vous cocktail: Volcan di me Tierra Tequila * Rhubarb * Honey * Hibiscus * Jalapeno -  exquisitely layered cocktail that was tart, fruity, and kissed with a hint of spice.

Alsatian Kougelhopf with whipped chive fromage blanc - What a way to start a dinner. Dreams are made of these savory little delights, perfectly paired with ethereal clouds of fromage blanc. We ate every slice of this despite knowing we might be overstuffed later and suffer from regret. But my friend said, "You'll REALLY regret it tomorrow if you don't eat every bite now" - and was 100% right. If only I could pick this up for breakfast daily. I wanted to sneak into the kitchen and steal a tray of these warm little treasures to hoard at home. I'm a little bit obsessed.

Amuse Bouche: sticky rice topped with mango, pickled vegetables and barley tea - this trio of tiny starters was a gentle nod to the approaching lunar new year. Standout here was the meaty barley tea, it was a lovely way to prepare for the next course. 

HAMACHI, BLACK TRUFFLE & FOIE GRAS MILLE-FEUILLE with celery * grapes * truffle vinaigrette - our first course was lovely, though the foie and truffle flavors did compete with the hamachi a bit.

LANGOUSTINE TARTARE with flying fish roe * salty fingers * cauliflower-macadamia purée - this was Perfection - this was our favorite course of the night.

CITRUS CURED BLUE COBIA with watermelon radish * wasabi * yuzu coulis - citrusy and refreshing, this is a lovely course for summer, but was completely overshadowed by the langoustine tartare.

In between the courses, another bread dish was served with butter (wheat maybe?) - while still warm from the oven, and lovely - nothing compares to the kugelhoupf, and this was overshadowed completely by it

STURGEON & SAUERKRAUT TART with caviar mousseline * applewood smoke - it's no surprise that this stunner is a signature dish here. The tart is brought to the table under a glass, and when the glass is lifted, smoke swirls around the table evoking fireplace memories of winters past. Tender and smoky, this is beautiful and delicious.

SEARED SULLIVAN COUNTY FOIE GRAS - combined with duck prosciutto and chanterelle mushrooms, this was pure decadence and an absolute joy

Another course of bread punctuated the dinner, this time two lovely rosemary rolls shaped like roses with a sort of meat lardo type spread. I had one bite, and then had to tap out given everything else we had already indulged in

GRILLED BLACK ANGUS BEEF TENDERLOIN with roasted salsify * hazelnuts * red wine jus - tender indeed, along with short rib, deceptively small looking - I could not finish this and had to make the birthday boy finish this (no complaints from him though!)

HARVEST * PEAR * CARAMEL with pear tatin * cider sorbet * caramel crémeux - I love pear desserts, and this was a welcome contrast to all the richness we had been enjoying.

DECADENT * CHOCOLATE * CARAMEL with mixed media crumble * chocolate mousse * caramel ice cream - I really enjoyed the contrasting textures of this dessert, and if you're a mousse fan, this will not disappoint.
 
In addition to our dessert courses, a separate hazelnut dacquoise dessert was brought out to celebrate my friend's birthday - complete with lit candle and chocolate well wishes written on the plate and garnished with sugar shards.

And still there was more!

orange cake: I failed to catch the name of these itty bitty bites, and they weren't on the menu, but they tasted like tiny bites of orange fairy cake. In my fantasy, a bowl of these decadent little morsels would sit on a bed-side table - perpetually refilling itself. 

Last, and certainly not least, a cocoa pod housed a couple of pieces of Gabriel Kreuther to round out to the night, I think we had the mexican chocolate and the vanilla, but to be honest, you can't go wrong with any of their chocolates.

This is everything I love about fine dining without any of the pretentiousness - I'm definitely a huge fan, and this is a great special occasion restaurant for special people in your life. I definitely want to return to enjoy seasonal changes!

I would definitely recommend all people who want to experience fine dining + Michelin stars while you are in NYC like me. This is the exact place and maybe even better than what I imagine fine dining in NYC. Service was great + Wine was perfect... Of course food was more than amazing.

YUM! Service, food and ambiance were all top notch here. The icing on the cake: they brought me a little mini coat rack to stand next to our table to hang my coat on. I've never seen this before! Only reason not giving 5 stars is the fact they were almost too attentive - several servers came over to us asking for our order / if we needed anything immediately after another just left. I liked the attention but was hard to talk with all the interruptions. Definitely a splurge so go with work if you can!

What a surprising experience! Discovering the culinary treasures of Alsace in NY...! For a French food amateur, it was really refreshing to discover a French Chef who offers a different angle.
Service was great and intellectually exciting, teaching us so much about the region's traditions. The wines, the tastes and the designs on the plates took us to a peculiar experience to recommend strongly.

Having been to many Michelin star Restaurants around the world and in the city, I can assure you Gabriel Kreuther is a class act. From the service on the phone to the entire evening itself, the entire staff was superb. The food was spectacular and the cocktail delicious. Absolutely worth the trip. Will be returning.
Great bar area if you need access to top notch food and drink with no reservation. You should also love sausage.

This the best restaurant I have been to in years. I have traveled around the World but now I can have great French food in New York. GABRIEL KREUTHER at 41 West 42nd St between 5th &6th Ave was a fabulous lunch. As you enter this fabulous Decor restaurant the Hostess gave me a smile. Right then I said this restaurant is great. The table for a single PERFECT. As soon as you sit you receive a taste from the Chef - Delicious. After looking online I wondered if the food wood taste great like the beautiful pictures. Well, YESeven better. 
The SEARED SULLIVAN COUNTRY FOIE GRAS was unbelievable delicious. The taste so good. It melted in your mouth. It was pure Heaven. I tried to eat slowly but couldn't it was too good. 
I ordered the FARRO CRUSTED BLACK BASS. I would give this main course an A++++. Succulent, with a crust that was so tasty along with black trumpets, braised Brussels sprouts that was finely chopped that was flavored perfectly that it blended together with the shellfish emulsion. WOW!!! Amazing taste. 
The dessert was also from Heaven. How they do this beautiful plating it's a work of art. The ETHEREAL* CITRUS * HERB yogurt PANNA COTTA surly a work of art. I just stared at it to try to see just how it was assembled. It was simply delicious and the tartness was perfect after such a  fantastic meal. Wish I could have personally thanked the Chef but Jonathan Garcia, server Captain was great explaining to me the beautiful plate settings. He was plus I must say ALL the staff was professional and lovely. All seemed happy working at such a beautiful restaurant. The red wine which was recommended to me was sue peen. GI Gevrey Chambertin was great with the fish and Foie Gras. 
Can't wait to return to try their Cavier and Truffles. Thank you Gabriel Kreuther for such a fabulous lunch on a great sunny warm winter day. 
Anita Trottman still thinking about my lunch.

Had the following and it was all delicious:

Pork tenderloin
Seared foie gras
Mandarin chocolate pb and strawberry panna cotta desserts
Two types of bread, amuse bouche, and petit fours

Lovely, friendly service. Very accommodating if you need to finish lunch in a certain amount of time.

Majority of my votes go towards the friendly and knowledgeable staff and the cocktails, and slightly less towards the food (Feb 2019 dinner menu).

Here is why: 
A michelin star menu means everything is supposed to blow your mind in terms of flavor right? Not all of my 4 courses did. 
The desserts, the Foie Gras Terrine, and the Langoustine Tartare were amazing! (too bad you can't just go for these two because they dont do a la carte lol)
Foie Gras Terrine is filled with flavors and makes you wonder how all the ingredients come together. But I didnt understand all the fuss about the signature dish Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart. It tasted like an egg benedict on a bed of crispy tortilla. 
The Australian Lamb and Maine Lobster entrees were tender and good size portions, but again the flavor was nothing unique that would make me think about them hours later...how I'm thinking about the the Foie Gras Terrine right now!
Also, what's with not having the same dinner menu as an a la carte option at the bar like how other fine dining restaurants are doing? (i.e. Daniel). I was so full at the end of my 4 courses because I also wanted to enjoy the bread.. I shouldnt have to feel forced to do a gazillion courses just to experience a fine dining restaurant. 
The dim lit ambiance by the bar/lounge felt extra romantic than the main restaurant area..I recommend going here but for the bar area because the cocktails are fantastic, with a more intimate vibe :)

I am very disappointed with the way I was treated yesterday by the maître d' and front of house staff.  I used to be a regular at Gabriel Kreuther; but after the treatment my husband and I received, I will no longer spend my money at the restaurant.  I wanted to sit at the bar for a glass of champagne to celebrate Valentine's day, the bar was empty 7 seats were available and I was told that I could not sit at the bar due to reservations.  I've celebrated Valentine's day at the restaurant every year since it opened.  I had my birthday party in the lounge with over 85 people and was told that the restaurant had never been that packed -- that they had a photographer come and take pictures so they could use it for content.  I am simply painting the picture that I am a frequent patron, and have never been treated the way I was treated by the prior front of house staff.  I am not sure if I was turned away because I was African American or another reason, but the staff was beyond dismissive and rude.  I hope the restaurant provides coaching to the new staff because the restaurant is great and the chef is amazing.

If it wasn't a thousand dollar meal I would probably giver it more then 1 star but given the price tag I have no choice .  At the bar I told the bartender I wanted a cocktail but couldn't decide I told him I don't like heavy dark liquors and wanted something light and fruity.  I'm going to assume he must not have heard me because he made dark liquor martini.  Thankfully he didn't charge me and swapped it out for a glass of wine.  Now on to dinner we picked the chefs course tasting menu with wine pairing.  The waiter had a very heavy accent and couldn't  understand what he was saying so had no idea what he was serving us.  In Addition my friend mentioned she had an allergy to coconut they served us an intermezzo made with coconut.  Thankfully my friend realized what it was before she ate it.  None of the courses stood out for me nothing was amazing.  They didn't even ask us if we wanted coffee and grabbed the check out of my hand before I was done with the meal.  I also told the waiter how much I love their chocolate and could I take it to go m, and would he mind giving me extra pieces.  Well after paying $1,000 and nearly killing my friend with coconut he couldn't even be bothered to give me a few extra pieces.  What a disgrace.  I do have to say that I love the chocolatier and is by far the best chocolate I've ever had.  My advice skip eating here and just get the chocolate .

My favorite aspects of the dinner weren't the dishes though some of my favorites were the Green-Walk Hatchery Trout On Cedar Plank & Four Cheese Ravioli (pictured below). What caught my eye the most were the plating options & presentation it served as a nice compliment for the modern perspective on the traditional Alsace dishes. What I found to be the tastiest at the dinner is one of the opening bread dishes called kugelhopf. Physically it is reminiscent of an angel cake, but it has one of the most subtle yet savory tastes with just enough garlic to prepare your palate for what's to come. Overall I would visit Gabriel Kreuther again during another season to see what they have to offer I'll also make an effort to visit Kreuther Chocolate next time.​
I've wanted to go to Gabriel Kreuther for so long, and my boyfriend took me here for Valentine's Day! Our waiter was super attentive. Loved the foie gras and truffle carbonara with yolk.

Wife's birthday dinner before a show. They knocked it out of the park and wasn't expecting anything less. Excellent food- so much variety and everything was incredibly tasty. The service was impeccable. Everyone here we encountered is a consummate professional. Quite expensive, but worth every penny. Highly recommended for a special occasion or business meal where you're looking to impress.

I've been to this restaurant three times and have loved every experience. Once for drinks, dessert, and finally the food!

Although I haven't had a chance to dine in the main dining room(recommend making res), I love the bar area. It's quite large with booths, tables, and of course bar seats. Bar menu is different from dining area menu but nevertheless great options!

Hen of the woods flambée: mushrooms are so good, perfectly cooked and slightly crunchy. Flatbread isn't too doughy, loved this. 

Duck confit with risotto: I believe our server said risotto(?) the grain tastes more like farro in texture, had more of a bite to it. The duck is so so good. Super tender meat and loved the sauce accompanying it. 

For dessert, you really can't go wrong with anything. I've had the apple pastry dessert, chocolate, and the beignets. 

I loved every single thing I've tried here and I seriously doubt you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. 

Service is amazing, friendly, love love Gabriel Kreuther.

I have been to many 2 and 3 star Michelin restaurants. This was my first visit to Gabriel Kreuther but if the food and service are always this good they'll be a three star next year. Was just at Le Bernardin on Saturday and it was awesome but GK just as amazing. Michael at the bar was charming and attentive and Chris (manager?) was really friendly and knowledgeable. We sat at the bar and had an amazing lunch. The space is gorgeous and the vibe is not pretentious but still very upscale. An amazing find. I only hope they don't get too popular!

Great food and incredible service. The staff are very friendly and I could tell they take a lot of effort. The dining room is huge and open, and very pink. The food tastes great while being interesting. Definitely deserve its stars.
Very knowledge stuff with delicious food ,one of my favorite restaurant in nyc now ,highly recommend .

Great service, delicious food but not memorable compared to other two-star Michelin restaurants. 

One interesting thing to share: the piece of Japanese newspaper under the tea cup had content about gynecological disease, which doesn't make sense at all for people who can read and understand...

We celebrated our anniversary there last month.
We ordered the pre theatre prix fixe menu.
If you choose that menu, make sure to arrive a little bit 6.30pm. My husband sat down at 6.33 and they. gave us the regular menu. We requested the pre theatre and we finally got it but the waiter looked at his watch, which I didn't like.

Price very good for this menu, $115
Their signature starter, the tart was wonderful
The fish and deserts were good 
The desert with the nice cake was amazing 
The bread was excellent 
We liked the little additional things they brought
The China was very refined
Service was very good
We had an additional desert  served to celebrate our birthday 

The decor was nice but to me a but a little bit too simple and a lot of people were there for business. They could enhance the experience with few more candles and flowers on each table 

It was overall a beautiful experience

The two stars are for the good service - the food was not good haha my friend and I were both very disappointed. I had read such great reviews I was really looking forward to dinner. Would not recommend. They were super nice though. When we left they handed us packed leftovers and we told them we didn't pack anything and the hostess said oh they packed up your stuff regardless. So we said oh ok brought it home and saw it wasn't our food!!!! So gross!
We have sat down for an hour and still no food. I'm terribly hungry. The bar area did not allow for us to have their real menu. It's been a disaster so far. I'm very upset.

Brought my mother here for a special dinner while she was visiting, and wow, we were so blown away. Service is impeccable, and I really have to thank the staff for treating my mother like a queen. 

We opted for the 6-course Chef's Tasting menu for $195, and we absolutely loved the experience. My mother is a great home cook herself, and is often hard to impress because many restaurants make dishes that we could easily replicate at home.. but every dish we got here was truly a culinary travel through the chef's creative mind. You cannot find these dishes anywhere else.

I also really appreciated that they took note of my dietary restrictions. The chef made each of our dishes differently to accommodate.. which means we got to try double the number of dishes! :) 

Highly recommend Gabriel Kreuther. This is a meal/experience to remember!

I went to Gabriel Kreuther with 3 others as a more intimate celebration for a birthday and I was very impressed.

The service here is phenomenal. The staff is highly attentive and extremely courteous. The servers go into careful detail and pride when explaining each of the courses and they leave you ample time to enjoy each meal as well as time between meals - we spent around 3-4 hours there for a 4 course meal. The food here was stellar - Gabriel Kreuther certainly stands to deserve its Michelin Star rating. And as it was for a birthday, the cake that they provided was perhaps one of the best cakes I've had.

I would highly recommend Gabriel Kreuther to any foodies and those looking for an amazing experience all around.

It was unfortunate that we couldn't try the tasting menu because our group of 10 people had to be seated at the bar section and apparently we cannot order the tasting menu there. 

Maybe we would have broken our group to 2 smaller groups so we could have moved to the main dining room but we were so devastated upon the news that we couldn't think straight. 

And I looked around the restaurant. It was the Friday lunch during March madness so it was not that the restaurant was fully packed anyway. So I don't really understand why we couldn't get the tasting menu just because they couldn't sit us at the main dining room because of the party size. It was like we were penalized by showing up with a big group of people.

Wow...just wow. Service was exemplary and food was out of this world. We did the six course chef's tasting with wine pairing. The chef for a few courses bought our table two different dishes and two different wines, so we got to experience so much more. The sommelier's wine choices were phenomenal, and he gave us a background of each one from the type of grape to the winemaker to the area it is from. Decor was beautiful as well! The kitchen was immaculate. Thanks to the staff and chef for one of our most memorable, if not most memorable, dining experiences we have ever had!
The food can be a little out of your comfort zone (foie gras is one of the dishes I had) but very delicious food and very attentive staff! I highly recommend!

Dined here March 29, 2019. Kitchen Table experience was exceptional. As many reviewers noted, one samples almost twice as many tastings which was not expected and incredible. There were a lot of interesting items that were new to our palates. Ordered the rendezvous cocktail (enjoyed the kick of the little pieces of jalapeno) and sampled the blanche de bruxelles beer (very refreshing) and the 2014 Cecile Tremblay Chambolle-Musigny Les Cabottes wine. Personal favs of the meal were the following: kougelhopf with chive fromage; caviar quail egg buttermilk mousseline; foie gras terrine & pecan praline; citrus cured blue cobia; farro crusted black bass (not huge on cooked fish but enjoyed this); local emmer pasta; the skin on the 14 day aged LI duck breast got devoured (normally the fatty parts get cut off & discarded but this was yummy); the decadent chocolate passion fruit (the chocolate crème that oozed out of the frozen top portion was divine - although many people enjoyed the ethereal rhubarb Turkish tea dessert); and the coffee cremo with speculaas cookie. The rosemary buckwheat roll was probably the least liked by the table (it was a bit hard) although the lard was interesting and worth a try. 

Staff was superb here with one exception (see paragraph below regarding sommelier). Our Table Captain Luis was really amazing! We got to take photos with the chefs and even got a grand tour at the end (taking us throughout the restaurant). Highly recommend this place - definitely well worth the money. We were NOT hungry afterwards (as some people feared beforehand). One receives the level of service you'd expect from a fine dining establishment without the stuffiness or pretentiousness. A handwritten signed card from GK himself was also given to celebrate the evening along with a scrumptious financier cake. It's also really cool to have given us our "soigne" that the Chef used for the meal. The tableware was unique especially the dinnerware which was different each course. Everyone walked out with some "goodies" and a nicely printed souvenir menu to commemorate the meal.

However, there was one low point to the evening: a bottle of wine was ordered at the table, and it was expected that both the bottle and the cork would make its way back to the table after it was uncorked; however, the cork got tossed. Typically, especially for special occasions, the cork is kept as a memento; however, he was rather flippant after the inquiry about the cork in saying one could "write him up". That attitude was not well received.

Where to begin? This is really one of our top dining experiences in the city (anywhere really). It's spendy - but the experience and quality are unsurpassed. Though formal fine dining, the staff strive to make the experience approachable, relaxed and inviting. Gabriel Kreuther exudes luxury without being too forced; they make fine dining comfortable. Even the space embodies this approach. Though white table cloths abound, the modern, airy design with its whimsical pops, averts the sleepy formality so many of its competitors exhibit. The cuisine is impeccable in conception, execution and presentation. No gimmicks here, a truly honest approach. Some may deride this as 'unmemorable' (wowed these days means a cool Instagram post of an edible something or other) - but I think just the opposite. Instead of hiding behind wizardry, the kitchen nails technical aspects and presentation is beautiful. Wine list is incredible, with a myriad of French gems, and we love Phillipe the wine director. So glad they earned a second Michelin star, well deserved!

Atmosphere
- Elegant luxe, a real fine dining sensibility, but with a refreshingly modern approach.
-Light and airy, high ceilings and windows unto Bryant Park.
-Formal, though not imposing. Most patrons are quite well dressed, but suit/tie are not mandatory.

Food
Chef Kreuther's food is flawlessly executed and superbly balanced. He has a real talent in mixing textures to achieve interest (even in the plating!). Enjoying his creations is a real treat, and we find the four course prix fixe ($155) to be an amazing progression, with harmonious components and precise implementation. Tasting menus ('Carte Blanche') are also available. We enjoyed:

- Hamachi, Black Truffle & Foie Gras Mille-Feuille (celery, grapes, truffle vinaigrette): How creative! A classic at GK - sense of the sea, but all of the flavors are delicately balanced.
- Foie Gras Terrine & Pecan Praline (cider poached quince, pomegranate, chestnut cornbread): Love the use of texture against the foie, particularly the praline. Elements pair so nicely and really evoke the season. Perhaps my all time favorite foie gras!

- Seared Sullivan County Foie Gras (apricot preserve, smoked prosciutto, amaretto gastrique): Another excellent use of foie with textural balance, similarly well paired. The smoked prosciutto makes the dish quite unique. More decadent, thought he fruit undertone helps cut through.
- Four Cheese Ravioli (sunchoke broth, bacon, pumpkin seed crumble): Delicate, with a sense of earthiness. Rich, but crunchiness of bacon and crumble avoid monotony. Highly recommend!

- Aged Long Island Duck Breast (salt baked celeriac, eucalyptus, truffle coulis): Served for two, with four separate mini accompaniments. Presented and portioned tableside. Glistening moist and tender. The coulis is insane. Very enjoyable and unique.

- Fragrant (sesame, yuzu caramel-chocolate parfait, halva, yuzu sorbet): Elegant - neither too sweet nor too dense. The yuzu was our favorite element. 
- Ethereal (citrus, herb citrus gelée, herb sphere, yogurt panna cotta): Lives up to the name! A refreshing, and light conclusion. The nuance of flavors is incredible, nothing gets lost.

Beverage
Gabriel Kreuther's wine program is among the best in the city and is filled with treasures. Naturally, it's focused on French selections having depth across regions. The list is extensive, and contains a mix of benchmark names and lesser known producers. Much of the selection is $250+, however there are plenty of sub-$150 bottles interspersed throughout. Also, wine pairings are available for both the prix fixe ($85-130 per person) and tasting menus ($105-230 per person).

We began with the Jean Velut Lumière et Craie Blanc de Blancs ($29/gl) which was outstanding. A range of unique sparkling selections available by the glass ($19-59). With our meal, we absolutely loved the 2009 E. Guigal Vignes de l'Hospice ($330/btl), a stunning Syrah from St Joseph - one of our favorites! To conclude, the 2008 Château Guiraud Sauternes was excellent ($29). You can't go wrong letting the wine team here guide you.

Service
-Incredible! Everyone we encountered in the dining room was warm, friendly, and truly hospitable. The staff really make the experience enjoyable and relaxed.
- Wine Director Philippe Sauriat not only knows his stuff, but is truly passionate about wine and we really love that he shares this passion with the guest.

Creative dish. Five star service. Well deserved Michelin two stars (at a reasonable price). Personal favorites are hamachi/black truffle/foie gras, langoustine tartare, duck breast, and the rhubarb dessert. Crafty chocolate on "chocolate" on "chocolate". Not too impressed by the famous Sturgeon and sauerkraut cart.

In summary, two michellin stars are more than justified for this treasure nestled on the border of Bryant Park, one of my favorite parks. The decor and ambience were both inviting and refined. We prepared our stomachs for the four course pre fixe, which could not have been more satisfying. The langoustine tartare was as satiating as it was transient. We feasted on the grilled black angus beef tenderloin and Australian lamb rack, which were grand. More than anything, one must try the dry aged, Iberian jamon before leaving this life. Dessert more than satisfied our sweet tooths, and service made us feel warm and fuzzy, allowing us to happily give away our dollars. Would recommend.

At one time a favorite. Now has descended to the depths of "who cares" which the pervasive attitude overall. The "bar" menu continues to vanish in variety and quality. The support staff try very hard to lift servers who are less than knowledgeable and who could care less about satisfaction of the patrons. The last three times we dined in the bar the decline was precipitous.

Alsatian Restaurant 
Alsatian Chef
Alsatian Art pieces
Alsatian Stork 

Perfect, divine, extraordinary, excellent, impeccable.
Rustic yet delicate

This restaurant is fantastic. The food, the decor, and the atmosphere is an amazing blend of elegance and comfort. 

We tried a number of items on the menu and were not disappointed by anything. 

The staff was educated and helpful and always right there with whatever we needed. 

GK's surpassed my expectations, even for a New York restaurant where the bar is set high. I will make this a mandatory stop every time I return to the city.

First - LANGOUSTINE TARTARE
Taste: 2/5 a bit salty and a lil bit sweet, but it ended up bitter, for real
Texture: the lobster was really fresh but it's like chewing gum after the first few bites

Second - SEARED SULLIVAN COUNTY FOIE GRAS
Taste: 3.5/5 it tasted okay but the dish was a bit too heavy
Texture: extremely smooth

Third - GRILLED BLACK ANGUS BEEF TENDERLOIN
Taste: 1/5 it came with three tiny pieces of beef in total and one of them was covered in roquefort. They noted that in the menu but I never had roquefort before (should have done some serious research). It turned out awful for me. But if you like blue cheese, you'll definitely enjoy it. The other two pieces were just dry and mediocre. I didn't enjoy the sauces at all.
Texture: see above.

Dessert - DECADENT * CHOCOLATE * PASSION FRUIT
Taste: 2/5 when they say dark chocolate crème, they are really serious about it. Don't even try if you're not a fan of bitter and strong dark chocolate flavors. I didn't really enjoy the mixture of passion fruit and dark chocolate itself, but I appreciate the effort.
Texture: Smooooooth

The service was 4/5, and our waiter offered me a chance to replace my third dish with a duck leg; it was much better than the tenderloin.

My friend who came with me had been there for 3 times, she had a strong feeling that the quality of food couldn't live up to her expectations anymore.

Love this French place so upscale and the food is excellent and service is excellent. My wife love eating there for her birthday, Valentine's Day and lunch. Lol She love there chocolate store next door!!!

Excellent food, somewhat chilly atmosphere, good but not great service.

Went here with two dining companions and had the shorter of the two tasting menus on offer: six courses, plus the obligatory multiple amuse-bouche and dessert bouche. I have a dairy (cow's milk) restriction and the restaurant was good about accommodating me. Unlike some restaurants that charge large for tasting menus and then serve low-cost ingredients like salmon and chicken, GK went with high end ingredients: foie gras for the first course, caviar for the second, white asparagus for the third, a beautiful trout for the fourth and an exception smoked duck breast for the final savory course. We added a cheese course and the server was kind enough to recommend two goat cheeses of the three cheeses offered so I could participate.

The atmosphere is very corporate. The space is repurposed from its original incarnation as part of the cavernous lobby of the Grace Building, and though they've done a decent job with fabrics and materials, the place is still very cool, almost cold in atmosphere. It's also surprisingly noisy for a restaurant with so much fabric to absorb sound. We were tucked into an alcove by the window but the sound from the harder-edged bar area made its way to us.

The service was generally good but we had three notable hiccups, surprising at this price point. First, I arrived after my companions were seated and they were already sipping a glass of wine. I was escorted to the table, made my hellos, and as I was still pulling in my chair the server came over right away, dropped the dinner menus and started to walk away. We had to call her back to ask for a drink for me. No "welcome to GK" or anything from her either.

Second, I had slightly different food from the rest of the table due to my dietary restriction. On one of the middle courses, the server was hellbent on getting in his required speech about what was being served - yes, depending on the course, you get either a short description/list of ingredients OR are subjected to a full-on "here's what you're getting, here's where everything's from, let me tell you the story behind why we do it like this, I'm sure you're interested." Well, we had a speechifying course and the server had put my plate in front of another diner at the table. We all tried to make eye contact and interrupt him, but he was going to get in that speech, dammit, so we had to wait. When he got to the end of the spiel and we corrected him, he all but harrumphed as he moved the dishes. Not even a "so sorry about that", just a petulant rearrangement and he was off.

Third and most egregious, which made me think about bumping GK down to three starts, wine service. One member of our party is a true wine person, and as soon as the sommelier approached, two of us indicated her and said, this is who will be selecting our wine this evening. She and the sommelier had a long involved discussion about Alsatian wines, the wine was chosen.....and then the server comes to show the bottle AND  pour the taste for the only man at the table. C'mon.

Overall I thought this was a very good but not great experience. I loved the food but was less enthusiastic about the less-than-polished service and all the talking that came with the presentation of each course.

Just left this fantastic restaurant..the room is beautiful and the service impeccably superior. We had Tanzia as our server who explained every single delicious tasting that was brought to us. Our water glasses were never empty.  This is an amazing dining experience from start to finish. My husband and I were celebrating my birthday and our anniversary and the desserts and presentation was beyond...loved loved loved

This was the perfect choice for our 15 year anniversary celebration. The service was superb from the minute we stepped in. We had the best corner booth in the venue and there was even a handwritten note from the Chef himself wishing us a happy anniversary. How sweet is that!  

We really enjoyed the meal as well. We opted for the 3 course meal and I had the wine pairing while my husband had a lager.  The food was delicious and the sommelier has the perfect wine pairings to go along with my choices. In addition to our dessert, we even received a special happy anniversary cake that we enjoyed very much!

Thank you GK and staff for making our celebration so special.

I was in town for a conference, and decided a late birthday celebration was in order.  I travel a fair amount for work, and am not uncomfortable dining alone, but have never done it as a 2 star Michelin restaurant before.

The space...elegant but not fussy, bright, and views of Bryant Park.

The food...incredible.  I've done my fair share of fine dining meals and usually, well, usually there's a course or two that you wouldn't be upset to never have again.  Not here..every single dish was utter perfection.  The caviar/crab, the trout, the polenta/shrimp, the duck, there's no way to name just one favorite.  And the wine pairings were divine, I also learned a ton along the way.

The service...honestly, they couldn't have done a single thing differently.  They made me feel at home, and not the least bit awkward for a solo diner at a special occasion place.

I loved everything about my experience here.  Can't recommend highly enough.

We did the heritage testing menu with wine parings. Absolutely worth it by any means. The service was extremely good, the containers are beautiful, the setting is gorgeous, everything is so elegant. We have a group and the chef decided to offer us different dishes even though we all go with the heritage tasting menu. Any they were give 2 Michelin stars end of last year! Bring your loved ones to this for special occasions!

This is by far the most FABULOUS restaurant we have been to in NY and maybe anywhere, and we do travel and visit some amazing restaurants.
Food, presentation, cleanliness and of course service, all is PERFECTION. They have received 2 Michelin Stars but they need 3 stars at minimum. 
They say the detail is in the detail, and this restaurant is a great example to the meaning of that very word. We will fly to NY just to eat here again very soon. 

To your kitchen and to your wait staff,
Please continue to do what you do, it may not be your name on the door but YOU, along with your fabulous Chef, are what this restaurant is all about! 
BRAVO!!!!
Top notch food and service. So many amuses bouches my mouth was smiling all night. Highly recommend the risotto. Extensive wine list.

It's a great place to get something to eat pre show. We had the heritage tasting menu and overall not bad, although some dishes are not adventurous and are more on the safe side. It's not difficult to create something very tasty with caviar, lots of butter, scallop, and salmon roe. Really these are fail safe ingredients. But for a restaurant this caliber I expected things to be more creative. 

The foie gras dishes were pretty memorable. The duck was slightly chewy at certain parts, but I enjoyed it because that's my favorite kind of meat and I'm biased. 

4 stars for the food and I'm taking another star off because the service is the weirdest I've experienced at high end restaurants. 3 of the servers were awkward, and the guy who I believe to be the sommelier (I might be wrong, we didn't order wine) seemed young and was nervous talking to us. We ordered drink with him but it was forgotten until we reminded them. Towards the end they forgot our coffee again, which is annoying because by the time they checked, we were already done with dessert. Furthermore the coffee tasted like water which indicated to us it probably was not made properly. The lack of staff training detracted from the experience

What can I Say:  this is a true fine dinning experience. The chefs at Gabriel Kreuther's are true Culinary Artist.  The service was impeccable, the wine was delicious and thoughtfully selected, the food was sublime.  This is a must experience restaurant for anyone who like fine food and best NYC top chef's have to offer. Go and spend an evening at this truly amazing restaurant.

SO BAD !!! I have been all these top restaurants all over the world ! This was one of the worse one! First of all, food was OK. nothing "wow" and nothing too bad. But the service is unbelievable bad. I arrived on time and the restaurant is half empty! The host asked me to wait at the bar for no reason. I mean if u have all the table ready you should have set people down. After I set down I have been waited for 30 mins to get my first course. Unbelievable slow ! And if you bringing your owe wine ? The fee is 105usd per bottle. Even per se and eleven Madison park all these top restaurants charges only around 40usd. Most ridiculous thing is. Can't bring over 2 bottles. ( even you are paying 105usd per bottle. !!!! Seriously! As somebody who has been to all these top restaurants. This one was really Bad !

Took babe here for his birthday and opted for the lounge since he's a very nonchalant diner and is pretty much happy with anything. We got a round corner table so we can sit next to each other, which is our favorite kind of seating. It was very intimate- the lights were slightly dim, we were sitting right next to each other, but you get the point.  The atmosphere was beautiful, the servers were good, but not as good as EMP (probably would have been better if we dined at the dining room). However, the food was better and more creative than EMP and that's what matters the most. If you're looking to celebrate anniversaries, birthdays, etc., this is the place! 

Savory Kougelhoupf ($8)-5/5 $8 for bread of this quality? GIVE ME. Where do I even start? The bread? The chive fromage blanc? Both absolutely divine. The bread is fluffy, moist, and cut so you can easily pick up the piece and spread their creamy and smooth chive fromage blanc onto it. They give a generous amount of the spread too so go wild! The spread just had the perfect amount of flavor and was not too overwhelming. A must for starters. 

Temperance ($12)- 4/5 I don't drink so I was delighted to hear that they had  some interesting non alcoholic drinks. This one had seedlip spice 94, strawberry, vanilla, and orange. It tasted great and refreshing, but you definitely get more of the orangey taste and a faint vanilla taste almost like orange soda but healthier.

Hens of the Woods Mushroom ($25)-5/5 Anyone who does not like mushroom has to try hens of the woods. They're just the best kind of the mushroom on Earth. I mean the flavor, the texture, it's amazing. Then they add the cheese to it so it's basically like a pizza. And cheese only makes things better so this dish was damn good. I also spread some chive fromage blanc onto it and it was delicious! For $25, GET IT. 

Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart ($42)-4/5 I chose this dish cause it looks so beautiful. The presentation was lovely as well. It's covered in applewood smoke and that aroma just fills you when they lift up the cover. The sturgeon reminded me somewhat of tuna (the texture and slightly fishy smell/taste). But it tastes great with the caviar mousseline and the flaky tart. 

Citrus Cured Montauk Fluke ($34)- 5/5 I'm not too too crazy about raw fish. I always feel like theres' a risk in eating it, but these were too good to pass. And I love fish with lemon or citrus, so I had to get it. This dish wasn't fishy and tasted like summer. It's cold, the watermelon radish and cucumber vinaigrette complemented the dish very well. 

Roasted Montauk Monkfish ($42)-3/5 This was my least favorite dish and unfortunately it was the main as well. I love fish and I especially love monkfish although it's a pretty ugly looking fish. But fish and tomato broth does not go well together in my opinion. There was also bread crumbs with the fish which I wasn't too crazy about. I don't really like squash either and that was all over the dish. But my man really enjoyed it so, maybe I'm just picky. 

Comfort- White Chocolate ($20)-5/5 Honestly, I wanted to try all their desserts, but we were quite full and the server recommended the white chocolate. It is probably one of the best desserts I've had. The lemon Tahitian vanilla soufflé was so soft, fluffy and delicate. The limoncello sorbet and lemon confit was perfect (not too sour or sweet). You have to dig to the bottom of the soufflé to really capture all the flavor and combine it with lemon and ughhhh it's so good.

I'm so happy I came here! Everything was excellent, including the service.  I was able to get a last minute reservation for same day, which I was happy about.

The dining room is gorgeous. It's like walking into a lodge, with exposed wood beams, highs ceilings, a very open floor plan, nice art, and an open window into the kitchen (which I appreciated). The bar space was separated off, but was empty. 

The service was impeccable as I'm sure you can imagine, and everyone had such gusto and you could tell they all enjoyed what they did. 

As for the food: 
1. Bretzels - like somewhere between a breadstick and a pretzel 
2. Pina colada snow cone/ moscatel pate de fruit/ Tarte flambee with bacon, onion and creme fraiche 
The tarte was so good. Rich and salty. I think they have large sizes of these on the bar menu! 
3. Foie Gras terrine - jack fruit, white wine gelee, banana bread  - the sweetness with the jack fruit and mango purée was very nice, I also appreciated that it was covered in bits of nuts which added a nice crunchiness to mediate the texture. (For the record I'm not usually a fan of Foie gras due to texture).
4. Citrus cured tuna - tomato water, avocado purée   And beluga caviar on cornbread - the tuna was amazing. Bright and light, all the perfect flavors. May have been my favorite dish! There were small geeen wasabi tobiko there that added a nice texture and flavor. This dish was phenomenal. The caviar bite was okay, I preferred the tuna in this pairing 
6. Trout on cedar plank and corn gaspacho - the trout with the sauce was really nice. Warm and hearty - not too heavy. The corn gaspacho, smoked tomato water has white balsamic for a little acidity. It was a nice addition. Overall a very nice dish. I liked all the flavors and textures here.
