7. Japanese black fish - emulsion of red peppers and Japanese eggplant. Another good dish, but I preferred the cooked fish dish before it. I did really like the red pepper emulsion, it added a nice flavor. 
8. Braised rabbit fleischnacka -- cucumbers, morel mushrooms. This was essentially a small piece of pasta wrapped in the shape of a snail with braised rabbit in the middle. 
9. Porklette - with crispy skin -- wowza was that skin good. Also with pork belly. There ware cut fruit with the pork belly I could have done without, otherwise a great dish! 
10. Cheese selection - I about hit my wall here, but all of the cheeses were good. 
11. The plum pre dessert was the perfect 2 bites, I was full and could have stopped here. It was light and Refreshing 
12. Chocolate - lot going on here. There was a passion fruit truffle lodged inside there. Lots of textures, I think I tasted hazelnut somewhere. 
13. Like frappe - it was a nice little bite.

Overall my experience was excellent. I would recommend my friends/family come here for a nice dinner or special occasion. Service and food were all impeccable. No misses on this one!

I sat in the bar area here with my friends after my reservation at L'Artusi was cancelled on my birthday. I was able to make a reservation easily a few hours before.

I was excited to sit in the bar and have a small bite to eat after hearing amazing things about the food here but I'm afraid my expectations may I have been too high as I only found the food to be good, not excellent. I got the pasta which was rich and decedent but seemed to lack a certain depth to it. The service was also a bit strange - my friends had planned a surprise birthday dessert for me and the waiter mistakenly came to me twice about it. They also did not put a birthday candle on the dessert initially despite putting one on the dessert on the table next to us.

I suppose this is one of those restaurants that you need to go to the main restaurant and get the full course to enjoy. I don't believe I'll be back to the bar after this experience.

My husband and I came here for my birthday and got the heritage tasting menu. The food was EXCELLENT. Fish, caviar, breads - Every plate was so artistic and flavorful. We were pretty full near the end that we couldn't enjoy their homemade chocolates which I'm still regretting!

Service is second to none. They are extremely attentive to detail and professional. For my birthday, they wrote a note and had an extra course with chocolate cake which made it extra special. Highly highly recommend!

Wonderful tasting menu with very creative courses! Fantastic service and the som had created an amazing wine pairing for me! The Chef de Cuisine Joseph was sitting beside me and he was extremely friendly! He taught me a great deal about the fine dining culture/industry of NYC! As a great touch he had them bring me his favorite Mezcal which was amazing and also brought me a sampling of their Iberico ham (see photo)! I will definitely be back!!!

It's our first Chinese valentine day. We made a reservation on Thursday night. To be honest, reservation is not necessary during weekday night, but just in case. We ordered the 9 courses menu, and chose Wagyu beef for the main course. Unfortunately, I don't like the wagyu beef, since with that price people would have more expectations, and the beef is just okay. The rest is good. Probably won't come back and will try other 2 star restaurant in the future.
Wow...everything was incredible!  Sat in the bar area and the ambience, service and food was truly impressive!!  I dream of the dessert I had. Can't wait to come back!!

Fine dining at its very best. Dined here shortly after the restaurant received its second Michelin Star. The staff was so excited to share the experience with diners and their enthusiasm was contagious! I had never dined at a Michelin starred restaurant in NYC before, but the staff made the menu feel approachable and made the evening very enjoyable for everyone all the way around. The restaurant is beautiful, too.

Superb meal and service !!!!! service impeccable and the food was artistically plated  with each course seemingly better than the last. This is a great place for a date ,special occasion or a night out with friends

We ate at the bar because main dining was full. I must say I was a little disappointed that the menu was such a small selection. The bartender was fun with his flare. It did feel a bit pretentious and uptight. The food was very good. I had the duck leg confit and my wife had the monkfish. The anniversary desert was very nice and also a card from Kruther.

A delicious Heritage Manu for a vegetarian and kosher style diner. Beautiful, inventive, special. Tomato consommé was the most delicious offering I have ever had. Apple smoked asparagus tart. Sarah did a beautiful job as our sommelier. A beautiful red and some sparkling wine to start. Service was beautiful.

I got the heritage menu. The food was so much more than expected. There were a lot of 0.5 and pre-courses. The amount of food didn't offset the service, quality and taste. It was a great birthday experience. I will definitely recommend this place.

Wonderful experience celebrating with amazing friends and even better wine and nibbles. Sam was the best sommelier and matched our delicious nibbles with even better wines. Couldn't ask for a better night out. Good friends Great wines!!!  Thanks Sam!!!

I visited this restaurant with my husband for a celebratory event when it was still a one-star Michelin restaurant and it was my virgin tour to Michelin star restaurants. We tried the 13-course full tasting menu (excluding three breads dishes) and it turned out to be a great start and a meaningful tour I would never regret. We arrived here an hour earlier than reservation time, see if we could be seated in by any chance. There weren't many customers in the restaurant so we were seated right away. The service here was great and it had a quiet ambiance.

Despite that it was a bit pricy (that's why I gave it a four star rating instead of five star), the food here was amazing. It was the first time that I truly understood the spirit of French food was sauce, sauce and sauce. The dining experience here also wiped out my previous arrogant attitude on the arts of plating. I guess a lot of Chinese foodies like me had similar issues of focusing more on the taste of food but questioning how important can plating be. After a dinner tour at Gabriel Kreuther, I had to admit that plating was indeed very important. It was important enough to improve my appetite to a large degree through visual stimulation.

Most of the dishes throughout the dinner were fantastic. The hamachi, black truffle and foie gras pate dish was like a harmonic waltz performed by French and Japanese dancers. The slight sour flavour of the scallop dish tasted like spring. We were pretty full and couldn't finish the two desserts dishes. If you are a big fan of French and Japanese cuisine, Gabriel Kreuther is a great choice worth flying in.

Came here for my first fine dining experiences and definitely deserved a repeat.  They have since gained another Michelin star which in my opinion is well deserved.

The amuses and intermezzos really set the experience apart from other establishments.  The staff are laser-precise and will tend even to the smallest details.  My wife and I forgot to print out our broadway tickets prior and our show was right after dinner - they printed out the tickets for us. (while it sounds trivial, the paper they printed on was also extremely high quality!)

Safe to say there will probably be a 3peat in the future.

Having eaten at Gabriel Kreuther several times I must say that it keeps getting better and better. Gabriel Kreuther never fails to impress. The cocktails are delicious. The wine selection is amazing. The food is unique and delicious. This was our first time in the lounge and it was a great dining experience as well. The more elegant dining room is a more traditional French menu, but always very creative. Gabriel Kreuther has certainly become one of New York's best fine dining restaurants.

For our first anniversary, we treated ourselves to a nice French place that I think is generally underrated and under the radar. Gabriel Kreuthers has been something that I've always wanted to try, and it's rated 2 Michelin Stars in 2019. We went bold with the Chef's Carte Blanche Tasting Menu. There are a total of at least 28 dishes spread through of what they say is 9 courses. Service was stellar as expected, so no complaints there. The wine pairing, if your stomach can eat that much, was quite good. At the end of the night, they do give you a take-home gift of more Kreuther chocolates. The ambiance didn't feel pretentious as I thought it would be, and all the waiters were very friendly. Reservations were easy to get, and so you don't have to contend against some of the other more popular French restaurants. For our anniversary, Gabriel Kreuther signed a card welcoming us to his restaurant. Whether or not it's his real signature, it's still a delightful and thoughtful gesture

This place is amazing.

I've been to many Michelin restaurants and this can be one of the top choices. Plus, this place is on the cheaper side as the three-course lunch is only $90, and four courses are $110. 

I had the montauk fluke to start. I'm sensitive to fishy taste and this one had none. The verbena oil gave it a refreshing taste. Try the fish fluke with the melon, the sweetness of the fruit will bring up the freshness of the fish.

The duck confit was the best duck confit I've ever had. The skin was crispy and not greasy at all. The meat was soft and tender. 

My boyfriend had the Pennsylvania trout. I had to say this dish is exquisite. The waiter said they change the veggies according to the season. This time were the summer squash and celery etc. It tasted great. The trout absorbed the aroma of the veggies, and had a perfect balance of flavors.

The desserts were normal - not extraordinary and also not bad. Honestly I don't have sweet teeth and don't care about dessert that much, so this review only reflects my personal taste.

Overall I really enjoyed my lunch here, and I'm going to try the dinner menu soon.

--------update 10/04/19--------

I tried the dinner menu. It was still an excellent experience. Some lunch courses were offered in the dinner menu, and for main course they offered a choice of either lamb or duck. Since I knew how the duck tasted, I tried the lamb this time, and it was as good as the duck. The meat was cooked medium - medium rare, very juicy, and the best part of it was that it did not have the weird smell of lamb.

The only two things I think can be improved are: 1) the corn ravioli was a bit too salty. 2) I prefer to see the menu and know / choose exactly what I'm going to eat.

The biggest problem with tasting menus is that you're bound to not be fond of certain dishes. However, the problem with this tasting menu was that there weren't any memorable dishes. In New York where there are so many tasting menus to choose from, you really need a few outstanding dishes to stand out.

The decor is fine, standard fine dinning and the service was also fine with a few awkward moments where we weren't allowed to hold onto the wine menu and the main server forgot to mention a certain dish that had rabbit in it. Two of five of us don't eat rabbit so they promptly substituted with a fish. They still charged the rest of us that dish though. It was an add-on dish to the tasting and although we all felt we shouldn't have been charged as rabbit was the main ingredient and he described this dish as mushroom tortellini, it was too late in the evening to argue. 

All in all, a very forgettable experience.
Amazing Experience dined during NYFW after the fashion show and every course with 9 total was exquisite. I was so full by the 5th course made it through all of it with Wine pairing.

What a shame. This overly pretentious Michelin  restaurant clearly does not value service and obviously needs a lesson on hospitality. The wine selection at the bar is poor/mediocre at best for the prices; the options are severely limited for food. While the ambiance is nice it does not even come close to making up for the so called "service". The funny thing is the Cheesecake Factory literally has better hospitality and service. My guess is this restaurant thinks that because they're a Michelin star holder they can treat their patrons like dirt and up charge at an obscene amount. You should be paying for the quality AND service. 

I sat at the bar this evening when it first opened (after working), and went to hang up my bag with my computer on one of the individual bag and coat hanger stands next to my bar seat because it was way too large and heavy to hang in between my legs, and was told rudely by the bar manager (?) with a man bun who rushed over to me that I needed to hang by bag elsewhere. He told me to take my bag off the stand no one was using, when there was zero other people seated nearby,  because these stands were apparently for seated patrons in the dining room only (there was no one there yet and several free stands for the taking scattered throughout). I said "oh? Someone brought one up to me at the bar last time to hang my items." He responded snarky: "oh, well that was nice of them"  And then proceeded to have me move my purse and place the stand back behind my seat. He was so rude and condescending. I was so embarrassed. When I went to leave, all of those mini stands had still not been utilized....and he was equally rude for the remainder of the evening. 

This restaurant lost a patron who works in the building and would have gone often despite the absurd pricing and limited selection. Last time I went they closed food service at 9 pm (odd for a Nyc restaurant) and the bathrooms were disgusting--trash everywhere and basically like a penn station stall. So enjoy this "Michelin" restaurant all!
Fantastic variety of creative and tasteful courses. An excellent, knowledgeable service staff.  My favorite restaurant in NYC.

Exceptional service and delicious course - well-deserved two Michelin stars!!

FOOD // This place fuses multiple cultures exceptionally well - it shows the thoughtfulness, creativity, and skillfulness in the Heritage Menu. Bear with me, this review is going to be LONG. 
Appetizer: Pretzel Grissini [5/5] - Beautifully displayed, looked like an elegant table display and inedible. The texture was amazingly crisp and well-seasoned - seriously have never had anything like this. 
Course #1: Alsatian Tarte Flambee [5/5] - Deliciously creamy and the onion and bacon was well done.
Course #2:  Pina Colada Snow Cone [2/5] - Tasted like mango with lime in a soft, jello-like texture. I was not a big fan of the taste or texture.
Course #3: Foie Gras Terrine & Sesame Praline with poached green strawberries, apricot jam, and spiced waffle [5/5] - Love this - Great flavours and accompaniments. Unique flavours and subtly sweet with the compote and strawberry and waffle. Interesting pairing of foie gras  covered in sesame and with a waffle, but it works so well! 
Course #4: Citrus Cured Yellowfin Tuna with crenshaw melon, avocado, and verbena oil [4.5/5] - Very fresh, avocado puree was lovely with the tuna. It was drenched in a sauce that was flavourful and fresh and did not take away from the tuna. 
Course #5: Royal Kaluga Caviar with scallion creama and nori cornbread [4/5] - Flavourful and a hefty amount of caviar piled on the cornbread. There was a sweet, lemon flavour to the cornbread that I didn't love with the caviar. 
Course #6: Whole Grain Ficelle with bobolink farm's cultured butter and whipped pork lardo [2/5] - Bread was too hard to chew and the whipped pork lardo was too salty. Flavours were there, but there was so much more potential. 
Course #7: Pennsylvania Trout on Cedar Plank with local purple potatoes, tomato confit, and green bean nage [5/5] - Really good flavours and the trout was so tender and well done. 
Amuse Bouche: Tomato and Butternut Squash Gazpacho drizzled with tomato olive oil [4/5] - Pleasantly nice, creaminess that cleanses the palate. 
Course #8: Dock to Dish Charcoal Grilled Black Bass with fairytale eggplant, melted leeks, and red pepper coulis [4.5/5] - Really good flavours, but the red pepper coulis took over the dish a little. I really liked the eggplant with the bass. I also love their Dock to Dish initiative where they work with local fishers and create a dish with whatever the fishermen bring that morning. 
Course #9: Savory Kougelhopf [4/5] - Bread was fluffy and warm and nicely buttery. My only complaint is that the chive fromage blanc (butter-like mousse) could have been a better accompaniment. 
Course #10: Aged Long Island Duck Breast Smoked in Hay with cherry glaze, soubise, and marinated zucchini [5/5] - Not seasoned, but beautifully smoked. I've never had such a wondefully smoked piece of meat. The duck was cooked to perfection and so juicy, and the skin was so crisp. The cherry sauce is a great pairing with the smoked duck.
Course #11: Duck Confit with Cream with tortilla and salsa verde [3/5] - It takes hard work to make a tortilla as thin as this one. This was a memorable dish, but it was a good segway from the smoked duck. 
Course #12: Hoja Santa Kombucha [5/5] - Really nice flavour and a great way to wrap up the dinner portion of the courses, with a hint of spiciness, paprika, and mint - Perfect digestif 
Course #13: Plum & Tarragon [5/5] - Reminded me of a crumble, I liked the jelly-like tarragon and the sorbet was very refreshing
Course #14: Decadent, Chocolate, Passion Fruit with dark chocolate creme, passion fruit caramel, and frozen truffle sorbet [4.5/5] - Extremely decadent and very rich. The passion fruit caramel didn't do it for me sine it made the dessert quite sour.
Course #15: Chocolate and Petit Fours [5/5] - The Petit Fours was delicious with the speculoos base and I loved that the salt flakes toned down the sweetness of the chocolate. The in-house made chocolate was delicious - one was cherry and the other coconut - it was very well done and a modest, yet satisfying finale. 

SERVICE // The servers are very attentive (I never ran out of water) and the service was exceptional. The Assistant General Manager, Paul, was extremely friendly and honestly made the experience amazing! He offered to take me to the kitchen to meet the chefs and it was definitely the highlight. My only complaint was that sometimes it was hear the dish's description since the servers either spoke quietly or seemed inconsistent with what they told me versus another server at a table near me.

ATMOSPHERE // The restaurant is beautifully elegant and tasteful. The tables are also well spread out that each dinner feels quite intimate.

PRICE // You're paying for the quality, service, and environment. It's pricy, but it's reasonable given all factors.

I would highly recommend Gabriel Kreuther for a special occasion! Two stars, well-deserved!

This is an amazing restaurant!! 

We came her for our wedding anniversary and had the Chef's Carte Blanche menu. It was a wonderful, perfectly coordinated meal.

We had so many amazing courses, we couldn't keep count. Some courses they switched up what they gave me and the hubby. Like foie gras two ways. We also had the jamon supplement. It was outrageous.

The cheese course was amazing and a wonderful conclusion to the meal. Dessert was also outstanding.

The wines were also amazing. We had champaign that started off like typical champaign but the finish was more like a glass of burgundy. Totally delicious.  

The space is beautiful and open. The staff is terrific and very pleasant to talk to. You can see they take pride in their work.

This is very much a special occasion restaurant, although I may or may not come back without an occasion....

Chef Gabriel Kreuther was from the Modern, another 1 Michelin Star Restaurant back then. Under his own, right across Bryant Park, a beautiful restaurant, Grande, spacious, the bar and lounge to the left of the entrance, the main dining to the right! 

Modern design, wooden column and glass, fresh bouquets, comfortable leather seats, table cloths, corner and all, make the place cozy and charming.

Not all tables are created equal, but it seems if you are celebrating a special occasion, they try to get you a better seats in the room. We got lucky, a nice table to celebrate our newlyweds and my birthday. 

Two choices of menus, a lot of amuse bouche, BIGGER portion than I'm used to at other 2/3 Michelin Stars in San Francisco Bay Area.

We were so fill because we ordered extra supplement dishes, Caviar 15 gram $90, Cinco Jotas Jamon Iberico $45, White Alba Truffle $85... It was too much good food, along with the tasting menu $200 (smaller one)! We were so full! We asked to skip 2 dishes!

Amazing wine list, very well priced compare to other restaurants in the same caliber, Relaix Chateau, Michelin Star, etc.

Love the cocktails list at the bar! Well crafted and well written with explanation so guests know what they want to try.

Caviar, veggies dishes, Duck were delicious. Every dish was presented nicely. Love how they served table side, sliced the duck for us! 

Only 1 fish we had trouble with was the tomato gellee, slightly over salted. 

Their bread was also delicious! Service was very nice and attentive, even they was packed, but our water was always filled. 

Corkage fee was $105 for the first bottle of 750ml. Same as other 2-3 Michelin Star in NYC. Sommelier Sarah was wonderful. Offered us the 1992 Champagne Pommery by the glass $70, delish. A lot more great Bordeaux and Burgundy on the list! 

For what we paid, we got a lot more than what we would get in Northern California. It was a lovely evening and we will definitely come back next time when we are in town.

This is of the best fancy, sit down places that you can go to in NYC hands down! While I have been to this restaurant before, my second visit left me equally impressed. 

Located right next to Bryant Park, Gabriel Kreuther is very easy to find. If you look for the Grace building, a white marble building with a sloping design, it should be easy to spot as Gabriel is on the first floor. 

After entering the restaurant, I was immediately greeted by a modern, open sitting area for dinner guests. Separate but not too far from this seating area was a well stocked bar. 

With respect to service, the maitre d had us quickly seated and I was honestly impressed with the skill of all the staff. Our water glasses were filled almost constantly.

Finally, and most importantly, the food was fantsatic. On the night I visited, I was offered two different set menus, each of which unlike other restaurants did not list the dishes that would come out. As such, each dish was a surprise. Each dish was extremely impressive and I would venture to say that all of the dishes had artistic qualities. 

A bravura performance.

It pains me to write this review but I must speak out about an event that happened to me at this restaurant about a year ago. I was a regular at the bar, taking clients once or twice a week. On one occasion, I took a group of ~10 women clients, who were all attorneys at a large financial institution, and who like myself are black. We are all professionals, professionally dressed and used to dining in upscale restaurants. We had a reservation and arrived between 6 and 6:30 pm. The manager was very upset because we had one extra person at a bar table. He made a big deal about accommodating by adding one extra chair when there was plenty of room at the table. We ordered and consumed a large amount of food and 1-2 rounds of drinks, at which point it was about 8 pm. The server came over and asked if we wanted any more food because the kitchen was about to close. We questioned that, because the dining room seemed full and we couldn't imagine that the 8 pm seating had already ordered in full and that there were no more seatings. We were told that all patrons had already put their orders in and the kitchen was closing. We ordered a few more items and did not further question though we did not believe the kitchen was actually closing. A few minutes later, the manager came over and asked us if we could keep it down because we were disturbing other guests. We weren't particularly loud but thereafter made a conscientious effort to be quieter, but could barely hear each other over the voices coming from the dining room. We ordered another round of drinks (round 2-4 for each of us). At this point it was around 9 pm. They brought us the drinks with the check (over $2,000 at that point). We said we hadn't asked for the check, at which point the manager came over again. He said that we had been over served alcohol and we needed to leave. Mind you, no one was visibly tipsy or drunk. When we said we didn't understand his issue, the manager told us that he had to protect the restaurant's Michelin star. Then guest service manager came over and said that she had to back up the manager and ask us to leave, even though she conceded that she didn't share the managers concerns. She told us that it was his first night and that perhaps he wad being conservative but that she had to support him. It was appalling to be there with clients and to be treated and to have them treated with such blatant disrespect. We decided it was better to leave than to further engage. A very nice bar tender followed us out - a young blonde guy - he was almost in tears and told us he had seen the whole thing and was embarrassed and sorry. 

I hadn't been back since until a few weeks ago when I had to go back for another business event. No issues at that event, but I felt dirty being there after their horrific treatment of me and my clients. I would advise you to take their blatant mistreatment of people they don't think fit their desired clientele into account when deciding whether to patronize this establishment.

I recently went to Gabriel Kreuther for a special occasion.  The restaurant is large, high ceilings, but still feels intimate.  Service is great, and the ambiance of the restaurant is very romantic -- there were a ton of couples dining there.

We opted for a prix fixe tasting menu due to our dietary restrictions / not being super hungry, as well as a caviar starter.  There is also a longer form Heritage menu that would have been great had we been more hungry.  The caviar was great and came with a crispy rice cracker I loved this pairing.

We had a really heavy fish menu, which I liked.  There were different variations of fish, including crudo and cooked.  I thought each dish was very well-prepared and fresh.  The cooked fish dishes were very nicely prepared, not dry at all.

I had a great meal at Gabriel Kreuther and would certainly return.  It is definitely worth going to for a special occasion.  For a more economic option, lunch is more reasonable, somewhat.

We had reservations at Da Dong just down the street as there were 9 of us (5 kids) and it was the night before thanksgiving and we wanted something fun for the kids- well, Da Dong got closed down and no one bothered to call us so there we were in Bryant park stuck without a place to eat. Gabriel's accepted a last minute reservation for 9 (tasing menu required) and so our food adventure began- the staff was amazingly accommodating given our kids were dressed for family style Chinese food (as were the adults) and the kids loved eating the fanciest meal of their lives - certainly a splurge but great memories (how many different ways can you describe caviar or venison tartar to get your 9 yr old to try it?), great food and delicious wines! Thank you for helping us out- can't guarantee it will be a yearly tradition but it was worthwhile!!

My friend made reservations for us because it was near our hotel and that people were raving about this restaurant's 2 Michelin stars. After SO had his meetings we went there for dinner. It is a large space without being sterile and elegantly decorated. 

We had the Carte Blance Tasting menu. Our server asked me if I had any allergies and I told her I had aversions to cilantro and beets. 

Our tasting menu:

Prezel Grissini
Picon Biere: confit orange and apricot
Alsatian Tarte Fambee: applewood smoked bacon with onion and creme fraiche
Salmon Roe Beggar's Purse: proscuitto and smoked sour cream
Foie Gras Terrine & Marcona Almond Praline: pickled jackfruit, Gewürztraminer gelée, banana pain d'epices
Savory Scallion Kougelhopf: chive fromage blanc
Royal Kaluga Caviar: Alaskan king crab, vadouvan and zucchini espuma
Citrus Cured Yellow Fin Tuna: toasted sesame, kohlrabi and Buddha's hand vinaigrette
Green-Walk Hatchery Trout on Cedar Plant: confit tomatoes, artichoke and saffron-champagne sauce
Castle Valley Mill's Polenta: charcoal grilled blue shrimp, braised scallops and sauce rouille
Whole Grain Ficelle: Babolink Farm's cultured butter and house cured pork lardo
Goat's Milk Raviolo: pancetta, truffle coulis and sunflower seeds
Hay Smoked Long Island Duck Breast: squash caponata, soubise, grilled broccolini
Barley Tea
Artisanal Cheese Selction
Aromatica: coconut panna cotta, golden kiwi granita
Chocolate Passion Fruit: dark chocolate creme, passion fruit caramel and frozen truffle sorbet
Lime Frappe Brulee: Tropical fruit cremeux, pistachio financier

It would take too long to review every dish we had....the menu was well thought out, balanced, bold AND delicate and everything went well together. For tasting menus there are dishes where I'm not a fan of but not in this case. It was worth the 4 hours we spent at dinner and we were the last ones to leave. 

Service was  attentive and they sent us home with the tasting menu (which came in very handy since I went in June and the menu is different now) and petite fours of their decadent chocolates.
The food had been amazing. The desserts are awesome! The main course and appetizers are also very good. Nice atmosphere for business lunch/dinner.

Had the opportunity for our annual foodie field trip with longtime friends.  My friend chose this restaurant as the destination on this wintery night.  Parking and traffic were a bit of a hassle as we had to deal with the hoards of people at Bryant Park enjoying the holiday festivities but once we arrived we were warmly greeted by the staff at the restaurant.  Loved the exposed beams, modern large pieces of art and high ceilings. There is a lounge area seating,  a chef's table,  and main dining area- modern decor, very warm and romantic.  We spent over the 3 hours talking, laughing and partaking in the Heritage Menu.  They were able to accommodate my friend who has multiple food allergies including shellfish, gluten and soy (how painful to be her).  All I can say is that every dish was delicious, thoughtful and beautiful.  The service was impeccable.  The corkage fee was $105 dollars so plan to bring your best bottle of wine and make sure it is not on their extensive wine list.  They did reject one of our bottles.  The best dishes of the evening were the Aged Long Island Duck Breast Smoked in Hay with cranberry glaze/butternut squash,  the Grilled Black Angus Beef Tenderloin with smoked beet, goat cheese, walnut crumble and the Green Market Course of : Red apple Consommé,  Gelee-Venison Tartare and Swiss Chard Tempura.  Desserts were outstanding....extra stars to the pastry chef!  Loved the White Chocolate Shiso Leaves, Petit Fours, Chocolate Chantilly.
For the past two years on our annual foodie field trip I coincidently sight Chef David Chang in the dining room- I kept looking around but no sighting this year- There were a couple of imposters, but alas the spell has been broken.

GO HERE. you don't need to know anything, GO HERE. this restaurant recently received it's second Michelin Star and wow it shows! I'm a bit of a star collector when I get the opportunity to visit and actually stopped in here with out knowing they were a Michelin starred restaurant and said to my husband "if they don't have a star they DEFINITELY deserve one!" before looking it up and seeing they had two! The ambiance and service is what you'd expect, the food is an excellent representation of where the chef hails from while toeing the line between very traditional northern French food and innovation. 

What really set this place apart to me was their full vegetarian tasting menu. I have eaten a vegetarian menu at a Michelin restaurant before which was excellent, of course, but clearly wasn't why that restaurant had garnered their stars. This menu however was clearly just as well planned, thought out, and complete! Full flavors, thoughtful accompaniments and dishes that could stand up to their carnivorous counterparts. I'm so incredibly pleased to see world class chefs finally flexing their creative muscles for plant based menus, and for me personally this is the best example to date! Truly worth the trip for plant and meat eaters alike, especially if you're tired of having iceberg lettuce thrown at you as your meat free option.

I attended a private event and made the Sous-chef aware I eat gluten free. Wow, did they make accommodations for me without making a scene. They brought over a selection of Hors d'oeuvre made on rice characters that were amazing and then a small gluten free pizza that was 10/10. Amazing. Then at dinner the table captain made sure to point out not only the choices, but each time a plate was delivered quietly reenforced the plate was gluten free. I was able to relax and enjoy what is now one of my favorite experiences. 

The best part of the experience, besides the amazing food, was the conversations were handled respectfully and confidentially. I did not have to explain or answer questions from others at the table. 

The chef addressed the crowd and mingled with the guest and was warm and easy to talk with. Appears to be a very kind soul and incredibly passionate about every decision regarding his gorgeous restaurant and his staff echos his
Love for sharing a meal. 

Thank you Chef!

What not to say about this place.  It is an experience.  I booked this reservation through my American Express platinum concierge service.  That went really smooth as this restaurant is no easy to get into.  We did the heritage tasting menu along with the wine pairing.  It was awesome.

We had an amazing night - 4 hours of incredible food and service.  We did the carte Blanche tasting menu. Each dish was delicious and beautifully presented. Our favorite was the foie gras. The duck was outstanding, but we were so full by the time it was served. Service was outstanding and the manager Paul was exceptional. Paul spent a lot of time talking to us and took us on a tour of the kitchen.

Came here to celebrate my friend's birthday and I have to say, one of the best fine dining experiences I ever had. The restaurant is beautifully decorated and the ambience is comfortable. A lot of times, the fine dining restaurants tend to be a bit stuffy but at GK, it wasn't. The food was amazing- presentation- wise and taste! We wish we had time to check out the bakery next door because his chocolate was delicious as well. Will definitely come back.

I want to start my saying thank you for making me happy during my birthday month and on Christmas Eve! So originally I had a reservation for two and then it turned out to be for only one on the night of the reservation,  which was for Xmas eve !  
My reservation was for the kitchen table ! Which is behind the scenes of the restaurant! 
I want to start off my saying my phone conversation was amazing with DANA ! She is vibrant , friendly , and most importantly great at what she does ! She sucked me in , even before I ate the food ! Not to mention she told me she will meet me that night of my reservation  and she kept her word, when I arrived she was there ! INCREDIBLE WOMAN YOU HAVE WORKING FOR YOU ! 
So they proceeds to take me to this hidden gem behind the wall , which is the KITCHEN TABLE ! My heart was already at bliss seeing what I saw ! It was perfect , it was beautiful! After that , I forgot I was alone ! I got welcomed by Benjamin who from beginning to middle was so helpful and attentive, I did not have to use my brain much , he did it all for me . He's amazing!!! !!!! Middle to end it was then taken over by Alvaro !! Absolutely amazing! Described each of everything to me without missing a beat ! 
Each dish was a burst of flavors ! I mean each plate was phenomenal! This was my third chefs table ! I was extremely happy and I will come
Back again and again ! Thank you so much for making my dreams and expectations come true ! 
And to the kitchen ! Wow wow wow ! I watched each and everyone of you work hard and make miracles happen ! God bless all of you

Someone please educate me - Why am I looking at staff sampling wine throughout my dinner?  They were about eight steps away from us. Also, I know it's picky but I don't expect a sommelier to be showing me wine with hands that look like they picked the grapes.  It was actually disturbing how poorly manicured they were.  And I don't understand why the tasting menu is not the same for each guest.  My girl and I switched plates back and forth so we could talk about the dishes and wine pairings that we BOTH experienced.  Food was good but not that memorable.  What stands out more is the lack of management and staff training.  Also, patrons were dressed very casually with most of the men missing jackets.  

Overall - if you're looking for a fine dining experience that is commensurate to what you pay - this is NOT your place.

If you are okay with they mess up your reservation for your celebration, or not getting the complete menu, then Gabriel could be the choice.

We are really spoiled by all the fine dining options in NYC, and chose to try the newly promoted 2 star for my husband's birthday. Now I can see why it's so easy to make reservation. And Michelin really needs to be careful when review all the restaurants.

They kindly offered to make the reservation for us before they open up the online system. However, our reservation was not made at all. Well, they happen to have seats available. (You know the reason why)

The service was very slow. I had to wait almost 30 mins for my drink, and asked twice to finally get it. Not mentioning waiving many times to get our waiter. 

The worst part it, two dishes was not served for the meal. They didn't give us the menu before hand. We only found out when we got home. I took photos for all the dishes we got. And this is not my first fine dining experience, we definitely know what to expect based on our menu!

Attached all photos I took that night, including the managers email. I'm very curious how did you do the investigation? Asking the understaffed waiter? The cheese dish and chocolates were asked to pack to go, and the pretzels at the beginning were too little to take photo.

It's such a shame that GK offers such poor management and service, as we really enjoyed all the food we had.

Ughhhh!! What a disappointment! I was reading reviews before my arrival and chose to ignore the recent unfavorable reviews. I mean 2 Michelin stars!! People!! Read reviews and listen to them. This was a $1000 meal , which would have been fine had I been Michelin wowed. Each course was more underwhelming then the next.. Another bread course, more gelatin , really??  Creativity was average, balance and textures were tired. And most of all flavors and decor were old fashioned.. And I agree with a review above. Do I really want to spend $1000 and be served by a server with chewed up nails and cuticles for 16 courses... gross.  Way better options for a special , creative, experience to be had in NYC..

It has always been my dream to dine at a Michelin Star restaurant and what better city (other than Paris itself) to indulge this dream than New York City.  The restaurant is pristine and has two separate seating areas.  One being the lounge and the other the main dining room.  I had the pleasure of dining in the main area and the service was impeccable.  Gabriel Kreuther offers 3 or 4 course meals for lunch.  Being a weekday, this place was pretty packed but I'm guessing it's the perfect place to go for a business lunch as they are speedy and efficient.  

The first course was a delectable foie gras that was served in a ball shaped covered with pistachios and a fluffy homemade bread on the side.  The foie gras was creamy and the pistachios added the crunch texture that typically isn't offered with this dish at other dining establishments but was pleasantly welcomed with happy tastebuds.  

The beef tenderloin was cooked a perfect medium rare and served with multiple purees and foams that made the plate look like a piece of art.  The goat cheese and walnut crumble were great accompaniments to such a tender piece of meat.  

Last but not least, the dessert was a delicious cherry sorbet with chocolate mousse.  What better combination is there than cherries and chocolate?  It was flaked with beautiful gold specks and placed into a chocolate tuille.  

Service, presentation and food was all star and I'd definitely love to visit more Michelin Stars in my future travels thanks to my first experience at Gabriel Kreuther.

I am amazed at this experience.
I have done them all.
This is on a different level.
I don't understand some of the reviews.  Maybe they had a bad night,
or maybe the price for this incredible experience surprised them.
But I have never experienced anything like this.
Perfection.  No other description fits.

Gabriel Kreuther was one restaurant that has been on my to-try list for the longest time. With its beautifully adorned mahogany interiors, GK's artistic food creations, and even to the unique building the restaurant resides in, this restaurant just screamed a must-try spot.Their food is Alsatian-inspired and elevates fine dining to another level. 

My boyfriend made a surprise reservation for me to celebrate Christmas here which was super sweet and made the experience that more special. We did the Chef's Carte Blanche menu, and I was STUFFED! To start, they give you pretzel sticks, but served within a crystal vase. They were light and crunchy, a perfect little starter. Each dish was presented with such mastery and featured the most impeccable ingredients such as foie gras, caviar, white truffle, and duck. I love that there were mini little dishes in between the main dishes. It just adds to the excitement and justifies the price tag a bit more. The one blunder of the night was one of the managers accidentally knocked over my drink prior to me eating and it spilled all over me. But they were very kind about it and comped our drinks and offered to pay for my dry cleaning. I mean, very uncomfortable to sit through a 3 hour course dinner, but at that point you have to make the best of it. Overall, it was an excellent dinner, great presentation and fantastic flavors. I was very filled at the end and happy. The restaurant itself is 100% worth a visit.

Great restaurant and exceptional service. Very much a place for a special occasion. We had the tasting menu, which ended up being a perfect option since there were a few surprises here and there for items we probably wouldn't necessarily order on our own but was impressed with the food and service we had. Special attention from the staff noticing I'm left handed so quickly and discreetly changed my silverware accordingly.
Came here with my other half for dinner. What a great time we had. Food was great, even got to see Mr. GABRIEL KRUETHER in action

Phenomenal place for a romantic evening date. With a starting dish of caviar, the 6-course prix fixe and wine pairing, I was too full to finish our main course. Such a bummer, as we were served the most tender yet flaky-skinned piece of duck I have ever had. But I wouldn't have wanted to leave any of the prior dishes uneaten either. There's so much diversity in flavor, presentation and creativity that really made this restaurant a rarity in our lives.

The sommelier was very knowledgeable and exuded so much enthusiasm for wine. It was such a delight having her serve us, and the selections were on point. She wrote down the names of all of the wines we tried, which was so generous. At the end of the meal, you're given a sweet goody bag with a printed menu detailing what you partook in. Finally, and maybe an exceptional occurrence, the receptionist even encouraged us to take one of their copies of the Relais & Châteaux Guide 2020. It was such a nice gift, even if they do receive copies like it's nothing. 

To add an obscure side note, I love the pink/white/gold motifs of the interior and decor. Very French parlor-esque.

We went there last night. Outdoor dining. It's just ok I mean the food is good. But service is really slow. We wait like 20 minutes for our 8pm reservation. When we got seated they seems ignored us a lot . They didn't give us menu. We wait like 20 minutes to get their attention to get the menu. I hope they can do better! Come on. It's 2 Michelin star restaurant .

A very unique experience(outside). We went there for dinner and all were amazing. Lovely service and reasonable price for a fantastic meal like what we had. Highly recommended. One of a better restaurant in NYC.

This review is for outdoor dining on the terrace. 

Overall: 4.5/5
Food: 4.5/5
Value: 4.5/5
Ambiance: 4.5/5
Service: 5/5

Came to Gabriel Kreuther for a special occasion dinner, where they have opened dining on their "terrace" given COVID. 

We had a variety of dishes from the a la carte menu, including the 5J Jamon Iberico ($28), Long Island Duck Leg Confit ($29), Steak Frites ($36), along with Albert Boxler Sparkling Wine ($18 per glass). 

The food is impeccable. Special mention here is the bread they gave which was served warm - heavenly. The 5J Jamon was delicious and high quality iberico. The Duck confit was incredibly tender, and paired well with polenta and rabe. The steak frites was also cooked to perfection and tender. 

Service was incredible. Everyone was friendly and attentive but not intrusively so. The staff all wore masks and kept a generally safe distance with minimized interaction. 

Value wise, it's premium pricing but worthwhile for the high quality food and presentation. 

As far as outdoor dining setups go, this is one of the best ones. It's substantial area in front of the restaurant on 42nd St with tables spaced comfortably apart - it's not an overly crowded narrow sidewalk here. Some tables even overlook Bryant Park. The restaurant provides coat racks situated next to your table for you to place coats and belongings. Sure it's a pretty busy street so the city noises are inevitable and every now and again noisy street traffic will be noticeable, but they've done a good job of setting a pretty nice ambiance for a refined and elevated dinner. 

Thank you Gabriel Kreuther for a fantastic experience! Will return and would recommend!

Overall: Definitely a great value for quality food. The four course meal (+ bread and ending treats) was $115 pp but we left stuffed. You shouldn't have trouble getting a reservation during the week, but I would book ahead on the weekend, especially if you want to dine outdoors. 

Location: GK has a very large patio that is nicely lit for evening dining (we were worried about sitting in the dark). When dining indoors, tables were socially distanced (I couldn't hear anyone except my husband who was with me). We were able to make a reservation on a Sunday very easily for a Wednesday evening (also the day indoor dining opened).

Service:  Service was excellent, as expected. We were greeted with free champagne - they were excited to be re-opened and very grateful. Gabriel went around to every table thanking guests and asking about the food. 

Food: We decided to go with the four course dinner, ordering almost everything. Here is what we thought:

Citrus cures fluke tartare - very refreshing and light. Maybe a little too heavy on cucumber vs citrus ratio.

Foie gras terrine and pistachio praline - this was my husband's favorite dish. They have a huge amount of foie gras (we were impressed!), and they managed to pack lots of flavor and texture (from a jelly to a cornbread). Definitely recommend ordering this one!

Sturgeon and sauerkraut tart - My husband enjoyed the smokiness (also the presentation when it was served was ). 

Housemate trenne pasta - Great, simple pasta dish (I've also never had trenne before - vs penne - so that was fun). Definitely on the heavier side, so I had to pawn some of it off to my husband. 

Greenwalk hatchery trout - I wish there was more sauce, but when you had a bite of the fish, roe, potato, and sauce it was great. 

Spice roasted lamb loin - This was a lot earthier than I thought. It wasn't my favorite, but my husband warmed up to the flavor after a few bites (and actually enjoyed it more than the trout). If you don't like earthy mains, this dish is not for you. 

Fig Carpaccio - I like how they added a crunch texture with nutmeg tulie, but it was a little too thick to pair with the soft fruit. My husband loved the pairing of fig, passion fruit gelee, and ice cream - he said it was like a Mediterranean swimming pool ‍

At the end of the meal, we also received a few chocolates and a bite-size coconut chocolate cake. It was the perfect final touch to a great meal!

What a great way to inaugurate indoor dining! The service and food were superb. The restaurant is very spacious and felt great. Outdoor dining was still pretty busy and dining indoors felt calmer without the traffic noise from 42nd street. 

The menu isn't back to its former glorious self as there is no tasting menu available. They are currently offering a la carte and prix fixe options (3 or 4 courses). 

The wine list also isn't completely ready, but, while speaking to the knowledgeable and pleasant sommelier, Sam, his focus for the list is value. There is a little bit of everything and most bottles are around $70-150 with a couple of standouts at $500. If a guest really wants something specific and they have it, he mentioned they can usually fulfill the request.

All-in-all a very pleasant experience.

A completely enjoyable experience, despite Covid.  Luckily there is enough space inside, now that Covid allows indoor dining, for separated seating without resorting to plastic barriers or portable curtains.

The food, service and ambiance were all excellent, and we were able to inform Chef/owner Gabriel Kreuther directly, as he spent a few minutes during service speaking to guests at each table (socially distanced, wearing his mask, of course).  

I was especially happy to glance through the giant glass window in the corner of the main dining room, looking into the main kitchen, and see a couple of women wearing toques - unfortunately there are too few at this very highest level.  Once again, this served to remind all of us how we have missed indoor fine dining - even with it's small idiosyncrasies. 

In any case, I am greatly anticipating returning for another amazing meal.

2020 10 08. M2.

So we came here to sit outdoors. The website says walk ins are welcome, but we will still went on Resy. There were later reservations available but we put ourselves on the waitlist for the (early pre-prime) time that we arrived. 
Save for one couple the place was completely empty outdoors. 
The waitlist said the wait time would be about 15 min. 
They would not seat us. We were a family
and explained that we would not be there for long, but they asked us to come back some other time. The maitre'd gave us her card to call her, but there was no name on the card. 
Mind you, the outdoor space was basically COMPLETELY empty. 

Gabriel. I hope you read this. Not to sound cliche but winter is coming. Indoor dining will remain limited, it's not something I would personally do with my family. But I was more than happy to try your restaurant outdoors, and it was pretty empty. But your hosts would not accommodate us. 

I try not to leave negative reviews during a pandemic, Yelp even discourages it. But this was just unacceptable. 
For those making reservations online or via an app, or going on the "waitlist" I'd advise you to call the restaurant to make sure they have their act together.

A real disappointment. Very slow service (30 minutes to get water, 65 minutes for wine), poor attention to detail (no explanation of cheeses on plate), and then occasionally rushed us despite the other long delays. Some outstanding dishes but also an overcooked fish and bland polenta, along with pretty ordinary lamb and steak. Lovely decor, but at $140 pp this place has the cost of a Michelin 2 star but we were utterly mystified as to how they were earned.

Wow.  Came for outdoor dining during covid times and was so impressed overall.  Large, pleasant outdoor dining area; just a bit loud from the traffic on 42nd St. 

Food was amazing!  Definitely deserving of its Michelin stars.  Only dishes I didn't love were the sea bass with breadcrumbs and chocolate sundae. Get the miso-marinated strip steak!  Perfectly cooked steak with perfect texture and flavor.  Loved the hen of the woods tarte flambé, keugelhopf, and fluke tartare.  I will definitely return!

Gabriel Kreuther is one of those quintessential French restaurants that will always check off all the boxes: perfectly prepared food, charming staff, and an upscale / modern ambiance. If you want a fancy place to splurge on French food, it's definitely a good pick.

My favorite was definitely the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart, a must try! I loved the combination of the sturgeon, cream, and the sauerkraut flavors and the tart pastry added a slightly flaky crisp texture. The duck confit was also pretty good, very tender meat with a crispy skin. If you like foie gras, i liked their take of it with the pecans and little cherries. Honestly you can't go wrong with any of the dishes, I highly recommend ordering different dishes so you can try everything! They also gave complimentary chocolates at the end, and I forgot how delicious their chocolates were. If you don't have time for dinner, you can still stop by their shop to buy a box of their melt in your mouth chocolates.

Very disappointed by the current menu. 
I always loved this place before Covid. The tasting menu was always full of surprises and without any technical mistakes. 

Last week was a disappointment. 
The current menu has some nice plates like the cocoa sundae, or the classic sturgeon sauerkraut tart.
But besides those two, it was ok or just plain. 
The fig carpaccio for example was very blend and lacks depth of flavors. 
At $400 for two, I was expecting way more. 
Not going to come back anytime soon.

This was, undoubtedly, the most underwhelming dining experience I've ever had in New York City after living here for over 3 years and dining at multiple Michelin-rated venues. I had heard great reviews about Gabriel Kreuther and decided to take my girlfriend there to celebrate my birthday. We arrived early for an 8:15pm reservation on a Saturday evening. After being seated and receiving water, we were promptly ignored for the next 40 minutes. Waiters walked by, and no one checked in with us. Guests who had been seated after us were attended to before us - it was almost as if we were sitting at Bryant Park, not a two Michelin star venue next door. I had to flag a waiter to take our drink orders when we weren't acknowledged by 9pm ET - even then, it was almost as if we inconvenienced them. Assuming the "fluke" in service was due to pandemic-related difficulties, I reached out to the restaurant twice afterwards to attempt to understand why the experience was so abysmal, and have not received a response yet. If you want to treat yourself and your loved ones to a special evening, I cannot recommend avoiding Gabriel Kreuther enough - there are too many other deserving restaurants that could do the bare minimum and exceed what I hoped to have experienced at such a "well-regarded" restaurant.

Came here to celebrate a birthday and it didn't disappoint. It was a much needed fine dining experience especially during covid times. All the waiters wore a mask and each table was provided with hand sanitizer bottle. The high ceiling and space made us feel safe to dine indoor.

I went here last night to celebrate my engagement. My fiancé and I love watching Gabriel cook on his Instagram and I have been an admirer of his restaurant from afar for a long time. We went last night with high hopes and unfortunately were very disappointed.  We started out with the mushroom flatbread which was extremely soggy and not very hot. The cheese was overwhelming and it just was not good at all.  We then got the sea bass which was overcooked and underwhelming in flavors. The cocktails were okay.  But the saving grace of the night was the desert, apple Mille feuille.  Creamy deliciousness with buttery crisps and a bit of tang tart sauce, a few apple pieces were mixed in too to add dimension. Also the service was fantastic and the decor was beautiful. We didn't mind ease-dropping on the fellow patrons, very rich snobby billionaires talking about their private chefs and vacations.  Was an interesting night, but most certainly not due to the food.  Defiantly watch this restaurant from afar and maybe only go for the chocolate or desert !!!

We've been here several times, before and after COVID lockdowns. Our first experience after lockdown was different, as, there was now an a la carte menu. We encountered an excellent and knowledgeable staff. Great pre-dinner cocktails and quality ingredients with every dish. Our second experience, while still the same in terms of staff, left something to be desired in either ingredient quality or preparation, unsure which. Regardless, we will return and hope Chef Gabriel and his staff continue to move this fine establishment forward.

Had dinner at Gabriel Kreuther on Thursday evening. A spectacular meal, which unfortunately highlighted how much COVID has changed dining. Would love to come back to truly experience what the restaurant has to offer, but would wait until some normalcy returns.

Quality: Gabriel Kreuther is held in high standing, earning two Michelin stars. Unlike many restaurants at this caliber, each dining option, pre-fixe or a la carte, provides guests a fair amount of responsibility in selection. We picked our way through the meal starting with the Foie Gras Terrine And Pecan Praline and their signature Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart With Caviar. Two of the best dishes we had on the evening, with the tart really providing a one-of-a-kind flavor. Next out were the slightly underwhelming and very heavy Hen Of The Woods Mushroom Tarte Flambee, and the delightful Alsatian Onion Quiche. The quiche was not on the pre-fixe, so even if you go that route, still make sure to order it. For our mains we had the Grilled Miso-Marinated Prime Strip Steak and the Long Island Duck Leg Confit "Cacciatore." Solid dishes, but the best bite of them for me was the roasted salsify, leek vinigrette, and parmigiano espuma served on the side of the steak. To end the meal we went with the Fig Carpaccio, which was boring and simple, but luckily was followed by a delicious Pumpkin Pie petit four. A top-notch meal that did not immediately wow me, but the tastes lingered and reflecting on it, I was very impressed.
Quantity: A pre-fixe menu is available, but we decided to pick and choose. We ordered a fair amount of the menu, and the dishes are a good size, so expect to fill up.
Value: $36 for Foie Gras Terrine And Pecan Praline. $40 for Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart With Caviar. $24 for Hen Of The Woods Mushroom Tarte Flambee. $17 for Alsatian Onion Quiche. $9 for Crispy French Fries. $48 for Grilled Miso-Marinated Prime Strip Steak. $34 for Long Island Duck Leg Confit "Cacciatore." $15 for Fig Carpaccio.
Ambiance: Gabriel Kreuther is located in Midtown Manhattan, across the street from Bryant Park. Currently they have outdoor dining set up on the long sidewalk out front, however, it seemed hastily put together and quite noisy with traffic. We opted to dine indoors, which was much more relaxed. The dining room is large and spacious, with high ceilings and massive features. With tables removed and music played low, it felt a little strange and cold. While this was not my first meal since COVID, it was certainly the most upscale, and it was clear that the energy could not be replicated with a reduced crowd.
Crowd: They are operating at 25% capacity as a result of COVID, but most of the tables were filled on Thursday evening. Even though outdoor dining was an option, most guests chose to dine inside.
Service: The most disappointing part of our meal was the failure of the service to live up to the expected quality. It felt understaffed, potentially as a result of COVID, and as a result they were not able to provide that touch expected of fine dining. We did not get descriptions of many of the dishes, and while the sommelier was excellent, he was being pulled in every direction. While the food is typically the most important element, for a meal like this service is nearly as crucial and unfortunately it was lacking.
Parking: Several parking garages less than a block away.

We really enjoyed celebrating my boyfriend's birthday at Gabriel Kreuther, the food was really amazing and their service was spectacular.

I made the reservation about 2 weeks in advance. 

My boyfriend walked away feeling spoiled by one of the few fine dining indoor experiences he encountered. The staff were thoughtful and there was a note prepared for us when we got there. We were sat promptly and they offered us some of the bread and spread (chef aumont) and then we also got an amuse bouche from when we arrived.

Next we decided to order a la carte instead because there were a few things we didn't quite like from the prix fixe menu (very good value, 3 course for below $100 and just over $100 for 4 courses).

We ordered the signature smoked sturgeon and sauerkraut tart which was smaller imagined but very delicious with the thin soufflé exterior. We also ordered the hamachi crudo which you pair with some sort of chip which was also quite delicious .

We then got our main courses which from reviews, the miso prime strip steak and the duck breast were the most highly rated- so good! I loved the duck the best because the duck fat just melted off of the crispy skin with each bite. 

They forgot our side order of polenta so they took that off our Bill and even gave us complimentary fries to make up for it.

Then for dessert we got a fig carpaccio which was very unique and so delicate and crispy. 

They then came out to surprise us with a dessert with a candle and they even wrote happy birthday for my boyfriend which was also a complimentary dish. To finish they brought out a few chocolates and two mini mandarin cheesecake bites. 

Very sweet experience. I highly recommend for anyone wanting to celebrate their birthday! Best of all, after feeling extremely stuffed at a 2 star Michelin restaurant the bill was $250 before after tax which is very reasonable.

Finally, fine dining is back!!! I've been deprived of paying so much for a meal. Jk. I do miss my monthly fine dining adventures though. 

They have indoor and outdoor dining with very strict social distancing rules. Gotta love NYC for that. I wanted a 10-course meal but they only had a four-course so our plan was to order all the options and create our own 10-course meal. Upon ordering, luckily the waitress informed us of how big these portions were! They were huge!! We ended up only ordering one extra entree. We were stuffed before dessert time. 

All the food was amazing and some more unique than others. And the special freebies were mind-blowing. The flavors just explode in your mouth and you have no idea what you are chewing or why you are drooling. I can't say the bread was anything special though. I think I was seeking more flavors since the presentation was deceiving.

Impeccable and impressive. Staff was the most attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. Lisa was amazing. We decided to get their outdoor dining experience. They have heaters all around and despite the noise outside the ambiance was pretty cozy with wonderful music playing too. We opted for Ala-carte and it did not disappoint. Kugelhopf was served warm and delicious. The caviar and foie gras definitely was a great choice. The highly recommended miso marinated steak came medium rare and tasted sublime. My husband ordered the sausage that tasted great too. We loved the Mille feuille dessert. They also served us the sweetest greeting with a chocolate cake and small pieces from their chocolate collection. We are absolutely pleased and satisfied with the whole experience. Definitely deserved their Michelin stars and more, especially with their staff and their service. Thank you very much Chef Gabriel and everyone who served us and made our meal. With Covid happening you definitely brought us joy for our anniversary. Highly recommended!

It's been awhile since we've done fine dining, and we were lucky this place still had some spots open! We went on a Saturday evening and it was pretty busy. We reserved a table on the outdoor patio. Thankfully it was 50ish degrees out, but if it gets any colder/windier, the heat lamps definitely wouldn't be enough, so keep that in mind if you're like me and don't deal with the cold well! 

Service was great and very attentive from the moment we sat down. We decided to just order a couple apps and entrees to share for the table: 

- 5J Jamon
- Cheese selection
- Miso marinated prime strip steak
- Wild stripe bass
- Long island duck leg
- 2 week aged duck breast
- Side of polenta and fries
- Dessert: Apple mille feuille and chocolate parfait 

Everything was delicious, but my favorite was the duck breast. It was cooked perfectly, paired well with the sauce, and was very tender. My girlfriend and sister both liked the miso steak the most, it was also very tender and the miso sauce definitely added a different twist. 

Overall, great experience in the midst of COVID and would return.
Went there for a birthday. One of the best dining experiences I've had in New York, especially during the pandemic.
I love there food and atmosphere, the best meal I have ever had in nyc and that's saying a lot. Must have the tasting menu and they are amazing very good about accommodating allergies.

This review is primarily for the outdoor seating and menu. We went on a rainy winter evening. While they didn't seat us until about 15-20 min past our reservation, the outdoor setup was in par with a high class restaurant. Plenty of outdoor heaters were set up, with plants, and other decor which set up a Michelin rated restaurant vibe. Aside from adjusting tables to accommodate picky diners, the staff and ambience did this place justice. Music was playing overhead, and despite the rain and wind outside, we were sheltered in the patio setting. 
The food--is on par with what you would get indoors. I am vegetarian, and I got a hearty polenta, vegetable entree which left me satisfied. All in all, for the current circumstances, GK does an exemplary job in setting up Michelin dining given the restrictions.

WARNING: Definitely one of the best French cuisine in town. Kreuther specializes in Alsatian cuisine, modernizing traditional dishes with an innovative twist. Hearty rich dishes like the Foie Gras Terrine are transformed into delicate refined presentation, and full of depth on the palette. From the outdoor seating to the entrance and interiors, the detail is unmatched. As we join a couple days before Christmas in 2020, an otherwise strange time during the pandemic, at Kreuther, we escaped back to the sophistication of unique NYC dining, while taken to a part of France where you will find yourself for a couple hours mesmerized by exquisite plating and German influenced French flavors. As we dove into the last course of this gastronomic adventure, a cocoa pod is presented by impeccable service with specialty chocolates made in house... my taste buds caressed by the rich and smooth dark chocolates, the buttery caramel and pralines... each tops off the meal that is enchanting, unforgettable. So remarkable, you wake up the next day wanting to go back. For now, we enjoy this small piece of fine NYC dining with captivating architecture and attentive professional service, that of which you would expect from a solid Michelin establishment.

Over Christmas weekend, we came for dinner at Gabriel Kreuther's outdoor dining space and weren't sure to expect. The experience far exceeded what we had in mind, especially given the circumstances. The space is somehow private, subtly luxurious, and comfortable despite being on the sidewalk right across from a busy corner of Bryant Park! The restaurant has done a great job of staging the outdoor dining area, and adapting to the surroundings. 

We tried the 3 course prix-fixe, for which you can choose 2 savory and 1 sweet options. We opted for the starter, entree, and dessert. Both starters were a wonderful mix of decadent flavors and textures. The smooth, melt in your mouth foie gras with the crunch of the pecan praline made for the perfect bite, particularly with a touch of the cherry tang. The spiced pumpkin bread was warm and dense and it was lovely served on a hot stone. The hamachi crudo was also a delight; we loved the combo of the tender fish and avocado sauce, finished with the crunch from the farro cake. Both a wonderful start to the meal, for the eyes and taste buds.

For entrees we had the miso-marinated steak and duck confit cacciatore. The steak had an interesting sponge like texture and each bite was so perfectly tender while maintaining a solid structure and slight char. The duck was lean but flavorful and apparently from Long Island. The meat was juicy and the skin was rich and crunchy. Only a few bites were dry. The mushrooms and creamy polenta served with the duck were actually two of my favorite parts of the meal.

Finally, we had the fig carpaccio and chocolate parfait for dessert. If the meal felt slightly off mark anywhere, it was the dessert. Both were interesting but not at the same level as the other courses. The fig dish was very dry, with only the ice cream for some moisture. The chocolate had some great flavors, but they didn't fit together as naturally. However. We did love the final bites of Gabriel Kreuther chocolates to close the meal - those were delicious.

Overall, it felt like the full experience, even if it was outdoors. The servers were attentive and coordinated and they do their best to maintain the ambience (in fact, when I tried to find the bathroom, one of the staff didn't recognize at first I was a guest and politely blocked my entrance to the indoor area. Honestly though, in the time of covid, this was a great sign of the team taking health precautions seriously). One small potential area of improvement was the lack of music. Since the restaurant is on the edge of Bryant park with the sounds of buses, car horns and crowds, music would've been a nice auditory addition to a visually beautiful space.

We were lucky enough to get in the week before the latest COVID closure.  They were very careful to follow all protocols and have everyone spaced properly.  The service and food were both fantastic.   While I enjoyed the flambees and the miso-marinated steak, the artistry was in the foie gras terrine and the hamachi crudu.   The desserts and the specially made chocolates were a great finish.   They did a great job with the outdoor area as well so I wouldn't hesitate to go back and eat outside in the beautiful, well ventilated area across from Bryant Park.

This year has been a tough one given the nightmare shelter in place and quarantine requirements we've all had to endure and just as I thought there would be some good news re vaccine availability, indoor dining in NYC was shut down. Having slaved away in the kitchen over Thanksgiving, I was more than ready to be spoiled by the best of New York and thankfully Gabriel Kreuther came through with the perfect, healthcode-compliant outdoor dining experience. As neither my husband or I are starving singer songwriter artist models, we decided to enjoy all of Gabriel's two Michelin star a la carte menu beginning with the aged duck breast, miso-marinated steak, broccoli rabe and carrot sides, and culminating in a non-traditional apple Mille feuille (where did the other 99% of my million layers go?) and my husband's fig carpaccio. The petit fours were also a lovely holiday surprise. We were both so spoiled and happy to have not set foot into a kitchen, this was the most amazing meal! As an aside, my glass of wine from Domaine Adrien Berlioz was the perfect accompaniment to my entree and I always love discovering new wines. Merry Christmas!

We were alittle hesitant to come here because its currently only outdoor seating in nyc.  Im glad we came because even though it was 40 degrees outside it was warm enough to take our jackets off.  Service is excellent and so was the food.  Even though it was outside it felt like we were inside.  This place definitely deserves its 2 michellin stars.  I started off with the gk scaffa cocktail which was amazing.  The tea smoke put it over the top of other cocktails you normally have.  If you are into martinis the oliv oil martini was one if the smoothest ive ever had.  To start I had the sturgeon and saur kraut tart which was amazing.  For my main I had the smoked duck breast which had crispy skin which I did not expect since it was smoked.  For dessert we tried the fig carpaccio and chocolate  parfait.  If you are craving something different go with the fig carpaccio but if you want a really good chocolate dessert I would suggest there chocolate parfait.  If you have fomo like me get both because the menu is seasonal.  They also gave us complimentary chocolates at the end which were melt in your mouth delicious.  I wish they wouldve sent us home with some chocolates but i guess thats reserved for 3 star michellin spots.  Can't wait to come back for more!!!

Two couples.  

Terrific evening.  

Exceptional service. 

See the menu for the spectacle. 

Cannot wait to go back

I recommend this place!!!

I want to eat here again. Everything we got was so good. 

Miso marinated steak. Duck breast. Carrots. Broccoli rabe. All of them were perfect. The duck breast vs steak is a tough choice. My recommendation is to skip lunch and have room for both. 

I find sides usually aren't that special, but at GK that's not the case. The carrots ... humble carrots ... cooked to be stars in the own right. And the broccoli rabe ... a hearty mound of delicious greens. Definitely recommend these.

Dessert was of course also yummy. The fig carpaccio was unique and very figgy, which was great since I l love figs. There is a gelee thing in the center, ice cream, and ... figs! FIGS!!! 

The service was excellent. Our server magically appeared just when I was about to want something, and left us alone to enjoy the food when we wanted not to be disturbed. It's possible they have a mind reading machine in the back. And they kept my hot water pot topped up.

The outdoor dining setup is very good. Good heat lamps, tables far far apart, and beautiful decor.

They cancelled on us at the very last minute (the day off). They said it was for unforeseen circumstances, but if they expected any sympathy, they should have expanded on why. I realize there is a pandemic and there could have been a good reason- but they should have just told me that and not been so cavalier as though this is a normal thing to do.  Not only that, they could have offered to rebook us for another day. This was for a birthday celebration and we had to find another place a few hours before dinner. I had been excited about trying this place and now I wont bother- too many other good restaurants in NYC where the staff actually have a good attitude.

Celebrated my birthday here with the 4 course prix fixe.  Started with kir royales.  Loved the foie gras and sturgeon courses.  The duck confit was also rich and delicious and paired well with a glass of red.  Perfect apple mille and chocolate parfait with cappuccinos to end.  A surprise birthday dessert as well.  All courses were thoughtfully prepared with sophisticated ingredients.  Only thing is I wish the cappucinos were larger.  Attentive staff and relaxing atmosphere.  One of my favorite Michelin restaurants.

I was looking at Michelin starred restaurants to take my husband for his birthday, unfortunately, many of them were temporarily closed for the season because of COVID.

I was ecstatic to have stumbled upon Gabriel Kreuther. Their outdoor dining set up was impeccable, and makes outdoor dining in the middle of winter, a dream. They managed to build the most chic and practical canopy that is properly ventilated with staggered wood beams, with heaters inside.

My husband and I enjoyed the delicious 4 course pre-fixe menu. Even though it is a pre-fixe menu, you can still choose from a few options what you would like to eat. Between my husband and I, we had everything on the menu, except three items: the slow poached farm egg, the trout, gnocchetti.

Everything we ate was delicious. From the savory bundt cake/bread with hints of green onion in the beginning, to the complimentary chocolates brought out at the end, in a cocoa bean, which was super cool. The wine list was also well-curated and reasonably priced. We chose the Vosne-Romanée to pair with our dinner.

Lastly, our server, Bridgett was wonderful. Her recommendations on the courses were on pointe. At the end of the night, she brought out a complimentary cake for my husband's birthday, and even offered to remove the wine label on our wine bottle as my husband collects them.

We'd love to return to dine again, next time inside, hopefully, where it's even more beautiful than the outdoor seating.

Delicious food and fantastic service! Our server Albero noticed my dining guest was a lefty and automatically provided a special left handed spoon! Also knew how to smoothly get us to order more drinks and such with open ended questions, from one sales person to another... props to you! Cocktails are pretty much $30, expensive. We did the prix-fixe dinner which is $125 for four course. Super great value for this quality food and service from a Two Michelin Star place. Our favorite from each course was the Hamachi Crudo for starters,  slow poached farm egg for our mid, and two week aged smoked hay duck breast was some of the best duck I've had. Gabriel Kreuther is known for doing great ducks including foie grad. Even packing my left over to eat the duck for work the next day it was still sooo amazing reheated up. The complimentary amuse bouche as well as the warm scallion bread with chive butter was so delicious as well. Ending with apple mille feuille for dessert was just lovely. Would highly recommend!

I knew it that they have a good food and good service. The are a two Michelin stars restaurant. Even though in my visit I was so surprised with the food and the service. It was a magical night with my wife. The staff was very attentive and the food it was delightful. The terrine, duck breast and desserts were amazing. More than recommended. It's a must in NYC.

The food and servers/manager on staff was 10/10! This is a must try restaurant, brought my boyfriend here for our first time and birthday.. they definitely made the night very special.
