The food, presentation, and service was phenomenal:) our server was Elizabeth super sweet and nice girl! Recommend her as well

Amazing place for an exquisite dinner. Was able to switch our reservation to have the Chef's tasting menus in the kitchen. Just amazingly- wow! The food was unbelievable, the service - impeccable and the atmosphere just pure joy. GKNY is a must for any foodie!  Thank you to the staff for an incredible evening and ensuring our safety as well.

A tale of of two prefixes. Depending on your selection, you may like it or love it. Excellence in service and a beautiful venue to boot. We got the 4 course prefix for dinner. If you want the love it selection, go with four gras , sturgeon (skip the caviar it doesn't add much to the dish), duck breast, and chocolate. That course was delicious. Don't be me and get the hamachi which was good to be honest, egg - ordinary, duck leg confit - dry, chewy, with pole to and mushroom that was bland, fig - funny after taste.

So go on and have an excellent meal, but choose wisely. The birthday cake was delicious, so we did really appreciate that, just wish ALL the dishes were delicious.

Came here for my birthday. Was surprised they raised their price just around the time for our reservation as the price was $10 lower when we made the reservation about two weeks prior.

Nevertheless, the service, food, atmosphere and just about almost everything was amazing. The dining room felt like a comfortable and luxurious bedroom (?) (my first impression) with beautiful decors. We were greeted warmly several times by the staff regarding my birthday and what we wanted and water was replenished and table was cleaned several times. In addition to the four course menu, we also had several complimentary small dishes/ desserts/chocolates in the beginning (even the bread was beautifully made and tasty), between our courses, and the end, as well as a surprise candle lit chocolate cake for my birthday (very appreciative). 

We had both the starters: foie gras terrine and crown toro hamachi and I definitely preferred the hamachi better and the ponzu sauces were unique and interesting to try. 

For the mid course, we had both the Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart  and Canestri Pasta. Unfortunately, the pasta felt too salty for me but the tart was a unique experience.

For the main, we had trout and duck confit. I must say out of all the dishes, I enjoyed duck confit the most and it was definitely a highlight of all the dishes. My boyfriend enjoyed the trout more. 

Finally, we also tried both the desserts and  I found the chocolate sticky toffee pudding to be extremely tasty and worth it.

Probably one of the best dining experiences I ever had thanks to the hospitality, food, and service, although I do agree that not all the dishes on the menu we had were tasty. Nevertheless, would 100% recommend!

I haven't written a review in a while but --

Went for lunch. Food was stunning and expensive as expected. Selected 2 desserts since I couldn't make up my mind- quite enjoyed the dessert courses the most, recommend both the pistachio brûlée and the wild strawberry mille fueille which were fkkin incredible. Got the hen of the woods flambe which was really not that tasty as people wrote so I don't recommend it (overrated). Like your app is supposed to excite you for the next course but it just fell super flat and bit overcooked with burnt bits that made each bite taste bitter, choked my piece down with water. Just didn't work for me. Instead thought their goat cheese spring salad app was incredibly delicious, not to sound pretentious and absolutely ridiculous but really tasted that spring had arrived lol. Trout was excellent but enjoyed the marinated brussel sprouts underneath even more. Didn't taste the shrimp or steak dishes but everybody said it was fantastic. Noticed a trend that everything was stunning but the vegetables were next level tasty for me... not to be weird but I thought back to the anime called food wars where shinomiya utilizes french finesse on veggies and blows everyone's clothes off and that was legit me 

I had taken my fam out for a nice lunch and the coolest part was one of the waiters realized we were speaking korean. My parents prefer conversing in their native language. Soooo when he spoke my mom was like omona and she was so incredibly happy! Thanks for going out of your way to make them feel comfortable, unfortunately didn't catch his name. I think she spoke like 15 mins straight about how *lovely* our Korean waiter was which beats the time she talked about our waiter at Jungsik lol. Bridgette/Bridget (sorry if sp is wrong) was super cool too. Anyways, really enjoyed our lunch. Thanks Kruether's lunch team!

We had Mother's Day dinner at their outdoor patio. 

Environment Wise [5/5] - Their outdoor patio is nicely built and situated right across Bryant Park. Noise level was quite high and I would suggest avoiding outdoor dining if you are looking for an intimated and romantic experience. Their dinning room is classic and elegant. This is a perfect place to celebrate special occasions. 

Service Wise [3/5] - Not the best services I have received and I think it could be better. Some staff was friendly, some was pretentious & some was emotionless. I noted in my reservation that I was here for an early Mother's Day dinner and only the host said something about it. No one said good bye when we left and hey I don't expect that in every restaurants but this is a Michelin Two Stars restaurant. 

Food Wise [3/5] - We ordered a la carte because the prix fixe menu didn't interest us. Most of the dishes were tangy and sour and I don't like sour foods. Duck breast was cooked perfectly - better than the infamous duck breast I had at EMP. I would come back for their duck. Also, don't forget to try the Sturgeon & Sauerkraut tart!

Food deserves a 4 rating but sadly the service deserves a 2.5 star rating. For a 2 Michelin restaurant we were expecting better service from our server. 
We made reservations at GK to celebrate our wedding anniversary on Saturday night. When we reached the restaurant we were promptly seated & someone offered us water. We opted for a four course prix-fix and our server helpfully switched my husband's main course from Duck confit to Duck breast. While my husband was promptly served champagne I didn't receive my mocktail until after the first course. That isn't a big deal; it was after the second course that the service went downhill. While the flow of courses between the introductory bite, first and second were perfectly timed, it took over 30 minutes to be served our main course. During that time nobody came over to ask whether we'd like another drink; it was as if our corner table didn't exist. After the main course, my husband hoped to order another drink with his dessert but no one inquired if we'd like to have a drink or coffee or tea with dessert. It took over 15 mins to catch someone's eye and order another drink. At that point my husband questioned whether the bar was closed hence no drinks were offered. There was no apology from our head server; he took my husband's order and left. We have been to Michelin restaurants across the world but the service at GK stood out, not in a good way. 
That being said, the food is very good:
Starters- Both starters are excellent (Fois Gras & hamachi crudo)
Second course- we opted for chef's speciality, Sturgeon & Sauerkraut). It was good.
Third course: the steak & the duck were both very tasteful, especially the steak (my favorite!)
Dessert: both desserts on the tasting menu were excellent; it's hard to pick a favorite. 

I would definitely like to go back & give their service another shot. Perhaps it was just a one off night when the service slacked. Only this time I won't be ordering a mocktail only to be charged $18 for a cocktail. We didn't want to make a fuss about it so we paid & left.

Went here on for my birthday way my parents, everything was a 10/10. Best meal I've ever had and everything was great, my personal favorite was the Foie Gras Terrine. COVID accommodations were also great, outdoor seating, staff wearing masks, hand sanitizer at table. Hopefully I have an opprotunity to go again in the future and try the tasting menu.

Well, there's a first time for everything and this is the first time I've rated a Michelin 2 star restaurant anything other than a 5/5.  First the positive:  the decor was fabulous.  It felt like a 1960's LA glam/ cabin in the woods mash up, but it worked!  The tables were appropriately spaced out for safe social distancing.  The food was most enjoyable.  The chef is to be commended.   My personal favorite was the smoked duck with asparagus.

The not so good: it was around 10 minutes before anyone took our order. My dinner date had to stop a service director walking by and ask if she or anyone could take our order!  When our waiter finally did arrive we ordered the chef's tasting menu, but explained that my date could not eat muscles, and asked if something could be substituted for this particular entree. The waiter brusquely replied that the muscles were for two, so if he couldn't eat them, then I couldn't have them, turned on his heel and marched away.  I've never had this treatment before at other Michelin restaurants. We've had the situation several times in the past and the waitstaff has always been accommodating and asked the kitchen what substitutions could be made for my date. It's never been a problem. My date was quite upset that I would be prevented from enjoying one of my favorite foods, just because he could not eat them.  Why should I be punished?  He again asked for the service director, Rachel,  who quickly and agreeably stated that a substitution could be made. She was really the star of the evening and salvaged the experience with her warm personality and attention to customer service.   Our waiter continued with his overall laconic, rushed manner but at least would comment on the food as it was delivered.  The final slight was at the end of the meal, my date asked for the remaining dessert that we did not finish to be packaged so we could take it home.  It was a wonderful assortment of dark chocolate that nearly tasted like pure cacao, passion fruit tarts and a birthday fudge brownie.  Upon arriving home, we were both disappointed to find that only the partially eaten brownie had been boxed. 

I understand that the pandemic has put a stretch on the restaurant industry. However, this is precisely why we have continued to provide our support by regularly dining where proper pandemic precautions are in place.  The service is just as important as the food for an enjoyable culinary experience, and both are expected to be superb at the price point paid at Michelin rated restaurants. Throughout the pandemic, this has been my first lack-luster experience at a restaurant of this caliber. Disappointing.

We visited the restaurant for our anniversary. It was also our first visit to New York and we were very excited to eat a restaurant with two Michelin stars. The night started out wonderful, We got seated on the patio, and a handwritten note from the chef was a nice touch. First the bread which was delicious. Slightly cheesy with a chive cream. Different and tasty.
Then a nice amuse, pallet cleanser was offered which looked modern an contemporary, I believe a melon soup with basil and another little bite that was tart but refreshing. As they were placed on the table, 5 seconds later the first course appeared and it obviously came a little to fast. But such a minor error in timing is no problem. The glass of rose champagne we started with made up for it.
Our first course was a goose liver dish and Hamachi crudo.  The goose liver was spot on, the sweet jelly and spice cake were perfect partners for this little golf ball of foie grass and the wine picked to accompany it paired beautifully.  The crudo was good, but not spectacular.  Dominated by the ginger and accompanied by a light cracker reminisced of Indonesian shrimp crackers it was nice but not wow.
Then the next course. Lamb ragout for me and Chef's signature sturgeon with sauerkraut in puff pastry, topped with caviar for my wife.
This is where the meal went off the rails a little bit for me. The lamb dish, with pasta, peas, pea shoots and lamb was rather bland and  uninspired. I could not detect any lamb flavor and the meat resembled ground beef much more then it did lamb. I was expecting a full bodied jus d'agneau for this dish, but the flavor fell flat despite the perfectly cooked pasta and peas. Technically nothing was really wrong except for the flavor, which was not worthy of a two star restaurant.  The sturgeon dish was very nice and my wife enjoyed it very much.
Time for entrees. My wife has the trout with a fennel sauce. A good dish, that was tasty, with delicious sauce, crunchy trout skin and fresh fish.
My duck confit on the other hand was a little underwhelming. Again I was looking for big and bold flavors. The duck confit was good confit, but that's where it ended. It could have use a touch of salt and maybe something else. This tasted like plain duck confit, slightly under seasoned. The morel sauce, with fava beans, was not strong enough to elevate and save the dish. Which is a shame, because duck can withstand bold and strong flavors that make a dish memorable. This dish was not. The lettuce that went with it, was ok, but a nice crème of celeriac,  truffle mashed potatoes, or salsify would have helped the dish a lot. The wine pairing on the other hand was very nice, the duck came with a Barolo that improved the overall experience.
The desserts were the highlight of the meal and probably the most memorable.  The rhubarb dessert for my wife and sticky  toffee pudding or cake, with passion fruit foam and caramelized banana for me.  The pastry chef stole the show with some phenomenal desserts and sweets . A complementary financier chocolate dessert was a beautiful touch and much appreciated.  
Overall it was good meal, but we came with sky high expectations that only were met with certain dishes. We feel the service team might have been a little short and although courteous and nice, they did have to cover a lot of tables and ground to make the night happen which is never a good thing if you aspire provide the best possible service.
We want to thank everybody at Kreutner for wonderful night and hope that they take this review as an opportunity to improve, because its certain not meant in spiteful way. We know that with 2 Michelin stars comes with high expectations and a lot of  pressure to perform and not everyday can be your best. As we both work in the industry, we appreciate the hard work and skill that went into this night but we feel we owe you a truthful review. Good luck in your pursuit of that that third star.  It you get it, we'll come back.

I was very excited to check out another Michelin starred restaurant. 

I ordered the 4 course prix-fixe menu for dinner. It consisted of:

Bread and butter - Absolutely delicious

To Start:
FOIE GRAS TERRINE AND CASHEW PRALINE - Never liked Foie Gras, but this dish was better than the other times I have had it
CROWN TORO HAMACHI CRUDO - Very good, well seasoned

Mid:
STURGEON & SAUERKRAUT TART - Very flavorful and had great textures
HOUSEMADE CANESTRI PASTA - Tasted rich and earthy

Main:
PRIME BLACK ANGUS STRIP STEAK - Perfectly seasoned and juicy
LONG ISLAND DUCK LEG CONFIT - Probably would not get again since whole duck cuts might be a better option

Dessert:
PISTACHIO FRAPPE BRÛLÉE 
CHOCOLATE STICKY TOFFEE PUDDING 

The service was excellent. The staff there was super attentive and accommodating. 

I am giving this place 4 stars because I have had better-tasting food and wish I did not go with the prix-fixe menu (regular menu has better options).

Truly disappointing experience. I was expecting way more from a 2 Michelin star restaurant. The food was average and so was the service. The waiter never explained the plates (as they do in other Michelin star restaurants). 

I ordered the 4-course pre fix. The foie gras was hard to eat, the sauerkraut tart was good, the duck breast was exceptional, and the chocolate flan was good as well. However, overall, the food was not what I expected and the experience was far from memorable. 

At first, I was skeptical to go here because it was the only Michelin star restaurant that had wide availability. Should have trusted my gut.
Simply outstanding. Get the duck or steak both are the best in the city. The waiters were inviting and friendly to share suggestion and history of the dishes

Dinner with drinks was over 500 hundred dollars (!!!), but I've honestly had better service and hospitality at almost every other restaurant I've been to in recent memory. 

The food itself was fantastic a 9.9/10, but when they serve you the wrong entree, don't take your order for 20 minutes, fail to explain anything about the menu, make your guests eat alone while they correct your order.....it's hard to leave satisfied. 

I hate to be critical because none of this was intentional, and Covid has obviously impacted the service industry immensely, but I think it's fair to let other diners know what to expect. Service needs to improve vastly before you should consider visiting.

What - meager - amounts of food I *did* have were quite tasty, but unfortunately service was abominably slow and a four course, scantily-portioned meal stretched out into three hours. I never thought I'd sit at a two Michelin star restaurant with a prefixe meal hungry, for the entirety of the meal. Now I understand why they offer side dishes prominently on the menu which are essentially pizza and cheesy potatoes because, guys, you're gonna need it.

It took a little while for the amuse bouches to arrive, but they were delightful. A melon gazpacho, a margarita congealed in a little cuboid gelee, a cheesy puff pastry. The bread course was an airy and fluffy thing with scallions and a whipped herbed butter.

For my first course I got the foie gras torchon. I enjoyed the combination of flavors - pickled strawberries, balsamic reduction, champagne jelly, accompanied by  ironically prosaic Pullman slices of rye bread.

The caviar and sturgeon second course was... prettier than it tasted. It is literally a smoke show that was figuratively smoke and mirrors. It was a piece of fish served on a few layers of phyllo dough, not the tart shell I was expecting.

The third course, I got the duck breast. We are two hours into dinner and finally the entree arrives. I am famished at this point, but I found the duck chewier than I'd like, with an unfortunately un-crisp skin.

The pistachio creme brûlée dessert was a delightful mess of textures - foam, compote, biscuit. The meal ended with a cherry coffee cake petit four and a coffee ganache bonbon.

Still hungry, I went home and I made myself a charcuterie board.

This is my 2nd time at Gabriel Kreuther and it was such a disappointment. Aside from the signature sturgeon and sauerkraut tart (so creamy, loved this!), entrees were really lackluster and upsetting. I took some out of town guests here and unfortunately, we were not impressed. 

Hatchery Trout: got this dish the first time I came here and it was amazing, I loved the sauce. The second time around, I guess they changed the sauce each season, but it tasted unappetizingly sour. I would give it a 2.5/5

Herb crusted blue shrimp: the shrimp was very tough and didn't seem to go well with the crust. The sauce was again, very sour... Don't get me wrong, I love some tarteness to my seafood but it didn't feel balanced. 2.5/5

Duck confit: duck was cooked well and I really enjoyed the polenta but the dish was a little too salty for me. Out of the 3 entrees though, this was probably the best one. 3.5/5

Strawberry Mille feuille: very good, love the Yuzu sorbet but very, very small portion compared to the desserts I got last visit 

For a 2 star Michelin restaurant, I was very disappointed at the new menu offerings. I thoroughly enjoyed the food during my first visit, I can't say the same for my second visit. 

Also, I did not experience any issues with service like previous reviewers had. Service was prompt and attentive during my visit. I tend to drink a LOT of water and my glass was never below halfway full.

Would not recommend dining in the outdoor terrace during rush hour traffic! Lots of loud buses and traffic. Really interferes with the ambiance. I would recommend going later in the evening.

The space was elegant and very spacious. Starting out, the first courses were just fine (got the hamachi as well as the langoustine tartare) but the second courses (foie gras and sturgeon tart) were great! For mains, the duck and the steak were both delicious. For dessert, I liked the lightness of the strawberry mille feuille. Overall, it was a really nice experience! Service was warm, but can be a bit slow. Would come again!

Came here for lunch and decided to go for terrace seating. Really beautiful outdoors and great service. Food is high quality and with great flavor but would wish the portions are a bit balanced.

We started with the mushroom tarte and it was rich, gooey, and filling. In some ways this appetizer and its portion felt more like two very large slices of New York Pizza, and while I appreciate that it helped fill us up, I wish that it would be the case for entrees.

For entrees we had the greenwalk hatchery trout and the Miso marinated prime stick steam. Both dishes were well balanced and full in flavor, technically flawless in their preparation and exactly as I would expect from this restaurant. My main critique is that the portion sizes are a bit everywhere, with the trout being light.

The dessert was good, presentation fell a bit flat on this one. We weren't sure of what happened to the chocolate store. 

Service was impeccable. Overall a great experience!

On a spree to collect Michelin stars and this place lived up to expectation in every way. Every dish was flavorful and exquisite, the service and ambiance were incredible as well. Will be back sometime!

A 2 #michelinstar dining--spent my dinner a few months ago there. Loved the service and the atmosphere, the food (we got their dinner tasting menu) was marvelous, but hoping it could be better. But overall, a great experience with its tasting menu!

Today was a good day. Gabriel Kreuther did not disappoint. We thoroughly enjoyed our first indoor dining experience since 15 months. We were wowed and treated royally.

Michelin Stars well deserved for the exquisite mix of French Alsatian and German haute cuisine. 

Lunch was an la carte affair vs the dinner multi course prix-fixe. Thus we stayed within our dietary scheme.
:)

Superb wine pairing, meticulous service, along with glowing splendid company topped off a fabulous beginning to this holiday weekend.

New York, we're back! xoxo

What is there to say? Came here for my first michelin star restaurant experience. 

We all chose the 4 -course menu for 145.

Started with a delightful/smooth/refreshing melon/lemon grass (?) juice followed by a savory/smokey "jello" shot. 

Next was this beautiful almost bunt bread presentation with sour cream/onion savory spread. 

Then we went in the next steps. I got the foie gras terrine - very buttery/smooth, spread on house rye. Break up with riesling gelee and pickled strawberries so refreshing. Others got the crown toro hamachi - so sweet and light.  

I chose the sturgeon & sauerkraut tart - beautiful presentation captured almost in a crystal vase - releasing it allowed the beautiful smoked fish to fill the table.  The others at the table got the seared sullivan county foie gras - that's the way to go. The sear just brings out a different flavor. And the peach jam with the foie gras - oh my. 

Main meal - you have to go the 2 week aged hay-smoked duck breast. Skin still crisp, but breast so juicy and fatty. Served on pumpkin seed cornbread that was just the perfect filler. 

Dessert went with the chocolate caramel flan - absolutely gorgeous presentation - cocoa nibs to break the sweetness, milk sorbet to break up the gorgeous heavy flan. 
But you can't go wrong with any of the other desserts - the pistachio frappe brulle was a beautiful blend of vanilla, cherry sorbet and almond, the pineapple carpaccio was also absolutely refreshing. 

Top it all off with the best almond amaretti you could imagine - sweet, sharp, chewy, and the best chocolate decadent squares with cocoa nibs. 

Wonderful service, napkin folded every time I left the table, water glass - I only got to the bottom once. Price per michelin star was great.

The food is something unbelievable. ! This is a perfect place if you have a special occasion. My boyfriend and I had our first anniversary and we decided to try Gabriel Kreuther. This place has really nice located right next to the Bryant Park. They have tables inside and outside. We reserved a table inside and the interior is beautiful there. Service was amazing, when we were seated at our table, we found a cute note that said "happy anniversary." Our waiter was nice, he checked on us every time. 

The food is something unbelievable. If you like to try different dishes and interesting tastes, this place is exactly what you need. We started with really delicious bread with some spread, that was probably the best bread I ever tried. After that, we had Prix fix from the chef and it was good as well. We choose a 3-course meal for each of us. For an appetizer, I had Foie Gras Terrine, the main dish I had 2 Week Aged Hay-Smoked Duck Breast, and for dessert Chocolate Caramel Flan. All three dishes were beyond the perfection, it was super delicious. 

However, after that, the waiter brought us small chocolate and candy to try. The serving was amazing, they put it inside the cacao bean! We were full but it was not eaten. The final was another dessert that was complimentary for our anniversary! This is super cute!

I highly recommend this place for special occasions.

Gabriel Kreuther is a luxurious 2 Michelin star dining experience.

The setting is classy and elegant; the service is attentive without being overbearing; the food was excellent. Some dishes were thoughtful and took you through an experience. Other dishes were tasty and well executed. We all left with full bellies and very satisfied.

We opted for the $145 for four courses. What I loved about the restaurant and fine dining, is the four courses blossomed to 6. With the amuse bouche and the petit fours and the additional ganache cake (we were celebrating a birthday and two anniversaries), there was enough food to go around. 

Amuse bouche was melon citrus gazpacho that was refreshing and a palate cleanser. There were gruyere mochi mini tarts that was savory and left you wanting more. 

Bread platter was a mini Bundt scallion bread that had a thin cheesy crust. 
It was light and buttery and came with a rich avocado cream.

1st course, I opted for the foi gras terrine. It was a flower arrangement of pickled green strawberries, Riesling gelee with house made rye bread. The foie gras was rich, served cold and my favorite part was the cherry balsamic sauce dropped on the dish.

K got the hamachi crudo with pickled rhubarb, avocado and black garlic ponzu. The fresh fish with the different sauces were refreshing and amazing. Def pick this one if it's available.

2nd course was Maryland Blue crab callaloo with smoked fried eel fritters, seaweed, gold rice and blue crab. I liked the blue crab and the green sauce but the dish got super salty at the end. 

My brother shared some of his sturgeon and sauerkraut tart. This had applewood smoke and kaluga cavair. It was flavorful beautifully presented dish. The cream went well with flaky buttery tart. The caviar added some saltiness. It was such a good dish. I liked it better than my soup. 

I tried the seared foie gras with peach jam and cocoa crumble. This was the best 2nd course. Seared foie gras melts and is buttery and paired well with the tart sweet jam. I wish I choose this instead.

3rd course was Hatchery trout baked on cedar with rye berries, cashew cream and yellow vinaigrette. This was ok. I could taste some smokiness but the sauces and creams didn't pair well. I also expected a crispy skin on the trout and there wasn't one. It was smoked fish.

K got the 2 week aged hay smoked duck breast. This blew us all away. The duck breast was juicy and had a beautiful smoked flavor. The skin was crispy. This was the best duck I've ever had. So it is possible to have a perfectly juicy duck breast and a perfectly crisped skin. It was amazing. 

You can skip the cornbread. It does pair well with the duck but the duck is perfect without it. 

Our friends told us how they dreamed of this duck. All the hype and the duck still surpassed our expectations. 

For dessert I had the pineapple carpaccio with matcha biscuit, fresh pineapple and mint granita. It was such a delicate well thought out dessert. The biscuit was buttery and crisp. I enjoyed the layer of coconut cream on top of the fresh pineapple. The shiso leaf didn't add to the dessert but it was fun to eat.

I enjoyed K's pistachio frappe brulee the best. It came with cherry-vanilla marmalade, almond biscuit and cherry sorbet. It was like an amazing deconstructed cherry pie. There were bits of buttery biscuit and cubes of shortbread covered in cherry compote. There were so many textures and flavors. I wish I had a giant bowl of this by myself. 

Chocolate caramel Flan was a classic beautiful French dessert. I enjoyed the coca nib feuilletine. It was crispy and buttery. The milk sorbet was smooth and rich. It was a solid good dessert but wasn't completely novel and mind blowing. 

For the birthday person, the waiters presented a lovely chocolate ganache cake. This was velvety rich and delicious. There were were toffee nut rectangles that framed the cake. 

For petit fours there were chocolate coffee caramels. The caramels were perfectly sweet and had a bite from the coffee. 

Lastly there were almond amaretti that tasted like cherry buttery flaky mini chewy Kouign-amanns. I was obsessed. I didn't think the desserts could get better but they did.

The desserts at GK outshone other NYC Michelin star restaurants. It was a filling tasty meal. Not every dish was perfect or mind blowing but every dish was well executed and satisfying. 

Price for the Michelin star meal was great.

I would def return for the hamachi crudo, seared foie gras, duck breast and cherry frappe brulee.

When I tell you this was the best meal of my life.. I'm not exaggerating. The service was outstanding and the waitress was so kind and had great recommendations. We sat outside in a cute little enclosed area which was nice and quiet despite the traffic. We did the tasting menu which was to die for & not my first time doing a tasting menu either. The duck was cooked beyond perfection, I need to eat it again soon. The fois gras was also delicious and the sauces and pairings were delectable. The desserts were also absolutely delicious. Definitely come have a meal here.

One of the best fine dining experiences in the city every time we come. The amuse bouches are always the perfect beginning to a meal, and it's incredibly difficult not to fill up on their bread before your first course comes. The mussels were the star of our most recent meal but you really can't go wrong with anything on the menu.

We were lucky to get a table for lunch as walk ins. 
The Hen of the woods mushroom tart was amazing. Light crust and perfectly cooked mushrooms. 
Crown toro himachi crudo was 2 tiny pieces of cured himachi. 
Herbed crusted blue shrimp comes with white beans. The dish comes with 4 shrimp. It is delicious. 
For dessert we had the chocolate caramel flan and the strawberry mille fuille. WOW!!! 
Glad they had a table for us the have a memorable lunch.

Gabriel Kreuther didn't disappoint. We had a good dinner with friends, absolutely delicious food. I did love the hamachi and duck. Though, I noticed some servers weren't able to answer some questions with the food which can be improved. I've eaten with some other michelin star restaurants and they can explain well about the food which I found different from Gabriel's. Overall, nice experience and lovely food.
First ever Michelin Star dining experience. The food was excellent and the dining room was beautiful.

The food and service were spectacular. The restaurant itself was very beautiful, although the entrance/exit seemed odd. There were tables out there and I had to go through them to enter and exit. It felt a little awkward for me exiting because I was walking through the tables, disturbing people's meals. 

I got the 6 course tasting menu with the additional upgrade to add another pasta and truffle course. Overall, it was pretty good and left me quite full, but I ate everything, including all of the bread by myself. I would go here again!

Came here for a birthday dinner. Prior to arriving I had read countless reviews on the service being exceptional so I went with high expectations. 

Everyone was very attentive and nice, with the exception of our specific waiter. I found this quite unfortunate and it also felt like he was judging us, only because most parties that were dining were definitely 50+ and appeared to come after work.

We decided to do the prix fixe and several a la carte options. 

The foie gras and duck were very nice. The dessert was also amazing.

The ambience and dining area felt comfortable and relaxing. 

I will definitely be back, but hopefully I won't get the same waiter again.

We loved the 4 course menu here and their cocktails. So many elements of the dishes and cocktails were infused with smoke - every time somebody ordered the famous sturgeon & sauerkraut tart, we would get a whiff of campfire! 

Highlights were the duck breast, strawberry mille feuille and the cocktails. Service was quite attentive - everybody checked on us regularly, and we only had to get somebody's attention to get another drink once. Our four courses were spaced out quite a bit, which was nice because it was a lot of food! So we took our time and spent a bit over two hours there enjoying everything.

visited for their 6 course tasting menu and wine pairing.  overall everything was good.  didn't find anything outstanding except perhaps our waiter.  they were very good about accommodating food preferences.  the wine pairings were mostly disappointing.  

one thing they did that we very rarely see is that they gave each of us (party of 3) a different dessert, which allowed us to share and try different desserts.  that was a particularly nice touch.

see pictures and commentary on each course

I made a reservation for a party of 7 a month previous. However, they insisted it was for 6. As a result my daughter was unable to join us for dinner although there were plenty of seats available. Our table was definitely able to accommodate 7. In addition, the service was subpar, especially considering that it is a Michelin 2 star restaurant. The server wasn't that great, in fact he was a bit rude. He stepped on three different people's shoes and caused some damage on one of them. Additionally, as he was cleaning the table he spilled some food scraps onto one of our party. This would have been acceptable, as accidents happen, had he apologized at all. Yet he acted as though he didn't notice at all and said nothing, though it had been obvious. A smaller concern was that for one of the dishes from the six course tasting menu was not introduced at all. However, considering the pandemic, I still put a $300 tip on the $1,447 bill. I will not be returning.

very nice outdoor dining experience.  they have both indoor and outdoor to choose from.

Extensive wine and drink list, cocktails are expensive but well worth it!

Food portions look small, but it is a French restaurant so still calorically intense and filling.  I had the kale salad and the fish entree-- quite nice.  My companion's food was delish as well and she graciously offered me a few bited which were heavenly.

Gets a little more people as the evening wears on, but tables are spaced well enough apart that it wasnt ovwrtly uncomfortable.

Summary: I enjoyed every item in this 6-course prix fixe. Was blown away. Received more than the $215 I paid (per person). I enjoyed this more than my other favorite Alsatian restaurant (Jean-Georges). This was my third time here.

My favorite dishes:

1. The 2-week aged duck breast was the best duck breast I've ever had. A few weeks ago I went to Jean-Georges which had a duck breast on the menu and this was a level above that. The [wet?] aging process made the duck breast smell and taste kind of like pork bacon. Total flavor bomb

2. I forget what it's called but it's this little cold dish with sun-dried tomatoes, goat cheese and other stuff. It had 5 layers of flavor that came in sequence on your tongue. Sour at the start and smokey at the end. From a culinary arts point of view, this was very impressive

3. Foie gras terrine... so fatty and flavorful with a long duration of flavor on your tongue. I always come to French restaurants expecting good foie gras and they delivered

The other savory dishes were all great but the above are the most memorable to me. 

The orecchiette was kind of so-so. I could hardly taste the flavor from the black truffle slices, and those crunchy bits dominated the flavor profile for me.

For their famous saukeraut and sturgeon tart... the presentation was stunning and the taste was good.

The dessert was more so-so. I am not a big raspberry sorbet guy but all these tasting menu places include that in their desserts. 

My one complaint with the experience, and I've been to Gabriel Kreuther several times so this isn't a one-off thing and it seems to be unique to this restaurant compared to any of its peers that I've been to. The sommeliers are arrogant and irritating. If you ask them for a recommendation they'll try to push you to a $300-500 bottle of wine, and they'll walk away mid-conversation without a word when you decline. Don't you think it's at least courteous to give a range to accommodate for budgets you didn't bother to ascertain?

My guy, I make at least 10x your paycheck but I still wouldn't drop $500 for a random bottle (which is probably marked up by 100%) that probably tastes 5% better than a wine I could get for $50 at my local store. Your job is literally redundant - you're a glorified high margin drinks salesperson and serious wine drinkers either already know what to get or can just use Vivino. The other wait staff are lovely, they teach us about the food, they are polite and make for a wonderful experience and they actually add value to the experience, but you are redundant.

Otherwise, service was phenomenal as expected

We made our reservation for dinner at Gabriel Kreuther online with Resy only 6 days prior.  It was so last minute that I was pleasantly surprised that they still had availability, and I wondered if we lucked out because of the recent reopening.  They checked all guests' COVID vaccination proof as mandated by the city.  

Gabriel Kreuther has a very elegant dining room, quite fitting for its Michelin 2-star status.  The seats are comfortable and far apart from other tables.  Our waitress went over the 3 different dinner options with us: 3 courses for $120, 4 courses for $145, and 6 courses/tasting menu for $215.  Only the tasting menu comes with the requirement for all guests at the table to order it.  Among the 4 of us, I was the only one ordering the 4-course dinner, and the waitress convinced my friends to order a flambee to share before they got their 3 courses, so that they won't have to stare at me eating my first course.  

Tasting notes:
Smoked heirloom tomato consommé: very refreshing on a hot summer day.  The crown toro hamachi was very fresh and paired well with the slices of cucumber.  A great opening to the dinner!

Seared Sullivan County foie gras: this was my appetizer, which does cost an additional $10 but is totally worthwhile cuz I love seared foie gras, and this one was completely satisfying!  The peach jam paired very well with the rich foie gras.

Hawaiian red crab callaloo: though I didn't try this one, my friends raved about this dish.  It has a very beautiful presentation.  

Charred Atlantic black bass: I generally don't like ordering fish at a French restaurant because I have some skewed taste buds that think fish is bettered served by Asians lol.  I've tried trout and other fish from Ledoyen, Paris and Le Bernardin, NYC (the latter is especially known for its seafood!) and continue to firmly uphold this belief.  Black bass, however, is an exception.  The bass was soft and mildly rich, and the polenta, marmalade, and vinaigrette not only complemented the bass well, they were also decently filling.  

2-week aged hay-smoked duck breast: this one is the winner of the night.  The duck breast tasted amazing with a very thin layer of crispy duck skin and meat so tender and juicy, and the portion was quite handsome.  I can't comment the sides since I only had a bite of my friend's entree. 

Chocolate caramel flan: this was the winner among desserts IMO.  The flan was silky and has just the right amount of sweetness.  The milk sorbet served as its perfect counterpart.

Pistachio frappe brûlée: this was my dessert, but I didn't like it quite as much.  It's presented with a nice color palette - a pastel green with gold sprinkled on top.  However, when I received it, its top seemed to have fallen off halfway (see picture).  The elements also don't seem to come together too well.  

The amuse bouche, my glass of brut, the petit 4, and chocolates were all very refreshing and enjoyable.  In fact, the chocolate was so good that 2 of us finished the whole big piece when the other 2 were full (We were full, too, but couldn't resist).  Overall, I'd give the food 4.5 stars and do think that it's on par with some of the Michelin 3-starred restaurants that I've tried around the world!  

We had a slightly unpleasant encounter with the service.  Two of the appetizers were accidentally switched and served to the wrong people at our table.  We didn't catch this until we had a bite of the food from the plates to find out.  When we raised this to our waitress' attention, she was initially defensive about this, insisting that the dishes were served to the right people and that they had ordered them that way (the only way I can interpret her words is that my friends were the ones who couldn't remember what they had ordered only 45 minutes ago?).  Therefore, when the waitress first left our table, we were left with the impression that nothing was going to be done to fix this mistake.  To be exact, she asked my friends to switch up their plates on their own, after they've taken bites of the food.  It wasn't until minutes later that the manager came out to let us know that they will fix this mistake and serve my friends 2 new plates.  While my friends were new to the Michelin restaurant experience, I've been to many of them, and it is exceedingly rare that a 2- or 3-starred restaurant would mix up an order (in fact, I cannot recall it ever happening to me), let alone not replacing something that the guests are not completely happy with.  It is unfortunate that my friends had to experience subpar service and think that's the norm for a Michelin 2-star restaurant.  Aside from this incident, service was okay but not exceptional (Did I mention that my napkin wasn't folded when I got up to go to the restroom? Lol).  I took a star off because of the service.  Having read other recent reviews, I seriously wonder if Gabriel Kreuther would've been a 3-star restaurant had it not been for its service...

Absolutely wonderful prix fixe menu at a reasonable price. Attentive but not in your face service and a great variety of tastes and textures.

For our 4 course meal we started with a light amuse bouche that was vibrant and delicious. Wonderful start. The tomato consommé was interesting, gelatinous tomato with a smoky flavor. Hamachi toro accompaniment was nice but it quite sure how it fit with the tomato dish.

The Sturgeon and Sauerkraut tart was the star for me. Delicious, unique, and one of the best bites in NYC.

The bass dish was nice; though unremarkable. And I tried a bit of the speciality duck and personally was glad I didn't order it (if you like bacon though, it might be for you).

And the dessert was top notch. Nice paired with an amaro.
Beautiful and exquisite food, wonderful wines recommended by knowledgeable sommeliers, and creative cocktails. Always a wonderful and relaxing evening at this special restaurant.

We had such a special Anniversary Dinner at Gabriel Kreuther last Friday (August 2021) and are now telling all our friends to come here!

PRICES: The price here is truly unbeatable, for both the exquisite food and 2-Michelin-star service. We went with the 4-course and still couldn't finish everything.
3-course prix fixe: $120
4-course prix fixe: $145
6-course tasting menu: $215

FOOD: Everything here was delicious, and some dishes (callaloo) were truly unforgettable for me. For each course I put first what I thought tasted the best. 

- Course 1: Smoked heirloom tomato consommé (light and refreshing) + Foie gras terrine

- Course 2: Hawaiian red crab "callaloo" (hands down my fave dish of the night, it had a very Southeast Asian taste!!) + Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart (my partner also enjoyed this)

- Course 3 (mains): Duck breast + Strip steak

- Course 4: (desserts): Anniversary dessert (I'm still dreaming of this! Think it was some sort of hazelnut mousse) + Stone fruit frappe brûlée + Chocolate caramel flan 

Also plus points for the beautiful plates and bowls! Thank you to our sommelier for giving us the card of the local artist who creates their ceramics, bowls, and plates.


SERVICE / ENVIRONMENT: I have so many examples of amazing service throughout the night. 1) Alvaro our server took dozens of photos of us, 2) when we gushed about our dishes, our sommelier immediately gave us the card of the local ceramic artist, 3) the restaurant manager checked in on us during our meal and made sure our experience was the best. Everyone was very nice and professional; the service was just enough and never overbearing (looking at you Jean-Georges), and we always felt attended to but not stifled. The indoor dining room is spacious and beautiful, and we got greats seats - I only wish the restaurant were more filled like it was before the pandemic. When we arrived for our reservation, our hostess also verified our vaccine status and showed us to our table only upon confirmation that we were vaccinated. Made me feel much safer.

11/10 experience - Gabriel Kreuther is a gem we'll return to for future occasions!

A beautiful dinner and amazing experience! Came with friends to have a special dinner at a Michelin Star restaurant and the entire meal was superb. We all ordered the Prix Fixe 4-course and chose different starters, mids, mains, and desserts and were able to try a taste of all the menu offerings. 

Service was always so kind and attentive without being overbearing and explained every dish to us as it arrived. We were treated so well with care and patience the entire time; I was even given a coffee with my dinner (even though it was a weird request at 9pm) and they brought me additional lattes once I finished without me even having to ask! 

We received complimentary bread and amuse bouche to start our meal. The bread here is incredible-- so soft, savory, and flavorful. It was hard not to get too full off of just the bread alone. 

Starters: 
- Hamachi Crudo: fresh fish and delicious sauce dollops, so well presented and beautifully crafted. The sauces tasted amazing and bursting with flavor.
- Foie Gras Terrine: creamy and decadent, pairing well with the acidity from the strawberries 

Mid (highly recommend the tart!):
- Sturgeon and Sauerkraut Tart: an iconic menu item here and one of their most popular offerings, presented  extravagantly with the waiter blowing smoke out of a glass when it is brought to you. A perfect savory flavor enhanced with caviar, juxtaposed with a delicate tart. Everyone at my table loved this one.

Mains:
- Greenwalk Hatchery Trout: Tender fish and fragrant champagne sauce, paired with local rye berries. I really enjoyed this one! 
- 2 week Aged Hay-Smoked Duck Breast: my friend really enjoyed the rich, smokey flavor of this duck dish. Well crafted and prepared, tasted sophisticated. 

Desserts (the best!!): 
The desserts here were all mind blowing and pure perfection, truly some of the most elevated and amazing desserts I've ever tasted. Our entire table was awestruck. Probably the best part of our dinner and the most perfect ending. 

- Pistachio Creme Brûlée (10000/10): This was INCREDIBLE. Super light whipped pistachio cream atop layers of berries and a light sponge. The playful mismatch of textures made every bite a delightful treat. Just the right amount of sweet and a perfect blend of flavors in harmony. Truly immaculate. I don't even have the words. 

- Strawberry Mille-Feuille (100/10): Amazing and worth the extra $7 add on. The caramelized puff pastry is nested around a yuzu sorbet. This had such a beautiful flavor and tasted fresh and decadent. An elegant dessert with the most beautiful presentation and a wonderful taste to match. 

- Chocolate Caramel Flan and Pineapple Carpaccio were also both incredible and amazing! Honestly you can't go wrong with any dessert you order here because all of the options were insanely delicious and beautifully crafted. 

The meal ended with complimentary chocolate with a berry filling and it was divine. Incredibly high quality and crafted with grace.

Amazing food with the most beautiful desserts and excellent service. Good value too at $145 for four courses at a Michelin Star restaurant with great service and the amount of carefully prepared and well crafted food. This was a wonderful dinner and I highly recommend a visit if you're looking for a place to celebrate a special occasion, or just to treat yourself to some of the best dessert ever.

Exquisite !
Dined here in June 

Surprise dinner for my Boyfriend's 30th ! 
 Had a lovely card signed waiting at the table which was a nice touch :)
The service , presentation, ambience everything was great :) 

We got the pre-fix 4 course

The Amuse Bouches were a nice touch :) 
The fresh bread and chive dip were just toooo good ! 

What we got 
To Begin 
-Hamachi 
-Foie gras terrine 

Great great start 

Mid 
Sturgeon and Sauerkraut Tart
You HAVE to get this ! 
It was recommended to us by our server and so glad we got it .

Main 
Greenwalk Hatchery Trout on Cedar Plank 
This was an experience. Melt in the mouth and a party
 of flavors !! 
2 Week aged hay smoked duck breast 
Definitely recommend this !!! Smokey , Juicy .it's served with  cornbread 

Dessert 
Pistachio frappé creme brûlée

They also brought out a chocolate ganache pastry for the birthday  . 

Thank you for a great night :)

For our wedding anniversary my wife and I always dine at Gramarcy Tavern, but they were very booked, so we decided to try Gabriel Kreuther for a relaxed and indulgent and expensive lunch for 2 (we spend $408 after the tip for lunch). The food was great, better food (but more expensive) than Gramarcy tavern. the dining room was beautiful and feels like you are dining in one of those extravagant Manhattan dining rooms like you see in the movies. But the service and overall experience were tarnished because of the cold, distant, unhelpful service of the waiter. The waiter just stood over our table and glared at us and asked us what we wanted to order. He did this every time he approached the table. There we no greeting, no openness to questions, no nothing in terms of hospitality or service. Any questions we had were met with cold glares and very little answers or explanations. Its like this guy was doing us a favor to just take our order and didn't want to deal with any interaction or simple questions from us regarding anything. It was such a turn off. It was the opposite of hospitality (which is what Danny Myer preaches and is why we love Gramarcy Tavern).
And this place is expensive - so we expected more. My duck was $38, the glass of Pinot Noir to go with my duck was $41. So that may not be a lot for some ppl, but is the most ive ever spent on a glass of wine in my life, and I don't mind spending money on good food and drink (the cocktail I had was $25 and was just ok, nothing special). 
So great food, really great food, beautiful dining room, but I cant deal with service that is cold, off-putting, unhelpful, and uninformative.

This is the best 2 Michelin star restaurant I ever ate at and probably the 2nd best restaurant I ever ate at.

Service was superb, I want here with someone for their birthday and they prepped a card welcoming her. They also have a free chocolate cake with a candle for her. 

The food was amazing:
1. Their tomato soup was the best dish of the night and basically a bacon tasting jello with tomato inside, it was both delicious and also eye opening 
2. Their sturgeon dish was really good too. Both the flavoring combo of artichoke, cream, caviar and fish and also the presentation with the smoke dome was great 
3. Blue shrimp pasta was the only disappointment of the night, it was so salty I had to drink water after every bite 
4. Their amusee Bouche was so good it was easily the best course of the night; their citrus mezcal Jell-O shot was simple but really really good

Absolutely perfect meal. Every element on every plate was perfect in execution. 

Miso Steak: Perfect smooth bite and savoriness. 

Seared Foie: Not quite as impressive a flavor as the foie terrine, but the execution was great. The smooth liver with the crisp edge and peach spread all came together in perfect balance. 

Sturgeon and Sauerkraut Tarte: This sounds odd, but it works. The light foam and caviar, the marine flavors, the subtle sauerkraut. 

The foie gras terrine was silky smooth and buttery in flavor. 

The bread was fluffy and buttery. And it's dipping sauce tasted like a high end ranch. 

My server suggested the French Meteor beer. It was the perfect selection. 

This meal was worth the $300. There are few places you will get a meal this interesting and well balanced with everything cooked perfectly.

This restaurant was the perfect choice for our anniversary dinner!

We opted for the 3-course prix fixe dinner and each course got better and better. Initially we were greeted with a savory chive kugelhopf with butter - light, fluffy, and savory. Then we got an assortment of treats as our amuse-bouche, gazpacho, curry, and some sort of almost gelatinous bites. The gazpacho was perfectly chilled and creamy, and the curry packed an amazing punch. 

For my first course I opted for the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart. The presentation was beautifully presented, the crust was very flaky, the sauerkraut was mild, and the caviar was delectable. 

For my entree I selected the 2 week aged hay-smoked duck breast with gold bar squash caponata, roasted eggplant, and the most amazing pumpkin cornbread. The portion was massive and perfectly cooked. The caponata had a lovely sweetness from the golden raisins, and the pumpkin cornbread was melt in your mouth delicious. I also tried the trout, and it was also delicious and I was obsessed with the smoky flavors. 

For dessert I selected the fig carpaccio. It had a beautiful flaky crust, wasn't overly sweet, and perfectly matched with olive ice cream on top. In addition, we also received the most delightful chocolate cake for our anniversary and Gabriel Kreuther chocolates. The ones on top of a speculoos cookie were my favorite. 

For cocktails, I selected one off the menu which included watermelon (I forgot the name). It was a great-sized portion and perfectly balanced without being too sweet.

Service was impeccable here and our servers were very attentive. I would love to return here for another special occasion!

I was really unimpressed unfortunately. This is my second 2 star Michelin and after several 1 star Michelin places, this fell flat. Unmemorable dishes and flavors. I went in fall of 2020 so almost a year ago, my bf and I sat outside and the environment was beautiful but I don't remember a single dish we ordered.

Proudly, one of the "triples"- i.e. this restaurant is 1 of the top 3 dining experiences we've had in 2021 so far. Our only nit was the hotel'ish like ambiance. Everything else in this review will, quite literally, be filled with superlatives- so I apologize in advance.

We actually went here for my birthday because this is essentially a special occasion type of place and it wears that moniker quite well.

But on to the food... we had the four-course prix-fixe. I had four dishes and my dining companion had four different dishes so that we could maximize our experience. Now cue the superlatives...

To say that ever single dish was excellent would be a significant understatement. Normally I would just leave it at that and let you go try it on your own. But for this restaurant I think I'll dive a bit deeper...

Starting with the SMOKED HEIRLOOM TOMATO CONSOMMÉ... how the chef managed to bring out the very essence of summer in every bite, we're still trying to figure it out...

And then the SEARED FOIE GRAS... do you know how much foie gras I've had in the past year (let alone in my life)? I would place this version in my top 10... of all time.

And for the mains, a tie for greatness between the HAY-SMOKED DUCK BREAST and the CHARRED ATLANTIC BLACK BASS... Greatness.

And then... and then, for no good reason except that it was just that kinda night, the chef sends out an extra dish that we didn't even order! A pasta dish with beautiful shaved truffles... And... it was the best dish of the night!... Maybe the best dish of any night, anywhere!

And at that point, our minds were blown, we ascended to a higher culinary plane, and the rest of the night was just a blur- I think we may have blacked out...

We also treated ourselves to the smoked bacon flambee, because... well because it was my birthday (keep up)... 5 stars

and several cocktails... 5 stars

and desserts... 5 stars

and for the excellent service... you get 5 stars

...5 stars across the board!!!

Very nice service here, but unfortunately I wasn't a fan of the food, especially at this price range. We had the 6 course tasting menu, and most of them weren't that memorable. Visually very pleasing, but I felt like I was having a "french version" of other cuisines (Chinese, Korean, Mexican, etc) that weren't executed all that cleanly. Would give 3 for food but the atmosphere and service brought my rating back up to 4. It was def nice having so much caviar in the first few dishes tho!

This restaurant is ridiculously over priced. The portions are teeny. We laughed throughout the evening at the ludicrous portions. 
I would not go back. Don't waste your time.

Gabriel Kreuther is wonderful in all respects, from ambiance to food to service. For me, it is the successor to Eleven Madison for the crown of Best Restaurant in New York, and one of the best in the US.

The dining room, with its dramatic arc of salvaged wood beams, is both open and intimate, with the tables spaced far apart to make each one cozy, and the ceiling high enough to afford a pleasant sound level.  A glass wall affords a view of the kitchen, which is a busy hive of about twenty chefs and cooks under the supervision of Chef Kreuther. The atmosphere seemed more convivial than in many of the Michelin kitchens I've encountered.

The restaurant's recommendation for first-time guests is the Six Course Tasting menu. This is not only a great recommendation but a great bargain. At $215 (as of this writing) it is, in short, a steal. I don't know how they came up with the number six, but including amuse bouche and ending sweets, there were at least 15 different dishes over a three-hour period. 

Speaking of dishes, these were some of the most beautiful serving pieces I've ever encountered, and the glassware is stellar as well.

As for the food, it is almost pointless to describe it, as everything was wonderful, and it was impossible to pick favorites. It changes regularly, but I will mention a few that rank among the best dishes I've ever had: pate de foie gras (best flavor/texture I've encountered), smoked heirloom tomato consume (more of a gelatin, and endlessly intriguing), sturgeon tart (delicate flavorful and complex), and all the breads (there were at least four, accompanying various dishes).

As mentioned earlier, service was near perfect, with two dozen wait staff performing an intricate (and high speed) choreography to synchronize each course at each table.

Compared to the food prices, the wine bottle prices seem like less of a deal, but are certainly not unreasonable for Manhattan. The wines by the glass are an interesting assortment of styles and places of origin.

This is my new favorite restaurant in New York.

Hubby & I traveled from Washington D.C. to NYC just to dine at this establishment & service & food fell short. We made reservations almost a month in advance. I called a couple times to confirm & also add that we are celebrating our anniversary. The day of, they even called me to confirm the reservation & asked if we are celebrating a special day.

Our server was very to-the-point but polite. No small talk or warm hospitality, which was fine. They were very busy on a Saturday night. The amuse bouche was an interesting start to the meal.  The tomato soup shot was super concentrated & just too tart. For my 1st course, I got the tomato consomme. It was difficult to eat & I couldn't finish it...extremely salty & too sour. The toro Hamachi that came alongside it was also very sour so it was just one note with no balance to the acidity. My hubby got the foie gras terrine which was exceptional. The balance of flavors were on point & the moist banana bread that came with it was divine. Definitely get this.

Next I got the sturgeon tart (one of their signatures). It was tasty but nothing exceptional. Basically puff pastry shell, with some fish & a cream sauce. Again, too salty. Hubby got the red crab callaloo. The eel fritters that accompanied it was again, way too salty & hard to eat. On to the next.

I got the duck breast which was chewier than I would've liked but the skin was perfectly crispy. Stuffed squash blossom & corn bread was excellent. Hubby really enjoyed his black bass. For dessert I got the the stone fruit frappe brulee. EXTREMELY sour. Again, could not finish it. Hubby's chocolate caramel flan was delicious. 

It was the end of the meal & still no recognition of an anniversary. We sat there & watched every table around us get a hand-written note & a comp dessert. When you spend $400+ at a 2 Michelin star restaurant, the service should be exceptional & each dish should be balanced in terms of flavor. We were very disappointed from our experience here. The ambience & decor is wonderful though. Overall, nothing special.

Very nice restaurant with several creative dishes.  Excellent service throughout the night.  A couple of dishes were a little disappointing - a taco which was no more spectacular that what you could get in a good Mexican restaurant and a pasta dish which also did not meet top Italian levels.  I guess the advice is that if you want to reinvent a classic, it needs to be truly fantastic.  Also, the wine recommendation was too expensive for the quality.

High end prix fixe meals that lives up to the reputation. They have a small outdoor patio as well as a beautiful vast inner dining room w tables spaced more than 6' apart. Service was excellent without being suffocating and the menu selections were fantastic. Loved being able to have foie gras again! You won't go wrong with your selection.
The interior is beautiful and the waiters were friendly. Food is good but some would say overpriced.

this was my first time spending so much on a meal and I did not regret it haha. I loved the atmosphere of this place. my friend and I got dressed up and decided we wanted to splurge and eat great food. we had food and tasted flavors unlike ever before and the staff was great. definitely recommended coming here for an anniversary or romantic date night. if you come here I recommend sitting inside tho since the area is noisy.
Had an amazing dinner at the bar. Service was great, cocktails and food were impeccable. Would love to try the tasting menu one day ... bar only had a la carte which we enjoyed immensely!

We dined at Gabriel Kreuther to celebrate our 20-year anniversary, and the restaurant did not disappoint.  The staff made this a true celebration, acknowledging our event and even including a personal note of congratulations.  They were friendly and surprisingly unstuffy for such a fine restaurant.  For starters, I ordered a martini, and it truly was the best I've ever had -- one of the servers told me the bartender uses a special vermouth, and it really made a noticeable difference.  And then there's the food.  I had the signature sturgeon and sauerkraut tart, followed by the smoked duck breast and the apple tartin.  All were simply fantastic.  This just became my favorite Manhattan restaurant.
I had dinner indoors twice... Gorgeous dining room. Incredible concept. Amazing food. Bumbling and inept waitstaff. Offensive management. SAD.

Flammekueche from a 2 Michelin starred chef? Yes please! When I saw GK was just two blocks from our hotel, I thought a late dinner in the lounge would make a perfect first meal in NYC and it did. Because it was late we opted for a la carte options. After the tarte flambe I had the signature smoked sturgeon and my wife had the hamachi crudo, both were sublime. For entrees she had the trout which was remarkable and I had the duck confit. I loved the dish, but it was rich the ample amount of polenta made it a bit heavy. The two breads - a savory kuglehopf and a sour dough roll were perfection. While we were really intrigued by the dessert options, we opted to try them on our next visit.

Absolutely amazing restaurant. The service was outstanding and the meal was to die for. Everything was perfectly cooked and delicious. The miso steak is a must try. Every dessert is as tasty as it is beautiful. For a Michelin star restaurant it is very reasonable priced.

One of my favorite places in NYC! Their hot chocolate is very thick and chocolatey, perfect for chocolate lovers! They even have a cocktail made from it. Their chocolate desserts are great. The set menu comes with this delicious warm scallion bread. Can't go wrong with anything on the menu! Also very attentive staff who left us leave our luggage with them as well.

I booked a table for 1 during the lunch rush, in which inside is nothing but! The atmosphere is one of Sophistication which invites you to sit back relax and take in the experience. I chose from the prix fixe menu and started off with the arancini amuse buche, which was delightful. The kougelhof was phenomenal. I was happy to be alone because I had it all to myself. That chive fromage blanc was devine. I'd come back to this restaurant for that only! I continued the course with the hamachi crudo, followed by the bass. Now, i love me some desert, and the chocolate caramel flan did not disappoint. It's everything I want in a dessert: perfect balance of salty and sweet as well as the light flan texture contrasted with the crunchy cocoa nib feuilletine. I honestly thought the portions were just right considering the multi course set up. The meal was capped off with a sampling of 3 chocolates from the chocolate shop. I love additional treats!! I was quite filled by the end and most importantly: HAPPY. The wait staff were very attentive. I was seated next to a fun couple who even sent me over a glass of Champagne. What a delightful experience. I'll definitely be back with family and friends. 5

My girlfriend and I came here for our 1 year anniversary and they made sure it was such an unforgettable experience. I was impressed with their coat service and the server was extremely polite, knowledgeable and timely. They went out of their way to help us celebrate our anniversary with a card and an extra chocolate mousse at the end.
We got the 4 course meal but don't let the sizes of the dishes fool you, we were more than full at the end especially with all the extra bread and starters they provide.
Standout dishes that you should definitely look out for include the langoustine tartare which had a beautiful balance with the langoustine being sweet and the tuna more citrusy.
The duck had a nice harmony with the hazelnut on top and in case the dish was getting too heavy for your tastes, the squash added freshness that alleviated all the fat.
The second best dish of the night was the foie gras which I honestly didn't expect to like. The flavor was strong but I can see the dish being on the heavier side.
The trout had to be first place. Incredibly tender pretty much literally melting in your mouth, Id say the fish is a must try dish here. 
For dessert, I'd say the Mont Blanc stood out among the rest. Sweet, light, creamy, perfection. 
Thank you GK for making my one year a memorable one!

Came here for an anniversary and GK really made the night so special. From the ambiance to their service, the whole place is perfect. They even made sure to give us a special card and chocolate mousse at the end since we were celebrating. 

Although the portions seem smaller you will definitely leave here full since they have a seemingly never ending array of delicious bread. The Langoustine Tartare was a little too sour for my liking, but everything else was so delicious. The eel and squid ink pasta was full of flavor and the egg yolk that splits on top gives the whole dish a savory richness. The duck was cooked to perfection with the squash purée on the side cutting the fattiness of the duck. Had the Apple Tartin for dessert but preferred the chocolate mousse cake instead. Not only was it beautiful to look at but the rich chocolate flavor was to die for. Truly a night to remember.

Completely underwhelmed. 2 stars as the decor is nice and the staff mostly pleasant, but everything else 1 star. I was looking forward to trying this 2 Michelin Star spot, but now that we went I am confused as to the rating. The ratings here seem to rave about this place, but I cannot for the life of me understand how after visiting this week. The restaurant decor is nice and chic, but the service and food is very okay at best. Granted we went on a week day, so maybe that's a different staff than weekend but for a $700 dinner, for two people, our expectations were much higher. Now, we have been to many Michelin star restaurants before so we have a bar we tend to assume these spots will hold up to, but Gabriel Kreuther wasn't even close. From the start: we sat down and ordered, our sever was nice and informative In the beginning (he lacked at the end, maybe he was tired and wanted to go home) but as for the wine serving gentlemen (I will not call him a som) his knowledge in wine was bare min if anything at all. He didn't explain the wine whatsoever to us each pour, we had to keep asking our sever for him to return to order another glass, and he seemed quite checked out. While he was polite, his knowledge in wine was clearly not there. Also, we're willing to spend money on drinks and we had to keep asking to find him!! Now the food, mostly bland and nothing beyond the ordinary like you'll typically receive at a 2star. We did the 4 course pre fix, since we were too late for the chefs table order and it didn't exceed any expectations. Our waiter told us most of the items on the pre-fix are on the chefs table anyways so we were not missing much/ well I am glad he said that because I would have been even more disappointed if we paid $1,000 for similar, basic, bland food items. Dessert was awful, honestly reminded me of a dry, tasteless Eucharist cracker. So we had poor wine service, bland food, and horrible dessert. We do not plan to visit here again. We went so we can say we tried it, but never again. Maybe those that enjoy this place haven't attended other Michelin restaurants that blow this one away by their food, experience and beverages.

Such great service and the portions are pretty large. We got the tasting menu for 3 people and I think if we got 2, it would have been more than plenty. 

We did family style for all courses so we got to taste a bit of each. 

They forgot about a drink order so they came with a special drink for the table. Very nice of them.

Gabriel Kreuther has become one of my go to places to indulge in food. The food is consistently good, but above all the service is always exceptional and the ambiance is calm and relaxing. I usually get the dinner prix fix and the variations with season are great. I've come here for birthdays and most recent my anniversary. The food is adventurous in plating and flavor, although I'm not the biggest fan of super citrus flavors like their red apple gelee. I highly recommend their classic dish of sturgeon & sauerkraut tart. It's a rich, creamy, but savory tart. Their duck breast is also a must when I go but I've heard great reviews of their steak from friends who get it. Their desserts are good. Dense and sweet. I'm usually satisfied and too full to finish them. I highly recommend their cocktails though! They're all amazing and well worth the price.

Fun Fact: there is bar dining walk up options
-
Let me preface this review by saying that seafood is not my cup of tea, and why my review might sway a bit less than someone who might. 

I opted for the 3 course & each of the 3 had a seafood option so it kept my options limited. The server was nice enough to offer a vegan pasta dish as a sub for one of them, but unfortunately very salty and it was a wasted dish. 

I'll start off with the great: beautiful restaurant overlooking Bryant Park. It's contemporary French American two Michelin star restaurant and named as one of the best in the world so I was excited to give it a whirl. 

The complimentary onion bread that came out was out of this world. I've never had anything like it before and was greatly appreciated. 

The Red Apple Consommé was absolutely a delight. Refreshing, just slightly sweet in the best ways, and an a beautiful piece of art. The root vegetable tempura that it came with was also perfectly crispy and delicious. 

Our vegan pasta was overly salty, and the duck breast was a bit gamey for my taste ( and yes I've had my share of duck before). 

Service was fine and the gentlemen were polite but nothing more. He didn't come back to ask how our food went but rather came back and forth to clear and clean our tables. We would have appreciated a bit more conversation so we could share our thoughts. Likewise, I didn't raise my hand to share as I did not want to be disrespectful. This was truly a one of a kind experience, though at the same time I did not feel my money spent was worth what I received. I may not have the right palette for this place, and I've heard great things- so to each their own.

Visit: September 2021, dinner

Michelin 2 stars, feels slightly more casual than other 2 stars in the city. The prix fixe menu is a good value ($140 as of September 2021), although in hindsight I would've gone with the 3 course instead of 4 as the portions were generous and I was stuffed. 

Came specifically to try Alsatian food. In general each course had layers of flavor and was a good portion size. Service was impeccable. My favorites were the smoked heirloom tomato consomme and the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart. Definitely worth a detour. I also noticed that many of the items are still on the menu with seasonal variations. 

We went for the first dinner seating. The entrance was confusing as it isn't shown as an entrance until close to opening time, so if you go early you won't see it. For the record, it's on the west side of the front. I didn't go to the bathroom but I heard that there are a lot of stairs. 

In order of service (with some shared courses):
- Kougelhopf, chive fromage blanc⁣⁣: my first kougelhopf and it did not disappoint. Perfect for sharing.
- Amuse bouche: 3 petit items - yuzu jelly, a puff, and a soup
- First course: smoked heirloom tomato consomme with a side of crown toro hamachi. Beautiful to look at and was great for a hot summer day. The pairing of flavors was unique and a perfect appetizer.
- First course: foie gras terrine. It came with pickled jackfruit, gelees, and banana bread! 
- Shared course: Cinco jotas (5j) jamon. Delicious. 
- Second course: sturgeon and sauerkraut tart. Presentation was 5 stars. The applewood smoke smelled heavenly. 
- Second course: seared Sullivan County foie gras. The cocoa crumble was a nice touch. For fans of seared foie gras, this will not disappoint. 
- Second course: Hawaiian red crab callaloo with smoked eel fritters. I thought this dish tasted a bit more Asian. I didn't care for it as much. 
- Third course: 2 week aged hay-smoked duck breast. Huge, thick portion (especially when compared to EMP's famous duck) with crispy skin.
- Side: zucchini gratin was ok. Ordered because I thought we would need it but it was too much. 
- Fourth course: stone Fruit frappe brulee was pretty but I guess I don't like stone fruit as much as I thought.
- Fourth course: strawberry mille feuille
- Fourth course: chocolate caramel flan. I thought this was one of the best ones. 
- Petit fours

Wow - probably one of the best if not THE best michelin star (two to be exact) experience ever- the candles, ambiance, service, attentiveness of the staff was impeccable- the food was like watching artistry play out on our dishes ... you felt like you were transported in time with the elegance and substantive presentation of allllll the things.... This place has not give up up on the old world elegance and charm for the new casual and at times flippant fads newer high end dining spots often feel like they employ... also the most "affordable" of the fine dining spectrum that we've been to! Loved it all!

8.5/10

Very enjoyable experience, on the pricey side but if you enjoy your food and the experience worth the trip.

I don't like getting to much into the specific flavor profiles of the different food because everyone is different, rather give a more broad review.

Restaurant is beautiful, the staff was very helpful, had a great balance of when to come over when to give you space.

You eat with your eyes nose and mouth and they ticked all the boxes. The presentation and theater of it all was outstanding. 

The food which is the reason your there for, OUTSTANDING a no complaints at all. They nailed it.

Would highly recommend to go and try if your a foodie, if your not into the food and the whole show, probably not worth the money.

We had dinner here today. It's definitely overpriced. We ordered the 225$ tasting menu. Some of the ingredients are cheap. And there is not enough protein. The taste of the food is not bad, but doesn't match the price.
On the other side, the service is pretty nice.

Usually not a big fan of French food, but decided to give GK a try since my friend raved about it. 

We opted for the pre fixe menu as we wanted to order all different things and try as much of their menu as we could.
