The bread at the beginning was amazing. I love bread and theirs was so flavorful and went so well with the spread. I probably asked for extra bread 4 or 5 times. 

The main, protein courses were great. Cooked well and enjoyed it although the portions were quite large and hard to finish. 

Moving onto the dessert - quite large and definitely on the sweet end. I definitely enjoy sweets but don't like overly sweet stuff. I think it was quite hard to finish toward the end. 

We felt super full afterward - not sure if it's just us though or if it's because it's quite heavy for our tastes, but we did notice that we would be SO full after eating at French restaurants (except atelier crenn). 

Overall, not bad - definitely one of the better French restaurants I've been to but still just not my taste.

Ingredients are very common, and tiny. I can probably get them from supermarket, like sauerkraut, chocolate, and potato. Very upset when 4 slices of potatoes were served. Cute plates and beautiful-looking food, but it's FORM OVER SUBSTANCE. 

Let's face the truth, it's not better than the 1-star Michelin restaurant Ai Fiori. Ai Fiori serves more protein food than Gabriel (see pictures). Only 1/4 pate was Foie Gras, not a full size of pate. Only 1 piece of duck breast was served, not 2 pieces showing in most Yelp pictures. It's not even better than a lot of non-Michelin star restaurants. 

1 star for the hard-working servers. 1 star for the environment. Ordered tasting menu $225/person.

Came for dinner with my husband. For a 2-star Michelin restaurant, the prix fix menus are extremely high value ($135 for 3 courses). The whole experience was wonderful. The interior of the main dining room is gorgeous - would definitely recommend it over the lounge and the outdoor area if you're someone who appreciates aesthetics. Ordered everything that was recommended by the waiter and loved most of it. The fois gras and the sturgeon tart were delightful. The trout was delicious as well. The duck itself  was good but I didn't like the rye berries. Perhaps I was just too full, but I wasn't impressed with the desserts. They were beautiful for sure, but I didn't care for the flavors. Got the mandarin panna cotta and the apple tatin. All in all, a great experience and totally worth the splurge.

Just amazing experience!
Everything was great!

Wine & Champagne recommendations for the dinner was perfect!

Nice atmosphere and good food. Live up to the expectation of a 2 star Michelin. 
I really like foie gras. The wine pairing there was good too, had a good time w my partners.

My bf and I came here to celebrate my birthday. I have to say this is best dining experience I've ever had in the same caliber of restaurants. We ordered the 6 courses tasting menu. It's a combination of what's on the menu and surprises from the chef. I LOVE the Sturgeon tarte and my bf can't stop talking about the carbonara. Wine list is very comprehensive. We got a 2018 CHASSAGNE-MONTRAD Jean-Claude RAMON and it's so smooth coming with strong bodied.
Leaving this review delayed from a trip last year. Service was quite slow and flavors were nothing special. Given the price I'd have rather gone to almost any other fine dining restaurant

So we came here on a Friday night and unfortunately we will not be back. I'll start by saying that the atmosphere and service was great. We did the chef's tasting menu and added on the more expensive option for the wine pairing. The Som who poured our wine pairing was not very knowledgeable about any of the wines he poured for us. He even said the wrong years for what he was pouring several times, and the years were on the bottles! It just seemed unprofessional and questionable as to weather he was really a sommelier or not. Next, the food. It was very bland and lacked flavor. Keep in mind that we have been to 13 Michelin star rated restaurants in NYC so far, we mainly come to the city solely to try the top rated restaurants. With that being said, this is the only one we haven't liked or loved so far. I wouldn't recommend coming here. It is expensive which we knew since it is so highly rated but it is not worth the money! I honestly don't know how they got their Michelin star rating. With so many other restaurants definitely skip this one.

Legendary restaurant in New York! Michelin 2 star is underrated! And you will love it more when you visit in person, especially when you tour the kitchen (just politely ask the waiter)!

The dinner experience was way more memorable than most of the michelin restaurants that I went to. There was a smell of love, care, passion, hard work, and collaboration in the air!

To start with, I went there for birthday, and on my dinning table, there lied a handwritten birthday card signed by the chef Gabriel. I was touched, because I had birthday dinners at other restaurants and they were not this fancy.

The waiter was caring, he was able to fold the napkin every time when someone left the table, and constantly clean up the table. 

The portion is actually VERY GOOD. I was worried a bit because I ordered a 3-course for myself and a 4-course for my girlfriend, but they kept sending up complimentary bites between the courses, and the food quality was top-notch. And thanks to those bites, time passes fast, I was able to spend 3 hours in the restaurant while thinking it was only 2.

Ok! Food itself! Plating and presentation is almost perfect, what's not so perfect is the lighting - I could take better photos if the lighting over the food were better. Everything was amazing, but the duck was the most splendid. And all the desserts were outstanding, I remember a lot about chocolate flavor. And my girlfriend loved the birthday chocolate dessert the most.

I was go to put 9/10 for the restaurant, due to some dishes a bit too salty for me (if my perfect salty is 100%, GK is 110%). But then I was able to tour the kitchen and met the kitchen peeps. I enjoyed the vibe in the kitchen and the peeps were super friendly and happy while they were busy in the kitchen, they even stopped what they were doing to take photos with me. They told me the chef Gabriel left right before I went over to the kitchen, so I was not able to meet him. But I did see him in his staff, because they respected him a lot. It was an unbelievable experience, so I had to boost the score up to 9.5/10.

Now the question - what is 10/10 in my experience?

1. Better lighting on dining tables
2. Less salty on some of the dishes (there was a green liquid in shot glass that was too salty for me)
3. If I could meet the chef in person when in kitchen, that would be perfect. (luck).

To summarize, I recommend this restaurant strongly, it's another level for dining experience. You can get good food in the dining room, and you can get good story in the kitchen, what more can you ask for? 

I spent $400 that night for dinner, and I felt it was well worth it!

I walked in it was my first fine dining meal I got seated and then this lady wouldn't  stop trying to sell me on wine. They got me started with tons of food  that I all spat out. 5 years later my appetizer came and that also joined the pile of spat out food on the floor. After another 5 years my entree came it was steak but it was edible just not great. the dessert I ate in one bite. Over all the best thing I ate for dinner that night was a tiny pickle. I walked out hungry from the tiny portions and wasting a lot of money and time. And lastly  how does it have 2 Michelin stars?

Who am I to rate this restaurant? This is the kind of place where you visit to watch, to observe, to learn. This is the kind of place where you come to learn what is possible, to learn about human creativity. To learn about the limits, or limitlessness, of human creativity. If you ever wondered what the ancient Greeks meant when they described arete or excellence, this is the place to see it realized. 

As mentioned on a previous post, my framework for rating restaurants is:
Can I replicate It at home?
Can I cook make it better?
Does it trigger the brain? 
Does it make me happy?

The answers here are two categorical 'nos' for the first two questions and categorical 'yeses' for the final two. I cannot replicate at home or make it better, and it certainly triggers the brain and makes me happy (I use happy here for a sensation of elation when I eat--not sure if you feel it as well, but it is a very distinct feeling). 

Yes, this is a pricy place, but from the service to the experience to the attention to detail, you must try it at least once. 

Oh, and the deserts. I am not a desert person, but the deserts here are to die for!!

Going to Gabriel Kreuther was a gift for my birthday. We LOVED that it's not overly pretentious. The hosts are a bit judgy but the servers and everyone taking care of us were so wonderful. We had short conversations with each of them, they answered any questions we had and were all so super nice and accommodating. We got some mocktails and went for it with the 6 course tasting menu. As with all tasting menus I've had, by the end, I as begging for it to stop! I don't want to spoil it so you just have to go and experience it all. The reason for one less star is because they got busy and we sat for almost an hour waiting for dessert and our bill and for our bill to be taken. I was beyond full and just wanted to go. It was a bit excruciating. But the dinner experience was perfect.

The food here was very good, a bit out of the ordinary, but I enjoyed everything. This place not too long ago went from 1 star to 2 and I feel its actually somewhere between. The cuisine, setting and atmosphere is certainly a step above other 1 star locations but the service was not at the level of 2 stars I've been to like Atera. When I ordered a beer it tasted more like a cider. So I asked the server, is this cider? He said, its beer, and just stared at me with a stone cold face. His demeanor has no place in such a nice fine dining establishment. And when my date got cold she put a napkin across her upper body. Two workers asked her if she was cold but didn't bring anything for her. One of them even walked away laughing a little. Wasn't bad overall but not what I expect from a 2 star. Maybe michelin could invent a 1.5 star rating for this place.

Had lunch here back in September 2021. The prix fixe lunch was around $110 per person which is an absolute steal at a restaurant with TWO Michelin stars. 

Needless to say, expectations were pretty high as we ran across Bryant Park in the pouring rain to get inside. The decor in the main dining room was simple yet classy. Couldn't help noticing we were the only young couple in the place. There was a group of impeccably dressed businessmen who were obviously there for a business lunch, a middle-aged couple with kids who weren't exactly thrilled to be there, and a group of middle-aged women knocking back glasses of champagne after spending their entire morning on a shopping spree. Quite the cast of characters for a Thursday lunch...

Anyway, I can't describe the meal itself between I honestly forgot most of it. It's not what you think. The 3-course meal was amazing. The only reason I don't remember much is because my main dish was that damn good. Hands down, the best sea bass that I've ever had. After tasting that piece of seafood heaven, nothing else mattered. The rest of the day was a blur because I was on cloud nine.

Chef Kreuther is a living culinary legend. Without a doubt the best (and most expensive lol) lunch l have had in NY.

Outstanding in every way. On par or above many of the world's fine dining. Masterful combinations of flavors - interesting and exciting without being too far and odd Extremely generous prixe fixe with multiple amuse bouche that rank in taste and presentation as high as the courses. The bread presentation is captivating. Service was thoughtful and impeccable. You and your tastebuds are treated beyond well. Treat yourself and someone you love to this amazing restaurant.

Service was amazing, food and ambience were pretty good - overall a decent spot for a nice dinner (bit of a splurge), but not quite worth the hype for me.

I got the 4-course prix fixe with Foie Gras Terrine & Country Pâté, Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart, 2 Week Aged Hay-Smoked Duck Breast and ended with the Apple Tatin Frappe Brûlée. 

Amuse Bouche ------ 

Chocolate w/ Strawberry filling: very good, eaten at the end of the amuse bouche, thin layer of chocolate w/ a very liquidy strawberry filling which reminded me of popping boba

Beet Red Velvet Bread(?): Amazing. Highlight of the amuse bouche. Great juxtaposition of soft, denser texture from the bread along with the soft fluffiness of the sauce with a baked outside.

Fish Taco: Not my favourite. Was sashimi and very fishy. Typically I love sashimi so a bit put off. Very cute though.

Green Shot(?): Friend described it as "drinkable salad dressing" which I think is the perfect description. A bit too sour for my liking, but some people loved it.

Appetizers ------ 

Foie Gras: I almost always get foie gras and like to compare them across restaurants. This one was definitely middle of the road. Came with this clear gelee which was sweet, flavorful and definitely cool. Rye bread wasn't the best pairing IMO. I would have preferred maybe a sweeter bread, with some nuts or something for a texture juxtaposition.

Sturgeon Tart: Very flaky and great texture. Wasn't a huge fan of the sauerkraut, but if you're into that, I'm sure you'd love it! Host told us that this is one of the top dishes on the menu and doesn't get replaced even when the menu switches out.

Main ------

Duck: Highlight of the meal for sure which was surprising since I'm typically more into apps. Duck was so tender and flavorful. A bit fatty (more so than I would have liked, but still good). Crisp layer on the top along with the soft soft meat was amazing. Broccolini was charred to perfection! Rye berries were surrounded by some sort of veggie (cabbage) which was so hard to cut because of its fibers, so my rye berries were a bit of a mess.

Dessert ------

Apple Tatin: Like a decomposed apple pie with some refreshing pear sorbet. Used to apple pie with vanilla, so this was a very nice difference that made the dish even more reminiscent of spring in NYC.

Chocolate Nib Tart: This was amazing - should have gotten this. So many textures. Chocolate quality was great.

Chocolate (free): Had miso flavors and something else. I wasn't a huge fan.

Black Sesame Dessert (free): Strong black sesame flavor - so good. Very small bites and cute. Tasted exactly like the Chinese black sesame crisps(?) that are basically black sesame and sugar.

A great 2 star michelin restaurant.
The food is modern French, Alsacian.
Very creative and full of flavors.
We took the tasting menu and wine pairing.
A good wine pairing, not amazing.
Overall a great restaurant. The service was not on par though.
Price was almost 3 star nyc. However, a great experience

It was my first time dining at Gabriel Kruether, and everything from the amuse bouche, to the cocktails, the 2-week aged duck, AND the desert was just perfect. I've dined at other other 2, and even 3-Michelin star rated restaurants (i.e. Le Bernardin & Per Se), and this was definitely one of the favorites to eat at. The food was incredible and the service, just as amazing. A huge shout out to my server, Alan, who was incredibly friendly, patient, and super attentive. I was dining alone and him and his server assistants all stopped to talk to me, for a bit, and told me about how much they enjoy working there, and made me feel right at home. Thank you, guys! 

I'll definitely be returning whenever I get the chance. Definitely worth a visit for anyone who enjoys fine dining or is visiting NYC. This place is MAGIC!

Went here to celebrate my birthday with my girlfriend. It was both of our first experience with fine dining. Our waiter (whose name I did not catch) was great. Her and I both have some challenging allergies and he did his best to guide us in the direction that was both safe and delicious. Tried a bunch of dishes I had never had before including duck, foie gras, caviar, and sturgeon. Overall, a phenomenal experience.
Worth every (many) dollar! Wait staff impeccable, wine pairing perfect with amazing food (we did the chef surprise dinner pairing) - no complaints about anything. Eager to return...

My wife and I had the pleasure of eating at the Kitchen Table last night for my wife's birthday. To say this was the best restaurant experience is an understatement. The service, food, wine list, cocktails, and atmosphere are world class. Our favorite dishes included the duck, clay wrapped asparagus and the famous sturgeon & sauerkraut tart.  However, everything was truly wonderful. We met the entire kitchen, heard stories about how dishes were created and spent the entire night watching how a 2 Michelin Star restraint is run, wow! A night we will never forget! Thank you to the entire staff for making our night extra special!!

I can only give 2-star to this Michelin 2-star restaurant.

We had the signature tasting menu. I am mostly disappointed. The starters are very salty. Its hard to taste flavour other than salty, felt very bad about that. The only few courses that I could express my appreciation were white asparagus and duck breast. Dessert and petit four are reasonably good.

Moreover, I think the service was rude as a 2-star restaurant , especially with the manager, which came to ask for our thoughts without any response, not even a smile. If you dont care your costumer feeling, why bother to this hypocritical thing? I would be even happier if the manager didn't come to bother us. What a shame for a 2-star restaurant. But the other waitress were friendly.

Overall, this caused us $700 which was absolutely overpriced even for such a great location in Manhattan. I become skeptical toward Michelin choice.

I shall recommend people to think twice before they come. Its kind of one of the most regrettable dinning experience in my life.
Such service! The food was lovely, and my guest's birthday card was a lovely touch. The duck breast, foie gras, and truffle pasta were all wonderful! For once I have no words!  Just go!

An extremely questionable two-star rating. Gabriel Kreuther probably just didn't match my palette well, but I honestly feel cheated out of a meal. I don't think there was a single plate that I liked, and service wasn't great either. No one really came to check in on me except to clear my plates and bring me food, and out of the many Michelin star restaurants I've been to, Gabriel Kreuther offered the most distancing experience. 

Food was really average. I think they try to do a bit too much when it comes to each plate, and I felt really confused after each bite. 

Overall, I wish I had gone to another two-star in the city because this was not my cup of tea.

In summary: Gabriel Kreuther goes above and beyond!

We ordered the three course prix fixe menu. Compliments of the chef we received an amuse bouche, three special appetizers and bread service which were all excellent. The prix fixe menu was all amazing- presentation of the dishes was beautiful throughout, and each dish was made with care- my personal favorite was the duck breast. Each course had additional side dishes tailored to match the main dish. Finally, although we did not order dessert in our prix fixe selections, we also received a complimentary selection of sweets at the end which were very good. We left full and satisfied, very pleased with the quality of the food as well as the portions.

It was very nice to meet Gabriel Kreuther in person, as he came out to personally greet guests.

Service was very excellent throughout the meal. Each dish was explained well. The entire staff from servers to management were very friendly and attentive, and made sure that every aspect of our experience went smoothly. There was a slight miscommunication during a phone call between myself and the restaurant earlier in the night which was not a big deal at all - however as we were leaving the restaurant, they made sure to send us off with a surprise gift bag of sweets to make up for it.

A very memorable part of our visit to NYC!

One of the best places I've tried in the city. The staff is top notch, knew the menu well, waters were always full etc. The waiter even knew the name of the ceramic artist who designed the plates off hand. I ordered the trout and the cocoa nib tart for dessert. We also ordered both tarte flambées for thé table to start. Everything was flavorful and a decent portion - sometimes these types of restaurants skimp you on the amount of food they serve, but this wasn't the case. The right amount without feeling too full. I went for lunch but Would love to come back for dinner!

I did not think the dinner I had tonight was worth 2 Michelin stars, perfectly adequate, but not worthy of 2 Michelin stars. The Restaurant is comfortable, and the decor is up to a 2 star standard, but the service was well below a 2 Michelin star standard. I was surprised to only see one foie gras dish in an Alsatian restaurant, and it was not particularly memorable. The duck, and the lemongrass marshmallow were very good, but the overall experience was not up to a 2 star Michelin standard.

This was my first Michelin star restaurant experience and boy did I choose the correct restaurant to start with.

Gabriel Kreuther offers ambiance, service, food, and presentation deserving of the Michelin accolade. Our server immediately greeted us with professionalism and personality as we entered the beautiful interior. 

We reluctantly chose the 6-course mystery tasting menu, entrusting our meal to the chefs while also hoping it included some of Kreuther's signature dishes. We were not disappointed as we did get to try the foie gras and sturgeon tart, but were also served with other equally delicious courses that were not on the general menu.

Two Michelin star didn't disappoint! The Amuse bouche was three items which were good. Also scallion bread, fluffy with amazing dipping sauce. The pre fix three course $155. The first was Foie gras pate (I usually liked seared but this was good). The second was the duck which was perfect and tarty. The trout was out of this world! Complex and yet simple dish. The desserts were good but the tropical one was most unique in a good way.

Woah! What an experience. First and foremost
The staff is so pleasant and patient! Not snobby and overwhelmed like in some nyc restaurants but truly welcoming! Last night was really amazing; this place gets every detail right and really makes you feel like you're watching a food performance. It's a show, it's a restaurant experience you have to try. We did the chefs tasting and everything was delicious, absolutely spot on and me and my wife just had an awesome time. The duck was perfect, the caviar was out of this world and every little in-between snack was just perfectly thought through. Come here, that's it, just come.

I had the prix fix and found that it was ample food even on the verge of too much. The taste and presentation were excellent but for the price just not worh it. The wine was way way overpriced. You are subsidizing office space.

Tried this place Friday and it was so decadent ! Loved the foie gras, pasta, duck and chocolate desserts. Unique and interesting flavors and combinations, but still a wonderful take on French cuisine. First time ever left a Michelin restaurant full, worth every penny. Definitely a new favorite restaurant for celebrations and special occasions

I've been here several times and have really enjoyed the dining experience and the food each time.  I didn't take photos to document my most recent meal but came here with a small group after work on a weekday.  We sat inside the dining room and enjoyed the calm, cool and relaxing setting on a hot summer day.

Enjoyed the Amuse Bouche selection to start.

Had the three course menu.

Smoked Tomato Consommé en Gelée to start.  Presented covered with a little smoke.  Very tasty.

Artichoke & Four Cheese Raviolis as the mid-course.  Enjoyed this, nice delicate flavor and version of ravioli.

Miso Marinated Brandt Family Strip Steak as the main.  A bit different then most NY steakhouses would do but this was a tasty version of steak, very tender and excellent sauces paired with the steak.

Had a few bites of Cocoa Nib Tart and this was a nice finish.

Overall well done and reliable restaurant for high end modern French cuisine right in the heart of midtown. I also love that they play classic rock music. How cool is that?

We were very excited to try Gabriel Kreuther on our recent trip to NYC to visit our daughter. This restaurant did not disappoint! The food was outstanding and the service impeccable. If you are looking for an elegant venue to share a memorable meal, this place is ideal.

Truly the best experience I had at my very first Michelin restaurant. The palette cleansers between meals were incredible( I really enjoyed the gougères and the Alsatian bread with chive cream). My favorite course of the whole meal was the duck with cornbread. Mmm so sublime! Unfortunately I wasn't able to finish it but I promise the next time I come to NYC, I'll finish the duck! The dessert was sublime as well( I had the Mont Blanc). I applaud the staff for their hospitality and for leaving me a card to review them. I promise you five stars. Hope to see you soon!

The meal was a highlight of the trip The place is nice and comfortable The service was very attentive and efficient The food was an incredible complex and balanced journey well planned and executed The pairing was incredible in both its versions.

Hugely disappointed. 
We were seated in the bar area as we made a reservation late last week. A waiter came to take our drink order and brought us 2 drinks to be poured at our table. His hands shook nervously as he poured. We ordered our dinner with him and he left. 
Another waiter came over 5 minutes later and said "I noticed you have drinks, would you like to order dinner?" We informed her we had already done so. Weird and uncoordinated for a wait staff of this caliber. 
Later, before any food came, the same waitress came and grabbed my wife's glass away with a quarter of it left. Approximately $5 worth. 
We ordered a cheese course and a 3 course prix fix dinner. The cheese course came and was honestly very tasty. I asked the sommelier for a glass of red with dinner. He suggested a few and left the wine menu with me. The first course came, a tomato consumee that was literally tomatoes in jello with feta on top. Nobody asked me for a wine order so I waited. 
Our duck breast came and it basically tasted like pork belly. Very salty and overcooked. Halfway through the main course the sommelier came by and noticed I didn't have a drink and asked me what I had decided. At that point I was over it since dinner was nearly done. 
We asked the waiter if they could do a half caff latte with desert. He had no clue what this was. Turns out it was a thing that someone had invented and that they could mix a decaf espresso and regular together in 50% increments. He assured us it would arrive with desert. Halfway through desert someone asked us about coffee. We explained and asked them to cancel our newly invented half caff drink as we needed to leave for the broadway show. 
We felt forgotten and ignored in the bar area. It was a stuffy and pretentious place and definitely not worthy of 2 Michelin stars (not even 1 really)
The food was mediocre and the staff was very poor in their roles. 
Would not recommend for the $300 we spent. $50 would probably be too steep for the dreadful experience. 
GK should be embarrassed T their effort. 
Desert came and was very

I made a reservation on Resy for Friday night dinner to celebrate my bf's birthday. It's actually pretty easy to get a reservation online, and I don't need to set an alarm to grab a spot at midnight. The restaurant is conveniently located across from Bryant Park. The dining room is spacious with elegant interior design. I like the decor and ambience. The service was impeccable. The server gave a card to my bf that says happy birthday with his name and signed by Gabriel Kreuther. The menu we received at the end of the meal also says happy birthday. 

We ordered chef's tasting menu. My favorite appetizer was the Smoked Tomato Consommé en Gelée. It's creative and refreshing. I haven't had anything like that before. My favorite entrée was the Hay Smoked Two Week Aged Duck Breast. It's tender and tasty. My favorite dessert was the White Chocolate Shiso Leaf. It's delicious and creative. I've never seen anything similar before. I've heard that Gabriel Kreuther is well-known for the dessert. The last dessert was the handcrafted chocolates. We also got a birthday dessert on the house. 

We both enjoyed the food and service here. It was an unforgettable night for birthday celebration.
My first 2-star Michelin experience. We chose the 5 course chef experience meal and it was a great journey. Looking forward to dining here again on my next NYC trip

Hands down, this was the best dining experience I've ever had, and that is really saying something (with as much humility as possible )!!!

The service was above and beyond any other restaurant I've been to - most other Michelin-starred restaurant haven't even come close.

Christian, the host, was exceptional.  He was dapper and friendly, while also executing on his job perfectly.  I'll get back to him later...

The wait staff was organized and operated precisely how one should be - the coordination between all of the staff was flawless.  The attention to detail was top notch - from the refilling of water glasses to the removal of courses... even down to the keen eye of one waiter noticing that my date was left-handed by how she was eating, and providing her with specific left-handed silverware!  My date could not have been more impressed by this.

Regarding the food - just superb!  Due to a time constraint on our part, we opted for the 4 course option vs the longer chef tasting.  We were served an amuse-bouche, a palette cleanser, bread, and other items before our first course arrived.  There was a raspberry kombucha poured over ice like a snowcone, a turmeric-ginger gelee, a "dinosaur egg" where I can't remember the details of what was in it, a hush puppy, and a savory bread that had a scallion flavor baked into with a scallion butter.  Each dish was on the scale of very good to excellent.  The texture and flavor of the bread was exceptional - and rare from my experience, as many Michelin restaurants put more emphasis into the look and design of the bread than to the taste and texture.  Gabriel nailed both and it was appreciated.  Again - the details were never missed!

For the first courses, we each chose the foie gras.  It was excellent - different from other foie gras courses I've had, but they still nailed the flavors and combinations of sweet with fat.  I enjoyed the unique twists done, like the addition to have a spiced banana bread accompany the dish.

My second course was a crab and rice "soup."  I honestly forget the word they use for the sauce, but it was poured table-side, was green in color and had a nice spice level to it.  For her second course, my date chose the ravioli.  I did not get to taste the dish, but it was beautifully presented, and there was nothing left for me to try .

For my third course, I chose the duck (as one of the wait staff said it's a must have if you've never had it at Gabriel's restaurant before).  The sauce was drizzled table-side.  Each item in the dish was very good on its own, but the magic happened when you took a little of each and combined them together.  Just excellent, and it's no wonder why it was a recommended dish.  For her third course, my date had the trout.  It was first presented to her in something like a cassoulet.  They then removed the fish from said "cassoulet" and plated her dish, including the pouring of a sauce table-side (coordinated with my table-side pour).  Once again, I was not able to taste hers due to there being none left.  

For our fourth and final course, I had the cocoa option while she chose the peach option.  Hers was plated beautifully yet again.  She absolutely loved her dish, with so much going on there is no way I can recall it all.  My cocoa dish was just what a chocoholic like me loves - chocolate in many forms!  It was excellent - the miso ice cream was a nice combination as well.

We were then provided coffee, tea, and petit four.  All very good.

As we were hand-writing our review on the review card provided with the check, Christian came over to our table.  (I told you I'd get back to him later) He said he noticed us taking a lot of pictures and wanted to give us a private tour of the restaurant and kitchen, in addition to taking our picture with the chefs.  In my almost 40 years on this planet, I've never seen this happen.  It was simply exceptional.  It further proves the attention to detail aspect, as he (as a host) observed how we acted and took the time to make our night truly unforgettable.

So... yes... the food is amazing, as you'd expect at any Michelin restaurant.  But, the service and detail go so far beyond anything I've experienced.  This restaurant has 2 Michelin stars.  It certainly deserves the third.  And whomever is responsible for the staff and overall operation is simply the best in the business.  

Gabriel Kreuther is simply masterclass in dining perfection.  They deserve a different level of rating on here as 5 stars doesn't do them nearly enough justice.

I can't believe I hadn't been to this spot until tonight, one of the best dining experiences I've had in quite a while. The ambiance, with very high ceilings in the grave building is perfect. Nearly everyone in the restaurant was wearing a blazer, I was wearing a sweatshirt and my friend was wearing a polo shirt, but they still let us sit here. We both did the 3 course pre fixe which was phenomenal. I started with the fois gras, which came with banana bread. I then had the smoked duck breast. I loved everything I had, can't wait to come back.

I spent last weekend in NYC visiting a friend, and we decided to try to snag a reservation at Gabriel Kreuther, a restaurant that had been on my list for several *years.* We felt fortunate to get a reservation for Saturday night and were sure to note our dietary restrictions in reasonably nuanced detail (me=broad seafood allergy that I described in a lot of detail, and friend=gluten-free and dairy-free) in the reservation notes. She separately emailed the restaurant to further detail her own dietary restrictions. My allergy and her dietary restrictions were verbally confirmed when we checked in for our reservation and we reiterated them again to the server when she took our orders. All seemed good. 

First, I'll try to capture the courses I had:
1. Kombucha shot and a vegetarian sort of glassy/gel dish. 
2. Smoked tomato consommé en gelée: Had a deep smoky, barbecue like taste. I really didn't care for this dish, alas. 
3. Rice dish with callaloo. This wasn't verbally described as having crab in it but looking back at the menu, that could have been the issue (the maître d' later said via email that my version was vegan). 
4. Bread mini-course in the middle of the meal 
5. There was a sausage dish here, which also caused a reaction. 
6. Orecchiette with some brown sauce after they brought the squid ink pasta

Next, I will highlight a series of communication issues that happened. The server who took our order gave a confusing explanation of the courses. She explained that my friend would need to have the six-course menu, and that the three- and four-course menus were not an option for her dietary restrictions, which was strange. I had been eyeing dishes on the three-course menu, mostly because I was allergic to half of the mid-course dishes shown on the four-course menu, but the hostess said I would also need to get the six-course menu. This was vexing given that it was not communicated in advance, and the restaurant had not stated this in response to my friend's email. 

The largest issue surrounds my having been served items that caused a visceral reaction that resulted in needing to depart the restaurant prior to the dessert course to locate a pharmacy. I think it was during the fourth course that I was presented with squid ink pasta, and I immediately informed the runner that I would be unable to eat that course due to my seafood allergy. He seemed a bit surprised by this but took the dish back to the kitchen. Our server quickly returned to apologize that an allergy-inducing dish had been brought to the table. This prompted me and my friend to wonder if any of my previous three courses had also contained seafood products, unbeknownst to me. 

By this point, I had had a strong reaction to a previous course that resulted in...let's just say a very unpleasant experience. This was unexpected and unfortunately happened a second time, at which point I realized that something was seriously wrong. I was also starting to experience several other symptoms that I normally only encounter during mild to medium allergic reactions (fortunately my throat did not close, phew). My second visit to the restroom was also interrupted by the quite unexpected presence of a woman in the single stall in the downstairs men's restroom who seemed to be talking to herself, which prompted me to leave that restroom and head back upstairs to await the opening of the one there. 

My condition quickly worsened, and my friend flagged down the server to inform her of what had happened (I was minimizing talking at this point as I felt that further talking might result in feeling even worse). I appreciated that the maître d' came over to inquire about the situation, and we departed to find a nearby pharmacy. I'll say I do appreciate that Nico, the maître d', was quite attentive once he was made aware of the situation.

We made our way to a CVS in Times Square to get medicine, and I spent the rest of the evening feeling miserable, and we had to cancel our jazz club reservation for later in the evening as I was unable to leave my friend's apartment. My symptoms did not fully subside until about 24 hours later, but fortunately I was able to take the train back home to Boston the next day.

There were various service mishaps throughout the evening, such as there being 30-40 minutes between several courses (except the second and third course, which were about 3 minutes apart) but those pale in comparison to what was a case of cross-contamination at best and a direct allergic reaction at worst. Across the various dishes we had, some of which were identical and some of which were different between the two of us, we overall were not impressed from a flavor perspective. 

I was so pumped to go to GK and it sort of pains me to write this review, as I do not believe I will be returning. If you have food allergies, I would suggest staying away.

A fun, friendly exquisite dinner.  Met the chef!  Every course was delightful and delicious.  Probably the best duck I've ever eaten.  I have no complaints, only compliments.  Incredible service.  Just a great evening.

Worth its two Michelin stars! Creative reinterpretation of Alsace cooking, superb service, fantastic tasting menu, and a great wine list and bar. Plus, was easy to get into at the last minute. What's not to like?

Came in for a late dinner. We ordered from the pre-fixed menu. We had the tarte flambée which was phenomenal and another appetizer which I do not remember the name of, but it was just okay. I got the trout which I thought was adequate. However, I tried the duck breast that my companion has gotten and found it exceptional so we actually ended up switching, since she liked the trout. I also tried steak that my other colleague has gotten and it was incredible, which says something coming from someone who typically do not like steak. For desert, we had the chocolate desert and pineapple carpaccio. Chocolate was exquisite, the pineapple was alright. Portions are small as every other upscale restaurant, it's more about tasting and the experience. Wine was excellent. Incredible service. There was a couple of times that our plates were about to be cleared out before we finished eating, which felt like we were being rushed but otherwise, the service was great, our waiter was wonderful. Beautiful decor. Pricey, but that was to be expected. Very pleasant experience overall.
Phenomenal. As good as it gets. One of our best Michelin star dinners ever. I can't speak more highly of this place. Will certainly be back.
Very good presentation and all around great dining experience. Small plates but lots of flavor.

Must be to try this 2 Michelin star French restaurant! First of all, there are plenty of seats are easy to make a reservation, just make a reservation a day in advance! Secondly, the food is classic and delicious, also theres a lot of small bites, the whole tasting menu experience a complete French meal. Finally, good service, good environment and spacious seats!

A 2 Michelin stars restaurant, the food definitely met its standard, ambiance is perfect as well. Very happy to celebrate my brother's birthday dinner here, we all enjoyed the night very much! Thank you our friend, the sous chef of Gabriel Kreuther, Rodrigo, who took a very good care of us that night. Despite he was extremely busy that night, he still found time to greet us, and took us for a kitchen tour and met Gabriel Kreuther himself! Thank you for giving us an unforgettable memory!

Everything was amazing. Ate in the Lounge. Service was incredible, the food was also incredible. Did the 4 course tasting menu, but with the bread service, complimentary apps, and post dessert snacks, it was like 7 course. Just great.

One of the few Michelin starred restaurant that really justifies the honor. It has 2 Michelin stars and one that I would gladly return again for a meal. The food is thoughtful and complex in flavor. Creative and beautifully presented. They serve you complimentary small bites and "tongue cleanser" as well as sweets. The orchestrated flavors of your food and small treats is well managed. Service is very good and professional but I must comment that it lacks the warmth and genuine courtesy. I decided to still give five stars as the food, the presentation is exceptional! Highly recommended.

Food was 5 diamonds. 
Service was 5 diamonds. 
Ambiance was 5 stars. 
Crowd was 4 stars. 
Experience was priceless. 

Took my girlfriend here for her birthday, and it was beyond special. 

All other restaurants I now go to are now compared to Gabriel Kreuther, especially the service.

Had an awesome experience trying out the lounge on a last minute reservation. 

Mixing and tasting the Four Course Prix with the Bacon Tarte Flambee to start was a fun way to experience the menu! 

I highly recommend the lounge as you can order with a ton of flexibility and also not have to book way ahead! 
The staff was helpful, friendly and provided excellent advice on all the choices.

I had a delightful meal here for my birthday. Though they were due to close their outdoor patio for the season, the restaurant decided to keep it open one more week so I could celebrate there when I explained to the reservationist that it was my birthday lunch and I'm high risk for COVID and don't eat indoors. Above and beyond service, but sadly, dear reader, the beautiful outdoor setup is now gone, though it was perfect for my visit earlier this month.

For lunch, you can choose between two items per course on a prix fixe  tasting menu, or order a la carte. We chose to do the prix fixe and order different items so we could try everything and were not disappointed!

The royal kaluga caviar amuse bouche was a divine and decadent start to the meal, along with a savory pull-apart bread with chive butter.

Both the citrus-cured fluke and foie grad terrine were fantastic, though if I could only get one I would go with the latter.

Likewise, the red snapper and miso-glazed steak mains were expertly prepped, and the winner for this course was definitely the steak. Though again, both were excellent.

We really enjoyed the deconstructed chocolate tart, but my vote for best dessert goes to the golden kiwi givre. So unique!

The meal was capped off with Kreuther chocolates served as petit fours. Such a treat -- I had been missing their chocolate shop next door, which closed earlier in the pandemic.

Service was superlative. Our waiter was charming and friendly, not overly stuffy. A bag hook was immediately brought for my purse without asking, and they happily obliged when I asked them to charge my wheelchair while we dined. The only thing I found odd was, just like on my last birthday visit a few years ago, no one mentioned the occasion. I guess they're not big birthday people lol, still a 5* experience and I really appreciated the gesture of allowing me to dine outside which was more than enough of a gift. Hopefully, they add an outdoor dining setup back in when it gets warmer again as the open air structure was a beautiful oasis from 42nd street.

Wheelchair access details: no steps from the street, a fully accessible restroom is available in the basement level via vertical lift.

Gabriel Kreuther is one of the best restaurants I have had the pleasure to dine at in New York City. It is located right across the street from Bryant Park so it is somewhat easy to find. The chefs table was a fantastic dining experience where the chefs come to the table and you can watch the sophistication of the kitchen. The kitchen has a presence to it yet a peculiar silence that was very interesting to witness. Nonetheless, the kitchen table was an experience well worth the money! The staff was very friendly and attentive. So attentive that my water was never not full. The restaurant catered greatly to dietary needs and the restaurant made sure that the dietary needs of some of the party did not impact the experience. Likewise, we were able to add additional dishes to the menu at an additional charge without a problem. My favorite two dishes were the trout and the orecchiette! Also their fish and duck portions are very generous without losing the precious flavor profiles. The Apple Tart Tarin was a great dessert and was a very generous portion. Likewise, the bread they provide are tasty! The tasting menu left me very full, happy, and was an experience well worth the money. Although the staff could have done a better job explaining how to eat the dishes but other than that it was the best experience I've had at a restaurant so far! 8/5!!!!

The experience at Gabriel Kreuther, particularly the chef's table was an amazing experience and well worth it!

We came in a group of 4 and sat in the kitchen with a great view of all of the chefs working their magic, which is always so fun and really makes you appreciate each course. The hospitality was first class as they took care of any dietary restrictions or preferences in our group seamlessly and fluidly. 

We started with 3 amuse bouches and some delicious cocktails. It was then followed by courses of: foie gras, sturgeon and sauerkraut, trout, squid ink ragu, duck, white chocolate shiso leaf pallet cleanser and 2 desserts of pomegranate and pear bite with cotton candy and an apple tart tatin. I also appreciated that we got 3 types of breads throughout our meal, though it meant by the end I was very full! My absolute favorite dish was the trout - the shrimp sauce poured on top and the mashed potatoes underneath were all so delicious and silky smooth. It was my favorite fish course I've ever tasted. The water buffalo ragu was also so good. 

The desserts were also very tasty, though my favorite was not on the tasting menu - the chocolate flan. Wow that was amazing. Lastly we ended with 4 bites each which were quite big, I was surprised.

All in all, an amazing night and even more amazing meal. We had the best time and really delicious dishes while having an intimate experience in the kitchen.
Unbelievable service!!! The food was define!!! The fine's restaurant I've had the pleasure visiting.

We came here for our first date and returned for our third anniversary! Chef Gabriel was kind enough to come take a photo with us and sign his cookbook! 

I have loved each and every experience at GK and the food here is always wonderful. Also I highly recommend getting Gabriel Kreuther's cookbook which is a beautiful presentation piece and tells you the back story about his life.

This place was great. 5/5 stars for the food - Gabriel is a culinary and creative genius. 

Our experience started out a bit rocky - we were about 20 minutes early to our reservation. We grabbed a drink at the bar to kill time. The bartender was great - answered all our questions, and our drinks were amazing. We ordered the pear cider and the mocktail that started with an "e." 

We were seated almost 15 minutes after the start time of our reservation. Two parties who arrived after us were seated before us. We were given a round corner table, which was nice. When we went to order the chef's tasting menu, our server did not know what a "lacto ovo vegetarian" was - they assumed it was the same as being a vegan, so I explained what it meant. Normally I wouldnt mind this, but I'd assume at a place with two stars, they'd know. So I docked a star for this and the late seating. 

We did end up getting the chef's tasting menu - one for a tree nut allergy, and another for a lacto-ovo vegetarian- and it was absolutely incredible. 

Each course was more creative and delicious than the next - I can't remember everything we had, but I do remember liking the first bread course so much that we ordered another. This was a mistake because we then were too full to enjoy the final two courses of the meal. Wait until the end of the entire meal to repeat a course! 

The food included a traditional Alsatian bread with a fromage blanc/chive sauce, daikon ravioli, a mushroom pasta, artichokes in vegetable broth, a porcini gingerbread man, and lots of other creative dishes. Most of the food was "shut up and let me experience this because it's blowing my mind" good, and those that were not were still really really good. 

At the end they brought out a cake for my birthday in addition to the dessert courses. I also ordered the royal Tokaji which came out in a crystal spoon on a silver platter. 

The ambience was upscale romantic - the kind of place you'd propose at. The staff was patient and answered all of my questions. The food was incredible. I'll definitely be back here.

We came here for our 20th year annivesary. The place excelled on every aspect. I am hard-pressed to find a single way to improve upon the amazing room, attentive knowledgeable servers, well prepared and executed food. I am not a huge desert person so I was able to do 3 savory dishes instead. We both started off with their mixed cocktails. I had their special Manhattan and the wife had their herbaceous martini as we scoffed down the shareable mushroom flat bread. So lite, so good flatbread. The amuse bouche was a playful presentation of savory dishes disguised as desert pieces. The open course was the aged yellowtail and king fish crudo. I ate the pate of foie gras. We washed it down with a 1/2 bottle of rose Ruinart. Not a bad start indeed. The next was the soup of smoked eel, fennel and crab. Our main was the sea bass and the aged smoked duck breast. Both were exceptional mains. My wife has a slight aversion to any foam dishes so we switched the main. Honestly both were well executed and delicious. I did think the duck was out of this world and would gladly dive back into that again. We had these dishes with a bottle of Nuits Saint George Philippe Pacalet. It drank lovely for a young wine. The nose was phenomenal. The sommelier  (Lara) it was her recommendation. Their menu consists of 10,000 bottles and 2000 producers. I know my wines but it would take a day just to navigate it. You may spend a pretty penny here on food and booze but I can not think os a better way to spend it.

Wonderful experience, tried the chefs tasting menu with a group of four. The staff was very attentive to our pace with each course, we really appreciated the attention to detail. Its always nice too when the Chefs smile at you while working these wonderfully inspired, creative dishes. Thank you for making our dinner memorable!

I wanted to leave a negative review after one subpar experience and one very negative experience at this restaurant, however, after reading through the poor reviews that have already been shared here I feel like there isn't much subject matter left to cover, so I will just say; there is a reason why its easier to get a table at this "two Michelin star restaurant" than your local Applebees.

Celebrated my anniversary here and did the chef tasting. The presentation was fun and you get a TON of food, but there are way better tasting menus to be had in this town. The service was also a little disjointed.

Food was overall great, though not the kind of mindblowing I like to experience at a tasting menu. The duck was my favorite dish, but nothing else was super memorable. Also, why was the butter hard?!

I will say the vibe/ambiance in the dining room was great. I would consider returning to try the smaller prefixe menu, but wouldn't do the chef one again.

Perfect place to spend a special evening. Every time I have come here, the service is extremely professional and welcoming. You should definitely come hungry. There are options for 3-course, 4-course, and a chef's tasting, and all of these come with more than what you expect. There are small courses before, in between and afterwards that are nice surprises and make you very full. Don't be shy if you need to take your food home. We definitely had to ask to package some to go as we could not finish all our food.

I opted for four courses - foie gras, sturgeon and sauerkraut, duck breast and the golden kiwi. The foei gras and pate was very light. It came with homemade rye bread that made me feel warm and happy. The sturgeon and sauerkraut tart was a combination I have never had before, so I liked trying this new flavor profile. The duck breast was cooked very well, but I think I will try the fish next time. The golden kiwi was also a unique dessert. The kiwi is hollowed out and made into a sorbet with coconut tapicoa balls.

My husband got the yellowtail crudo, strip steak and the chocolate truffle. He especially like the milk ice cream in the dessert. Next time he also said he would like to try the fish. 

Definitely will return again for a special occasion. Lastly, Gabriel Kreuther, himself came to greet all the guests at the end of the night! He was so professional and kind. We also got a private tour of the kitchen as well. Amazing restaurant that goes above and beyond.

What a treat to dine at Gabriel Kreuther. From the moment we were greeted by the charming and welcoming host and entered the stylish, spacious, (yet cozy) room, we enjoyed every moment. And that was before the food!  We had the prix fixe lunch tasting menu and each course was absolutely delicious. Every plate had at least 5 different tastes, in addition to the principal dish. Spectacular. We oohed and aahed with every bite (and we don't often have that experience in a restaurant, of late).  The service was perfect--friendly, informative, professional, and, much appreciated. We look forward to returning soon. Thank you to the wonderful staff for a memorable meal.

Popped by today to pick up the most adorable and decadent Easter Candy. We chose these chocolate marshmallow treats and a box of chocolates. The detail on each is so beautiful. Everything from packing and presentation to taste is simply divine. Definitely try!

Incredible restaurant and design! !
The dinner was a amazing.
The services rendered was perfect .
The sommelier reference for pairing wine was excellent.
All dishes was state of the art.
The chef was surprising with additional flavors.
It was gorgeous evening.
Highly recommended

I had a very nice dinner here recently. The host was warm and friendly when I arrived--enough that I really remembered this. 

The drink list is cool and included some interesting spirits that I was not familiar with. This may be a chance to try something new. 

You will receive more than is listed for the tasting menu, as they bring out small bites as well as two different types of bread (at two different times, so not bad thing but a little wonky) between the courses. Even if individual dishes are not huge, you end up with a lot of food overall. 

A few of the in-between items were okay, not great, while the dessert and main course were delicious and beautifully presented. The excellent service and overall nice experience upped things a notch, though.

This is such a wonderful place to go for a special occasion! My boyfriend took me here for my birthday. The restaurant went above and beyond to make sure it was incredibly special. Chef Gabriel had signed a "Happy Birthday" note for me, and that was just the start.

We went with the three course menu (other options are four course and chefs tasting menu). We then got the Bacon Flambé to share.

To Share

Bacon Flambé: 7/10

I was extremely disappointed in this dish. First of all I don't know why they are using the term "flambé" when this is a flatbread. It is a white cheese flatbread with bacon. Definitely not what I expected. It was still tasty though. The flambé and bacon tasted super smokey. It was very strong and a unique experience to be smelling something so strong and Smokey but the mouthfeel was so delicate.

First/Mid Course

Scallops: 8.5/10

The scallops were delicious! The truffle didn't come through that much, but I loved the mouthfeel of the foam and the thin slices of scallop. I expected the scallops to be bigger but they were thin and delicate.

Ravioli: 9/10

You only get two ravioli but man are they delicious. They are perfectly cooked and the sauce is incredible. I highly recommend this dish!

Second/Entree Course

Duck: 10/10

The duck was incredible. The lives of meat were nice and thick and juicy. The skin was perfectly crispy and there was a nice thin layer of fat to make it very tender and create the perfect bite. If you don't order this you're missing out.

Steak: 10/10

If you don't like duck, get the steak. The steak was incredibly soft and tender. It was perfectly cooked too. The side of potatoes was also delicious.

I honestly don't know how to further describe these dishes because there are no words. I loved every bite!

Dessert

I have a nut allergy, which limited us.

Kiwi dessert with coconut tapioca: 9/10

The kiwi sorbet was AMAZING! I had never tasted anything so smooth. It wasn't freezer burnt and the kiwi flavor was not artificial at all. The presentation was very cool too. The tapioca came in a kiwi and they put the sorbet on top. The dessert also came with a caramelized cake stick that tasted like banana bread.

Our meal also came with free wine - to celebrate - and some hor dourves, which were presented nicely. We got some homemade specialty chocolate and jelly cubes. We also had the scallion bread with chive cheese dip. Absolutely incredible we embarrassingly ordered seconds.

Overall the experience was incredible and the food was very good. I loved all the little surprises and supplements that made the meal even more special and over the top. The staff was so friendly and it was a birthday well spent!

Another great fine dining experience. The only down thing I can say is that the chef was not there during our visit. We did, however, get a tour of the kitchen and have an extraordinary meal paired with great wine chosen by their sommelier. The meal was definitely Michelin quality.

Came by here for lunch recently. The service at this spot does not disappoint, everyone was so attentive. It's no wonder they have 2 michelin stars, the food and service were both incredible.

We ordered a couple dishes from the a la cart menu and requested to split everything into two. The dining experience was just WOW - even though we ordered a la cart, each dish was individually plated for the two of us and presented in an order from light (salads) to finish with protein (fish). I was very impressed.

We started our meal with a few amuse bouche compliment of the kitchen. We got shots of passionfruit kombucha with ice crystals which were delicious and margarita jelly cubes. So fun!

Then the meal proceeded with our bread service. This bread was super soft and golden, it truly glowed. Our meal then continued with salad and foie gras, and finished with the fish. For each course, the staff came to explain to us what we were eating so even though we chose an a la cart experience, the entire culinary journey still felt as if we had a tasting menu. Very well done! 

I will certainly be back and will have to try the tasting menu next time!
