This is easily the best restaurant I have ever been to. These are not just words, it's justifiable proof across the board that excellence exists and is strived for, which is exactly what this restaurant does. 

As you walk in, absolutely stunning decor and sophistication become crystal clear. With over 30 servers, assistants and everyone else who is trying to make you happy it's virtually impossible not to emerge a celebratory mood. The 30 I mentioned are only people facing, there's an exactly the same amount of professionals cooking your meal in the kitchen. Yes, it's 60 employees building your food experience to perfection. 

Oh yes, the food. It shouldn't be called that. It's really artwork for your pallet because once you realize the effort, the mixtures of tastes and their unrivaled originality, you are experiencing Michelangelo on your plate. I would say to not consider it a restaurant as much as it is an experience, one that you will never forget.

Spent our 49th anniversary dinner here and it was certainly memorable.  Three hours of being spoiled.  All personnel were so friendly, professional and willing to inform.  The sommelier recommended a new to us rose champagne and it was perfect for each of our courses.  We chose four courses and added another starter...which was really too much in the end with all the amuse bouches, the extra anniversary cake and a few extra desserts!  Three different breads were also served through the meal...worth every calorie. Only misstep was the server never asked us before she opened a second bottle of water at the end of our meal just to top off our glasses.  We had already met our limit.  Every course delivered maximum taste experiences.  The only thing that was sent back was an amuse bouche that was supposed to end the savory courses....ramped up chicken soup.  At the end of the meal we were ready for sweet....and we were not disappointed.  Five or six...I lost count!  Had to take home the house made chocolates as we couldn't eat another two bites.  It will be a nice reminder when we have them with some rose champagne and reminisce.
The Copeland's ate there for David's retirement party. Lilly called it "the best meal of my life"

Stopped in for the lunch menu - at $115 for the prix fixe, it's a solid deal that includes amuse bouche, bread service, 3 courses including dessert, and petit fours to wrap up.

Beautiful, open space, it wasn't full but I couldn't hear any of the other tables.  Service was sharp, pacing was good, food overall good but nothing blew me away. My favorite dish was the hay smoked duck - cooked perfectly, with an insane layer of skin, but could've used a touch of salt to bring everything together, and I didn't love the purees served with it. Additionally it felt like the broccoli rabe was just put on the plate but didn't integrate into the dish well as a whole.

Shockingly disappointing! I've had better service at Chipotle compared to this place. Gabriel Kreuther, I hope you will look into what's going on in the front of house because this was definitely not an acceptable Michelin Star experience. 

We had reservations for 8PM on a Saturday night. It took at least 10 minutes for someone to even bring menus or acknowledge us after we had been seated at the table. I had no idea that the person who brought us the menus was our waiter because he didn't introduce himself or give us any background on the menu or restaurant but just handed us the menus and walked away. At the 25 minute mark after being seated, we still had not even placed any orders at this point, so we had to flag someone down ourselves. The waiter (Stewart/Stuart?) finally returned, and when my friend remarked that we didn't know he was serving us because he didn't introduce himself or say anything about the menu he gave some attitude but finally took our orders. 

First impressions are lasting and important, and this meal was already off to a bad start. We still ordered the 6 course chef's tasting menu, which is the most expensive item, so you would think that they would provide better service than what was initially offered. Alas, the service from our waiter continued to be lacking and while a few others that came by to bring courses or drinks were nice and friendly, our experience was tainted. 

The pacing between the courses was horribly off. Sometimes there would be less than 2 minutes in between, and other times we waited over 20 minutes for the next course. We were there for 3.5 hours in total for that 6 course meal, which is absolutely insane. We had to flag someone down for the check because again our waiter was nowhere to be found, and we didn't want to be stuck there for 4 hours. The table next to us asked for one of their courses to go because the service/food was that slow. 

Food: Whoever made the bread, small bites, and palate cleansers was the real MVP of the kitchen tonight. I was overall thoroughly disappointed by the food though and absolutely not worth the wait or money that we spent. Luckily they left the bottle of water at our table because we had to keep refilling the water ourselves since the waitstaff barely came around. We did let the waiter know that some of the dishes were really quite off, but he didn't offer any sort of apology or even have the manager come speak with us. 

Bread: 
- Chive bread (Kougelhopf): Warm, delicious, and soft pillowy texture

Small bites: 
- Ginger and pineapple kombucha with coconut snow: delicious and refreshing 
- Juniper hush puppy with Meyer lemon meringue: excellent small bite 
-Shiso mojito with white chocolate and mint powder: interesting combo 
- Mezcal paloma pate de fruit: excellent palate cleanser 
- Local ramp and potato panisse with herb aioli: despite its small size the potato flavor is incredibly well highlighted 

Starters: 
- Aged yellowtail kingfish crudo: delicious and light 

- Hawaiian red crab & Kumamoto oyster and bison tartare: excellent course in both presentation and flavor 

Courses: 

- Foie Gras Terrine & Country Pate: scrumptious and beautiful 

- Sturgeon & sauerkraut tart: love the textures with the flaky pastry in combination with the sturgeon 

- French white asparagus cooked in kombu and clay: the presentation made this dish seem so fancy since the wait staff broke open the clay to reveal the white asparagus. It was essentially just a fancy version of asparagus and hollandaise style sauce. They also gave us a creme brûlée with white asparagus, which was underwhelming and had a strange texture (almost like a quiche). 

- Baked bucks county polenta: so incredibly salty!! Their sauce was overly reduced. I don't know if they didn't taste this before serving, but I had to chug the rest of my water afterwards. 

- Hay smoked duck breast with sweet potato and apple mustard brown butter: We each only got 1 piece of duck even though pictures on Yelp show that the dish should come with 2. I really wanted to like this because duck is one of my favorite proteins, but it was underwhelming. The meat was slightly tougher than I would expect it to be. 

Palate Cleansers: 
- Roasted Farro and Chicken Consomme: interesting presentation since they used a traditional Japanese style tea set to pour this, but it was a warm flavorful chicken broth 

- Carrot sorbet with buckwheat sable and orange cream espuma: inventive and delicious. Loved the presentation for this one. 

Desserts: 
- Fraise des Bois Frappe Brûlée: Presentation on this one really needs work. Flavors were nothing special. 

- Petite fours: the banana foster one was actually disgusting. I was pretty shocked at how bad it was. The other ones were not as offensive thankfully.

Overall: Incredibly overpriced and overrated. Undeserving of their Michelin star status.

Modernly crafted French cuisine served over 8-9 courses. Good service and an extensively elaborate journey of trying different textures and flavors. We were seated outside, which had a nice ambiance as it overlooked Bryant Park but was sheltered from the crowd on the sidewalk. Overall, it was a fun experience which could be further improved by shortening the serving time (~3-4 hours) and introducing some more creativity and flavor into the vegetarian options as those didn't seem to be too thought out. A bit too much use of foam and jelly textures that we could be swapped with focusing more on flavor. 
Overall, it was a fun experience if you wanted to spend a few hours wining and dining by Bryant Park!

Julien, the maitre de is fantastic along with very caring, attentive, to every detail of staff service. Food is outstanding, creative, and perfect preparation and presentation. The tasting menu was fabulous and on par with the great peers in USA and Paris ( as matter of fact, exceeds most in Paris and certainly London).
Definitely will return and recommend most highly to all.
The service was incredible. Such kind, talented bartenders. It enriched my life to chat with them. Great cosmopolitan. Lovely wines.

This was an amazing fine dining experience that we had in the city right across Bryant Park. They are well deserving of their two Michelin stars.

We were greeted by fantastic hosts and hostesses, who made us truly feel welcome. The servers were very attentive, came very frequently, kept the table looking fresh in between each course. All of the staff members we encountered were so nice and accommodating. I can't say enough about how each of the staff went above and beyond for us.

We went with the four course option and we were very happy with our choice. They were able to adjust the dishes to our dietary restriction's without issues. The courses that you picked are a first course, midcourse, entree, and dessert. However, in between each of these courses, we received complementary drinks and finger food to cleanse the palate in between each dish. Here were our selections: 
1. Foie Gras & Pate - Diver Scallop - Smoked Duck Breast - Citrus Mousse
2. Asparagus & Snap Pea Salad - 4 Cheese Ravioli and Morel Mushrooms - Roasted Golden Bass - Buttermilk Panna Cotta

For the entrée, I would highly recommend the duck breast which was very rich tasting, smoked to perfection, and had such a unique savory taste, and was nicely complemented by the sweet topping. Also really liked the Seabass which had a more mellow flavor, and all of the components of the dish complemented each other very well. 

Food was amazing, and each dish had several layers of flavor and texture, nothing like I have had in the past. This was truly a top of the line culinary experience. We left the restaurant very full and satisfied. 

I did a good amount of research before choosing this restaurant, and compared it to several other two star Michelin restaurants. My experience here was nothing but positive, and I would highly recommend this place.
Great food, service and ambiance! And quite an expensive champagne list if you are celebrating! We look forward to being back!

2 Michelin stars for a reason! 

Made reservations online and was greeted and seated promptly for an early dinner reservation on a Friday night before our Broadway show. Service was amazing throughout and we really enjoyed the Chef Tasting menu! It took the two of us about 2 hours to get through everything and we were so full!

When you check in, they will ask if you need to leave at a certain time prior to a show so they make sure to accommodate your needs. There was also a vegetarian option of the Chef Tasting Menu as we overheard the table next to us order that and they seemed to enjoy it.

We opted for the Chef Tasting Menu because we wanted to be surprised and delighted with the items that came to us, and we were told it had more of the tableside flair/performance of pulling the dish together, which we really enjoy.

Every bit deserving of the 2 Michelin stars.

I wasn't a big fan of fine French food but Gabriel Kreuther changed my mind. Took my girlfriend here for a birthday dinner. From the moment we walked in, the ambience and grandeur swept us away, eagerly teasing the culinary experience that followed. We were seated in the main dining room but with a view of the kitchen, which piqued our curiosity even more. 

Our server was polished, polite and delivered exactly the kind of service you would expect from such a fine establishment. He was extremely knowledgeable about the dishes and made useful suggestions. We ordered a bottle of D'Henri "Fourchaume" Chablis, the minerality of which perfectly complemented the delicate cuisine that followed. It was served ice cold. We opted for the 4 course tasting menu, which had a savory start.

Bread: Someone who looked like GK's son served us this Alsatian-influenced soft delight with a really special goat cheese spread in lieu of butter. It rivaled Crown Shy's bread, my girlfriend liked it even better.

Amouse bouche: Some very interesting textures and flavors. I really enjoyed the ramp-wrapped potato and fried mushroom "croquette", which was served on a bed of hot stones. 

First Course: I opted for the white asparagus and snap pea salad. Fresh leaves, along with the crispy prosciutto di parma, made for a salad of wonderful texture, glazed with subtly sweet vinaigrette. My girlfriend ordered the yellowtail kingfish crudo, which she really enjoyed.

Mid Course:  The ravioli serviette was probably my favorite dish. The saffron-infused emulsion on top of soft ravioli with squash and crispy pancetta was a perfect combination. My girlfriend opted for the scallops but wasn't enthused. 

Entree: The steak was delicious, soft, red inside and just short of melting in your mouth. The garlic-soy glaze felt somewhat Japanese inspired but was great nonetheless. It wasn't the best steak I've eaten and I wish I tried the duck instead, but they upsold me well on the $45 supplement... My girlfriend ordered the spice roasted golden bass, which competed with the ravioli for my favorite. 

Dessert: We shared the chocolate truffle and coffee/hazelnut craquelin. Nothing to write home about but satisfactory for the sweet tooth after a great meal. 

I would highly recommend GK to celebrate a special occasion. Not easy on the wallet but still great value for a tasting menu of this quality.

I am one year late in posting this review so I can barely remember the details of what I ate. BUT what I do remember is that this place was simply DIVINE!!! The food, the experience, the service was amazing. I would absolutely come back despite the price. Horrible review but you're going to have to just take my word for it...

Outstanding Food and Service Experience!  Everything was well seasoned, prepared and cooked!  Duck and Wagyu skirt steak were amazing!  Will be back!

We did the pre-fixe-4.  Highly recommended.

Did the Chefs tasting menu. Unfortunately, there was a piece of something that looked like a Brillo pad in the 1st course. They were apologetic but rather than asking how they can make it right, they just said they were adding an extra "truffle" dish, which honestly I did not want. We already had  bc 7 courses as part of the menu. Something must've been going on bc the service was SLOW in between courses. We were there for almost 4hours while our server was well aware we had to leave by a certain time. Any other restaurant I could tolerate it, but a 2 Michelin star and almost $2,000 bill, I expected better service and better service recovery. Im very disappointed. 

The food quality and cocktails were overall good. The people were friendly and professional and the space was nice. 

But the service, 4hour dinner and lack of service recovery was extremely disappointing. Unfortunately would not return.

Sad to leave only three stars as I was really looking forward to try Gabriel Kreuther. I still believe they probably just had a bad night, but a restaurant of this caliber in such a competitive dining environment city can't run into some of the things that happened when we came by. 

My first remarks are the positive ones - the team was impeccable in the pre-dining experience, as we needed to have our child with us and they were great at accommodating such and opening an exception. The food also has, as I expected, great quality and beautiful plating, as I'll describe below. The service was mostly a disaster, and that's what leads to this classification - when we were asked in the middle of the meal if we were enjoying it and expressed our disappointment the team made an effort to improve, including serving an extra dish, and I highly value that, but overall the quality of the service was not even near a one Michelin star restaurant, much less a two stars. The meal lasted forever, not in a El Buli or Trois Gros lasted forever good, but in a "lasted forever because of near 45 minute delays in between one of the dishes and total lack of coordination between kitchen and serving team".

The first fail was at the start - we were there for my wife's birthday - which had been discussed and had a card for Happy Anniversary waiting on our table. The meal then started and, as I alluded above, globally I enjoyed the cuisine - the tasting menu started with multiple small bites - savory kougelhopf, shiso mojito, ginger & pineapple kombucha, meyer lemon meringue, mezcal paloma pate de fruit, and a ramp & potato panisse. The first main dish was an aged yellowtail kingfish crudo that was very good. This was followed by crispy squash blossom and a marinated snap pea taco that was creative. Next in the list was a foie gras terrine, not my favorite way of eating foie gras, but it was equally very good, and this was followed by a sturgeon and sauerkraut tart. After nearly 45 minutes of back and forth of where was our food, came a french white asparagus that is cooked in kombu & clay that is broken table side (unless you were hungry for waiting so long for the next dish and felt like hammering the clay yourself), with a caviar aioli. It was paired with a savory walnut creme brûlée. This was followed by the extra dish for our waits - diver sea scallops that were fresh and well cooked, though somewhat bland in presentation. After this came a delicious duck breast. Desserts started with a cherry and vanilla sorbet, a birthday financier to sing happy birthday, a frappé brûlée, a smoothie pate de fruits and a selection of chocolates. You end the meal getting a copy of your chef's tasting menu and to add to the mishaps of the night there are at list two dishes listed - including the black winter truffles - that were not actually served (not that there was lack of food, but still...).

A final word for the wine pairing that was served from start to end as if you were ordering a lager at Buffalo Wild Wings, basically not with much more information than reading the label of the bottle. When a wine pairing costs as much per person as the tasting menu I expect that to be part of the experience and to enrich the experience itself, not to be a cold and emotionless bit of my meal, as with that value I could buy 3 or 4 bottles of much better wine myself.

Really hoping it was just a really really off night, as errors happen to anyone in any line of work, but for a restaurant of this caliber I was (we were) really disappointed.

Very overpriced, service is "too much" Food is interesting, but not tasty.
Pretends to be classy, but its not. 
Do not recommend.

Side note: This review pains me. This was my favorite restaurant for years and it just isn't anymore. 

I went back here on 8/21 for the Chef's Tasting Men; very specifically the one done in the kitchen. I've been here a ton of times and normally I leave stuffed with amazing food. As per always, the service was immaculate and the best in any restaurant I've ever been to. I like the ambiance here also with the kitchen in back being rather quiet outside of hearing "yes chef" and the call of orders. However for spending $295 a person plus tax and tip (so 380 or so,) we left hungrier than I have left before during their 3 course, 4 course meal, or even their bar offerings. The portion sizes have shrunk down to maybe 40-60% of what they were before and honestly it wasn't really worth it. I'd go back for their three or four course meal or especially their lunch. To drink, I had an Amer Bière as per usual; a cocktail made from beer and some amaro. Two others had wine and they liked it a lot. As we had a whole lot of food, my descriptions aren't in full.

Savory Kougelhopf- Chive fromage blanc. Always delicious and still a favorite bread.

Amuse Bouche:
Chilled Summer Melon- Lemon verbena sea salt
Yellow Tomato Gazpacho- Basil oil
Mushroom S'more- Cocoa hush puppy, porcini meringue
White Sangria Pâte De Fruits- Spice soaked raisin
Local Ramp & Potato Panisse- Fines herbes aioli

Of the amuse, my favorite were the Mushroom S'more (very good umami) and the White Sangria Pâte De Fruits which had a good kick from the alcohol but still balanced. Gazpacho was also very tasty, the Panisse was alright (a bit oily,) and the Melon was just OK (lacked said spice.)

Courses:

1. Aged Yellowtail Kingfish Crudo- Marinated zucchini, avocado, cucumber vinaigrette 

One of the better dishes of the night. The kingfish was buttery and delicious and it came with a tiny croquette (I believe kingfish also) which was also very tasty albeit one bite.

2. Foie Gras Terrine & County Pâté- Pickled jackfruit, riesling gelée, house-made emmer loaf

Always good though this definitely a lot smaller than before. Flavors are always solid and this loaf was okay. I heavily preferred the banana bread aux épices they used to be served with this.

3. Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart- Applewood smoke, sabayon, imperial ossetra caviar 

This was basically the same portion as before. Not my favorite but the chef somehow made sauerkraut fancy and I commend them for this.

4. East Coast Shellfish- Scallops cooked in banana leaf, black truffle-miso sauce, herb grilled mussels, focaccia 

Best dish of the night along with the duck. Scallops were amazing with a lot of buttery and sweet flavor. That sauce could have done anything and it had an umami hit. There was also some type of vegetable with the scallops (I believe turnip) which was cooked down and tasty.

5. Local Water Buffalo "Fundido-" Fermented red cabbage, beat hot sauce, beet crêpe "tortillas" 

I'd more call this an unfundido. I didn't get this and I hated this. We shared this plate and made one taco each. The cheese overpowered the buffalo and it didn't really taste special. The red cabbage just tasted normal and the hot sauce wasn't hot. This was by far the worst dish I've ever had at this restaurant and the fact that this was one of the main dishes was a joke.

6. Hay Smoked-Two Week Aged Duck Breast- Cherry-miso jam, toasted pistachios, scallion-cheddar cornbread 

Always delicious though I would say the skin wasn't as crispy this time and the duck was one piece and not two now. The jam was very well spiced and went well. The bread was delicious though crispier than most cornbread. Half the portion but still delicious but why?

Palate Cleanser:

Kombucha- Ginger beer, earl grey, chamomile. 

Very lightly fermented for a kombucha. Alright. I preferred their prior sorbets or other things.

Pre-Dessert:

Cherry- Créme madame, cherry & vanilla sorbet 

Very tasty albeit tiny. Strong cherry flavors. 

Dessert:

Frappé Brulée- Herry's Berries strawberries, tarragon sorbet, sablé breton 

Honestly delicious. One of the better desserts I've had from them. Fresh strawberries and not too sweet with very appealing textures. Would add this to the main dessert menu if it's already there.

Petit Fours/Mignardises/Chocolates from GK:

Smoothie Pâte De Fruits- Passion fruit, banana. Tiny but good flavors with a good chew.

Raspberry cheesecake macarons: Delicious as always. One of my favorite macarons

Apple caramel bonbon: Very good. Not my favorite (that goes to the caramelized banana/coconut) but very tasty 

The two milk chocolates, I believe one was yuzu and the other was caramel were also good. 

We ended the meal full but not super full and compared to prior experiences, that's quite different. I used to call this one of the best deals for any Michelin Star restaurant but I wouldn't call that anymore. The food here is still amazing outside of that one dish but it just wasn't as worth it anymore.

My wife and I dined here for the first time to celebrate our 15th wedding anniversary and were not disappointed -- the duck (her favorite dish) was extraordinarily good, as was the black bass (my selection). Desserts were all you could expect from a chef known for his chocolate specialties. The restaurant very kindly and subtly acknowledged our anniversary, which was an added treat.

Service: Attentive but thoughtful and reserved. Ambiance: One of the most quietly elegant settings in town in the main dining room. We will perhaps be back for our 16th anniversary -- and maybe even before then.

The positives:

The food was great, there's plenty of options at all prices and we liked that. It is still an expensive restaurant for a special occasion. 
The drinks were also great
The place is nice, good ambiance.

The bad:
Service was not great. We had to constantly chase somebody to get a drink with my food or ask a question. The waiter was nice and maybe he was having an off day, but the dinner is not cheap and it was a struggle. The waiter rarely checked on how we were doing or if we needed something else, such a shame, there's definitely potential.

Gabriel Kreuther is the epitome of fine dining! We came here for a celebratory graduation dinner for my husband, and everyone loved the experience. From the chic and stylish decor to the top notch service to the mouth watering food, we were impressed. 
Our waiter was charismatic and sold us on the wine pairing for the whole table. Let's just say that made the whole dinner even more fun! It was a lot of wine and we were more than tipsy by the end of the evening. But the pairings were exquisite!
Our waiter also convinced us to try the caviar, and I can honestly say that was one of the highlights of the meal! We opted to split one caviar can among 7 people (I think it was $300, so we didn't want to get two). It was still enough for everyone to have a good taste. 
Of the courses, I will mention a few favorites: We loved the Mezcal Paloma pate de fruit. These small morsels literally exploded with flavor. The Crispy Squash Blossom was light, and the texture was perfect for a light tempura. The Greenwalk Hatchery Trout Cooked on Cedar Wood was delectable; we loved the presentation with the champagne sauce. The Hay Smoked Two Week Aged Duck Breast was tender and juicy. 
Of the deserts, I loved the handcrafted chocolates the best. There was a spread of pieces to sample from. 
The service was impeccable. Our sommelier was the best! The waiters paid attention to every single detail. The plates, dishes, carafes, and glasses were stunning. We felt like royalty for a night. 
This restaurant definitely earns its two Michelin stars. It was a night to remember!

We had a pleasant Monday evening. 
It was 70% filled on a Monday night which isn't bad.
Service was attentive.

*Complimentary bread was YUMMM.
*Amuse Bouche was okay, not very memorable.

First Course 
*Foie Gras Terrine & Country Pâté - very good, love the layering. Simple and delicious.
*Citrus Marinated Langoustine Tartare - a bit too shrimp flavor driven, I think they cook the langustine head into the sauce. Texture was good though.

Mid Course
*Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart - tart was very delicate and flaky. Smoked sturgeon was good. Maybe too much sauerkraut.
*Baked East Coast Diver Scallop - fav dish, cooked very well and love the miso truffle sauce.

Entree
*Ora King Salmon Cooked on Cedar Wood - cooked very well. The veggie at the bottom seemed pickled. The acidity works nicely with the fatty salmon.
*Hay Smoked-Two Week Aged Duck Breast - cooked very well, love the different types of sauce presented. A very fall feeling dish.

Dessert
*Fig Carpaccio - okay
*Coffee & Hazelnut Craquelin - our favorite. Perfecto combination of ice cream, mousse, and Craquelin. YUMMM.
*Stone Fruit & Caramel Parfait - it was okay.
Should have got Chocolate Truffle instead...!!

Petit Four was very cute, well presented and delicious!

Not sure about 2 Star but overall we had a great night!

Absolutely mind blowing!!!
We've actually expected it to be almost twice as expensive than it turned out to be. Preferring to select specific dishes we set at the Lounge area where we didn't have to stick with the 3 or 4 course options.
We love to travel and love food, everything we ordered was amazing! Do pay attention to the chef's purpose to bring traditional taste with a twist and something unexpected. We couldn't put our finger on a spice for example that made a familiar appetizer a little more unique, delicious but just a tiny bit unusual.
We were happy with the wine selection too, matching her dish with a white wine and mine with red one of our choice easily. I actually tend to avoid wine I always feel is overpriced though after tasting a couple options I went with one of those choices. Whether the quality of the wine, the enchanting ambiance or our overall great experience was behind that I don't know but again it was worth every penny!
Our service staff were all great especially our waiter who helped us select everything and answered our questions, ended up surprising us with some additional deserts, and was overall attentive throughout without being even slightly annoying.
Definitely recommend the place and the experience!!!

After having the prix fixe menu at lunch the last time that I was in NYC, I knew that I needed to come back and try out their 12 course tasting menu.
All of the dishes were very unique, the table side plating of the white asparagus cooked in kombu was so cool, and I especially could not get enough of the white asparagus miso crème brûlée on the side. I've never had anything like that before. 
One of my other favorite dishes of the night was the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart, it had such perfectly balanced flavors, I haven't had sauerkraut in a fine dining setting and I was surprised how well it worked in the dish. 
Another delicious course of the night was the "Baked Bucks County Polenta", it was so comforting yet refined, and I loved how they gave you a bowl of breadcrumbs on the side to top the polenta with! 
Every dessert that i've had here has been incredible, the first time that I dined here it was the chocolate truffle dessert and this time it was the best strawberry dessert that i've ever had, "Fraise des Bois Frappé Brulée", it was so perfect and I wish that I could have it again. The other dessert was one that looked like a carrot (for the spring season) and I couldn't get enough of that one either. 
The service was also wonderful, everyone was very friendly and happy which I didn't see much of at other restaurants in New York. Our waiter also took a bunch of great photos of us after our meal! Gabriel Kreuther is one of my favorite restaurants, I will be back in the future for sure.
If you're thinking about going then just do it, you won't regret it! 
(May 2023)

A MUST try. We had the chefs tasting menu and was pleasantly surprised by thing I would have never ordered on my own. Everything was delicious and the service was attentive and caring, 10/10 experience!

Amazingly good meal! No wonder they got a Second Michelin Star! They are one of the best restaurants in NYC and one of the most reasonably priced Michelin Two Star restaurants anywhere in the world!  They start with delicious amuse bouches and end with tasty mignardises and every course in between tasted fabulous!

The restaurant is elegant and the service is professional and, dare I say, indulgent.  Wonderful place for a business dinner, a romantic dinner, or just a fun dinner with good friends!

I can barely wait to go back again the next time I am in NYC!

Amazing restaurant and amazing service. I got the prix fixe option and was absolutely blown away with the craftsmanship of the dishes. Definite must try restaurant and very deserving of the Michelin stars!

What I got: 
- Foie Gras Terrine
- Scallop
- Duck Breast
- (cant remember the name of the dessert) 

I came here for my birthday and they threw in this cute little cake as well. I want to say it was pistachio flavored but I can't tell besides the fact that it was green. 

Amazing place and I can't wait to come back again!

Started at the bar with a brandy Alexander which was good. Served homemade (stale) potato chips. Ordered a bottle of water and was served tap water instead. On to the food: started with caviar that was very good but it was served with a bread type of cracker that had too much flavor so it altered the taste of the caviar also the cracker wasn't exactly flat which caused the caviar to fall off of it. Then we had white truffles shaved over pasta. The truffles had very little flavor. They had to be stale they seemed to have lost their pungency. Certainly not worth the extra money. Had black bass for the main course. It was very good but the white sauce that was poured over it was not to my liking. The wine was  nowhere near ready to drink (too oaky). Desert was good. The water service was not. Sparkling water was poured over still water as well as tap water poured over bottled water. Was this a two Michelin star dining experience? I don't think so. I will not even mention what this all cost. It was a disappointing dinner.

What an amazing experience from start to finish! I came here with my husband for our anniversary and the team made it special from the start! We were welcomed at our table with a cute card and also a special dessert and the end. A few other couples around us were also celebrating anniversaries - would highly recommend for any special occasion or otherwise, though!

Come hungry, because the portions were generous. By the time I got to the main course, I was already getting stuffed, ha! All of the food was amazing but the highlight for me was surprisingly the gazpacho (and this is coming from someone who typically doesn't like soups)! Also loved all of the desserts, especially the chocolates.

I've been to other Michelin starred restaurants in NYC but I have to say that Gabriel Kreuther may be my favorite to date!
Phenomenal Michelin 2 star dining experience, and the first in NYC for me. Flawless from start to finish. Wine pairing was excellent.

Easily one of the best fine dining experiences of my life!

Decided to go with the 4 course prix fixe menu and it was layered with surprises. I was astounded by some of the flavor pairings that were done - the highlight being the foie gras terrine with this amazing citrusy gelatin. Was one of those enthralling, spiritual moments that reminds you why fine dining experiences are worth the price. The $195 menu is one of the best deals around as far as fine dining goes in Manhattan! Service was white glove as expected and executed flawlessly throughout the meal. The sommelier also came up with brilliant suggestions. The bottle we settled on complemented each course perfectly - sweet and savory - which is an incredibly difficult feat. 

Will definitely be back!

I'm just gonna say it: this place was too fancy for me haha. 
It was an interesting experiencing to say the least. The food was amazing. I'd expect nothing less from a Michelin-star restaurant that cost $500 per person. I don't remember everything I ate but I remember near the end I was like "oh man i'm full". 
Service was impeccable, although I'm pretty sure out waited thought we were out of our depths being at a restaurant as fancy as this one and not dressed to the nines. The couple at the table next to ours were also mocking us for our uncouthness. Sorry we don't shell out $500 every week to eat at fine dining restaurants. Most people don't have that kind of money to spare.
Needless to say, I did like the food and maybe one day, we'll go back when we have more money to throw around.
The Chef Tasting was truly exceptional. Despite relatively small portions, the abundance of courses contributed to an overall enjoyable dining experience.

Chef Gabriel Kreuther is the chef and the name behind this restaurant, offering a 3- or 4-course Alsatian tasting menu, lunch and dinner menu, as well as a chef's table option.

 We opted to do the chef's tasting menu, which included the following:
+Savory Kougelhopf - with chive fromage blanc
+Shiso Mojito - with white chocolate and mint powder
+Ginger & Pineapple Kombucha - with coconut snow
+Meyer Lemon Meringue - with a juniper hush puppy
+Mezcal Paloma Pate de Fruit - with aleppo and sea salt
+Local Ramp & Potato Panisse - with herbs aioli
+Aged Yellowtail Kingfish Crudo - with fermented farro, pickled purple radish, and mandarin vinaigrette
+Hawaiian Red Crab - with pickled jicama, aji peppers, and lentil "hummus"
+Kumamoto Oyster & Bison Tartare - with golden kaluga caviar, yuzu, and einkorn cracker
+Foie Gras Terrine & Country Pate - with honey-poached rhubarb, husk cherries, and housemade butter bread
+Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart - with applewood smoke, celery, root cream, and imperial kaluga caviar
+French White Asparagus Cooked in Kombu & Clay - with garm egg aioli, celery root cream, and imperial kaluga caviar
+Baked Bucks County Polenta - with riverine rach water buffalo, local butternut squash, and red wine mornay
+Hay Smoked - Two Week Aged Duck Breast - with spiced sweet potatoes, toasted cashew, and apple-mustard brown butter
+Roasted Farro & Chicken Consomee - with kelp oil
+Carrot - with buckwheat sable, orange cream espuma, and carrot sorbet
+Fraise des Bois Frappe Brulee - with sable breton, fresh fraise des bois, and tarragon sorbet
+Banana Foster - with passion fruit sauce and macadamia toffee

Everything was plated beautifully, and the succession of the courses with its pacing was good.  I just wasn't fan of some of the ingredients, such as the mint powder, the farro, or the aleppo as it was too overwhelming and ruined the dish.

Service was friendly and attentive.

The interior is nice, as it seems like you're having a meal in some type of an enclosed garden or a patio.

+chef's tasting menu
+overpowering ingredients
The best place I ever been. Food and atmosphere were superb and all of people were so kind.

GB makes the grade as a Michelin two star. Very civilized, superb food, comfortable ambiance, and competent staff. But no extra touches that might point to a third star. 
The adjacent bar offers a much lower cost option for those interested in a drink and a light bite. For the latter, bar seating and tables are available.

We celebrated my husband's birthday at Gabriel this year and couldn't be happier with our choice. The food, the service, the ambiance, everything is top notch! The tasting menu is elaborate and every dish looks and tastes fantastic. The BEST, really BEST, Foie gras I've ever had, and I've fine dined in Paris! I've posted some of the photos from our dinner but there was more. We will be back!

Loved Gabriel Kreuther! Came here with my husband for our anniversary dinner and really felt appreciated! The space is beautiful and we were sat in this gourgeous area with lots of space between each table. Our server was extremely attentive. By the end of the meal, they gave us an extra pastry for celebrating our anniversary and a hand-written card from Gabriel Keuther congratulating us on our anniversary! My husband has a lot of food restrictions and we were able to order off the menu a la cart. Everything we ordered tasted s delicious! The presentation is just as good as the taste too. The price was so reasonable for a wonderful Michelin star restaurant! Would 100% recommend for those looking for a romantic night out!

What more can I add that already hasn't been said about GK. An absolutely outstanding evening eating some of the best food I've tasted in quite awhile. We sat in the lounge area and service was absolutely stellar. The interior is lush, upscale without being stuffy or over the top. We opted for the 3 and 4 course menu. Everything was absolutely fantastic but the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart, duck breast and venison were three incredible dishes. Seriously, the  tart is simply iconic. Price point wise, yes GK is not cheap but a tremendous value for the money spent. I will not be surprised if they earned a third michelin star in the not too distant future.

Fantastic experience.  Came to celebrate a birthday and the restaurant, from the hostess, to staff, including a complimentary cake with candle, did everything it could to acknowledge the occasion.  The tasting menu, with breads, amuse bouche with a star of clams and green caviar, was exquisite.  The venison was the best meat I ever tasted.  I topped it off a Broadway Boulvardier cocktail (bourbon, smoked), red wine and scotch.  Beautiful decor.  You see where they get their two stars!!

v eastern french slightly german influence 
with modern flair 

came here last minute before a broadway show having passed the location on multiple occasions evoking a sense of curiosity about this 2 Michelin star restaurant. we were sat in the lounge area due to a mixup with the reservation party count, but it was still very nice. 

one of the servers wasn't assigned to our table but we still flagged him down when we were ready to order. yet when faced with questions of the menu and a bit of hesitation, he had an unpleasant air of disdain 

the other servers and hosts were very nice (except for the one i spoke to over the phone who was very unaccomodating) 

the food was delicious everything was exceptional except for the foie gras which was just okay and the dessert at the end which was too much chocolate (we didn't know the compliments of the chef were also chocolate so we ordered a dessert menu). 

would love to come back another time to try other things

Came here for a private room corporate dinner. I got the hamachi which was good but not amazing. The gnocchi was delicious and so was the red snapper. And the tropical cheese was very good. The service was great. We had passed appetizers such as mushroom flatbread which was great and bacon flatbread not my fav but i don't love bacon. The duck fritters were also ok but not amazing. And the veg tapenade was very good as well. The space is a bit old school and i can't comment on the price since i was invited on a pre fixe menu. But out of the Michelin star restaurants I've been to- i would say this is good but nothing out of this world. There's definitely better for the price.

Worth it!  Love the ambience, service and definitely the food.  This is a 2 Michelin Star restaurant!  And it deserves to be one!  It is a kind of restaurant I could only make a dish of because they all need 6-10 people like me to fix the entire dinner from amuse bouche to desserts and after dessert treats.  Every sauce and bread and dips are one of a kind flavors immersed.
Tasting menu has unique and delicate courses. There are lots of cavier throughout the tasting menu. The different types of bread throughout the menu was a highlight and nice surprises.

First time at a Michelin star restaurant. Very impressed with the service, everyone was great. This was a last minute decision after a Broadway show. Food was unique and not really my cup of tea but I was impressed with the selection and presentation. The rest of my party loved everything they ate.

came here to celebrate a special birthday and I have to say I was blown away. the food was incredible but what was also amazing was the service. the entire staff wished a happy birthday multiple times, sent out a free dessert, as well as the chef to come and speak with us and sign a menu for my husband. it was such a special birthday indeed and i'm so happy that I chose gabriel kreuther to celebrate. you will not be disappointed!!!

It was the first Michelin restaurant my gf and I ever ate it. It was a disappointment. The waiter was great. Most the food was genuinely bad. Not just by fancy restaurant standards. I mean in general. One of the dishes was literally the equivalent of a microwaved flatbread. The duck tasted like ham. One appetizer was essentially canned salmon. The cocktails were bad as well, except this one fruity red one. I forget the name. And needless to say, the bill for the sub par food was astronomical. Do not go here. It was one of the biggest dining let downs I ever had.
Everything is precisely executed. Fantastic place. Worth a try in your life. Food is always consistent. Service and dining room, one of the best in town.

Have been longing to go to Gabriel kreuther for couple of years. I don't know why I didn't make out time earlier to be here. 
Place is a gem. A gem where it is right next to Bryant park. A gem where place is well design for dining experience. A gem where no matter 3,4 or even chef tasting menu are all accommodate to all type of people. 
I love it. 

We had chefs tasting menu which consists of 7 courses. (But they have so many complimentary small dish ). 
Starting with appetizer, it is refreshing. I love the freshness to start the meal.  
We had ravioli, tartar, fluke and duck breast for main entry.  Every single dish is exceptional. I like the duck breast the most. 
Desert is the most disappointing part. I wish they could go with some traditional French dessert but ended with a strawberry styled something(sorry I am bad at names).  I just felt like it didn't match with my expectations. 
Overall, a solid dinner for me. 
I would give 4.5 for the food.

What an experience! We were absolutely blown away by this restaurant. We have been to other Michelin star restaurants and this is by far our favorite. We were treated like royalty. We had impeccable service, outstanding food, and an unforgettable evening. They even ask if you have plans after dinner so they can time the check (we did have a Broadway show). It was like they covered everything. My husband and I had the three course prix fixe, we had the foie gras, squash panna cotta, the lamb saddle, the duck breast, and the chocolate choux frappe. Everything was outstanding, even the bread service. Our servers were so kind and attentive. And to top it all off, we were invited to tour the kitchen and meet the chefs afterwards, and we told them how much we appreciated their art. They even took pictures with us. It was really a special night and we will definitely be returning!
Incredible food, top notch service, the place looks beautiful inside, celebrated my wedding anniversary here and it was well worth the experience.

Came here with my family to celebrate my birthday along with my 2 kids age 7 and 9. It's not my first time here so needless to say, it is one of my favorite restaurant in the city hence I wanted to come back for the special occasion.  Gabriel Kreuther is one of very few fine dining restaurants in nyc that, in my opinion, welcomes and accommodates children (some say they do but will tell you kids will also need to order the tasting menu).  

We opted for their 4 course prix fixe menu for each adult and they were very easy going in terms of how we want to order for our kids. We decided to order one more prix fixe menu for both kids to share and in addition, we ordered an extra entree and their applewood smoked bacon tarte flambée to share. The flambée, although I didn't get a chance to try it because both of my kids devoured it in no time, was said to be the best "pizza" ever according to my kids. Their amuse bouche was impressive and abundant. Each little bite was refreshing and well executed and it was like a mini 4 course meal before we dive into our actual meal. 

I ordered their spiced tuna loin as my first course. It was refreshing and well seasoned and I loved the added texture from the melon. The smokiness and acid from the tomato water added another level of flavors and was well executed to bring out the freshness of the fish.  I ordered the sturgeon and sauerkraut tart for my next course and this one never fails. It's amazing how there can be so many different flavors and textures in one little tart. The flavors were well balanced between the saltiness from the fish and caviar, the sourness from the sauerkraut, and the creaminess from the sabayon so it didn't feel very heavy at all. I ordered the duck for my entrée and this is one of my favorite dish. The duck was tender and cooked to a perfect medium, the skin was crispy and I think the ginger jus is genius. It can mask away the gamey taste from the duck and neutralize the heaviness of eating meat altogether. For my dessert, I ordered their citrus panna cotta. It was pretty, the fruits were fresh, and the acid was well balanced with the pomegranate sorbet and the panna cotta. This is the perfect dessert for a hot summer day. Their portion is generous. I was so stuffed that I was only able to eat 1 of the duck breast pieces. We had so much food that we had to pack some of the food home which is rare at fine dining restaurants. The 4 course menu at $195, in my opinion, is very reasonable especially when compared to how much the restaurant business increased their price post Covid. Since their portion size was so big, our party of 5 was able to taste many different dishes by ordering different items in their menu and sharing amongst ourselves. 

Their service was impeccable from the moment we walking into the restaurant until the time we walked out. Everyone was very friendly, attentive and accommodating.  I've been to many Michelin rated restaurants in the city and this is definitely one of my favorite. Every dish was solid and well executed and I didn't have anything to complain about.  This is the place I will continue to return over and over again.

This place I've been dying to try to eat for over a year since I discovered it on social media. And I was not disappointed a bit. In fact this was probably one of the best meals I've ever had. And all I do is travel and eat at the best restaurants in the world, and this is definitely in my top 5 restaurants I love! Every single dish I had just blew my mind, jaw dropping and just wow. Service was amazing as expected. Very knowledgeable and friendly. Decor was modern and beautiful. Didn't feel pretentious at all. Just soothing. Over all, can't wait to come back!

The atmosphere is good, the service is first-class, do not look at the waiter, because a casual glance, or a small move, he will come right away!  
Cost-effective is medium, can be regarded as "spend a small amount of money loaded big force"  how to say is also M two ah
Meals are optional, with 3-Course and 4-Course or the brainless $255 chef tasting Menu
It was quite good, there were one or two amazing dishes, but overall it was delicious 
The speed of serving food is ok, and will not be sleepy

Service is amazing, trumps other boutique restaurants in the city. Everyone is so personable and amicable, they make you feel relaxed and comfortable. The drinks are wonderful, large selection of wine and exotic cocktails. 

The fresh bread and butter, omg! So good lol the rest of the food is obviously splendid. Each dish is created to perfection and the presentation is just wonderful. The ube and chocolate desserts are a work of art. All desserts are simply incredible. Love this place, will be back for more!

As very frequent patrons of Michelin-rated establishments, throughout the US and abroad, this one missed the mark, especially for a 2 star.

Food - we opted for one selection from the "to share" menu and then did the 3 course menu from there.  All of the savory dishes were quite good but the desert, Ube Pearl, was gimmicky and far too sweet, lacking balance.

Service - simply put, unsophisticated at best.  Sure, everyone will stand aside as you make your way through the restaurant but our server lacked polish and, quite frankly, was weird and socially awkward.  He would stop by to initiate the most random, out of left field discussions and then walk off.  Upon placing our order, we inquired about 2 dishes on the menu and our server's response was just, 'what do you want to know about (blank)?' Instead of going into a description of where the ingredients were sourced (truly a miss for the Montauk Royal red shrimp which many diners likely do not know what makes them special), or to artfully explain the preparation, and/or presentation.  Once we were done with our entrees, our plates were left sitting in front of us for almost 20 minutes before being cleared.  Both fails for a restaurant meant to be of this caliber, IMO.  We also waited far too long for our drinks when first seated.

Decor - where to even begin here?  The design of the space is all over the place.  It felt equal parts industrial, French country, Las Vegas and your grandmother's all rolled into one.  From an ergonomics standpoint, there are uncomfortable pillows placed along the benches and every table we observed had cast them aside because they were miserable to rest your back against.  They were also red in color with the only other red in the space the exit signs, and lost in a sea of greens, ivories and blacks against the mismatched wood, metallic ceiling and wrought iron with a random hanging bird installation hanging from the ceiling.  If you are looking for a serene setting, this is most certainly not it as one cannot help but feel overwhelmed by the chaotic and schizophrenic design selections which, along with the mediocre service, takes away from the food which, again, was quite good minus the desert.

Lastly, I would say that the restaurant felt tourist-heavy with guests dressed in everything from tuxedos to hooded sweatshirts and sneakers.  Maybe it was because it was a Saturday and the restaurant is Times Square-adjacent but it just felt unsophisticated.  

For $900 for two people, there are far better options up and down the Michelin rating scale in NYC to take advantage of instead of this one.

Tasting menu Lunch at Gabriel Kreuther was absolutely fantastic! The service was impeccable--attentive, warm, and perfectly paced. The food is rich and regal, with each dish feeling like a work of art. Despite the indulgent mains, the desserts were a delightful surprise--light, playful, and a perfect way to end the meal.

To top it all off, I left with a signed cookbook, which made the experience even more special. If you're looking for an unforgettable dining experience with a touch of elegance, Gabriel Kreuther is the place to go!

I haven't eaten in a Michelin restaurant in so long. I truly enjoyed everything I ate at Gabriel Kreuther. Jesus was our waiter but everyone in the restaurant works together. 
I loved that they have us extras like kombucha, tequila, chocolate. We all ordered from the 3 course price fixed many. I ordered the tuna for my appetizer and the trout for my entree and your pizzelle for my dessert. We also ordered two bottles of wine and that was delicious as well. 
The service was immaculate and the ambience spectacular. Sometimes you have to treat yourself to a wonderful meal.

For a restaurant with two Michelin stars, this place is very disappointing to say the least. 

The Long Island duck and the beef tartare were decent and pretty flavorful. Otherwise, the food was unsatisfactory, especially for a two Michelin star restaurant. Portions were also small and overpriced. 

On top of that, the service was very slow. I was told that the prix fixe menu would take an hour and a half, but it actually took three hours. The staff were not very attentive and barely checked on us while we waited 45 minutes for food.

I walked out of the restaurant feeling displeased and not even full. I will not be coming back.

this is an absolutely devine delicious restaurant worthy of it's prestige.  the food was stunning and i loved how the place looked, it was just so spacious and beautiful.  the drinks and the desserts are out of this world!  Love this place!

The atmosphere in the dining room is spacious, yet a bit minimalist and sterile. Nonetheless, the food was fantastic. The foie gras torchon, the ahi tuna, the duck and salmon, were delicious although I thought the entree dishes were a bit on the larger side given we had 4 courses. That said, the standout dish was the sabayon/sturgeon tart. It's been on the menu from the opening and it is a must have.

2 Michelin stars but probably deserves a 3rd!  Place is great all around and one of my favorite experiences.  Staff was on point and food was beyond top notch.  Ambiance was great too.  Will make this a regular place to visit!

Visited in November of 2024. California resident (me) very much was shocked by the generous food portion and flavorful tastes from the lunch chef's tasting menu in this NYC two Michelin star restaurant. Service style fits me. And the dining area is fine too. The food tastes are German related - I recall tasting sauerkraut under the caviar starter. Also thankful that the kitchen switched the ube pearl for me in the menu. The ube pearl is so pretty! Didn't want to knock it apart to eat. Definitely will go back for a la carte or the short pre fixe menu.

While expensive, Gabriel Kreuther is a classic and beautiful establishment with great food art! They kept bringing out these beautiful plates I was shocked as one by one they brought out different items! Everything about the meal was perfect from the menu to the server to the interior design. This is definitely a spot to take and impress your guest

This week, I had the pleasure of dining at Gabriel Kreuther to celebrate my birthday, and from the moment we arrived, the service was on point--attentive, professional, and genuinely warm. Everyone, from reception to our servers, congratulated us, and we even received a personally signed card from the chef, which made the night extra special.
We opted for their 4-course prix fixe menu. Since our selected wine wasn't ready, we were offered a complimentary glass of sparkling wine to start. Throughout the meal, amuse-bouches between courses added delightful surprises, making the experience even more exciting.

First course
* La Belle Foie Gras Terrine - delicious start, paired with pistachio, wild rice streusel, and marble brioche. The foie gras was smooth and rich. 
* Cashew & Wild Mushroom Pâté with Ossetra Caviar - one of my favorites! The earthy mushroom flavors paired beautifully with the salty caviar.

Mid course
* Sturgeon & Sauerkraut Tart - a GK's signature dish, and I see why! The imperial kaluga caviar and applewood smoke took it to another level. Every bite was incredible. 
* Gewürztraminer Poached Sullivan County Foie Gras - served with quince consommé, artichoke, and ginger froth, and it had a perfect balance of sweetness and richness.

Entree
* Hay-Smoked Two-Week Aged Hudson Valley Duck Breast - was perfectly cooked, tender, smoky, and packed with rich flavors of blistered cranberries, parsnip cream, and sweet potato. 
* Spiced Red Venison Loin -  cooked very well, the slight sweetness of the cranberries complements the dish beautifully.

Dessert
* Chestnut Mont Blanc with Vanilla Cake - light, airy, and delicious.
* Chocolate Tart Soufflé - I only had a bite since I'm not a chocolate fan, but my boyfriend loved it.
Additionally, I received a special complimentary dessert with a personalized congratulatory message--such a lovely touch!

This was easily one of the best fine dining experiences of my life. If you're looking for an exceptional meal in an elegant setting, Gabriel Kreuther is a must-visit--perfect for any special occasion!

After a long hiatus, we visited Gabriel Kreuther and had a superb dinner and experience. Every part of the evening was exceptional and so far superior to many of our recent "fancy" dinners in NYC.  The service is friendly and professional, perfectly so. Each course was excellent and we still really love the bread...We appreciated the recommendations of the waiter who took the time to advise us based on what he thought we might enjoy best. (I have to say that the only course I did not love - my desert - was one that I did not take the waiters suggestion). And the wine was superb - they still have an excellent wine list. We will be back again, sooner than the last interval...

Place is really nice. Big and open. 

I sat down and greeted by server. He explained the options. 
I ordered the Chefs menu since I wanted to have the full experience. 
I also ordered the reserve wine tasting as well. 
Now, you would think that when you spend that kind of money the wine person would spend time with you...not the case here. She was rushed. 

Overall a good-ish experience. Not sure it's worth the cost.
